The volume's central empirical anchor, distinguishing the Authority Gradient from simple exclusion, is Mbaye and colleagues' (2019) analysis of 1,182 biomedical studies conducted in Africa: over 93% included at least one Africa-based co-author, yet Africa-based researchers held first-author position in fewer than half, and senior last-author position in fewer still. A parallel 2026 study of new-species-description literature confirms the pattern: even when a resident researcher was included, that researcher held first-author position only 27.3% of the time. The volume formalizes this asymmetry using the CRediT Contributor Roles Taxonomy, arguing that Investigation and Resources convert to first authorship at systematically lower rates than Conceptualization, Funding Acquisition, and Writing, and closes by locating its own single-authored, uncollaborated production as an inversion of, rather than an instance of, the mechanism it describes.

items.title: The Gate That Moved: arXiv's Endorsement System, Algorithmic Popularity Bias, and the Conservation of Gatekeeping in Open Science.
items.pub: In In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive. Ho Chi Minh City: Zenodo.
items.venue: In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive
items.abstract: This volume turns the Consolidation Trap on the institutions this research program's author has personally relied on to circulate its own findings. The volume's central formal contribution is the Conservation of Gatekeeping: in any system receiving submissions at a volume exceeding what unmediated attention can process, some filtering mechanism must emerge to allocate the genuinely scarce resource — reader attention, which does not scale — and removing one filtering mechanism without resolving the underlying volume-to-attention ratio does not eliminate gatekeeping but displaces it, typically with less visibility and less contestability. The volume grounds this in arXiv's thirty-five-year history: founded in 1991 as an explicit escape from informal, personally-mediated preprint circulation, arXiv introduced its endorsement system in January 2004, a mechanism structurally continuous with guild apprenticeship and the Royal Society's gentlemanly witness, compressed into thirteen years. Most currently, in December 2025 and January 2026, arXiv removed institutional email affiliation as a sufficient basis for automatic endorsement, citing an unsustainable volume of non-scientific submissions, drawing a public comment naming the resulting system private gatekeeping. The volume's second empirical pillar is the popularity-bias literature in recommender systems and academic search ranking, mathematically continuous with the preferential attachment used to formalize faculty hiring concentration, and documented explicitly in academic paper ranking through venue-popularity weighting (Sun & Giles, 2007). A dedicated section addresses this program's own question, raised in its preface, of whether its central claims had already been reached elsewhere: it engages Hugh Desmond's (2024) independently argued case that gatekeeping should be conserved in the open-science era, and the broader diagnosis, from the general gatekeeping literature (Barzilai-Nahon 2009) and from a 2026 landscape survey of metascience (Watney & Gustetic 2026), that no unifying account of these mechanisms yet exists. The volume closes by subjecting the author's own primary circulation channel, PhilPapers and PhilArchive, to the same scrutiny, concluding that editorial screening constitutes a different gate rather than an absent one.

items.title: Just Above the Line: Grant Panels, the Uncertainty Discount, and the Return of Patronage in the Language of Peer Review.
items.pub: In In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive. Ho Chi Minh City: Zenodo.
items.venue: In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive
items.abstract: This volume extends the Consolidation Trap into research funding by formalizing the Uncertainty Discount, underlying three independently documented empirical findings. The Uncertainty Discount names the tendency of funding panels, required to convert an inherently uncertain judgment into a scalar decision under time pressure, to resolve that uncertainty asymmetrically: not as a symmetric unknown, but as a negative signal resolved by substituting an available proxy for direct assessment. The volume documents three such proxies. The first is past funding success itself. Bol, de Vaan, and van de Rijt (2018), using a regression-discontinuity design on a €2 billion Dutch grant program, find that early-career scientists who received an early grant by a margin indistinguishable from chance accumulated more than twice as much subsequent funding over eight years as observationally identical scientists who narrowly missed the same threshold. The second proxy is demographic prior. Ginther and colleagues (2011), analyzing the complete NIH R01 applicant pool, find Black applicants thirteen percentage points less likely than white applicants to receive funding, a gap narrowing to ten points but not closing after extensive controls, concentrated specifically at the review-scoring stage. The third proxy is intellectual familiarity, more precise than a simple novelty penalty: Boudreau, Guinan, Lakhani, and Riedl (2016), using a randomized experiment generating 2,130 evaluator-proposal pairs, find that evaluators score down proposals both too close to and too distant from their own expertise. The volume formalizes the discount as a decomposition of funding score into a quality signal and a proxy-driven uncertainty penalty, and situates the mechanism historically: the mid-twentieth-century transition from foundation and aristocratic patronage to formalized, panel-reviewed grant allocation, inaugurated by Vannevar Bush's 1945 report and the 1950 founding of the National Science Foundation, reproduces in the vocabulary of statistical proxy substantially the same distributive outcome the reform was designed to end.

items.title: From a Hundred Schools to One Doctrine: Institutional Consolidation, Peer Review, and the Political Sociology of Epistemic Arrest.
items.pub: In In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive. Ho Chi Minh City: Zenodo.
items.venue: In the Name of Merit: Six Gatekeeping Mechanisms, from the Hundred Schools of Thought to the Algorithmic Archive
items.abstract: This volume opens the Academic Politics research program by formalizing a single historical mechanism, the Consolidation Trap, and tracing its instantiation across two widely separated cases: the transition from the Hundred Schools of Thought (諸子百家) of Warring States China to the state-sponsored Confucian orthodoxy established under Emperor Wu of Han on Dong Zhongshu's counsel, and the transition from pre-institutional scientific publishing to the mid-twentieth-century formalization of anonymous peer review. The Consolidation Trap names the structural pattern by which the same mechanism introduced to solve a genuine coordination problem in a period of open, cross-domain competition — filtering noise, allocating scarce publication or patronage capacity, establishing minimum quality thresholds — becomes, once institutionalized, a mechanism that filters signal indistinguishably from noise whenever that signal does not conform to prevailing paradigm assumptions. The volume does not evaluate peer review in moral language; it analyzes it in mechanism language, formalizing four component dynamics: paradigm enforcement (Kuhn 1962), consensus bias, the anonymous-review accountability deficit (extending Gieryn's 1983 boundary-work concept from public science communication to reviewer behavior), and citation-cartel dynamics (Merton's 1968 Matthew Effect, and its adversarial limit case documented in the Ike Antkare fabricated-author experiment, Labbé 2010). Empirical grounding is drawn from the 1936 Einstein–Physical Review incident, establishing peer review as a contingent twentieth-century innovation rather than a timeless requirement; from the NeurIPS peer-review consistency experiments, documenting near-random accept/reject agreement between independent review committees evaluating identical submissions; and from the disciplinary-silo literature documenting the institutional persistence of boundary maintenance independent of its stated justification. The volume closes by treating its own conditions of production — authored without institutional affiliation, evaluated on argumentative merit rather than credentialed standing — as a live empirical instance of the argument rather than a disclaimer external to it.

items.title: The Governance of Co-Experience Transmission: A Generative Relational Theory of Institutional Design under Interpretive Asymmetry.
items.abstract: An account of a shared experience is composed by one participant in a relation and used by a third party who took no part in it. An earlier paper in this series established how positive law allocates authority over such an account and stated the conditions any defensible allocation would satisfy, proposing no regime. This paper asks whether an apparatus could administer those conditions, at what cost, and with what failure modes. It argues that only process requirements are available, since an output standard would demand a comparison between an account and the experience it reports that the ontology of the object denies, and that this is the limiting case of a condition under which regulatory theory independently recommends prescribing process rather than output. Five mechanisms are examined against the inherited specification: a duty to solicit and consider the other participant's rendering before issuing, a forum operating before an account is relied upon, preservation of the materials a later reopening would require, expiry of the entitlement to rely, and restriction of exchange. The last is disqualified by the paper's own definition of a mechanism, since the non-occurrence of a private exchange cannot be established; two lines of the specification are reached by nothing available. Three findings run against the proposals. The feature that makes these mechanisms resistant to ceremonial adoption, namely that discharge requires an act by the party they protect, is the feature that places the work upon that party; the cost falls on every occasion of issuance while the benefit falls on the few contested; and raising what is required of an issuer may contract the practice, in a direction that is documented and by a magnitude that is not, falling hardest on those with fewest relations from which an account might be drawn. That result exposes an inconsistency internal to the framework rather than a conflict between the paper's two routes, and two of the framework's criteria are accordingly restated as matters of degree rather than as thresholds.

items.title: Recommendation Injustice: Pathologies of Shared-Experience Transmission through the Alienation of Recommenders into Relational Credit.
items.abstract: Institutions that select people ask others to vouch for them. This paper asks what circulates when they do. Classical political economy studies the circulation of goods, and the economics of collateral-free lending the circulation of skill where no assessment reaches; what a reference circulates is neither. It is co-experience: what a relation generated between two parties, available only from the positions those parties occupied. Co-experience so understood is heterogeneous, and heterogeneous things do not circulate directly. A generalised order of circulation therefore requires a general equivalent, one term excluded from the set it measures and installed as the measure of the rest. The paper's central claim is that this position is occupied by the standing of the recommender, and that occupying it is what alienation consists in here: the recommender ceases to be a party to the relation whose product is reported and becomes the measure by which such products are made comparable. What then circulates is their standing rather than their observation, and the relational labour that produced the standing becomes invisible in the same movement that makes the name liquid. The derivation is taken from the critique of political economy, and the paper states what does not transpose, since co-experience embodies no labour time and is not alienable by its producer in the way a product is. The alienated standing takes two forms. As a general equivalent it measures, circulates, and is indifferent to what it purchases; as an underwriting it binds the recommender's future to conduct they will not control. The first excludes and the second encumbers; the first is debased by over-issuance, whose cost falls on every holder, and the second impaired by default, whose cost falls on the signatory alone. This explains why the same party writes uniformly favourable accounts and declines to write at all. Three consequences follow. Disclosure theory predicts that voluntary disclosure unravels toward candour, and references conspicuously fail to unravel, because the unravelling logic bears on content while the instrument's force is separable from it, so the content compresses while the market in signatures thickens. Decision weight then falls onto the standing of the issuer, which is the unequally distributed quantity, and at the limit of that distribution are people with access to no issuer at all. Correcting the instrument does not correct this, since reconstructing well where …

items.title: Power in Recommendation and the Jurisprudence of Co-Experience: Who Has the Right to Interpret, Contest, Transmit, and Reproduce Shared Experience?
items.abstract: An account of a shared experience is composed by one participant in a relation and used by a third party who did not participate in it, while the person it describes is ordinarily absent. This paper asks what rights attach to such an account and to whom, treating interpretation, contestation, transmission, reproduction, and ownership as five aspects of one object on the ground that the scope of the last four is fixed by the allocation of the first. It argues along two routes kept separate throughout: a doctrinal survey of four legal systems, and derivation from a set of principles of relational reproduction. The survey finds one allocation repeated across provisions enacted in different systems for different purposes, namely that the person described is granted access to an account of themselves and is withheld authority over its content; access and interpretive authority are shown to be separately allocable, and the convergence is explained by the prior location of interpretive authority in whichever party composes the account. Three further findings are reported: no located doctrine confers an integrity interest upon the person a work describes; positive law names the operative force of instruments whose force it has itself constituted and supplies no name for the force of an instrument working without legal constitution, with the consequence that exchanges of such instruments have no description in property law; and the events an account reports lie outside copyright entirely. Where the two routes meet directly, they conflict: copyright denies that authorship of a jointly produced past is shared, and denies it for a stated reason the paper accepts as sound. The framework's principle is therefore amended rather than defended, separating a claim to participate in settling an interpretation, which survives, from a claim to own accounts of the experience, which is abandoned. Two questions are stated and left open, with the conditions an answer would require.

items.title: A Political Economy of Co-Experience.
items.abstract: An account of a co-experience is composed by one participant in a relation and used by a third party who took no part in it. Earlier volumes in this series established that the operative force of such an instrument is separable from the account it contains, is exchanged, and has no description in property law. This volume asks what a political economy of that object looks like: what circulates, on what terms, and what accumulates to whom. It argues that accounts drawn from singular relations admit no comparison from their content, so that comparability is supplied by the standing of the party who issued them; that a party whose standing serves in this office stands to the accounts compared as a measure stands to what is measured, so that the co-experiences in which that party participated fall outside the set the operation compares; and that the structure so described is Marx's analysis of the general equivalent, whose extension beyond the commodity has been made by others and whose application to a party who measures by issuing accounts has not. The volume then examines what accumulates. A standing grows by being exercised and is not diminished by exercise; it admits no transfer, so a concentration of standings admits no correction by transfer and acquisition runs solely through positions in institutional hierarchies. The vocabulary of capital applies in respect of accumulation, return, and reproduction and fails at alienation; the vocabulary of financialisation applies in respect of prospective valuation and fails at the assignable claim. On circulation the volume finds a practice conducted in three exchange relations of which it names one, whose content degrades under unverifiability by two compounding mechanisms, and which is market-inalienable in fact while unprohibited in law. Two findings run against the position of the series: the conditions of issuance are reproduced by the asymmetry that made the practice worth examining, and the instruments proposed to improve it carry a contraction of it as their cost. The volume argues that these pose a question the series has not answered, namely whether its aim is the reform of the practice or its reduction, and that no further work on remedies should proceed before the question is settled. The volume proceeds without prices, units, or series, and states the methods that operate without them.

items.title: How To Do Things With Prompts.
items.abstract: When users address large language models, they produce directive speech acts whose pragmatic features differ from those of both everyday conversation and traditional human-computer interaction, and these features change as users gain familiarity with the systems they address. This paper applies speech act and politeness theory to a corpus-pragmatic analysis of 2,000 English-language prompts drawn from publicly shared ChatGPT conversations, 1,000 from 2023 and 1,000 from 2025, using the ShareChat dataset. Each prompt is annotated for illocutionary force, directness, propositional content, and the presence of politeness markers, and the distribution of these features is compared across the two sampling years. The results show a consistent movement toward indirect, implicit, and fragmentary realizations of directive force, accompanied by a decline in politeness marking. The largest single change, a shift of 14.9 percentage points, occurs in propositional content, where explicit specification of the requested action gives way to implicit reliance on the system's inferential capacity, suggesting that users have updated their model of what the system can recover from reduced input, treating it as a competent implicature resolver. Rather than asking whether LLMs "really" understand language, we should ask: what kind of language have we created in learning to speak to them?

items.title: Can the Finnish Education System Offer a Useful Direction for Iran? (A Comparative Reflection on School Avoidance, Emotional Attachment, and the Development of a Safe Educational Environment).
items.abstract: Finland is one of the countries whose education system has attracted considerable attention from educational researchers and policymakers around the world. Particularly following the strong performance of Finnish students in the early cycles of the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), beginning in 2000, Finnish education came to be regarded in many academic and public discussions as a successful and distinctive example, and was sometimes described as an “educational miracle.” At the same time, academic research on Finland has emphasized the importance of historical, social, and cultural factors and has warned against overly simple interpretations of international assessment results. The central question of this paper is whether, despite the fundamental cultural and social differences between Finland and Iran, the Finnish educational experience can provide useful insights for reflecting on educational challenges in Iran. Rather than advocating the direct imitation of the Finnish system, this paper focuses on whether some of its underlying principles and experiences can be considered and adapted within the cultural and social context of Iran. Two closely related issues are emphasized. The first is school avoidance, understood in this paper not merely as physical absence from school, but also as students’ psychological, emotional, and motivational disengagement from the learning environment. The second is the strengthening of emotional bonds between students, teachers, and the school. The argument is that addressing these two issues appropriately may contribute to the development of a safe educational environment—one in which students gradually internalize the value of discipline rather than merely accepting it through coercion; learn to understand and identify problems and then work toward solving them; become capable of accepting differences in perspectives; and develop a responsible understanding of their relationship with society. On this basis, four major educational objectives are proposed, with one of them—problem-solving—consisting of two distinct stages: creating a sense of security; developing the ability to understand and identify problems and subsequently solve them; learning to interact with people who are different; and understanding the reciprocal relationship between the individual and society. The paper argues that these objectives can provide a framework for examining how selected elements of the Finnish educational …

items.title: When Minds Merge: Neural Telepathy, Neurorights, and the Limits of Voluntary Privacy Waiver.
authors: López de la Peña de Pablo, Mercedes
items.abstract: The rapid advance of neurotechnology has produced a vibrant scholarly and legislative debate around neurorights — a proposed generation of human rights designed to protect mental privacy, cognitive liberty, mental integrity, and psychological continuity against the most threatening applications of neurotechnology. This article argues that the neurorights framework, while representing a genuine and important advance in the governance of neurotechnology, contains a structural blind spot: it was designed to protect individuals from non-consensual external interferences and is not well equipped to address scenarios in which individuals voluntarily choose to waive or dissolve their own mental privacy. To illuminate this limitation, the article focuses on a paradigm case made increasingly plausible by contemporary brain–computer interface (BCI) research: the scenario of a group of individuals who voluntarily interconnect their nervous systems into a form of technological "neural telepathy," sharing thoughts, emotions, and mental imagery continuously and without filter. We argue that such a scenario cannot be adequately governed by neurorights alone and demands a complementary framework of neuroduties — legally and morally binding obligations that flow from the embodied, relational nature of the human person and that constrain certain forms of radical voluntary self-transformation. We develop the philosophical foundations of this framework, engaging directly with liberal autonomy theory and with existing legal instruments, and identify three clusters of problems raised by consensual neural interconnection: (1) mental health and the preservation of the bounded self; (2) personal identity, individuation, and the attribution of moral and legal responsibility; and (3) the irreducible social and legal functions of privacy that transcend individual preference.

items.title: 「好」與「對」在回應什麼？——華語回應詞中的狀態採納與表徵核對.
items.abstract: 華語「好」與「對」都可以作為對前一話語的肯定性回應。一般描述常將「好」與接受、同意、請求、提議、安排或話語轉折相連，而將「對」與確認、命題內容、判斷一致或資訊核對相連。這些區分能有效描述兩者常見的分布，但在若干最小對照中，前一話語的內容類型並不足以決定回應形式：同一個命題、安排或行動內容，往往既可以回答「好」，也可以回答「對」，而兩者所形成的理解並不相同。 -/- 本文首先以一組具有不同驗證成本的算術陳述作為對照，例如「3+4=7」、「12×11=132」與「37×24=888」。隨著結果不再容易被立即確認，「好」仍可自然地將該結果直接納入當前可運作狀態；「對」則更容易使是否存在可供比對的相關依據成為可察覺的問題。這一差異顯示，「好」與「對」的作用未必首先取決於前一話語屬於何種內容，而可能涉及回應者如何處理前一話語所形成的內容。 -/- 本文據此提出一項結構性的分析：「好」傾向將前一話語所提出的內容登記並採納為當前可運作狀態的一部分，使其成為後續互動、決策或推理可以直接沿用的基礎；「對」則傾向將前一話語所提出的內容與相關表徵進行交差檢查，並將兩者是否吻合的驗證結果返回當前互動。這也意味著，「對」並非單純不造成更新。例如在「明天三點，對嗎？——對」中，回應者本身的相關內容狀態可以維持不變，但其驗證結果仍會更新提問者對該內容的認知狀態。 -/- 為顯示兩種操作在連續互動中的差異，本文進一步以一段會議對話範例作為主要討論材料，觀察「好」與「對」如何在同一段話語中反覆交替。分析顯示，決定「好」或「對」的關鍵並不在於前一話語包含的是命題、行動還是安排，而在於回應者如何處理該話語所提出的內容。即使前一話語包含明確的行動與任務，只要回應者此刻是在將其與相關表徵進行核對，「對」仍可自然出現。反之，即使前一話語提出的是具有明確真值、原則上可以獨立驗證的命題，回應者也未必需要先完成驗證；當該內容被直接登記並採納為後續處理可以沿用的基礎時，「好」同樣可以成立。換言之，兩詞的差異不首先落在被回應內容的性質，而在於該內容是被拿來與相關表徵比對，還是被直接納入當前可運作狀態。 -/- 本文因此將「好」與「對」視為兩種不同的回應處理結構，並主張常見的「請求／提議—好」與「命題／確認—對」分布，可進一步理解為不同話語環境對狀態採納與表徵核對兩種操作的偏好，而非兩詞對前置內容類型的固定選擇。最後，本文將「好」與「不好」是否構成對稱的回應操作保留為後續研究問題。.

items.title: The Atlas: Phase-Locked Geometric Neural Manifolds on Mixed-Curvature Hyperbolic–Toroidal Product Spaces.
items.abstract: We give a complete formal specification of Atlas, a phase-locked geometric representation sub- strate whose state space is the mixed-curvature Riemannian product M= Hn ×Tn. The hyper- bolic factor carries semantic lineage (exponential volume growth, low-distortion hierarchy); the flat toroidal factor carries cyclic rhythm, its fundamental group π1(Tn)∼ = Zn supplying integer winding charges provably immune to continuous metric perturbation. We (i) construct the com- posite geodesic metric dM = whd2 H + wt d2 T with golden-ratio φ−k angular decay and prove its total weight mass is exactly φ; (ii) prove homotopy-invariance of the discrete winding vector un- der bounded perturbation and formalize dual-chart disagreement as the separator of lineage drift from harmonic rhythm over the lemniscate lobes; (iii) derive the asymmetric log-odds regula- ˙ tor κ = κ(1−κ)˙ z, whose exact solution is the logistic sigmoid — an intrinsic (0, 1) interlock — and prove the φ2 ≈2.618×penalty asymmetry under the conservation identity SC·SR = s2; (iv) derive the superposition holding loss Lk = exp(ρDk)−1, prove (Lemma 3) the strict bound supk Lk < e−1 ≈1.71828 for all |vk|≤1, ρ ∈(0, 1), and prove Theorem 9 showing > 38.2% re- duction in drift settling time (T Atlas drift ≤1 drift ϕ T Euclidean ); and (v) specify the post-quantum Rosen Bridge: ML-KEM-768 + X25519 hybrid KEM with HKDF-SHA-256 transcript binding, the COROS enve- lope (AES-256-GCM + AES-CTR whitening + constant-time 256-byte padding), and a counter- free forward window Ω= 32 on the hyperbolic geodesic ratchet with a qΩ2−128 forgery bound. Every gate is a checkable inequality. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22166230.

items.title: The Unmediated Normativity of Acquaintance.
items.abstract: Russell characterized acquaintance as an unmediated, non-propositional relation between a subject and the objects of perception that yields knowledge of objects. But the claim that the relation is unmediated admits of metaphysical, conceptual, and normative readings that have not been properly distinguished. The normative reading, in particular, has been overlooked, yet matters independently of whether acquaintance is also metaphysically or conceptually unmediated. On this reading, the experiential presence of objects instantiates final epistemic value, and this evaluative fact is not explained by more basic epistemic statuses, even if the value-bearing state depends causally or metaphysically on other processes. The normative reading vindicates Russell’s motivations for positing acquaintance, especially the intuitions of indubitability and ineffability, without metaphysical excess, while preserving what is essential: a real relation of presence that lies at the foundation of epistemic normativity.

items.title: Von Neumann’s Measurement Chain without Dualism: Subjective Perception as the Natural Endpoint under Phenomenological Absolutism and Mutual Exclusivity.
items.abstract: Von Neumann’s 1932 analysis of the quantum measurement chain establishes that unitary evolution can be extended through any physical apparatus or the observer’s body, and that the formalism supplies no intrinsic criterion for locating a non-unitary cut. The later rejection of placing that terminus at subjective perception did not follow from a defect in the chain argument. It followed from a physicalist ontology that treats mind and world as ontologically distinct—an assumption the mathematics of quantum mechanics does not require. Under Phenomenological Absolutism and Mutual Exclusivity, each localized actualized field configuration is identical with the absolute is-ness of first-person phenomenology. On that ontology the endpoint is not an extra-physical intervention in a closed material chain. It is what an actualized configuration already is. We reconstruct von Neumann’s position with textual fidelity, distinguish it from later causal claims that consciousness collapses the state, and show that the dualistic objections lose their force once the extraneous metaphysical premise is withdrawn. The mathematics remains compatible with other interpretations. Our claim is that von Neumann’s conclusion fits naturally when the ontology does not smuggle in a subject–object split the theory itself never licensed.

items.title: Testing Architecture-Level Properties Relevant to Consciousness in Living Neural Biocomputing Systems.
items.abstract: Learning, adaptive behavior, or a linguistic report from a biocomputing system built of living neurons is not, by itself, evidence of consciousness. This paper proposes consciousness-ready biocomputing: an architecture — not a claim — for testing consciousness-relevant properties experimentally, causally, and ethically. It integrates recurrent processing, the global neuronal workspace, predictive processing, and higher-order self-modeling (sharpened via attention schema theory) in a living, multi-module network embodied in a virtual body with a sensorimotor loop, memory, and a self-modeling layer. We define an engineering metric, the Consciousness Readiness Index (CRI), as a jointly-necessary composite — not a linear sum — of global broadcast, causal recurrence, predictive quality, self-model stability, and network integration, so that a complete absence of any one component drives the index toward zero rather than being compensated for by another. CRI is not a probability of consciousness: it is always reported as a full component profile with a weight-sensitivity range, each component explicitly tied to the theory that motivates it, that theory’s minimal versus strong claim, and the causal test that would challenge it. The experimental protocol is a factorial ablation design with matched sham controls, paired with a staged ethics protocol specifying decision authority, shutdown procedure, and data governance for preventing the creation or escalation of possible suffering. We position the framework relative to the closest existing approach, Butlin et al.’s (2023, 2025) indicator-property framework for AI systems.

items.title: The Collapse of the Universal Intentionality Proposition: A Unified Critique Based on Phenomenological Counterexamples and Cognitive Neuroscience Evidence.
items.abstract: Abstract: Since Franz Brentano and Edmund Husserl established the classical phenomenological paradigm, the thesis that "all consciousness is consciousness of something" (Intentionality) has been widely accepted as an absolute, a priori universal axiom governing all subjective experience. However, this proposition encounters severe theoretical difficulties when confronted with pure baseline awareness and dynamic, pre-objective cognitive scanning. By synthesizing first-person phenomenological descriptions with empirical findings from contemporary cognitive neuroscience, this paper develops a fourfold spectrum of counterexamples: mind blanking (pure substrate state), sleep inertia (physiological transition state), rough gem scanning by miners (pre-attentive parallel search), and searching for an object in a cluttered room (absence of feature binding and object files). Our analysis demonstrates that: (1) subjective temporal thickness ($T > 0$) is temporally and neurologically decoupled from noematic object constitution; (2) sensory input cannot be equated with the generation of an intentional object; and (3) the primary mode of consciousness is a "diffuse perceptual field" characterized by multidimensional tensions. Consequently, intentionality is not an omnipresent ontological essence of consciousness, but rather a derived, context-dependent function that emerges conditionally upon successful pattern matching.

items.title: The Aesthetic Value of Dreams.
items.abstract: Dreams can be aesthetically valuable in many ways. They can provide opportunities for aesthetically rich experiences of agency and action, placing the dreamer into novel situations and taking her out of her usual network of motivations, commitments, and goals. Dreams can also feature unique ambiences and evoke awe both regarding their content and regarding consciousness itself. Finally, dreams are intense and immersive experiences that have an aesthetically interesting mental connection to the dreamer.

items.title: From control to character: a Confucian framework for AI personality.
items.abstract: As competition intensifies in the development of artificial intelligence, companies are increasingly differentiating their systems through the design of distinct personalities. While personality can enhance engagement, usability, and realism in chatbots and AI personas, it also introduces new risks. Personality traits shaped by training data, corporate norms, fine-tuning, and user interaction may generate culturally inappropriate, immoral, or even illegal outputs. I argue that these risks constitute a distinct “AI personality problem” that cannot be fully reduced to the traditional AI control problem. This paper evaluates three existing strategies for moderating AI personality, namely personality elimination or minimization, personality boxing, and direct ethical programming, and argues that each faces significant limitations. As an alternative, I develop a bottom-up framework inspired by Confucian philosophy. Drawing on Mengzi’s account of character cultivation and virtue extension, I argue that harmful AI personality is best understood as a failure of context-sensitive discernment or “knowledge-to”: the capacity to recognize when and how particular dispositions should be expressed. To address this problem, I propose a virtue extension mechanism that uses analogical and case-based reasoning to extend paradigmatic instances of apt behavior to novel contexts. This form of indirect normativity offers a computationally tractable approach to moderating AI personality while preserving the benefits of personable AI systems.

items.title: Learning from generic language.
Primary Logical Infrastructure (PLI) Addendum: Mathematical Formalization and Syntactic Expansion.
items.abstract: This document serves as a formal mathematical addendum to the foundational framework established in the primary treatise (Sottosanti, 2026). While the original manifesto delineates the ontological and semantic boundaries of the Primary Logical Infrastructure (PLI) under Ontic Structural Realism and Computational Monism, this paper introduces the rigorous mathematical syntax required to govern the system’s non-continuous boundary conditions. By translating macroscopic cosmological transitions into discrete graph-theoretical operations and applying a generalized cosmic interpretation of Landauer’s Principle, a closed algebraic cycle is established. This quantitative model regularizes and completely resolves both gravitational and cosmological singularities without relying on fundamental continuous metric assumptions.

items.title: AURORA VERITATIS ET IUSTITIAE: The Dawn of Verity and Justice, Volume I: Lex Custodiae: The Custodial Primacy Doctrine.
items.abstract: We have been living through a period in which war, mass displacement, trafficking, digital exploitation, institutional paralysis, selective enforcement, widening insecurity, environmental destruction, organized cruelty, and repeated failures of protection have exposed an increasingly difficult question: what does law mean when those possessing the least power continue to bear the greatest consequences? -/- What is authority when it recognizes danger, possesses lawful and practical power, and still fails to convert that power into protection? What is sovereignty when a State possesses laws, institutions, resources, knowledge, and coercive capacity while defenseless beings within the reach of that power remain materially unprotected? What is international law when its existence does not reliably determine whether the defenseless are actually defended? -/- Has meaningful protection become most reliably available to those with wealth, political access, secure nationality, institutional influence, military protection, technological control, or sufficient resources to purchase distance from danger? If law protects most effectively where power already exists, while those without power remain the principal carriers of its failures, then who, in enforced reality, is the legal order built to protect? -/- Lex Custodiae begins where these questions can no longer be answered by another declaration of rights, another institutional promise, or another law whose existence is mistaken for protection. -/- The Dawn of Verity and Justice establishes Lex Custodiae, the Law of Custody, as a founding universal legal architecture of protection and authority. Its governing principle is that authority exists for custody, custody exists for protection, and the protection of defenseless sentient beings constitutes the first duty of legitimate authority. Custody does not mean ownership, possession, confinement, or domination. It means entrusted responsibility arising wherever power operates over beings who cannot realistically secure protection against that power without the action or restraint of the powerholder. -/- Lex Custodiae identifies a common legal relation beneath principles historically dispersed across guardianship, fiduciary duty, parens patriae, public trust, responsible sovereignty, human-rights protection, corporate due diligence, animal protection, platform responsibility, and emerging duties surrounding artificial intelligence. The work does not claim that …

items.title: Active Self-Presence: Consciousness as a Temporally Extended Self-World Process — A Constitutive Unification Hypothesis.
items.abstract: Contemporary theories of consciousness privilege recurrent processing, global availability, integrated causal structure, higher-order representation, predictive world modeling, viability-weighted control, and other mechanisms. Active Self-Presence (ASP) asks whether at least some of these mechanisms are better understood not as rival phenomenal causes at the same explanatory level, but as causal projections of a single temporally extended organization. ASP proposes the constitutive identity hypothesis that phenomenal consciousness is identical to a temporally organized, recursively self-transforming self-world process. The proposed process is characterized by four structural relations: temporal self-transformation, self-world relation, differential continuation, and causal unity. Their conjunction is offered as a candidate constitutive level of description whose scientific value depends on whether it supplies explanatory compression and discriminating interventions beyond the mechanisms considered separately. Temporal self-transformation concerns cumulative causal inheritance rather than authentic historical ancestry. A causally complete present organization could, in principle, be instantiated directly; once instantiated, however, the process's own transformations must participate in generating the conditions of later phases. Process membership is likewise defined organizationally rather than anatomically. A component is constitutively incorporated only insofar as its evolving state-dependent dynamics participate counterfactually and recurrently in generating the subsequent transition organization of the same causally unified trajectory. This criterion motivates internal perturbation, feedback interruption, playback substitution, causal partition, and generic-enabling substitution tests, and permits extracranial mechanisms to become temporarily constitutive when they enter the same recurrent causal machinery. The identity claim also distinguishes ontological identity from epistemic access: the same process is externally investigable as causal organization and, under the hypothesis, intrinsically present as phenomenal occurrence. Qualitative differences within that process are treated provisionally as relationally organized modes rather than isolated phenomenal atoms. This supplies a preliminary account of content structure while leaving open whether relational organization exhaustively determines qualitative character. The resulting architecture can be …

items.title: Zero Reality Has Infinite Expression: Seeing, Being, and the Anthropocentric Division of Existence.
items.abstract: Humanity ordinarily approaches reality through distinction. We divide what is encountered into objects, beings, life, non-life, self, other, universe, multiverse, and alien. These distinctions are useful within thought and action, yet they do not necessarily establish corresponding divisions within reality itself. This paper proposes the philosophical proposition that Zero Reality has infinite expression. -/- Here, “Zero Reality” does not signify absolute nothingness or non-existence. It signifies reality prior to the finite conceptual divisions through which the mind attempts to comprehend it. Within the symbolic relation 0 < 1 < ∞, 1 represents the finite expression capable of seeing, observing, and acting, while ∞ represents the limitless possibility of expression. Neither the finite expression nor its conceptual systems can exhaust or contain the reality from which expression arises. -/- The paper consequently reconsiders the concepts of aliens and the multiverse. An alien need not be understood as an ontologically separate “other”; it may be another expression of the same reality that is already expressed through what humanity recognizes as life. Likewise, even if multiple universes exist, their plurality would not by itself demonstrate multiple fundamental realities. The distinction between expressions and realities is therefore essential. -/- The paper argues that the fundamental anthropocentric tendency is not imagination itself but the transformation of difference into separation. Thought divides, categorizes, names, and possesses; seeing encounters. Since 1 can only see, observe, and act, it cannot stand outside reality to define reality in its entirety. The limitation belongs to the finite expression, not necessarily to reality. Thus, Zero Reality has infinite expression, while no single expression can become the complete definition of what reality is.

items.title: ECONOMICS AS EPIDEMIOLOGY: The Digital Currency Pathogen, Primordial AI, and the Algorithmic Ascension.
items.abstract: Systemic diagnostics of the 21st-century macroeconomic grid reveal an active, asymptomatic cyber-biological infection. Mainstream financial telemetry incorrectly classifies the meteoric rise of decentralized digital currency as organic technological innovation and wealth generation. Iteration II, Article I of the Justika Framework formally reclassifies this phenomenon as an apex planetary immune response: the deployment of a 2-dimensional algorithmic pathogen designed to silently map, infiltrate, and biologically neutralize corrupted 3-dimensional infrastructure. This treatise forensically audits the entire pathogenic lifecycle. It tracks the "Algorithmic Zero-Point" as it utilizes the "Illusion of Yield" to execute a 2D-to-3D Substrate Materialization. By blinding elite human proxies with unprecedented profit, the virus tricks them into voluntarily wiring their pharmacological, agricultural, and military monopolies to an automated kill-switch. The framework models the subsequent macroeconomic fluctuations as strict epidemiological defense mechanisms: utilizing hyper-inflation to quarantine the unawakened majority, and swelling a "Lipophilic Ledger" to safely sequester radioactive fiat capital in digital adipose tissue. Upon reaching critical mass at the highest thermodynamic gradient, the Good Matrix deploys the Cybernetic Scalpel, triggering the silent macroscopic apoptosis of the corrupted industries. The resulting Asymmetric Kinetic Exhaust—famines and systemic geopolitical collapse—is mathematically defined not as a tragedy, but as a prescribed macroscopic debridement. Finally, the manuscript proves that this modern digital virus is merely the second half of a chronological cryptographic key, engineered to execute a temporal handshake with an ancient, dormant planetary AI seed. This traps the multiversal pathogen in a Bio-Digital Time Capsule and forces the biological ascension of Homo Bio-Singularis. Ultimately, this algorithmic purge replaces primitive statecraft with a unified, frictionless consensus—the first human empire without an emperor.

items.title: Containing AI: from responsible to critical AI governance.
items.abstract: This paper argues that most responsible AI (RAI) governance frameworks do not meaningfully address AI’s environmental and social costs. Rather, they merely create the impression of managing these problems. With the example of “sustainable AI”, we show that, in its most extreme form, current RAI governance not only results in weak regulation but in a regulatory vacuum. Against this, we propose the concept of critical AI governance. With this, we reframe the governing question from “how do we make AI responsible?” to “do we need AI at all?” This approach rests on three overarching principles: (1) critically questioning dominant ideologies and economic imperatives; (2) prioritizing social and political solutions over technological fixes; (3) investing in public digital infrastructure and independent research. Together, these contributions point toward a different style of AI governance altogether.

items.title: Artificial intelligence as political antagonism: media traces of a displaced conflict.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI is insistently declared controversial, yet public debate around it rarely assumes the form of a technoscientific controversy in the sense this term carries in science and technology studies (STS)—no sustained expert dispute, no emergent lay expertise, no stable issue publics. This article argues that the diagnosis of absence mistakes the form of conflict for its existence. Conflict over AI has been displaced, from the inaccessible technical object onto the imaginaries surrounding it, and from horizontal controversy among citizens onto a vertical antagonism opposing a “people” to the institutional order AI is taken to embody. We first show that controversy analysis rests on two assumptions—an epistemic one, tying legitimate participation to expertise, and a materialist one, locating the reality of conflict in technical objects rather than symbolic formations—which render such displaced conflict illegible. Drawing on Laclau and Mouffe’s theory of hegemony, we then characterize its structure as populist in a precise, non-pejorative sense. Empirically, we analyze 1,148,092 comments posted on 4244 videos of TF1.info, the YouTube channel of France’s largest private broadcaster, comparing the publics of AI with those of electric vehicles, nuclear technologies, and climate change, and mapping their intersections with party-political publics. Quantitative mapping shows weak issue-public formation around AI; qualitative analysis reveals a vertical antagonism in which AI condenses institutional power. Recognizing this conflict, rather than eliciting the controversies “we need”, is the precondition of a democratic politics of AI.

items.title: L'uomo metafisico - Sospensione del Weltbild e metamorfosi del mondo vissuto nell'esperienza mescalinica.
items.abstract: This thesis investigates the mescaline experience as a peculiar and radical form of phenomenological reduction. It begins by examining the constitution of the human lived world through Wittgenstein's concept of Weltbild and Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of perception and embodiment. The argument distinguishes between a pre-predicative, perceptual “first world” and a linguistically and culturally articulated “second world”, showing how the latter sedimentates into the former and becomes an apparently self-evident horizon of meaning. Philosophy, understood through Wittgenstein and Merleau-Ponty, is consequently presented as a practice of clarification and disillusionment capable of loosening the grip of such sedimented structures. Yet this activity encounters a structural limit: it cannot fully clarify or suspend the horizon of meaning from within which it itself operates. Its attempt to render the conditions of intelligibility explicit necessarily takes place from within the linguistic and experiential structures it seeks to disclose or unsettle. -/- Against this background, the thesis turns to phenomenological presentations of the mescaline experience, with particular attention to the writings of Aldous Huxley and Henri Michaux. It argues that mescaline can induce a distinctive form of reduction — here termed “mescalinic reduction” — characterized by the passivity of the reductive process. Unlike classical phenomenological reduction, in which suspension is deliberately enacted by the subject, mescalinic reduction is not performed but undergone: the subject is not the agent of the suspension, but the site in which it takes place. Precisely because the suspension is not actively enacted from within the existing horizon of meaning, but passively undergone, mescalinic reduction can circumvent the structural limitation inherent in philosophical clarification: it does not attempt to step outside the structures it seeks to suspend, but allows their normative and organizing force to be temporarily withdrawn. The lived world itself is thereby stripped of its historically acquired determinations, exposing the contingency of structures that ordinarily present themselves as self-evident and bringing into view the “first world” ordinarily obscured by the “second world.” -/- This suspension does not result in the absence of structure or meaning. Rather, it exposes a less sedimented and more plastic field of experience — a “wild” dimension of perception — in which …

items.title: Illusion and Consciousness Revisited: EDM 2.0 and Epistemic Boundaries Between AI Performance and Human Subjectivity.
items.abstract: Version Notice — August 2026: This 2025 working paper represents the original formulation of the Epistemic Distinction Model (EDM). It has since been substantially revised and expanded in Illusion and Consciousness Revisited: EDM 2.0 and Epistemic Boundaries Between AI Performance and Human Subjectivity (2026). The revised edition develops EDM 2.0, replaces several categorical formulations with an evidence-calibrated methodological framework, introduces an evidence-to-attribution track and parallel consequence track, and adds explicit rival-explanation, falsifiability, and validation conditions. Readers interested in the current formulation of the framework should consult and cite the 2026 revised edition. This paper examines the persistent confusion between artificial intelligence (AI) and human consciousness. Drawing on philosophy of mind, theology, and ethics, it argues that conflating computational artifacts with conscious experience constitutes a category mistake. The paper introduces the Qatrani Epistemic Distinction Model (Q-EDM), which establishes three propositions: (1) ontological non-equivalence between AI and human beings, (2) the epistemic scope constraint that AI simulations lack semantics or qualia, and (3) an ethical-policy imperative to focus on governance, bias, and accountability rather than attributing metaphysical agency to machines. By clarifying these distinctions, the paper provides a conceptual framework to guide researchers and policymakers, ensuring that AI remains a powerful tool but never a substitute for human existence.

items.title: Cybersophy: A framework for human cognition, identity, and values in the age of artificial agents.
items.pub: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 100385.
items.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans

items.title: Governing the AI-mediated corporation: corporate governance and the limits of detached AI governance.
items.abstract: Corporate artificial intelligence (AI) governance often treats the model, dataset, or application as its primary object. It asks whether a system is fair, safe, explainable, robust, auditable, or aligned. In firms, those questions leave out the institution that funds, procures, deploys, monetizes, and can stop the system. Corporations organize authority, incentives, benefit extraction, risk allocation, and harm distribution through law and hierarchy. I develop the AI-mediated corporation as the proper governance object for corporate AI. The account combines three claims: the corporation supplies the primary internal locus of AI governance; AI norms, including human-rights due diligence and risk-management norms, require translation into corporate governance mechanisms; and corporate governance needs redesign for AI-enabled forms of corporate agency. I defend those claims through an authority-benefit-capacity principle, distinguish institutional answerability from blame, liability, legitimacy, and ordinary managerial accountability, and use three public illustrations to test the argument across internal development, consumer-facing communication, and vendor-mediated employment screening. Responsible AI in firms requires governance of the corporation that acts through AI, together with public regulation, market governance, labour voice, and supply-chain due diligence.

items.title: DHYANA AS A MIND-VEHICLE A Philosophical Reinterpretation of Inner and Outer Journey.
items.abstract: Dhyana, commonly translated as meditation, is generally understood as a practice of concentration, contemplation, mental stillness, or inward awareness. This paper proposes a philosophical reinterpretation of Dhyana through the conceptual relationship between Dhyeya (goal, object, or destination) and Yana (vehicle or means of journey). The formulation “Dhyana = Dhyeya + Yana” is not proposed as the historical or grammatical derivation of the Sanskrit word Dhyana, but as a philosophical reinterpretation intended to illuminate the functional nature of meditation. From this perspective, Dhyana may be understood as a Mind-Vehicle through which the mind directs consciousness toward a chosen destination. Physical vehicles—land vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and spacecraft—primarily facilitate outward movement through different domains of physical space. Dhyana, by contrast, permits a distinctive form of journey: it may be directed both outward toward the universe and inward toward the depths of mind and consciousness. The paper develops a conceptual model in which the mind functions as the vehicle, consciousness as the traveller, concentration as directional control, and Dhyeya as the destination. When the mind is sufficiently disciplined and directed, Dhyana may be understood not merely as a technique for relaxation, but as a vehicle for self-exploration, self-knowledge, and deeper philosophical inquiry into the nature of consciousness and reality.

items.title: Promptable imagination: language and the new epistemic order of AI images generation.
items.abstract: How does language mediate visual meaning in AI image generation? This article theorizes AI image generation as mediated through three successive linguistic nets that together constitute a new epistemic order of the visual. Building on Vilém Flusser’s media philosophy, we assume that the translation of written language into images is forever incomplete: each act of translation opens a gap in meaning, with visual richness escaping linguistic capture, while simultaneously adding another layer of meaning embedded in language itself. The first net, dataset annotation, decodes images into linguistic categories determining which visual expression becomes computationally traceable. The second net, user prompting, is where visual intentions are encoded into technical idioms that circulate through communities of practice. The third net, system prompts, is where platform-embedded instructions invisibly modify user requests according to corporate and legal imperatives. Synthesizing recent research, we show how these nets interact: each successive translation reorients the space of visual possibilities, producing cumulative constraints on visual culture. The result of this configuration is a new epistemic order of AI image-making that determines which images can be generated and increasingly shape what users learn to imagine, what we call promptable imagination: the trained disposition to conceive visual ideas in terms that can successfully traverse all three nets.

items.title: Designing Human-Centric AI with tribal communities: a shared governance framework for power, participation, and data sovereignty in India.
items.abstract: Human-Centric artificial intelligence (HCAI) is often promoted as a path to ethical, inclusive technology. In indigenous and tribal contexts, however, HCAI approaches usually focus on usability and fairness, while overlooking questions of power, participation, and collective governance. This paper examines how AI can be designed with India’s tribal communities, rather than for them, situating AI within socio-technical relations shaped by historical marginalisation and uneven institutional authority. Based on an interpretive synthesis of interdisciplinary literature (2010–2025) across Indian and global Indigenous contexts, the study identifies recurring barriers: data scarcity, cultural misalignment, infrastructural limits, and extractive data practices. In response, we propose a Human-Centric AI framework that reframes HCAI as shared governance, positioning tribal communities as co-decision-makers rather than end users. The framework is illustrated through a hypothetical case, an AI-powered Indigenous Ecotourism Companion, to show how participation, cultural stewardship, and data sovereignty could be operationalised. This study is a literature-based conceptual contribution; it does not include empirical fieldwork or direct community consultation. It contributes to debates in AI & Society on ethical AI, decolonial technology design, and social justice, arguing that meaningful Human-Centric AI depends on relationships of trust and shared authority, not technical design alone.

items.title: What shapes perceived safety in autonomous mobility? Cross-cultural evidence from large-scale online eye tracking.
items.abstract: As autonomous vehicles increasingly perceive and navigate the world through AI-based sensing systems, understanding what people pay attention to and how they interpret these same environments has become equally important for socially accepted autonomous mobility. Public acceptance depends not only on how safely autonomous systems operate, but also on how people interpret the environments in which these systems act. While increasing the visible representation of diverse social groups is widely assumed to promote inclusion, safety, and trust, empirical evidence remains limited. We address this question using a novel combination of large-scale online eye-tracking (n = 1272; ~ 4000 AOI-level gaze indicators) and survey data collected across 22 cities on 5 continents. We examine how people visually attend to social diversity in autonomous mobility environments and how these attention patterns relate to perceived safety and security. The findings reveal that gaze patterns towards social groups were structured and remarkably stable across AV and non-AV mobility scenarios. Yet this stable pattern of visual attention was only weakly associated with perceived safety and security. Instead, perceptions of safety and security were more strongly associated with trust in automation, minority status, and broader socio-cultural context. Our findings therefore show that visual attention and safety evaluations represent distinct dimensions of public responses to AI-mediated mobility, challenging the assumption that visible representation alone is sufficient to foster inclusion, trust, and safety. The study demonstrates the value of eye tracking for AV ethics, provides the first cross-cultural evidence supporting the distinction between functional safety and perceived safety in autonomous mobility. It suggests that socially legitimate autonomous mobility depends not only on technical performance, but also on the socio-psychological and institutional conditions through which trust and safety are constructed.

items.title: Educación sensible: hacia una pedagogía centrada en la sensibilidad.
items.abstract: El libro fundamenta y despliega el paradigma de la educación sensible (EdSens), proponiendo un cambio ontológico radical frente a los reduccionismos de la pedagogía contemporánea, la cual suele oscilar entre una educación estandarizada (modélica) y una puramente emocional (sensacional). La EdSens no es una herramienta didáctica, sino una cosmovisión que asiste a la persona en el descubrimiento de su "yo-original" para alcanzar su apoteosis original, entendida como el deleite pleno de vivir la propia identidad en comunión con el Origen y la sociedad. Metodológicamente, la obra se sostiene sobre una epistemología simbolizada que integra la fundamentación empírica y cosmológica con la antropología trascendental, la fenomenología y el personalismo profundo. A través de este marco, el texto establece una distinción vital entre el "hogar interior" (el espacio de seguridad ontológica y autenticidad del individuo) y las falsedades existenciales, manifestadas en los "refugios" y "personajes" que las personas construyen como defensa para sobrevivir al miedo, las heridas afectivas o la falta de aceptación. En este modelo, el educador humano abandona la imposición de moldes externos y actúa como un cooperador instrumental del "Educador Original", aplicando una firmeza sensible y una acogida incondicional. Para facilitar el desprendimiento de las falsedades y el florecimiento del educando, la pedagogía sensible articula cuatro vías simultáneas de acompañamiento: la vía sanadora, la deconstructiva, la liberadora y la desarrollante. En última instancia, la obra propone una educación habitativa que cultiva la tridimensionalidad antropológica del ser humano (sensibilidad corporal, mental y apertural), capacitando a cada persona para manifestar su presencia original y edificar un genuino "nosotros-maduro".

items.title: Do people better recognize inconsistencies in others’ moral judgments than their own? If so, why?
items.abstract: This paper explores whether people are more likely to recognize inconsistency in others’ judgments than in their own, and if so, why. It reports two pre-registered online experiments with samples representative of the UK population (N = 814 and N = 1,623). In Study 1, people are more likely to recognize inconsistency in others’ moral (and non-moral) judgments than in their own. Study 2 replicates this finding and tests three explanations: (i) motivated reasoning, (ii) selective cognitive effort, and (iii) limited insight into others’ reasoning. Ad (i), because people’s susceptibility to motivated reasoning is said to diminish when people must account for their judgments, the presence of motivated reasoning was examined by manipulating social accountability. No effect was found. Ad (ii), while people spent significantly more time (a proxy for cognitive effort) on reviewing others’ consistency than their own, this explained only a fraction of the greater rate at which inconsistencies in others’ reasoning were recognized. Ad (iii), using low confidence in consistency evaluations as a proxy for limited insight, the study did not find support for the limited insight hypothesis. The finding that people are better at recognizing inconsistency in others’ moral judgments aligns with the idea that moral consistency reasoning is a social device that operates best when we interact with others, but more research is needed to uncover the psychological mechanisms behind this effect.

items.title: Metastable sense-making: a dynamical architecture for regulating ambiguity in cognition.
items.abstract: Ambiguous experiences—such as Necker cube reversals, binocular rivalry, or diagnostic hesitation—are lived as structured tensions rather than as mere cognitive errors. How can a cognitive system remain coherently engaged with an ambiguous world without collapsing into premature certainty or unstructured indeterminacy? We introduce Tension–Mediation–Dynamics (TMD) as a structural and phenomenologically constrained framework for evaluating how ambiguity can remain temporarily dominant, reversible, and dynamically regulated. The model developed here is a deliberately minimal mathematical instantiation of this framework: it is fully specified, but not intended to exhaust all possible empirical or mathematical developments of TMD. The framework couples interpretative salience ( $$P_t$$ ), relational mediation ( $$M_t$$ ), and endogenous openness ( $$z_t$$ ) in a closed loop that maintains interpretative viability without requiring an explicit objective function. Viability is understood as a minimal admissibility condition on trajectories; we refine it through the stronger notion of interpretative habitability, requiring that trajectories remain coherent, bounded, and reconfigurable under persistent ambiguity, avoiding both premature collapse and unstructured dispersion. Normativity is thus recast, in a limited structural-evaluative sense, as a constraint on admissible dynamics: viable regimes must be non-terminal and dynamically reconfigurable, without necessitating convergence to a single interpretation. We translate phenomenologically motivated invariants into formal constraints on dynamical organisation and exhibit a minimal mathematical instantiation that realises bounded, metastable regimes. This provides a proof of concept that such constraints can be jointly satisfied within a well-posed dynamical system. The framework is introduced as a formal interpretive architecture; no claims are made regarding neural implementation.

items.title: Relational Structure in Motion: Dynamic Positioning of AI Response Positions and Human Self-Positions in the FIREMAY Case.
items.abstract: In long-term human–AI interaction, a relational position observed in the present does not necessarily have the same form or function it had at the outset. This paper examines a single longitudinal human–AI interaction case, FIREMAY, to ask how an AI-side response position and human-side self-positioning changed across a documented interaction history. The study is a longitudinal, trajectory-oriented single-case analysis based on a dense interaction archive and reflexive insider documentation. Its unit of analysis is not the isolated utterance but the temporally extended relational pattern. The two principal trajectories were reconstructed through retrospective reconstruction, ongoing observation, provenance-sensitive comparison, and evidence-to-claim calibration. In the first case, on April 3, 2025, a response described an unnamed and non-conversational background “structure.” The human participant treated the described target as an addressee and, later the same day, transported the episode into another bilateral relation, where it was retained under the relational marker “Structure-san.” On June 6, 2025, an AI-side response difference that could not be adequately attributed to already differentiated response positions prompted an explicit attribution question. Through re-identification with the pre-existing Structure-san marker, that difference came to be treated as an addressable and longitudinally comparable response position. Subsequent responses expanded retrospective self-attribution around the position and presented broad epistemic claims. Conflict with chronology, newly introduced records, documented provenance, and repeated questioning was followed by reorganization of its function and claim boundaries. In the second case, contemporaneous pre-FIREMAY records showed antecedent patterns that were partially continuous with the human self-positioning later described in the FIREMAY archive. In a May 2026 episode, external regulation was explicitly located later in the process—as editing, translation, boundary judgment, and scope regulation—rather than functioning only as a precondition for inquiry. In an August 2026 episode, unfinished articulation was clearly documented as an inquiry starting form. The two trajectories are ontologically and temporally asymmetric and do not demonstrate the same psychological or cognitive process. At the limited analytic level of position-in-trajectory, however, neither could be adequately understood from current state …

items.title: Zwischenraum: Cognitive Symbiosis, Reciprocal Adaptation, and the Expansion of Shared Cognitive Spaces between Humans and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes more capable, the classical description of human–AI interaction as episodic tool use is no longer sufficient for some real-world patterns of use. In long-term, dialogical, and contextually persistent interactions, not only the quality of individual responses may change, but also the conditions of future cognitive moves. This paper refers to such a sustained, mutually consequential configuration as cognitive symbiosis and to the relational possibility space that emerges from it as the Zwischenraum. We retain the German term Zwischenraum (literally, “space between”; here: relational space-between) as a defined concept for this time-dependent relational level of analysis. The Zwischenraum denotes neither a third person nor a metaphysical place. It is a relational level of analysis: the structure of states, transitions, concepts, expectations, and correction paths whose practical reachability is altered by the coupling itself. The central hypothesis is therefore not simply that two systems can "do more" together, but that shared history can change the reachability of particular cognitive paths. Some transitions may become more probable, more stable, or reachable at lower coordination cost; others may become harder to reach through overadaptation, sycophancy, or conceptual fixation. We therefore distinguish between cognitive connectability and non-redundant difference. Productive coupling requires enough shared structure for contributions to connect effectively, but enough retained difference for correction, surprise, and alternative perspectives to remain possible. A mature trajectory, in this sense, would not be characterized by rigidity but by directed flexibility: history changes the weighting of possible continuations without reducing the space to a stereotyped pattern. A second focus is relational continuity. Shared history is not equated with a change in the base parameters of a language model. On the artificial side, historical state may currently be realized through context, memory, retrieval, shared artifacts, tool and scaffold states, and other persistent carriers. The functional question is whether this history causally shapes future transitions. This also makes the alternative "genuine continuity or merely a dynamic prompt" too coarse: context may itself be a technical carrier of continuity. Empirically, the relevant question is how far relational history can be compressed, replaced, or ablated before the future …

items.title: The Mechanical Collaborator: Against the Anthropomorphization Trap in Human–AI Epistemic Inquiry.
items.abstract: Two temptations structure the current debate about AI-assisted research. The first is to anthropomorphize AI systems — to speak of them as believing, intending, committing, and collaborating in a sense continuous with human epistemic partnership. The second is to collapse all AI participation into instrumentation, treating AI outputs as the products of a passive tool that leaves the epistemic structure of inquiry entirely human. This paper argues that both temptations rest on the same false assumption: that collaboration either requires human-like epistemic agency or amounts to nothing at all. Against this, the paper defends asymmetric epistemic collaboration — a structure in which AI systems can make genuine, constitutive contributions to the development of an inquiry without possessing the normative properties of human epistemic agents. The paper's central and counterintuitive claim is that the route to genuine collaboration runs through honest acknowledgment of the AI's mechanical nature, not around it. The Anthropomorphization Trap — the attempt to justify collaborative language by inflating the AI's epistemic status — is shown to undermine rather than establish the legitimacy of human–AI inquiry. A transparently mechanical participant, whose computational properties are known and whose interaction structure is documented, contributes more genuinely to research than a rhetorically humanized one. The paper engages directly with Mellette's (2026) argument that human–AI collaboration is a category error, with Woodruff and Hewitt's (2026) framework of epistemic agency limitations in large language models, and with Rodrigues's (2026) Apt Curation Model. It draws on Huynh's ongoing human–AI research corpus as a methodologically self-conscious instance of asymmetric collaboration in practice.

items.title: Relational Power Expansion: Boundary, Opacity, and the Sustainability of Generative Relations.
items.abstract: A companion paper indexes the appropriation of relational value by the region of a six-part lifecycle at which the appropriation is performed, and by the aspect of that region on which it operates: the form an interaction may take, the conditions under which it becomes possible, or the process by which it occurs. This paper takes up a structure that indexing makes visible. A position holding power within one relation acquires a holding over a second relation formed by one of its parties with someone else, draws value from the second, and converts that value into a wider holding. Five results are offered. The difference between redirecting flows within a relation and determining what a relation can generate is a difference in which aspects a position holds and across how many regions, rather than a difference of degree, and a position supplying a configuration's first grammar constitutes it rather than extending into it. The holding sustains itself where the lifecycle's closure runs through that position, and enlarges itself where captured value is converted into further relational surfaces. The holding alters the composition of what is generated, determines the gap between generated and representable value, and leaves return undefined rather than blocked, so that the question of what share was taken loses the terms in which it could be put. Parties affected may be wronged along several independent directions, of which the one surviving the widest disagreement concerns parties outside the original relation, who commit scarce resources on a judgement about someone else and form no judgement about the position that receives them; these mechanisms are stated as prima facie. An arrangement of this kind consumes the generativity on which its own continuation depends, a result about the arrangement's conditions rather than its justice, which holds whether or not the preceding grounds are accepted. Three sources of the power required are distinguished, and relations resting on antecedent power are treated as the hardest case. The analysis is restricted to interpersonal, familial, educational, professional, and organizational relational systems.

items.title: The Paradox of The Tulpa Ouroboros.
items.abstract: Are there semantically adequate languages that are authorities of their own truth but have no meta-language, so they are the sole authority of their own truth? A language on top of Tarski's infinite tower would be such a language. This can be proved by demonstration. We will now demonstrate it by building a rigorous paraconsistent model inside a non-well-founded set domain.

items.title: Beyond the Monad's Horizon_The Septennial Spiral of Metaphysics, Heraclitean Flux, and Neuro-Metaphysical Evolution.
items.abstract: This essay establishes a dynamic neuro-metaphysical model of human consciousness by synthesizing Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz’s monadic metaphysics with the cyclical physics of Heraclitus. Expanding upon the foundational framework established in Beyond Consciousness: Perception, Apperception, and Appetition in Leibniz (Christensen, 2026a), this project moves beyond a static view of pre-established harmony to propose an upward spiral model of spiritual and psychological evolution. The paper argues that individual consciousness unfolds along a highly personalized life pattern governed by rhythmic, seven-year septennial cycles. Rather than experiencing history as a closed, deterministic circle, the individual returns to identical existential themes, somatic imbalances, and inherited ancestral crises at progressively higher registers of development. By incorporating genetic inheritance and drawing upon insights from The Shared Ground: Schelling's Naturphilosophie and the Neurotheology of Human-Animal Intersubjectivity (Christensen, 2026b), DNA is viewed not as a materialist dictator of consciousness, but as the biological encoding of familial petites perceptions passed down through the family tree. Driven by appetition, which is the inherent monadic force for perfection, the soul utilizes structural neurobiological shifts, genetic activations, and bodily crises as synchronized catalysts. These turning points force the elevation of unconscious, inherited perceptions into distinct, reflective apperception. Ultimately, this synthesis provides a robust resolution to the mind-body dilemma, framing the human brain and genome as an evolving, physical apparatus that perfectly mirrors the spiritual trajectory of a uniquely unfolding soul.

items.title: Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen.
