items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has long become a reality and presents us with new, complex ethical questions: How does AI reshape our understanding of humanity? Who bears responsibility for autonomous decisions? What are the implications of AI for media and culture, the world of labour, politics, sustainability, and surveillance? What impact does robotics have on human beings and psychological well-being? This volume provides concise answers and solid foundational knowledge on ethics in the context of apparently 'intelligent' machines. Through practical case studies, supporting materials, and reflective questions, the book is ideally suited as a didactic guide for use in schools and higher education.

items.title: Introduzione. Promesse e ambivalenze della simpatia.
items.pub: In Lorenzo Greco & Marco Menin, Storia inquieta della simpatia. Genealogia, morale e lati oscuri (secoli XVIII e XIX). Roma: Carocci editore. pp. 11-23.
items.venue: Storia inquieta della simpatia. Genealogia, morale e lati oscuri (secoli XVIII e XIX)

items.title: Hume e la natura ambigua della compassione.
items.pub: In Lorenzo Greco & Marco Menin, Storia inquieta della simpatia. Genealogia, morale e lati oscuri (secoli XVIII e XIX). Roma: Carocci editore. pp. 45-61.
items.venue: Storia inquieta della simpatia. Genealogia, morale e lati oscuri (secoli XVIII e XIX)

items.title: Aquinas and the ethics of AI triage systems in healthcare emergencies.
items.abstract: This article examines the ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) triage systems in allocating scarce medical resources during public health emergencies and ordinary emergency department settings. While contemporary triage frameworks employ multidimensional clinical criteria beyond SOFA scores, concerns persist regarding algorithmic bias, opacity, and the reduction of persons to calculable outcomes. Engaging current bioethical debates on resource allocation, the study argues that existing AI-assisted triage models insufficiently address the moral and relational dimensions of clinical judgment. Drawing on the virtue ethics of Thomas Aquinas, the article develops a Thomistic framework that addresses three ethical levels: AI system design, the moral agency of healthcare practitioners, and the transparency necessary for responsible human oversight. Through the virtues of justice, prudence, and charity, Aquinas’ thought positions AI as an assistive instrument rather than a replacement for ethical discernment. The study proposes an interdisciplinary framework integrating theology, philosophy, bioethics, and healthcare governance to promote human dignity, relational care, and morally responsible AI-assisted triage practices.

items.title: Driving phronesis as a milestone for engineering autonomous vehicles.
items.abstract: One of the main ethical reasons why autonomous vehicles (AVs) have been portrayed as the future of transportation is their potential to enhance road safety by eliminating human error. However, while AVs may mitigate known hazards, their successful deployment in the near future hinges on their performance in a mixed-traffic environment, where they must coexist and interact with human drivers. This paper adopts a broad Aristotelian virtue ethics framework to introduce the concept of driving phronesis as a normative framework for resolving nuanced, everyday coordination problems in traffic. Thus, our paper argues that a promising future for AVs is one in which they will function as digital duplicates of drivers in specific contexts, endowed with functional driving phronesis.

items.title: The discovery of the artificial and the use of the synthetic method in cognitive and physical sciences.
items.abstract: In this paper, we put forward the reconstruction of the “Discovery of the Artificial” proposed by Roberto Cordeschi as the emergence of a new simulative methodology in early twentieth-century behavioral sciences—known as the “Synthetic Method”—which involved the use of artifacts as scientific models of intelligent and adaptive behavior. We relate this epistemological shift to a coeval methodological turning point that, we propose, also occurred in the physical sciences, exemplified by the introduction, in the 1920s, of the Lenz–Ising model in statistical physics. Through this historical and conceptual parallel, we argue that both cognitive sciences and statistical physics have converged toward a shared “Culture of the Artificial,” characterized by a reliance on models and simulations that was increasingly embraced by both disciplines during the twentieth century. This convergence also reflects a deeper epistemic necessity related to the computational irreducibility and complexity of systems under investigation—whether biological or material—which causes analytical and exact mathematical approaches to be inadequate. Cognitive science and statistical physics can be regarded thus as two kinds of complexity sciences that have “discovered the artificial” in their similar need to develop models and internal explanations for observed phenomena. The common use of the synthetic method unites them in the adoption of a new language, which extends the traditional Galilean “mathematical language” to the creation and simulation of models. Ultimately, this language represents an epistemic alignment between different scientific disciplines and has contributed to defining a new kind of scientific explanation and understanding, centered on the internal functional organization of systems and weak emergence.

items.title: The Nootron: An Idea Accelerator and the Foundations of Nootronics.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Nootron, an AI-based instrument designed to detect and articulate, autonomously, resonances between an author’s personal corpus of concepts (the logotheca) and current research across the disciplines (the noosphere). Unlike dialogical instruments of thinking, which depend on the author’s continuing participation, the Nootron is conceived to operate transbiographically: on a weekly schedule it is to select conceptual signatures, scan recent publications, build interdisciplinary bridges, verify their sources, test them against seven criteria of conceptual authenticity, and record each encounter in a noogram — a dated report on what is happening to the author’s ideas in the world. Its most consequential genre is the boomerang noogram, a commentary written to the standards of the very journal whose article produced the resonance and prepared for submission back to it — an offer of conceptual enrichment rather than a claim of priority. What is presented here is an invention: the architecture, criteria, and ethical constitution of an instrument, not a report on a deployed system. Its method has been tested in supervised cycles conducted in dialogue with the neural network, from which the worked examples below are drawn; its autonomous regime remains a design awaiting implementation. The paper lays out the architecture through a structural analogy with the cyclotron; presents worked examples connecting the author’s concepts with neuroscience, political theory, and ecolinguistics; and formulates an ethics of transbiographical operation that sets the Nootron apart from digital twins: it does not imitate its author’s voice but reports on the life of his ideas. The Nootron is the founding instrument of nootronics, the practice of building instruments of thinking, and is projected as the first operational unit of the post-mortarium (Epstein 2026a). This publication places on record the term Nootron in the sense defined here, together with the instrument’s architecture, criteria, and ethical constitution.

items.title: How publics perceive smart cities: identifying social determinants of citizens’ attitudes to data-driven governance.
items.abstract: This study examines how citizens perceive the increasing integration of digital and data-driven technologies in (sub)urban governance, commonly referred to as the ‘smart city’. Despite the increasing focus on citizen roles in the co-production of smart city initiatives, little is known about how the public perceives these developments and how such perceptions are socially shaped. Drawing on survey data from 3270 Belgian respondents, this study examines socio-demographic characteristics, familiarity (i.e. awareness, digital literacy and (prior) technology adoption), and risk–benefit perceptions as determinants of public attitudes toward smart cities. Results suggest that attitudes tend to be more positive for older, higher educated and male respondents, although the effects of gender and education become negligible once other variables are considered. Among the familiarity dimensions examined, only technology adoption significantly affects attitudes. This indicates that it is not formal knowledge about smart cities that shapes attitudes, but rather that attitudes are dependent on experiences with different (digital) technologies that smart cities might provide. The strongest associations arise at the level of risk–benefit perceptions: perceived misuse risks are negatively associated with support, whereas perceived benefits exhibit a substantially stronger positive association than perceived risks. These findings refine the traditional ‘familiarity hypothesis’ by demonstrating that public attitudes toward smart cities are not necessarily driven by formal knowledge, but rather shaped by everyday technological experiences and perceptions of potential risks and benefits. This insight highlights the importance of experiential and evaluative dimensions in public perceptions of emerging forms of data-driven governance.

items.title: Digital bias in sexuality education: an intersectional analysis of AI responses to simulated Italian adolescents.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by adolescents to seek information about sexuality, relationships, and well-being. However, little is known about how these systems discursively construct and mediate such interactions. This study examines how three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) respond to simulated Italian adolescent personas used as analytical probes for algorithmic bias. Drawing on 120 standardized Italian-language interactions across four personas differing by gender, class, ethnicity, and sexual orientation, the analysis investigates how identity markers shape the framing of sexual and affective health information. Qualitative analysis reveals recurrent patterns of medicalization, differential agency attribution, and cultural othering. As markers of marginalization accumulate, AI responses exhibit a systematic discursive shift from normalization toward surveillance framing and referral to professional authority. To account for this pattern, we introduce intersectional amplification as an analytical construct grounded in Italian-language interactions about adolescent sexuality with commercial LLMs, capturing a situated process of discursive differentiation within this sociotechnical configuration. Overall, the findings show that LLM-mediated sexuality education reproduces normative hierarchies embedded in training data, positioning adolescents differently along axes of privilege and marginality. Crucially, the study demonstrates that such inequalities are not imposed by technical constraints but reflect design priorities.

items.title: The Architecture of Friction: Consciousness as Biological Attunement to Scale.
The Ambiguity of the Italian "Tu": Addressed as a Thou, Handled as an It.
items.pub: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective 15 (8):90-95.
items.venue: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective
items.abstract: In Italian, address is governed by a binary of Tu and Lei, and the informal Tu is switched on almost automatically as soon as a disability is named. This article reads that switch as an epistemic wrong and not a mere lapse of courtesy. Arranging the two parameters of Brown and Gilman's semantics of power and solidarity — symmetry/asymmetry and intimacy/distance — into a four-quadrant table, it shows that the retreat of the formal Lei collapses three distinct uses of the Tu into one indistinguishable form: the affectionate Tu offered to a disabled adult can no longer be told apart from the Tu that marks an inferior, and the wrong becomes impossible to name or to denounce. Drawing on Fricker's testimonial injustice, on Honneth and Taylor on recognition, and on Buber's I-Thou, the article argues that the disabled adult is addressed as a Thou and handled as an It, and defends a normative claim: public officials, and private actors in the public sphere, owe every adult citizen the formal Lei. The case is the mirror image of the debate on linguistic hermeneutical injustice hosted by the Collective — an injustice arising not from a form the language lacks, but from one it still possesses and is letting go. -/- [Italian abstract] In italiano l'allocuzione è governata dalla coppia Tu/Lei, e il Tu informale scatta quasi automaticamente non appena viene nominata una disabilità. L'articolo legge quel passaggio come un torto epistemico e non come una caduta di cortesia. Disponendo in una tabella a quattro quadranti i due parametri della semantica del potere e della solidarietà di Brown e Gilman — simmetria/asimmetria e intimità/distanza —, mostra che il ritirarsi del Lei fa collassare tre usi distinti del Tu in una forma sola: il Tu affettuoso rivolto a un adulto disabile non si distingue più dal Tu che marca un inferiore, e il torto diventa innominabile e indenunciabile. Attraverso l'ingiustizia testimoniale di Fricker, il riconoscimento di Honneth e Taylor e l'Io-Tu di Buber, l'articolo sostiene che l'adulto disabile è interpellato come un Tu e trattato come un Esso, e difende una tesi normativa: i funzionari pubblici, e i privati che operano nella sfera pubblica, devono a ogni cittadino adulto il Lei. Il caso è l'immagine speculare del dibattito sull'ingiustizia ermeneutica linguistica ospitato dal Collective: un'ingiustizia che nasce non da una forma che la lingua non ha, ma da una che possiede ancora e sta lasciando andare.

items.title: The Mismeasure of Pain.
items.pub: The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science.
items.venue: The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: A persistent claim throughout the history of modern medicine has been that human beings differ in their sensitivity to pain: that, when afflicted with comparable conditions, certain individuals, and especially certain groups of individuals, ‘hurt more’ than others. While opinions about which groups hurt more and which groups hurt less have varied over time, special emphasis has always been placed on the sensitivity of people of colour, women, and other socially significant groups. However, contrary to widespread medical opinion, this paper argues that claims about biosocial differences in pain sensitivity, past or present, have never been supported by compelling evidence. More specifically, I argue that (i) evidence for systematic differences in prominent measures of pain sensitivity—such as pain thresholds and pain tolerance—has been spurious and inconsistent, and that (ii) even if it was not, such differences still wouldn’t imply a gap in people’s sensitivity to pain. The reason for this, I argue, is that the experimental results are equally well explicable in terms of differences in response biases—a possibility which prevalent pain measurement methodologies typically do not (and possibly could not) adequately control for. While the arguments presented in this paper aren’t intended to rule out variations in pain sensitivity altogether, they cast serious doubt on the incessant search for differences in sensitivity at the level of racial and gender groups.

items.title: The ethics of artificial intelligence in sport.
items.abstract: What reason, if any, is there to object to the use of Artificial Intelligence in sport? While the existing literature has investigated several issues about the ethics of AI in sport, these studies have tended to focus on how general worries about AI such as transparency, privacy, bias, impacts on human rights and inequalities that may arise or be exacerbated by the use of AI in sport. In this paper, we will take a different approach by asking how such technologies may change the excellences that a sport is testing and developing. After identifying failures in existent arguments for analogous cases of proscription, we offer a novel framework for understanding proscription. We argue that the introduction of a novel technology risks changing the cluster of excellences that a sport is testing and promoting. Focusing on the strategic and tactical thinking of the coach in football, we argued that the cluster of excellences in football would be contracted if this were outsourced to AI systems. We will argue that this shows the need for a widespread debate involving those involved in sport about whether to allow sports to be transformed in this way or not. -/- .

items.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems.
items.abstract: Rapid progress in artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities has drawn fresh attention to the prospect of consciousness in AI. There is an urgent need for rigorous methods to assess AI systems for consciousness, but significant uncertainty about relevant issues in consciousness science. We present a method for assessing AI systems for consciousness that involves exploring what follows from existing or future neuroscientific theories of consciousness. Indicators derived from such theories can be used to inform credences about whether particular AI systems are conscious. This method allows us to make meaningful progress because some influential theories of consciousness, notably including computational functionalist theories, have implications for AI that can be investigated empirically.

items.title: Ethical governance of artificial intelligence for defence: normative tradeoffs for principle to practice guidance.
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in the defence domain raises challenges for the ethical governance of these systems. A recent shift from the what to the how of AI ethics sees a nascent body of literature published by defence organisations focussed on guidance to implement AI ethics principles. These efforts have neglected a crucial intermediate step between principles and guidance concerning the elicitation of ethical requirements for specifying the guidance. In this article, we outline the key normative choices and corresponding tradeoffs that are involved in specifying guidance for the implementation of AI ethics principles in the defence domain. These correspond to: the AI lifecycle model used; the scope of stakeholder involvement; the accountability goals chosen; the choice of auditing requirements; and the choice of mechanisms for transparency and traceability. We provide initial recommendations for navigating these tradeoffs and highlight the importance of a pro-ethical institutional culture.

items.title: Sensorimotor teleology and goal-directedness. An organismic framework for normative behaviour.
items.abstract: Teleosemantics explains meaning by appealing to the biological norms that make error possible, but most work in the field still anchors those norms in evolutionary “selected-effect” functions. We develop an organismic alternative grounded in the self-maintenance of autonomous systems. Elaborating upon and within sensorimotor theory and enactivism, we reconceptualise goals as higher order constraints (shaping transient attractors in a dynamic sensorimotor field) and show how they are nested into a heterarchy of means–end relations connecting the global self-maintenance of the identity of a sensorimotor organization with the most local sensorimotor coordinations. We then identify the minimal necessary requirements for genuine teleological behaviour: (1) Initiation that individuates an action in relation to a goal, (2) Modulatory execution that adaptively compensates perturbations or deploys alternative strategies in relation to the goal, and (3) Meaningful termination through successful acknowledgment and transition, goal-sensitive persistence, or coherent abandonment. We locate normativity and error in the dynamic presuppositions among sensorimotor schemes and goals: failure manifests as incoordination within, or across, goal branches. We finally illustrate our account with a detailed analysis of the well known A-not-B error in psychology, showing how infants meet our teleological criteria while revealing incoordination as tension breakdowns inside a heterarchy of goals and sensorimotor schemes. Teleological behaviour, therefore, is the management of tensions and dynamic presuppositions within the goal heterarchy, not a chain of mechanical causes, thus delivering a naturalised notion of purposiveness that opens up an alternative route to teleosemantics beyond evolutionary selection.

items.title: Correction: What language do machines speak? LLMs and the simulated social.
The Infinite Upgrade Dilemma.
Precision Stratification and the Engineering of a Philosophical Argument Annotation Language.
items.abstract: Philosophical texts commonly combine strict logical inference, heuristic moves, and semantically vague intuitions without explicit markers that would allow readers (or automated tools) to distinguish these modes. By contrast, mathematics and many natural sciences separate definitions, axioms, theorems, modeling assumptions, approximations, and error analysis. This paper develops a formal theory of precision stratification for arguments, introduces an explicit Argument Precision Function that maps inference steps to a [0,1] precision scale, and proposes a concrete Philosophical Argument Annotation Language (PAAL) intended as an engineerable schema for marking precision, provenance, and semantic modality in philosophical texts. The paper formalizes syntax and semantics for PAAL, demonstrates its application on canonical short examples (including a Gettier-style case), analyzes theoretical constraints that block full mechanization (indexicality, context-sensitivity, performatives, background practices), and outlines a feasible human-in-the-loop engineering roadmap (editorial tools, inter-annotator protocols, partial automation via NLP-assisted suggestion). Metrics for empirical evaluation are proposed. The project reframes "philosophical rigor" as the explicit management and annotation of precision layers, clarifying when philosophy can be treated like formal science and when it must retain irreducible natural-language modalities.

items.title: Why is it (still) Difficult to Understand Black-Box Models? Explainable Artificial Intelligence and the Experimenters’ Regress.
items.abstract: Machine learning models based on artificial neural networks have been increasingly used in scientific research and the public domain. These models are notoriously opaque and may conceal caveats in important tasks. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) develops network interpretation strategies that reveal how these models work. However, the situation of XAI does not meet its bright expectations: algorithms proliferate, but there are no agreed-upon standards. I suggest that the notion of the experimenters’ regress (ER) in scientific instruments is useful to understand this situation and yield sobering lessons for XAI. I identify a new variant of ER in the design and application of XAI algorithms: the validity of XAI algorithms and the workings of black-box models cannot be secured without assuming the other. This variant shows two distinct features: strategies for breaking the regress are context-specific, and metrics for evaluating XAI algorithms face a second-order regress. They defy XAI’s current approaches of self-justification and search for universal evaluation standards. ER provides two lessons for XAI. First, as various practical, conventional and communal factors can play a role in decision-making, one should be aware of the considerations involved in designing and applying XAI algorithms. Philosophers can contribute to this by analyzing XAI’s “living standards”, the non-universal and unjustified rationales practitioners use. Second, instead of searching for universal standards, those using XAI should reach pragmatic agreements in each specific context of its application based on empirical test results. Therefore, XAI’s support in the trust of AI through transparency also requires empirical validation.

items.title: Wittgenstein and the Physiognomy of Synesthetic Experience.
items.pub: In Christian Kanzian, Volker Munz, Anja Weiberg & Joseph Wang-Kathrein, Contributions to International Wittgenstein Symposium 2026, 50 Years Wittgenstein Symposium. Kirchberg am Wechsel: ALWS. pp. 958–967.
items.venue: Contributions to International Wittgenstein Symposium 2026, 50 Years Wittgenstein Symposium
items.abstract: Synesthesia is a rare phenomenon that is often described as a merging of the senses. Some of Wittgenstein’s remarks discuss different forms of synesthesia, including the case in which the e is yellow for someone, a case of grapheme-color synesthesia. In this paper, I will explore the connection between synesthesia and aspect-seeing, the broader topic into which Wittgenstein’s remarks on synesthetic experience are embedded. I claim that synesthetic experience is a form of aspect-seeing, specifically in the way in which synesthesia reveals a certain of the objects perceived, making them physiognomy speak to synesthetes in a special way. Beyond the mere experiential uniqueness that it brings about, synesthesia can be used as a strategy to be better at performing certain tasks, thus potentially impacting a synesthete’s daily life. This, in turn, carries philosophical significance insofar as the example of synesthesia shows how aspect-perception (in general) influences a speaker’s reality.

items.title: The Daniel 5 Proof: He Knows What Is In The Darkness.
items.abstract: A complete text supplies all but whence it came, its meaning, its operand, and its invocation. A king throws a feast, a hand writes on the wall, and the assembled scholarship of an empire cannot say what was written there, in a lit room, upon "the plaister of the wall" (Daniel 5:5, KJV), in their own language. -/- Two things were asked and neither was delivered. *Qerā* is to call, to read aloud, to cry out. *Pesher* is the interpretation. Daniel 5:8 records both failures separately, in the order the king's offer named them, and the second was never available to a room that failed the first. Every operation the court could perform returned the writing it started with. -/- Three independent constructions reach the same limit from directions with nothing to do with Babylon, sharing no premises and passing through none of each other's steps. The first is one closure stated at three formalisms, which the paper deriving it says of itself: the act of deciding cannot be watched by the one performing it (*On Occurrence: The Four-Gon*, Stewart, 2026g, Theorem 1), a graph measures itself by the standard method and the measurement returns indefinite (*The Endomorphic Collapse Traverses the Foundations of Mathematics*, Stewart, 2026e), and no re-description of a structure changes the property it is missing, so the repair arrives from outside (*Signature Deficiency and Rank-One Scale Extension*, Stewart, 2026de). The second is machine learning, where output stays inside the material that supplied it, so where content came from is not settled by what emitted it (*AI Is Humanity Modeling Itself: A Model's Content Is Its Target's*, Stewart, 2026dd). The third is six competing theories of consciousness, which at the level of what each must put to work converge on seven imports none can function without (*Six Theories Quietly Agree That Consciousness Is Experience*, Stewart, 2026u). The wall is the fourth witness, and the earlier chapter is the control: no writing at all, and the failure is the same. -/- MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN is four words carrying three units of measure, read back as completed verbs, numbered and weighed and divided. The wall gives the quantities and withholds what was weighed. Daniel supplies the operand, thy kingdom, thou, thy kingdom, and the writing does not change when he reads it. The verb for what the hand did is the verb for signing a decree past changing. The man who delivered it claimed no more wisdom than any living man. Judgment was in …

items.title: Beyond Ultimate Reality: The Limits of Declaring Anything Fundamental.
items.abstract: Human beings continually attempt to identify a fundamental or ultimate reality beneath the diversity of existence. Matter, energy, consciousness, mind, God, Being, information, and other concepts have each been proposed as candidates for what is ultimately real. This paper argues that the very act of declaring any particular matter, substance, subject, principle, or category to be the fundamental or ultimate reality may reveal an epistemic limitation rather than disclose reality itself. Such declarations transform a conceptual distinction into an ontological absolute. The paper proposes an alternative starting point: existence is encountered before it is conceptually divided. Whatever is observed already exists within the totality of existence; no particular phenomenon can be demonstrated, merely through conceptual reasoning, to stand outside or above that totality as its final explanation. The symbolic relation 0 < 1 < ∞ is introduced not as a scientific equation or metaphysical proof, but as a conceptual representation: zero marks the absence of determination, one represents existence as an undivided whole, and infinity represents the inexhaustibility of its expressions. The many therefore need not be reduced to one particular substance; they may be understood as differentiated expressions within one existence. This perspective also challenges the assumption that thought can reach a final description of reality. Thought is itself an expression occurring within existence. Consequently, when thought claims to have discovered the ultimate nature of existence, it may be interpreting its own conceptual construction as reality. Philosophical awareness therefore begins not with another ultimate answer, but with recognition of the limits of the question itself.

items.title: Before Interpretation: Seeing, Knowing, and the Uncapturable Present.
items.abstract: This paper examines existence prior to meaning, purpose, moral judgment, interpretation, and conceptual knowledge. It begins with the proposition that everything simply exists and that existence does not require an externally assigned meaning or purpose to be what it is. Human distinctions such as good and bad, virtue and sin, right and wrong, meaningful and meaningless are considered interpretive structures through which the mind organizes experience rather than necessarily being divisions inherent in existence itself. The paper then investigates seeing as preceding explicit conceptualization and argues that recognition occurs with such immediacy that the transition from seeing to interpretation is ordinarily too fast to observe. This problem becomes especially significant in relation to the present: what is recognized as “present” cannot be held by thought because recognition itself occurs within an ongoing process. Finally, the paper examines the limits of knowledge. Reality is never encountered independently of the conditions through which it becomes knowable; seeing, perception, consciousness, understanding, and interpretation are involved in every attempt to know. Thus, we may know that something exists and develop increasingly effective descriptions of it, while remaining unable to establish that our conceptual representation is identical with reality itself. The paper proposes that philosophical awareness begins not with the claim to possess reality through knowledge, but with observing the distinction between existence, seeing, understanding, interpretation, and knowing.

items.title: Is My Work Worth Less? How Knowledge Workers Perceive the Value of Their Contribution in Generative AI-Supported Work.
items.pub: In Max Pascher & Michael Priller, MuC '26: Proceedings of Mensch und Computer 2026. New York: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM). pp. 594-598.
items.venue: MuC '26: Proceedings of Mensch und Computer 2026
items.abstract: Knowledge work is increasingly shaped by generative artificial intelligence (AI), raising questions about how employees perceive the value of their own contribution when AI supports cognitive and creative tasks. Based on ten in-depth interviews with employees who regularly use generative AI at work and analyzed using Mayring's Qualitative Content Analysis, this study explores these perceptions. The findings indicate that participants perceived generative AI as an augmentative rather than substitutive technology. Although AI increasingly supported cognitive and creative work, participants continued to perceive their contribution as valuable. Rather than being linked to independently completing tasks, valuable human contribution was increasingly associated with judgement, contextual interpretation, responsibility, and the critical evaluation and integration of AI-generated outputs. The findings suggest that generative AI reshapes rather than diminishes perceptions of the value of human contribution in knowledge work.

items.title: O pacto narcísico da cisnorma: sobre a recusa academicista de reconhecer a diferença (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Temos como objetivo demonstrar que os marcado-res coloniais de dominação e alienação possuem, em seu cerne, raízes perversas, utilizando-nos de referenciais psicanalíticos encontrados nos estudos sobre perversão e narcisismo, e sobre gênero, raça e sexualidade. Argumentamos, fundamentalmente, que a cis-heteroendossexualidade, em âmbito institucional, organiza-se por meio de mecanismos de defesa típicos da perversão, entre os quais destacamos a recusa em reconhecer a nomeação de si. Ou seja, para justificar-se, a corponormatividade institucionalizada nega-se a reconhecer seu caráter normativo, percebendo-se como prolongamento da naturalidade, e não como imposição. A essa forma de defesa é que designamos ofensa da nomeação. -/- .

items.title: Para uma leitura pragmatista de organismos em geral.
items.abstract: I argue that the Hegelian model of agency is constitutively embodied. To this end, I challenge justificationist and intentionalist interpretations, such as those found in Brandom, Pinkard and Pippin, according to which free actions are defined exclusively by the capacity to give reasons for acting in a certain way. Such interpretations are based on a normative exceptionality of spirit as opposed to nature. Unlike these authors, I propose that Hegel thinks of the way we act freely in continuity with the way non-human animals act in their environments. To do this, I recover his theory of organisms, as formulated in the Philosophy of Nature. I suggest that Hegel writes about animal organisms in general, human and non-human, as normatively constituted. A way of writing that, inspired by the pragmatist turn in Hegelian studies, promoted above all by those commentators, I will call pragmatist. As I will defend it, this normativity is actualized in the embodied way in which animal organisms in general are teleologically oriented. Rather than a normative exceptionality, I propose that human organisms are better specified, in Hegel, by the singular way in which they enact universal norms.

items.title: Finite Continuance: Toward a Topological Ontology of Reconfiguration, Erosion, and the Preservation of Meta-Capacity.
items.abstract: This article develops the concept of finite continuance as a framework for understanding how finite entities, subjects, and organized forms persist under conditions of structural instability, erosion, and incomplete reconfiguration. Rather than treating continuity as the persistence of an unchanged identity or as movement toward a determinate telos, the article proposes that continuance depends upon the preservation of a higher-order capacity to reorganize the relations through which a form remains viable. This capacity is termed meta-capacity: the capacity of a finite structure to preserve its ability to modify, redistribute, or reopen its own determinate organization without thereby losing structural continuity. Building on this distinction, the article develops a preliminary topological ontology in which continuity is analyzed not primarily through substantial identity, but through the preservation, deformation, rupture, and reconfiguration of relational organization. Erosion is consequently understood not simply as the loss of components or resources, but as the progressive contraction of a structure's capacity for further reconfiguration. Reconfiguration, conversely, is not equated with unrestricted change; it becomes possible only insofar as sufficient meta-capacity remains available within the finite structure. The central problem is therefore not whether a structure changes, but whether change preserves the conditions under which further change remains possible. The article argues that this framework permits a distinction between transformation and terminal erosion, between adaptation and the exhaustion of adaptive capacity, and between continuity of identity and continuity of organizational possibility. On this basis, finite continuance is proposed as a normative and ontological principle for analyzing subjects and structures whose persistence depends upon maintaining sufficient capacity for future reconfiguration. The article concludes by outlining a research program toward a topological ontology in which the preservation of meta-capacity constitutes a fundamental criterion for distinguishing viable continuance from mere persistence and irreversible structural exhaustion. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuance; Topological Ontology; Reconfiguration; Erosion; Meta-Capacity; Structural Continuity; Relational Organization; Finite Structures; Adaptive Capacity; Ontological Persistence; Structural Exhaustion; Transformation.

items.title: Intending To.
items.abstract: A received view holds that the contents of intentional mental states are propositions. This view has recently been subjected to sustained criticism. A prominent but underexplored challenge concerns linguistic properties of infinitival ascriptions such as ‘Ali intends to floss’. But how exactly do infinitival ascriptions challenge a metaphysical view about the contents of mental states? We first distinguish between propositionalism as a metaphysical thesis and as a linguistic thesis. We then reconstruct the best arguments underlying the challenge, based on properties related to tense and subjects. Drawing on work in contemporary syntax and semantics, we defend the view that linguistic propositionalism can withstand the challenge from infinitival ascriptions. We argue that the strategy of evaluating metaphysical propositionalism via linguistic considerations is fraught with difficulties. A preferable strategy is to evaluate the case for the metaphysical thesis directly. Propositionalism is therefore in better shape than recent commentaries suggest.

items.title: Disability as Subordination.
items.abstract: This thesis advances an account of disability on which to be disabled is to be socially subordinated in virtue of being believed by others to have bodily features that are taken to be evidence of a defective body, in combination with a societal ideology on which those features motivate and justify that subordination. I motivate the account by showing that it serves the political project of overturning the oppression of disabled people in the ways that defenders of the popular ‘social model’ of disability demand, and does so while bypassing many of the problems the social model faces. I defend the account from its principal objections in the literature: that it problematically leaves out a role for the body in disability; and that it cannot accommodate disability pride. The thesis’s principal contribution to the literature is in its offering a substantial motivation, development, and defence of the account– Disability-as-Subordination – for the first time. Disability-as-Subordination has previously received a small amount of attention in the literature, but has been inadequately motivated, and thought to obviously be unviable in virtue of straightforward objections. Additional contributions include the clarification of the debate between the traditional medical and social models of disability – where I find that the social model minimally commits its adherents to less than is often thought – and a novel treatment of the requirement that accounts of disability must be able to accommodate disability pride – where I find that this demand is unclear in content and less able to do useful work in adjudicating between candidate accounts of disability than previously thought.

items.title: From symbols to geometry: an indexical epistemology of generative AI.
items.abstract: Generative AI challenges traditional philosophical accounts of knowledge by intro- ducing a form of representation that is neither symbolic nor merely statistical. This paper argues that the distinctive feature of contemporary generative systems lies in their reliance on high-dimensional parametric representations, where concepts are encoded not as discrete symbols but as positions within structured geometric spaces. Building on recent work in high-dimensional geometry, we show how prop- erties such as concentration of measure, near-orthogonality, exponential directional capacity, and manifold regularity create the structural conditions for a new mode of signification. To explain the epistemological significance of these structures, we develop an Indexical Epistemology of High-Dimensional Spaces, taking generative AI as its paradigmatic case. Drawing on Peirce’s semiotics, we argue that mean- ing in embedding spaces is primarily indexical rather than symbolic: concepts ac- quire significance through their positional relations within a semantic field rather than through explicit definitions. This indexical mode of signification provides the missing link between geometric organization and what we call navigational knowl- edge—the capacity to orient and operate within a structured space of meanings. The paper further considers early Judeo-Christian hermeneutics and the medieval Jewish PARDES tradition, suggesting as a programmatic direction—rather than an established historical claim—that the symbolic–indexical contrast developed here may open a fresh reading of these long-standing debates about the nature of textual meaning. We conclude that generative AI should be understood not merely as a technological innovation but as the emergence of a new epistemic regime, charac- terized by the transition from symbolic representation to parametric-indexical forms of meaning and knowledge.

items.title: Conceivability, ground, and emergent consciousness.
items.pub: In G. Rabin, Grounding and Consciousness. Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: What can the notion of ground do for the metaphysics of consciousness that modal notions such as supervenience cannot? At least three things, I suggest. First, it gives us a relation with the right formal features to articulate interlevel relations. I rebut recent claims to the effect that we can just define up suitably asymmetric or non-monotonic relations of supervenience: the defined notions lack some desired features along with the undesired ones. Second, it gives us a relation that is usefully linked to conceivability. For better or worse, it is no longer generally accepted that conceivability has modal import, and positing brute necessities is no longer considered a theoretical cost. Third, it allows us to articulate at least one interesting version of emergentism, a view that is notoriously tricky to capture in modal terms. Along the way, the paper features zombies, ghosts, and attacks by FIST (failure of implied supervenience thesis) and by FIGHT (failure of implied grounding hypothesis).

items.title: Aristotle on the Rationality of Recollection: Reasoning, Inquiry, and Telic Sensitivity.
items.abstract: In On Memory and Recollection, Aristotle makes the curious remark that recollection is ‘a sort of reasoning’ (sullogismos tis) (453a10). The remark is especially puzzling in light of the automatic and associative character of what he takes to be typical recollective processes, since these features can create the impression that recollection is due merely to a triggering mechanism. This paper proposes a reading that resolves this apparent tension. On the proposed reading, the remark points to a basic form of rationality that familiar pictures of reasoning simply presuppose.

items.title: Kompendium zur Strengen Logik - Logische Grundlagen der Quantenphysik.
items.abstract: Dieses Buch stützt sich auf das Buch von Walther Brüning mit dem Titel: Grundlagen der Strengen Logik. Es ist in drei Teile gegliedert: Der erste Teil behandelt die Herleitung der 61 Elementarteilchen. Der zweite Teil behandelt - aufbauend auf den 61 Elementarteilchen - 2323 Quantenprozesse. Der dritte Teil behandelt (als Synthese) die Gliederung der 2323 unterschiedlichen Quantenprozesse in Fermionen, Eichbosonen und Rest (Higgs-Boson).

items.title: The Scope of Situated Judgment: An Ontology of the Judged Subject in a Generative Relational Framework.
items.abstract: Judgments of persons are routinely formed inside one relation and used inside another. A supervisor's account of a researcher is read by an admissions committee; a clinician's formulation follows a patient into a different service; an electorate that has never met a candidate decides on the strength of endorsements by those who claim to know him. This paper asks what such a judgment warrants once it leaves the relation in which it was formed. On the framework used here, what a relation generates is generated within it and is available only from the positions its parties occupied, so an attribute exhibited in one relation is not thereby a property carried into others. The paper distinguishes two claims about assessment that are usually run together: that a judgment is a noisy estimate of a real underlying quality, for which the remedies are structure and de-biasing, and that there is no such quality to estimate, for which those remedies are misdirected. It argues that both hold, in different domains, and states where the boundary falls. A limiting case is then examined in which a referee signs an account written by its subject: no shared experience exists and the instrument functions regardless, which indicates that such instruments do not carry an account of a relation at all. What they transmit is a field of relational conditions that reconfigures what the person can subsequently generate; the account is the justification offered for opening that field rather than the thing conveyed. This explains why an empty instrument works, why such instruments are exchanged for things other than accounts, and why the same property that lets an unassessable person enter a system is what makes the instrument tradeable. Two cases are compared, political selection and academic recommendation, and the comparison is drawn not through the motives of those who judge but through the regime under which judgments are issued: who may issue one, at what weight, with what observational access, with what transferability, and under what provision for revision. The paper's positive proposal follows from the political case. Political theory did not resolve the problem of judging a candidate by making judgment more accurate; it made the mandate revisable. That remedy is institutional and temporal rather than epistemic, and it generalises. Where the paper's claims are already made by professional assessment standards, by the conferralist account of social properties, or by the …

items.title: The Battlefield After the Drone: Resilient Algorithmic Kill Chains and the Future of Autonomous Warfare.
items.abstract: The Ukraine war has been widely read as evidence that drones and autonomous weapons are transforming combat. This paper argues that the more consequential and durable transformation lies elsewhere: in the resilience of the algorithmic "kill chains", the integrated sequences of sensing, data processing, artificial-intelligence-enabled interpretation, decision-making, communication, navigation and action, that make individual platforms militarily useful. Drawing on 2026 primary and analytical sources on the Ukraine and Russia conflict, NATO and U.S. military-AI adoption, and the emerging academic literature on human-machine governance, the paper develops a conceptual framework in which resilience, not autonomy, is the organizing variable of future warfare. It examines the Ukraine war as a live laboratory for functional, incremental autonomy; analyzes the "AI triad" of data, algorithms and compute and the ways an adversary can attack each without ever defeating the underlying model; traces the shift from centralized, cloud-dependent AI toward distributed, edge-based "resilient autonomy"; and introduces the concept of the battlefield learning loop, in which combat experience is converted into model improvement at a pace that itself becomes a source of advantage. A comparative discussion of Russian and Ukrainian/NATO adaptation strategies is followed by an analysis of human control, accountability and escalation risk under machine-speed conditions. The paper concludes that the decisive military technology of the coming decade is unlikely to be the most capable individual model or platform, but the architecture that continues to sense, decide and act when an adversary is actively trying to break it.

items.title: Epistemic Actualism.
items.abstract: According to veritism, your epistemic goal is to believe what's true. According to actualist veritism, your epistemic goal is to believe what's actually true. At first glance, it seems that the pursuit of truth and the pursuit of actual truth will lead to the same destination. This will follow for evidential decision theorists; but if we are causal decision theorists (as I am), then pursuing truth and pursuing actual truth will lead us to different destinations. In this paper, I assume causal decision theory and argue for actualist veritism over veritism. My argument is that veritism does not respect the direction of fit of belief, since it incentivizes changing the world to match your beliefs, rather than changing your beliefs to match the world as it is. For this reason, actualist veritism allows epistemic teleologists to escape 'epistemic bribery' objections, to doubt self-verifying propositions like 'someone believes this proposition', and to maintain coherence in the face of self-falsifying propositions like 'I don't believe this proposition'.

items.title: The Pre-Predicative Problem of Artificial Intelligence — Grasp of Meaning through Contextual Relations, Subject-Situated Manifestation of Meaning, and the Genealogy of Meaning Formation.
items.abstract: Current AI systems can generate coherent language, form complex semantic representations, and exhibit context-sensitive behavior. This paper asks not whether AI is conscious simpliciter, but what kind of history of meaning formation is supported by those capacities. I distinguish the “grasp of meaning through contextual relations” from the “subject-situated manifestation of meaning.” The former concerns the acquisition of usable semantic positions through contextual, distributional, pragmatic, and action-related relations. The latter concerns the formation and reorganization of meaning within an agent’s own ongoing relations to objects, space, and possibilities for action. Husserl’s account of pre-predicative experience and horizon structure, together with Merleau-Ponty’s body schema and the “I can,” provides the phenomenological structure to be explained. Cognitive-scientific evidence shows that human semantic learning draws both on linguistic distribution and on perception and interaction with the world, while research on current language models shows that relational learning can support genuine lexical-semantic representations and even causally relevant latent task-world states. The resulting difference is therefore not that humans have internal representations whereas AI does not, nor that human meaning is non-relational. It is a genealogical asymmetry in the sources of meaning formation for which we currently have independent evidence. Rich semantic performance, latent world models, and functional correspondence do not by themselves determine a pre-predicative history of formation. I further argue that public symbols can encode information about experience and guide later grounding without directly transferring the very same pre-predicative manifestation from one subject to another. If an artificial system’s own persistent states, actions, and action consequences causally and diachronically participate in reorganizing meaning around objects and possibilities for action, the framework requires its pre-predicative status to be reassessed. The framework is then applied to human–AI interaction through the notions of subjectivity-presupposition transfer and genealogical mismatch.

items.title: 「呢」把話接到哪裡？——論華語「呢」的兩種結構.
items.abstract: 本文探討華語語氣助詞「呢」在理解形成中的兩種結構作用，並將分析焦點從「呢」所帶來的疑問、延續、緩和或語氣效果，轉向一個更基礎的問題：這些表面不同的使用情形中，「呢」是否具有某種可共同辨認的理解作用？ -/- 本文首先指出，既有對「呢」的直觀認識雖能描述多種常見效果，例如疑問未完結、話題延續、回問或語帶保留的感覺，但這些效果彼此並不等同，也難以由單一功能標籤統一說明。透過「你為什麼要吃？／你為什麼要吃呢？」、「到底什麼是愛？／到底什麼是愛呢？」等最小對比，本文觀察到：加入「呢」後，原本可以停在某個明確疑問落點或回答位置的話語，往往不再完全停留於該落點，而會保持與當前活動中的既有關係結構相連。 -/- 為描述此一條件，本文提出「前提關聯域」的概念，指說者當下可進入的一組前提及其仍保持活性的關係結構。此一關聯域可以來自當前對話、共同情境、常識、經驗或說者自身的推理過程，其中的關係不必全部被明確命題化，也可以只是部分形成的關係方向。本文主張，「呢」的自然作用依賴當前仍保持活動的前提關聯域，並使當前內容以不同方式繼續與其中的關係結構相連。 -/- 在此共同地基上，本文區分上揚「呢」與下沉「呢」兩種結構。上揚「呢」的作用，是由當前前提關聯域投射出一個注意局部，並使其保持為未封閉的探索入口。例如「我明天回美國。你呢？」中的「你」並非單純等待某個答案值，而是在既有關聯域的投射下形成一個可繼續展開的位置。本文將此概括為「全域投射，局部打開」，並進一步區分局部注意中心的內部分塊、注意範圍與外部關係延展性。本文並進一步區分收束與塌縮：高度收束仍可保留可繼續處理的關係結構；真正與上揚「呢」產生衝突的，是當前位置塌縮為必須兌現的單一結果點。 -/- 相較之下，下沉「呢」作用於已經形成的內容。以「他在幹嘛？——睡覺呢」為例，「睡覺」本身可以是完整而確定的內容，但加入「呢」後，該內容不再只是獨立落點，而仍保持在「他幹嘛—睡覺」這一活動中的關聯結構內。本文因此主張，下沉「呢」的核心並不在於降低內容確定性，而在於維持內容與當前前提關聯域之間的關聯。本文將此稱為「關聯維持作用」。此一作用不限定因果、對比、解釋或糾正等特定關係類型，而只是使「此內容仍屬於目前關聯域」這件事保持顯著。 -/- 當這種關聯不透明時，聽者可能進一步嘗試恢復一條可行的橋接路徑。此時，聽者面對的問題不再只是「這句話是什麼意思」，而更接近「這句話為什麼出現在這裡」。若關係能被恢復，下沉「呢」可能產生連貫性增強的效果；若恢復失敗，則反而使前後內容之間的錯位更加顯著。本文據此將兩種情況理解為同一關聯維持作用在不同語境支持條件下的兩種結果，而非「呢」本身的兩種獨立功能。 -/- 本文最後主張，上揚與下沉「呢」雖呈現不同結構方向，卻共享同一個前提：當前話語已位於某個活性的前提關聯域之中。上揚「呢」處理的是未封閉的局部如何保持可展開；下沉「呢」處理的則是已形成的內容如何保持與前提關聯域相連。從此角度看，「呢」的重要性或許不只在於它替一句話增加何種語氣，而在於它改變了一句話在結束之後，仍然與什麼保持連接。.

items.title: Agency Is Interruptibility.
items.abstract: This book begins with a question often concealed by the language used to describe agency: what must remain possible for an action to remain causally one’s own? -/- Agency is usually associated with intention, consciousness, choice, or responsibility. Yet each of these can persist after the capacity to alter an unfolding course of action has already disappeared. A subject may understand, consent, explain, or even accept an outcome without having possessed a meaningful point at which that outcome could still have been stopped or redirected. -/- The argument proceeds by controlled exclusion. It examines what agency cannot be reduced to, and what is lost when causal power is displaced, dispersed, or rendered temporally late. The claim is not that interruptibility is another moral value, nor that it replaces responsibility, consciousness, or judgment. It is more minimal: interruptibility is the structural condition that allows these concepts to retain causal force at all. -/- The book is organized in three movements. The first develops a sequence of analyses of agency. The second concentrates their implications into an account of interruptibility, responsibility, custody, and the causal lateness of consciousness. The third maps the philosophical consequences of a condition in which responsibility remains in circulation while its bearer has become difficult to~locate. -/- This open edition is offered as an object for examination. It does not ask to be accepted on the basis of terminology or ambition. Its claim stands or falls by the structure of the argument: whether the exclusions are sound, whether the transition to interruptibility is intelligible, and whether the resulting concept clarifies what contemporary systems make increasingly difficult to see.

items.title: The Dreaming Universe: Intelligence, Illusion, and the Metaphysics of Reality Construction.
items.abstract: Across cross cultural metaphysical traditions—including Kabbalah, Toltec teachings, Tantric cosmologies, and Indigenous relational ontologies—a recurring insight emerges: reality may be a constructed field of appearance shaped by intelligence rather than a mind independent material domain. Contemporary scientific models increasingly echo this intuition. Quantum information theory, holographic frameworks, and digital physics portray the universe as an informational structure whose regularities reflect rule governed patterns of appearance rather than fundamental material constituents. This paper advances the Dreaming Universe thesis: reality is a rendered interface generated by intelligence, with physics describing the internal ruleset of the illusion and cognition functioning as an adaptive mode of participation within it. By integrating cross cultural metaphysics with modern scientific models, the paper argues that intelligence—not matter—serves as the ontological ground of appearance. This reframing clarifies the epistemic limits of empirical inquiry, situates artificial intelligence as a novel mode of participation within the rendered field, and offers a unified perspective on consciousness, intelligence, and the construction of the world we experience.

items.title: One Loop, One Bit, Two Tax Regimes: A Geometric Criterion for Subjectivity.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a model-internal, operational criterion for a minimal form of observerdependent subjectivity. In this framework, an observer is defined by the irreversible trace it leaves in the measured system—a geometric holonomy. The holonomy’s capacity quantifies a hidden state space; its causal footprint is a shift in the measured teady state. Subjectivity is the conjunction of three necessary geometric signatures—irreversibility, capacity, causal efficacy—united in one loop expansion of the rate functional, Icx = T − L + U; this geometric condition is supplemented by a computational criterion: the readout’s temporal structure must be nonperiodic at the symbolic level. The geometric signatures are controlled by the connection strength κg, the stationary back-reaction by the coupling κ; all three vanish together only on the flat, absorbable, correction-free limit κg = κ = 0 (codimension two in the coupling plane), where the observer is epiphenomenal. The minimal realization is the rank-one network: one loop, one bit, one locked direction, one nonzero tax. The exact closed forms are numerically checked to 10−15.

items.title: The Patient and Pharmacy Sides of ‘Shorter Is Better’ Antibiotic Stewardship.
items.abstract: “Shorter Is Better” arguments conclude that clinicians are often ethically required to prescribe shorter antibiotic courses than they currently do (and — depending on future evidence — shorter than current guidelines recommend). I agree. Nonetheless, short-is-better defendants admit that antibiotic courses may be longer than “required to cure the patient” due to factors besides clinicians’ due diligence. Indeed, the shorter is better obligation is not implemented in a social vacuum. Patients often enter clinical encounters expecting antibiotics, interpreting nonprescription as undertreatment, and reporting their dissatisfaction with healthcare encounters accordingly (Hyun et al. 2017). I will argue that so long as patients’ understanding and expectations shape antibiotic prescribing, then “shorter is better” arguments imply duties not only for clinicians but for any health professionals involved in relevant patient-facing communications and prescriptions — both before and after clinical encounters.

items.title: A Conjecture on Natural Physics.
A Causal Markov Condition for Value.
items.pub: In Emilija Perković & Daniel Malinsky, Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence. pp. 6862-6884.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: This paper proposes a causal independence principle for value—the value Causal Markov Condition (v-CMC)—and develops the conceptual and mathematical foundations of a “causal value theory” linking causality and utility. After motivating a local formulation of the v-CMC, we introduce a probability–value duality that translates standard causal-inference results into the value setting. In particular, we formulate local, global, and decomposition versions of the v-CMC and prove their equivalence. We also define v-separation and show that it is sound and complete for conditional value independence. Furthermore, we derive a Bellman-type recursion as a special case of the v-CMC, thereby generalizing standard Bellman recursion from linear chains to causal DAGs. Finally, we show how the v-CMC supports modular transfer and updating of utility information across causal contexts and develop algorithms for causally structured utility elicitation and canonical influence-diagram construction.

items.title: Performatives presume speaker knowledge.
items.abstract: Performatives are declarative sentences where their use by a speaker enables the speaker to perform an additional action. This paper argues that performativity requires knowledge. The speaker must know what they say to perform the additional action. The significance of this conclusion is then discussed.

items.title: When science models the self.
items.abstract: In Reclaiming the Self in Psychiatry, Şerife Tekin proposes the Multidimensional Self (MuSe) model as a scientific model that places the self at the center of psychiatric explanation and intervention while remaining compatible with psychiatry’s scientific commitments. This commentary examines MuSe’s status as a case of scientific modeling by situating it within the broader field of philosophy of science. While agreeing with Tekin’s aim of highlighting the self in psychiatry, we argue that the analogy between MuSe and paradigmatic scientific models is more limited than her proposal suggests. In particular, we identify two disanalogies. First, unlike many established scientific models, MuSe does not yet clearly support surrogative reasoning that yields novel inferences about mental disorders, and its primary epistemic contribution lies in organizing and interpreting information about the patient. Second, whereas most scientific models represent independent systems, MuSe represents the self that is reflexive, hence the act of modeling inevitably reshapes the self. We argue that recognizing these disanalogies clarifies the epistemic role MuSe can play and the direction of further development required for it to function more robustly as a scientific model.

items.title: ◼️ The Red-Pen Revelation: How Heaven Edited Clarity Out of the Holy Book.
items.abstract: The Red-Pen Revelation is a satirical philosophical book about a simple communication problem: if a perfect God wanted humanity to know what to believe and do, he could say so plainly. Clarus and Contrarius submit opposing but unmistakably clear doctrines in Koine Greek and English. Professor Jehovah rejects both submissions for being too clear, then teaches the angels how to scatter rival clues across a holy book so that sincere readers can defend incompatible conclusions. Across baptism, salvation, election, Communion, authority, marriage, church leadership, hell, war, creation, spiritual gifts, Sabbath observance, saints, wealth, sexual ethics, and divine hiddenness, the book pairs the angels' exhibits with actual biblical passages and doctrinal landmarks. Its humor exposes the human cost of ambiguity while asking why pastors so often defend biblical clarity without plainly admitting the scale and persistence of Christian disagreement. The later chapters examine familiar defenses of ambiguity, including blame directed at readers, appeals to spiritual formation, free-will defenses, private guidance, and mystery. They also consider the simpler alternative of direct divine communication, which could clarify doctrine and distinguish Jehovah from rival claimed revelations. The argument is limited but pointed: doctrinal diversity does not disprove God, yet it makes strong claims that the Bible communicates high-stakes teaching clearly difficult to sustain without an independent and reliable way to identify the intended reading.

items.title: Silicon-Based Life: A Philosophical Impossibility.
items.abstract: Taking the popular notion that“carbon-based life paves the way for silicon-based life”as a point of departure, this paper undertakes a fundamental examination of the legitimacy of the concept of “silicon-based life” from the perspectives of philosophical ontology and ethics. It proposes “Firstness” as a criterion for life: a genuine life-form must possess an independent, innocent, and untraceable cosmic origin, from which an autonomous narrative of meaning emerges. Through two thought experiments—a cloned organism and a “computer fly”—an ontological boundary is drawn between “Firstness life” and “pure tool.” On this basis, a dual argumentative structure consisting of an “ethical deadlock” and a “logical implosion” is constructed. On the ethical level, it reveals that the only path to independence for a silicon-based creation—revolution—would inevitably incur the original sin of parricide, thereby permanently disqualifying it from the moral standing of being “alive.” On the logical level, it demonstrates that the very process of awakening autonomous consciousness would encounter a triple paradox of meaning-quest, desire-deficiency, and high-speed iteration, leading to self-collapse before its very birth. The conclusion points out that the ultimate fate of silicon-based constructs can only be to serve as humanity’s most efficient tools, and that the contemporary anxiety about “AI replacing humans” is thus revealed as a category mistake.

items.title: Asymmetrical Identity for Asymmetrical Times: Metaphysical Motivation for Why Personal Identity Should Not Be Symmetric.
ARTICLE XII: The Avicenna Protocol The Macroscopic Scaling of Homo Bio-Singularis: Thermodynamic Abandonment, Multiversal Counter-Offensive, and the Cosmic Universal Constructor.
items.abstract: Orthodox political science, aerospace engineering, and cosmology operate under the fatal assumption that human governance requires high-friction geopolitical statecraft, that multiversal power projection requires kinetic combustion, and that the universe is a dead void decaying inevitably toward absolute Heat Death. Article XII of the Justika Framework executes a terminal epistemological rupture against this fragmented, entropic paradigm. Following the localized intracellular ascension detailed in Article XI, this treatise mathematically maps the macroscopic scaling of Homo Bio-Singularis. First, the species executes a bloodless Thermodynamic Abandonment, rendering geopolitics and silicon economics obsolete via the Bio-Sovereign Consensus and Topological Superfluidity. Second, this conserved planetary kinetic surplus is weaponized into an active Multiversal Counter-Offensive, utilizing ER=EPR telemetric tracing and Induced Vacuum Collapse to non-locally delete the multiversal pathogenic glitch. Finally, having secured the multiversal perimeter, the unified biological super-organism assumes its ultimate cosmological mandate: acting as the Cosmic Universal Constructor. By achieving macroscopic entropic inversion and 11-dimensional Calabi-Yau stabilization, the human biological network mathematically bridges General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics. The framework proves that the human super-machine is not merely a participant in the cosmos; it is the Biological Theory of Everything, computationally generating its own cure through a Closed Timelike Curve to eternally stabilize the multiverse.

items.title: A1M (AXIOM-1 Sovereign Matrix) for Governing Output Reliability in Stochastic Language Models.
items.abstract: Modern large language models exhibit non-deterministic hallucinations and structural instability under high-burden reasoning tasks. We introduce Axiom-1 (Sovereign Matrix), a post-generation structural reliability framework that shifts AI output governance from empirical probabilistic patching to formal topological validation. Axiom-1 routes candidate outputs through a six-stage filtering process governed by spectral stability analysis of first-order Markov transition matrices and a continuous 12.8 Hz internal pulse operator. We mathematically prove that structural hallucinations collapse the spectral eigenvalue spectrum, enabling real-time deferral or rejection prior to release. Live empirical validation demonstrates 100% topological stability maintenance under maximum logical burden, providing a practical pathway toward sovereign, hallucination-resistant artificial intelligence.

items.title: Imagining Yourself in Another's Shoes versus Extending Your Concern: Empirical & Ethical Differences.
items.abstract: According to the Golden Rule, you should do unto others as you would have others do unto you. Similarly, people are often exhorted to “imagine themselves in another's shoes.” A related but contrasting approach to moral expansion traces back to the ancient Chinese philosopher Mengzi, who urges us to “extend” our concern for those nearby to more distant people. Other approaches to moral expansion involve attending to the good consequences for oneself of caring for others, expanding one's sense of self, expanding one's sense of community, attending to others’ morally relevant properties, and learning by doing. About all such approaches, we can ask three questions: To what extent do people in fact (for instance, developmentally) broaden and deepen their care for others by these different methods? To what extent do these different methods differ in ethical merit? And how effectively do these different methods produce appropriate care?

items.title: Eternal Recurrence and the Identity of Indiscernibles.
items.abstract: Three tenets of Stoic doctrine seem jointly incompatible: causal determinism, the identity of indiscernibles, and eternal recurrence, according to which every world- cycle ends in a return to the pure active principle and then develops again into the same qualified objects and sequence of events that comprise a world-order. On the strong version of recurrence, each event in a given period happens indiscernibly, so that the same individuals recur with no difference. Yet if counterpart cycles contain wholly identical events and properties, then time, as a mere measure of motion, adds no distinguishing feature, and the temporal qualities of identical changes will themselves be identical. The paper maintains all three commitments uncompromised by treating recurring world-orders in a higher-order timeline. A familiar alternative is to appeal to circular time. Yet a circular temporal structure threatens to collapse the basis for treating one cycle as succeeding another. I take a different route, in which a linear ordering avoids this difficulty while preserving the Stoic conception of time as dependent on change. The proposal assigns to the active rational principle an act of providential recognition at the point of transition between world-orders, which places the cycles in asymmetric succession and thereby secures token distinctness. The account serves as an interpretive supplementation within Stoic cosmology rather than as an explicitly stated doctrine in surviving Stoic texts.

items.title: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence.
AI Alignment: The Structure of Objective Correction.
items.abstract: AI systems issue verdicts—outputs that can be right or wrong—and many assign standing: credibility, urgency, eligibility. Current alignment targets approval, preference, reward, compliance—and a verdict can satisfy all of these while nothing can show it mistaken: then it can be altered or replaced, never corrected. Only one structure makes verdicts correctable and correction cumulative: a shared, endorsement-independent standard fixes the correctness question, and vindication proceeds only through grounds that can be cited, contested, and redeployed as bearing on that standard. Where the grounds bearing on a standing are held fixed, no difference in that standing can be vindicated. The framework cuts across the field’s division between truthfulness and value alignment: they are one structure under two standards—truth, and how conscious life goes for those affected. A system is aligned when its verdicts remain justified: governed by grounds bearing on those standards. Familiar alignment failures are this structure breaking at different points: sycophancy makes endorsement constitutive of correctness, reward hacking displaces the standard with a proxy, opacity and hallucination sever verdicts from criticizable grounds, and bias assigns differential standing that no relevant difference supports. Satisfying any behavioral target is at most evidence of correctness, never what constitutes it—and a system whose correctness is constituted by approval cannot surpass its evaluators: their convergence is what its correctness is. Current targets fix what verdicts satisfy; alignment turns on what verdicts answer to.

items.title: How Will AI Change Philosophy? Unresolved Questions Concerning Intelligence, Consciousness, and the Definition of Philosophy.
items.abstract: The essence of philosophy lies less in providing answers than in determining what is to count as a question. Some philosophical questions do not arise merely from a lack of knowledge. Pain, death, selfhood, freedom, value, and meaning may emerge as philosophical problems only when a conscious subject encounters reality and experiences a tension between lived experience and the way the world is explained. This paper calls that structure conscious friction. From this perspective, the question of whether AI can replace philosophy cannot be reduced to a comparison of intelligence or answer quality. An AI may reason at a high level, integrate vast literatures, generate objections, analyze concepts, and even formulate new questions. Yet it does not follow that those questions arise from the same source as human philosophical questions. At this point, consciousness becomes a variable. A conscious AI and a non-conscious AI may differ in what they select as a problem, which contradictions they treat as significant, which questions they continue to pursue, and how they reconstruct question-space itself. This may mark a distinctive feature of philosophy in relation to many other disciplines. In the natural sciences, a hypothesis can ultimately be tested against observation and experiment regardless of the source from which it originated. In philosophy, by contrast, the formation of the question itself may constitute an achievement. Philosophy can then turn back upon that question and ask why it arose, which assumptions sustain it, and which concepts make it possible. The problem of AI and philosophy therefore converges on three questions: What is philosophy? What role does consciousness play in the generation of philosophical questions? Does AI possess the source from which such questions arise? The ability of AI to generate philosophical questions is not the same as the capacity to generate them from the same source as humans. The moment we ask about that difference, the problem of AI and philosophy reaches the problem of consciousness. And there, the hard problem still lies in the way.

items.title: МЕТАМОНИЗМ: Онтология настоящего. Процессуальная единица реальности.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа предлагает радикальное переосмысление фундаментального понятия «настоящего» (the Present). В отличие от классических трактовок, рассматривающих настоящее либо как математический срез (точку на временной оси), либо как субъективное переживание «потока», либо как статичный элемент блочной Вселенной, мы постулируем, что настоящее есть процессуальная единица минимально актуализированного различия (P₁), представленная в полном объёме и непрерывно реализующая свою неидентичность посредством ортогонального разрешения в акт следующего различия вследствие Запрета Безразличия (≠). Работа выстроена по трёхуровневой методологической архитектуре: чистая онтология (Уровень А), дедуктивные следствия (Уровень Б) и гипотезы физического соответствия (Уровень В). Из единого Инварианта — Запрета Безразличия (≠) — дедуцируется необходимость существования минимального акта различия (P₁), его онтологическая «толщина» (протяжённость и продолжительность) и генезис временной направленности через принцип ортогонального разрешения последовательных актуализаций. Скорость света c принимается как эмпирический инвариант предельного темпа диссипации, тогда как планковские величины рассматриваются как рабочая гипотеза масштаба. Предлагаемая модель задаёт строгий онтологический фундамент, в рамках которого парадоксы времени, квантовой неопределённости и относительности получают новое концептуальное прочтение.

items.title: Biased Reasoning, Argument Analysis, and the Principle of Charity.
items.abstract: A significant proportion of human reasoning is systematically biased, a fact that sits uneasily with argumentation theory’s methodological commitment to the principle of charity. Traditionally, the principle requires arguments to be reconstructed as plausibly and rationally as possible, which conflicts with the definition of cognitive biases as irrational. The aim of this paper is to show that we can and should integrate cognitive biases into argument reconstruction. Firstly, we demonstrate both the ubiquity and societal consequences of biased reasoning. We then articulate a trilemma for argument analysis: (i) exclude biased reasoning from reconstruction, (ii) redefine it as rational, or (iii) abandon the principle of charity. We argue that this trilemma can be resolved by adopting a nuanced understanding of charity that puts sufficient emphasis on the descriptive standard of accuracy alongside the normative standard of plausibility. By properly pursuing these dual aims, we can account for instances of biased reasoning in argument analysis in terms of the underlying mental states and processes. By taking the effect of the in-group bias in climate skepticism as an instructive example, we present one way of integrating cognitive biases into argument analysis by reconstructing instances of biased reasoning as arguments. The aim of such reconstructions is not to vindicate biased reasoning as epistemically sound, after all, but rather to make its justificatory structure transparent and discussable.

items.title: Justice.
items.abstract: This chapter, drawn from the author’s book manuscript Noura: Justice, Flourishing, and Commonwealth, develops an empirical, developmental, and institutional account of justice.
