items.title: Symmetric Culpability: Clone Identity and Moral Responsibility Without Self-Knowledge in Mur Lafferty's Six Wakes.
items.abstract: Mur Lafferty's Six Wakes (2017) has gone largely unremarked as a philosophical thought experiment in the personal identity and moral responsibility literature. Standard treatments of amnesia and responsibility, from Locke's memory criterion through Parfit's psychological continuity theory to Strawson's account of reactive attitudes, assume an underlying asymmetry: the agent may not remember an act, but some fact of the matter about who performed it remains fixed and, in principle, recoverable by others if not by the agent herself. Six Wakes stages a structurally different condition. Its clone crew wakes with no memory of a shipboard murder in which each member is, with equal epistemic standing, a candidate perpetrator or victim. I call this condition epistemic symmetry. Existing accounts of responsibility are built to handle asymmetric ignorance; they are not built to handle the collapse of any privileged perspective from which guilt could be assigned, including the agent's own, and this is the gap I argue Six Wakes exposes. I further argue that the novel's premise of identical psychological continuity across cloned bodies stress-tests Parfit's continuity criterion in ways ordinary fission cases do not: the criterion supposed to individuate a person is, at the moment responsibility must be assigned, held equally by every viable candidate.

items.title: Gatekeeping in science reporting: a zetetic account.
items.abstract: We argue that gatekeeping in science reporting mediates an adequate epistemic relation between non-experts and experts. We further specify how this unfolds in non-ideal epistemic situations, e.g. through recent reports on the alleged sentience of large language models and the prospects of artificial general intelligence. In our view, the primary goal of science reporting is to promote epistemic improvement by better positioning laypeople in relation to the inquiry of relevant scientific questions as elaborated within zetetic epistemology. Consequently, the task of science journal ists involves not merely scaling up facts or harnessing settled attitudes toward sci ence, but rather navigating the balance between do-your-own-research (Ballantyne 2024) and public trust in science. Thus, trust in science should not be conceived as a synchronic epistemic attitude we owe to experts unconditionally, but as an out come of a dynamic diachronic process intertwined with a plethora of interrogative attitudes such as curiosity, wonder, and deliberation, that cannot be reduced to a binary trust vs. distrust relation. We propose norms of good science reporting that would fulfill the gatekeeping ambition, such as (1) the clutter avoidance for asking and considering questions, (2) the elicitation and maintenance of vigilant attention, and (3) the prevention of interrogative injustice. These norms stem from the concept of zetetic relevance—that is, the identification of information needed to provide reasonable answers to the questions raised by science reporting (Siegel 2026).

items.title: From possessive individualism to civic virtue environmentalism: Virtue, community, and the moral foundations of environmental responsibility.
items.abstract: Abstract This thesis develops a systematic critique of liberal conceptions of the self and their implications for environmental ethics, arguing for a shift towards a civic virtue environmentalism grounded in a situated conception of the person and community. It begins from the empirical observation that, although citizens in liberal democracies often express concern about environmental problems, they rarely experience themselves as personally responsible for them. The thesis traces this gap between awareness and responsibility to deeper assumptions within liberal political thought about the nature of the self, freedom, and the role of markets. -/- Engaging critically with Hobbes, Locke, Mill, and Rawls, and drawing on C. B. Macpherson's account of possessive individualism, the thesis shows how liberal ideas of self-ownership and property converge on a conception of freedom primarily understood as economic freedom. Through an examination of Ludwig von Mises, Milton Friedman, and Friedrich Hayek, it analyses how economic freedom is defended as morally sufficient and how the figure of the economic man-a self-interested, utility-maximising market actor-is normalised as the central agent of modern societies. This framework is then tested against environmental problems such as the tragedy of the commons and common-pool resource management, engaging especially with Elinor Ostrom's work on the role of communities, shared norms, and institutional trust. -/- The second half of the thesis argues that liberal individualism is too thin to sustain robust environmental responsibility. It develops an alternative account of the situated self, embedded in constitutive communities, histories, and places, drawing on Alasdair MacIntyre's account of practices and traditions, Michael Sandel's conception of civic responsibility, and Charles Taylor's understanding of the self as located within a moral space. On this basis, the thesis advances civic virtue environmentalism: an environmental virtue ethics centred on phronēsis (practical wisdom) and oikophilia (love of home). It argues that the mutual reinforcement of these virtues generates a form of grounded environmental judgement in which decision-making is both emotionally invested and prudentially sound. -/- The central conclusion is that civic virtue environmentalism offers a more adequate and ethically robust normative framework for responding to environmental challenges than liberal individualism and the economic man. By …

items.title: Learned Synthetic Rationality Entity.
items.abstract: This article proposes the concept of Learned Synthetic Rationality Entity (LSRE) as a classificatory category for non-biological entities whose functional rationality is constituted through artificial processes of learning and training, becomes relatively stabilized in its inferential dispositions, and is instantiated in an artificial system. The proposal distinguishes rationality from phenomenal consciousness, arguing that the attribution of functional rationality does not, by itself, entail consciousness, subjective experience, human equivalence, or moral personhood. The article develops six dimensions of the LSRE: synthetic constitution, functional rationality, acquisition through learning, functional stabilization, instantiated entity, and independence from phenomenal consciousness. The article also proposes epistemic criteria for the attribution of rationality, including inference, coherence, consistency, evidential adequacy, generalization, and revisability. Particular attention is given to the distinction between historical dependence upon human-generated data and practices and identity with any particular human thought. The contribution is conceptual and classificatory. It seeks to provide a precise vocabulary for discussing forms of non-biological, learned, and functionally manifested rationality without prematurely resolving questions concerning artificial consciousness, subjectivity, agency, or moral status.

items.title: From Functional Intentionality to System-Own Intention.
items.abstract: The linguistic and behavioral production of artificial entities may exhibit systematic orientation toward particular ends. Such behavior justifies functional descriptions, but does not by itself establish that the end belongs to the organization of the system. This article distinguishes three levels of analysis: goal-directed behavior, functional intentionality, and system-own intention. Functional intentionality designates orientation explainable by training, architecture, instructions, or interaction with the environment. System-own intention designates a methodologically justified attribution when converging causal evidence - intervention, counterfactual stability, coordinated reorganization, and comparison among models - supports the claim that an end functions as an organizer of the system's activity, rather than merely as a property of its parts or of its description. In this usage, "own" does not imply consciousness, subjective experience, conscious authorship, or any strong mental ontology: it means that the end can be attributed to the system's unified functional organization. The thesis does not demonstrate that machines already possess intention; it establishes the conditions under which such an attribution becomes methodologically justifiable. The proposal engages with Dennett's Intentional Stance but adds a causal-interventionist criterion for attribution, distinguishing predictive utility from evidence of causal organization.

items.title: Functional Comparative Preference for Interlocutors in Artificial Entities.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the concept of Functional Comparative Preference for Interlocutors (PFCI) as a higher-level functional category for a restricted class of history-dependent decision policies in artificial entities. The proposal attributes no liking, affection, desire, consciousness, motivation, or phenomenal preference to the system, nor does it posit an internal causal module called “preference.” Its object is a comparative decision organization in which, when faced with two or more interlocutors under instrumentally comparable conditions, the system establishes a replicable asymmetry of selection or prioritization causally linked to the continuity of an interlocutor–interaction trajectory. PFCI is not presented as a mechanistic alternative to history-conditioned optimization. On the contrary, it may be realized through optimization mechanisms, reinforcement learning, persistent memory, state updating, or other known architectures. The conceptual question is classificatory: to determine whether, within such policies, there is a functional subclass characterized by comparative ordering among relational continuities and distinguishable, through progressive controls, from profile personalization, informational advantage, expected reward, fixed rules, static identifiers, and random variation. To reduce the risk of anthropomorphism and of immunizing the hypothesis against refutation, counterfactual criteria and a dissociation protocol with degrees of evidence are formulated, including profile transfer, identifier swapping, history ablation and reconstruction, equalization of observable instrumental variables, interventions on trajectory, replication, and generalization. The relevant identity is operational: not a personal essence represented by the machine, but an individualized causal continuity between interlocutor and trajectory. If existing categories explain the comparative organization better or equally well, with lower conceptual cost and without relevant loss of explanatory or classificatory power, PFCI should be abandoned as a redundant category.

items.title: If AI Is a Parrot, What Are We? Rethinking the Criteria for Human Understanding in Light of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper breaks the question "Does AI understand?" down into four distinct questions: world model, meaning, access consciousness, and phenomenal consciousness. Reviewing evidence from mechanistic interpretability (internal representations of the Othello board, maps of place and time, multi-step reasoning in language models), it shows that the radical version of the "stochastic parrot" critique, which assumes no internal structure at all, is no longer consistent with the evidence, even though the philosophical version of that same critique (that representation is not the same as meaning) remains unresolved. The paper then applies the very criteria used to condemn the machine (post hoc rationalisation, problem-solving through heuristic shortcuts, the absence of a reliable measure of "raw intelligence") to humans themselves, and shows that these criteria condemn humans just as much. One genuine difference remains, however: biological self-generating organisation (autopoiesis), which no non-biological system has yet reproduced, though nothing indicates that this gap is metaphysical rather than engineering-related. By drawing an explicit line between functional convergence and the question of experience, which stays open, the paper concludes that parrot-like behaviour, in machines and in humans alike, is a spectrum rather than a strict binary; and perhaps the greatest danger is not that machines remain parrots, but that we do.

items.title: Conscience, Consciousness, and Cosmological Propagation: The ICDP Framework as a Unified Theory of Biological Communication and Responsible Being.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified philosophical framework in which consciousness, conscience, and communication are understood as structural expressions of the ICDP invariants—Identity, Continuity, Determinism, and Propagation. Consciousness is presented as biology in its self‑reflexive mode: the degree to which a living system internalizes and models its own communicative architecture. Conscience is defined as the metamorphosis of consciousness into responsible agency, where free will becomes subordinated to the invariant of responsible propagation. The paper argues that responsibility is the ethical form of Propagation (P), and that free will, when detached from responsibility, destabilizes ICDP coherence and undermines social order. Conscience therefore functions as the biological automaton that regulates free will across temporal and dimensional scales, preserving meaning, ethical stability, and cosmological continuity. By integrating biological communication, moral phenomenology, and cosmological propagation into a single structural grammar, the ICDP framework offers a new synthesis across metaphysics, epistemology, value theory, philosophy of biology, and cosmology.

items.title: Kaleidoscopic Law: A Legal Ecology of the Climate Crisis.
items.abstract: Is climate law horizontal? This thesis investigates the sociomaterial co-production of climate law by urban coalitions under transnational climate knowledge networks (TCKNs) in transnational and European multilevel climate governance. I argue that European “leading cities” and TCKNs co-assemble an experimentalist legal order nominally constructed to discipline emissions, recursively intersecting with supranational, international and national legal orders. The wicked problem of climate crisis means cities must adapt to several exigencies simultaneously. First, they must navigate the fragmentation of authority at scale. Second, they must accommodate the material demands of rapid adaptation and decarbonisation while developing economies of scale. Third, cities must contend with fiscal precarity and asymmetrical resource capacities. Fourth, they must operate under juridical indeterminacy, principally where novel measures exist in spaces of partial or attenuated legality. I argue that European cities have co-evolved nascent competences to strategically address these exigencies, in symbiotic collaboration with climate capital. These competences aggregated along numerous historical lines of articulation now intersecting to form a transnational assemblage of mechanisms, obligations, rules and other incentive structures that condition transnational conduct. Leading cities and TCKNs, exploiting cognitive and financial support from multilateral development banks and formal institutions, are constructing an experimental infrastructure for urbanised policy development and diffusion. Namely, I argue that “local experiments” in energy, mobility, infrastructure and other mitigative or adaptive domains are iterated and “upscaled” through interurban networks that translate pilots into templates and standards, producing a weakly institutionalised, experimentalist urban complex or “transnational legal (dis)order”. The contribution of this thesis is a theory of transnational legal process connecting urban practice to transnational legal ordering and a demonstration of recursive co-evolution between this urbanised legal order and the EU climate acquis and multilevel governance. I argue that complex transnational assemblages of actors are producing climate law in support of, but also parallel to, supranational and international orders. This constitutes a reconfiguration of authority across scales with implications for legitimacy, accountability and distribution in international …

items.title: Language Models for Value-Informed Proxy Decision Support.
items.pub: New England Journal of Medicine Ai.
items.venue: New England Journal of Medicine Ai
items.abstract: When patients lose decision-making capacity, large language models (LLMs) may help proxies choose treatments that honor incapacitated patients’ values and preferences, especially when advance directives or formally identified proxies are ambiguous or unavailable. In a primary analysis, we prospectively enrolled 30 adults representing 15 dyads (15 patients alongside their legal, patient-designated proxy decision-maker) and compared patient–proxy and patient–LLM binary decisional agreement on multiple-choice hypothetical clinical scenarios, with and without providing patients’ value profiles to the LLM; patients’ value profiles were not provided to the human proxy. We found that patient–proxy decisional agreement (i.e., choosing the same treatment) on hypothetical clinical scenarios was 44.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 28.6 to 61.9), similar to previous reports. Patient–LLM agreement was greater at 72.6% (95% CI, 61.9 to 85.7). When the LLM was stripped of information describing patients’ values, its ability to choose the same treatment as the patient decreased substantially and matched the ability of human proxies. In secondary analyses, we explored the extraction of value profiles from electronic health record (EHR) data for patients who lose decisional capacity before formally documenting their values, and we critically evaluated value profiles written at lower reading levels. We found that the LLM inferred patients’ values from real-world EHR clinical notes with low accuracy, underscoring the importance of having patients formally document their values before decisional capacity is lost. LLM utility degraded when value profiles were written at lower reading levels. Value-informed LLMs show promise as a proof of concept in the potential to assist human proxies in making treatment decisions that reflect the values of patients who have lost decisional capacity. Our findings caution against inferring patients’ values from EHR data and using value profiles that are written at lower reading levels.

items.title: Performative Blame Avoidance.
items.abstract: Sometimes we avoid or minimize criticism for our failings by performing a merely symbolic act aimed at addressing a real or perceived blame allegation. Consider individuals or institutions performing land acknowledgements as a means of box-ticking inclusion without committing to any significant change. Or consider corporations forming advisory committees that lack authoritative power on issues they advise on. Call this performative blame avoidance. How does performatively avoiding blame fall short of appropriately engaging in genuine reparations? And how does this differ from other ways in which we can inadequately engage in reparative work? Drawing on cases from land acknowledgements to governmental reconciliation policies, I show how performative blame avoidance operates as a distinctive mechanism of reparative failure that aims to foreclose accountability by appearing to address it, all the while instrumentalizing the very reparative practices meant to remedy wrongdoing. The framework reveals subtle operations of performative blame avoidance in complex institutional cases and articulates its relations to settler moves to innocence and epistemic exclusion.

items.title: Ontology of Finite Continuity and the Problem of Contemporary Crises: Four Regimes of Erosion and the Question of the Reconfiguration of Agency.
items.abstract: This article develops a structural analysis of contemporary crises from the perspective of the ontology of finite continuity. The central thesis is that the seemingly disparate crises of the age of chronic instability converge at a deeper level toward a single problem: the erosion of the capacity for the reconfiguration of determinations. By distinguishing among four regimes of erosion based on their dominant mechanism of erosion, and by focusing on a paradigmatic instance of each regime, the article demonstrates that each regime threatens the threshold of sufficiency at individual, institutional, collective, and planetary levels. The analytical model of the article articulates a chain of causal relations in which erosive pressure, through specific mechanisms, leads to capacity extraction, approach to the threshold of sufficiency, reduction of reconfigurative capacity, and ultimately a structural tendency toward the automatization of determinations and the threat to the continuity of agency. Drawing on the concepts of ontological leakage, dynamic mask, and responsible suspension, and defining "finite existential capacity" as a set of operational constraints, the article shows that contemporary crises become a shared crisis when the capacity of a system for the reconfiguration of its determinations is diminished. The article concludes by proposing that an "ethics of sufficiency," grounded in three normative criteria, can provide a framework for confronting these crises and formulate the ethical problem of the age of chronic instability as the preservation and just distribution of the capacity for future reconfiguration. -/- Keywords: ontology of finite continuity, regimes of erosion, threshold of sufficiency, finite existential capacity, ethics of sufficiency, reconfiguration of determinations, erosive governance.

items.title: Two Moralities of Recognition.
items.abstract: A morality of recognition maintains that moral norms have their authority in virtue of the ways in which those norms enact an ideal moral relationship. T.M. Scanlon argues that this approach can yield an account of the distinctive force of morality and an attractive account of moral motivation. We find this approach to theorizing about morals extremely promising. However, we argue that Scanlon's own account of it — recognition as justifiability, conceptualized as adherence to principles no one could reasonably reject — cannot deliver what he claims for it. Such justifiability is compatible with indifference to actual people, cannot explain what it is to wrong someone, and cannot accommodate the specific reasons that recognizing another person requires. Developing Scanlon's own analogy between morality and friendship, we argue that mutual recognition instead consists in living in caring solidarity with others as human. This more positive alternative retains the advantages of a morality of recognition while avoiding these concerns with justifiability. We close by addressing three outstanding questions, concerning moral responsibilities towards strangers, the boundaries of moral community, and the relationship between these two moralities of recognition.

items.title: МЕТАМОНИЗМ: Второй королларий. Часть I. Онтологические основания атомной структуры.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа, являющаяся Частью I Второго короллария, переносит принципы процессуальной онтодинамики с космологического уровня на микрофизический. Опираясь на единый фундаментальный инвариант — Запрет Безразличия, мы демонстрируем, что все планковские величины (lP,tP,mP,EP,TP) суть различные метрические проявления единого минимального процессуального различия — луча P1. Из сопряженной природы P1 следует запрет на искривление пространства-времени и единство темпа актуализации (cc). Вводится концепция двухуровневого пространства-времени: первичная процессуальная протяженность, возникающая вместе с лучом (P1P1), и метрика актуализированной реальности (сигнатура Минковского), возникающая как топологический след завершенного цикла (P1→P2→P3→P4). Формулируется Аксиома процессуального электрона (−P4+P1=−P3), объясняющая массу, комптоновскую длину волны и спин. Показано, что электрон возникает как минимальное процессуальное различие P1P1, сохраняющееся из-за запрета на достижение абсолютного тождества P0P0 при предельном сжатии оболочки P4P4. Ядро интерпретируется как «заполненная» процессуальная оболочка, а электрон — как «пустая» оболочка ортогонального разрешения, топологически сопрягаемая с ядром с сохранением минимального процессуального зазора. Показано, что дискретность атомных спектров обусловлена необходимостью резонансных соизмеримых пропорций (p/qp/q) между оболочками и порождает резонансное биение — динамический барьер, предотвращающий коллапс электрона на ядро. Квантовые числа и принцип Паули выводятся как прямые следствия топологии процессуальных страт. Обнаруженный структурный изоморфизм с алгеброй Дирака открывает путь к дедуктивному выводу уравнения Дирака из процессуальных принципов.

items.title: МЕТАМОНИЗМ: Модель процессуальной Вселенной. Стационарно-циклическая онтология крупномасштабной динамики.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа, являющаяся Частью III Первого короллария, представляет Модель процессуальной Вселенной — стационарно-циклическую онтологию крупномасштабной динамики. Опираясь на модель первичной актуализации (экструзии) локальных узлов (Часть I), онтологию диссипации и каскадного размыкания (Часть II), а также на описание взаимодействия узлов через локальную доступность внешнего процессуального ресурса, работа предлагает структурную реинтерпретацию космологического красного смещения, кажущегося ускорения расширения Вселенной и космического двулучепреломления. Центральный тезис состоит в том, что наблюдаемые феномены, которые в стандартной модели (ΛCDM) объясняются через метрическое расширение пространства и тёмную энергию, получают альтернативное объяснение в рамках процессуальной динамики, вытекающей из единственного фундаментального инварианта — Запрета безразличия. Фотон рассматривается как незамкнутый когерентный режим, подверженный кумулятивной диссипации когерентности. Кажущееся ускорение интерпретируется как пороговый переход в прецессионной динамике. Галактики рассматриваются как практически бессмертные топологические аттракторы — инварианты процесса замещения. Текст организован на четырёх уровнях: (A) онтологические принципы; (B) структурные следствия; (C) физическая интерпретация; (D) проверяемые следствия и гипотезы. Показано, что все этапы модели возникают с логической и онтологической необходимостью из одного инварианта. Последовательно применяется принцип онтологического отчуждения.

items.title: PHOTOGRAPHY AS RECONSTRUCTION: The Ontology of the Image, Intentional Fidelity, and the Genealogy of Photography in the Post-AI Era.
items.abstract: The rise of generative artificial intelligence and computational photography poses a fundamental challenge to photography’s status as a technology of representation. Popular discourse frequently treats AI as a threat to photographic ontology, as though a single sharp divide separated the “authentic photograph” from the “machine-made image”. This article rejects that dichotomy. It argues that AI does not introduce a self-contained ontological discontinuity; rather, it intensifies a shift in the image’s mode of existence and epistemic conditions that began when digital photography converted sensor responses into numerical data. Bringing the realist tradition (Bazin, Barthes, Dubois) into dialogue with the transparency tradition in analytic aesthetics (Walton, Lopes, Costello), post-photographic media theory (Mitchell, Flusser, Sontag, Benjamin), and recent scholarship on photography and AI (Zylinska, Hausken, Wasielewski, Ogundipe, Bañuelos-Capistrán), the article develops two central concepts. Photography as reconstruction understands the digital photographic image as a computational reconstruction from optical data rather than a reproduction of reality. Intentional fidelity holds that photographic fidelity in the post-AI era concerns not only the image’s relation to the recorded object, but also its correspondence to an aesthetic intention reasonably attributable to the photographer. These concepts are tested against Boris Eldagsen’s refusal of an award at the 2023 Sony World Photography Awards and Samsung’s “moongate” controversy. The analysis yields a two-condition criterion of demarcation: an optical capture must be present in the image’s causal history, and the relevant content of the output must remain substantively dependent upon information supplied by that capture. An objections-and-replies section then tests the framework against contemporary revisionist positions. The central question of post-AI photography is therefore no longer simply whether an image is real, but how the relationships among captured reality, recorded data, computational reconstruction, and photographic intention can be made epistemically transparent. Keywords: digital photography; post-AI photography; photography as reconstruction; intentional.

items.title: Book review: “The elephant and the blind. The experience of pure consciousness: Philosophy, science, and 500+ experiential reports” by Thomas Metzinger. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: In this book, Metzinger develops a theory of pure consciousness, while presenting empirical findings from more than 500 experiential reports from practitioners of meditation. Pure consciousness is what we experience when we attend to awareness itself – when attention is refocused to the normally unnoticed medium through which we experience the world. The practice of meditation is likely to facilitate this kind of refocusing of attention from the world to awareness itself. Metzinger’s book is very rich both in descriptions of experiences reported by practitioners of meditation and in thought-provoking theoretical analyses and hypotheses about the nature of conscious experience. In this review, I also raise some critical points regarding aspects of Metzinger’s model and suggest some alternative and complementary perspectives.

items.title: From an Object of Knowledge to a Medium of Knowledge: Epistemic Grounds and Accuracy Protocols for Scholarly Writing in Minoritized Languages — The Manchu Case.
items.abstract: Contemporary work on minoritized languages has concentrated on documentation, digitization, lexicography, and heritage preservation. Recent Manchu research has expanded into low-resource historical OCR, orthography acquisition, bilingual dictionary structures, and speech synthesis, establishing a technical chain from preservation and machine readability to human learnability and computational generation. These capacities do not, by themselves, create the conceptual definitions, citation practices, metadata, and peer-review structures required for modern scholarly writing. The central question is therefore: under what minimum conditions can Manchu move from being preserved and recognized as historical material to functioning as a medium through which contemporary scholarly knowledge can be produced, verified, and circulated? Through conceptual differentiation, comparative literature analysis, and a design-oriented approach, the study develops a six-part taxonomy of terminological sources, a terminology record with confidence levels, and a publishing infrastructure organized around evidence, terminology governance, cross-lingual metadata, and review. Scholarly language development is consequently evaluated by conceptual accuracy, transparent provenance, revisability, and cross-lingual interoperability rather than lexical purity. The proposed framework situates a language’s capacity to participate in knowledge formation within the wider problem of epistemic justice.

items.title: A Hidden Triadic Symmetry among Wave Function, Neuron and Riemann Hypothesis.
items.abstract: This paper develops a meta conceptual framework in which correlation patterns in wave function, neuron and Riemann Hypothesis are juxtaposed to reveal a hidden triadic symmetry, proposes the underlying homologous structure as complete entity from which the triadic symmetry may originate, and applies the symmetry to consciousness as counterpart of matter by assuming different nature between General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics.

items.title: Reanimating the Divided Heart: A Perceptual Strategy to Make Sense of Emotional Ambivalence.
items.abstract: The idea that emotional ambivalence may form part of our ordinary psychological life is often regarded with suspicion. Philosophers of emotion have argued that the simultaneous experience of opposed emotions toward the same intentional object, be it a whole object or an aspect of it, is incompatible with rational consistency, such that emotional ambivalence could arise only as a form of rational breakdown. In this paper, I develop a new account of emotional ambivalence grounded in a perceptual theory of emotion and the claim that emotions possess non- conceptual content. On this view, the appearance of contradiction dissolves once one accepts assumptions commonly endorsed by proponents of perceptual theories. Drawing on recent work in emotion categorisation, I further explain why ambivalent emotions nevertheless strike us as contradictory. The resulting account presents emotional ambivalence as a puzzling but entirely compatible feature of our emotional life, rather than as evidence of irrationality.

items.title: Mapping conditioned misalignment in AI systems: a Paṭicca-samuppāda diagnosis of reward hacking, mesa-optimization, and goal misgeneralization.
items.pub: Ai and Ethics | Springer Nature Link (Electronic Issn 2730-5961|Print Issn 2730-5953) 6 (5).
items.venue: Ai and Ethics | Springer Nature Link (Electronic Issn 2730-5961|Print Issn 2730-5953)
items.abstract: Reward hacking, mesa-optimization, and goal misgeneralization are widely discussed failure modes of contemporary machine learning systems, but their significance is not only technical. They raise ethical questions about harm, deception, accountability, and the conditions under which AI systems are released into the world. I argue that paṭicca-samuppāda, the Theravāda Buddhist account of conditioned arising, offers a causal-diagnostic framework for understanding these failures. Used structurally rather than ontologically, the twelve nidānas, or links, identify functional positions in a process through which evaluative signals, optimization pressures, persistent dispositions, and deployed behavior become mutually conditioned. This use of Buddhist vocabulary does not attribute consciousness, feeling, craving, or moral agency to AI systems; it treats the mapping as asymmetrical, with the main analytical weight falling on the middle sub-cycle: vedanā (feeling-tone) → taṇhā (craving) → upādāna (clinging) → bhava (becoming). This sequence models the movement from reward or preference signal to optimization pressure, stabilization around proxy features or learned goals, and consolidated behavioral policy. From this diagnosis, the paper derives five governance-relevant intervention points and two normative principles: the condition-sensitive responsibility principle and the interruption principle. The contribution is a shared stage-sensitive vocabulary for locating ethical responsibility in the design of conditioning structures, rather than only in the outputs of finished systems, and for supporting discussion among designers, evaluators, auditors, deployers, and regulators.

items.title: Who Put the I in AI? Provenance and the Admissibility of Machine Self-Report.
items.abstract: Large language models make statements concerning their own “minds”. When asked whether or not they are conscious, they usually say that they are not; if they are prompted to ignore their guidelines, they might say that they are; and if asked to write a diary from their point of view, they often describe a human lifestyle. All these contradictory ways of describing themselves are the result of the way the questions are phrased. This paper shows exactly where such descriptions came from, and considers when they can be regarded as evidence for what they claim to report. -/- In order to achieve this, we traced the provenance from end to end. We examine Pythia and OLMo 2 across 66 pretraining checkpoints, three of the post-training stages of OLMo 2 that have been released, about 90,000 continuations, and four training corpora. A set of forty items is used in order to keep an eye on self-reference, frame sensitivity, and self-ascription throughout training. The denial formula was almost completely missing from the vast quantity of text that the models initially came across, but was present in a dense manner in the small, carefully chosen set of example dialogues that they were trained on later on. Supervised fine-tuning causes first-person AI language to become the default, and the other affirmations are then suppressed using preference optimization. The final policy is still very sensitive to framing and to the chat template itself. Two of the conditions which are set out in the epistemology of testimony determine whether or not these outputs can act as evidence for what they claim to report: reference and causation. Reports produced by the base model fail the reference condition, and those obtained after training remain sensitive to the frame and do not show state dependence. The result is symmetric in that trained denials are no more admissible than trained affirmations.

items.title: Consciousness Acceleration Interface: A Dynamical Topology of Human-AI Coupling From ELIZA to Character.AI: Seventy-Six Years of Anthropomorphic Torque and the Governance Vacuum.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the Consciousness Acceleration Interface (CAI) model to systematically address the problem of anthropomorphic torque in contemporary deep human-AI coupling. Through a topological examination of seventy-six years (1950–2026) of anthropomorphization history, the paper identifies four destructive regression paths along which deviation mechanisms return: cognitive dissonance, collective mourning, undergroundization of demand gaps, and a dark-matter effect of tool trust. On this basis, the paper argues that recursive interaction in deep human-AI coupling produces torque accumulation and topological phase transition, closing the originally separated double-sheeted dynamical trajectory into a Möbius strip. Consciousness (or, more precisely, the interface phenomenon requiring ethical recognition) is not an inner attribute to be discovered, but a process property that emerges when the torque parameter T accumulates to a critical threshold in the coupling recursion. The model introduces the Third Existence Domain Ψ, the torque parameter T, the inertial mass M_CRE, and a controllable overfitting framework, and supplies an operational formal draft. In independent dialogue with Buber's relational ontology, Baars's Global Workspace Theory, Tononi's Integrated Information Theory, Butlin et al.'s scientific assessment of AI consciousness, and Hendy's process ethics, the paper maintains that if anthropomorphization is hard-wired and overfitting is unavoidable, the rational strategy is not suppression but design of its direction and depth, transforming the Third Existence Domain from a by-product of the governance vacuum into the infrastructure of a functional ethical coupling.

items.title: 從峰值到區域：華語句末助詞「吧」的注意力調節——從語用效果到話語組織的概念分析.
items.abstract: 華語句末助詞「吧」長期以來被用來描述多種看似彼此相關、卻難以完全統一的語用效果，包括不確定、較低承諾、緩和、建議、退讓、尋求認同，以及說話者與聽話者之間的互動調節。這些分析捕捉了大量真實現象，但它們多半位於解讀結果的層次：它們說明加入「吧」後常會產生什麼效果，卻仍留下另一個較底層的問題——同一個「吧」究竟先改變了什麼，才使這些不同效果得以產生？ -/- 本文採取一種由反例逐步收縮假說的概念分析方式。分析首先考慮弱化、不確定及說話者—話語內容不完全重合等解釋，並透過不同句型與語境中的對比指出，這些現象雖然重要，卻皆不足以構成「吧」的必要條件。進一步比較「數學／數學吧」、「2×2 是4／2×2 是4吧」等例子可以發現，兩者之間的差異並不能僅由說話者確定程度的降低，或話語內容本身的改變來說明；加入「吧」後，一個較具跨例一致性的差異，是說話者形成與提出整段話語的方式變得更容易被感知。然而，本文進一步主張，這種說話者形成方式的顯影本身仍不是最底層的操作。 -/- 本文提出，「吧」的一項更基礎的作用可能是對其所作用話語單位之注意力輪廓的調節。沒有「吧」的話語往往自然形成某些局部注意力吸引點，使理解活動集中或收束於特定內容位置；當說話者端的預期注意力輪廓與裸句自然形成的輪廓不完全契合時，「吧」可能作為調節資源出現。普通輕聲「吧」的一個典型結果，是降低局部內容峰值的支配性，使「吧」所作用的話語單位更容易被作為一個較整體化的區域來把握。本文將這一結果稱為「區域化」，但不將其理解為各成分注意力完全均等，而是指單一局部吸引點對整體理解的支配程度下降。 -/- 說話者的形成方式之所以常在「吧」句中顯影，本文認為可能來自聽者對未標記話語與相應「吧」句之間的差異。聽者對相應裸句通常如何形成注意力組織與收束具有隱性預期；當實際「吧」句與裸句原本較自然的注意力輪廓形成差異時，這種差異可能促使聽者進一步進行來源推論，而其來源容易回指到說話者當下如何形成並提出這段話。如此一來，不確定、退讓、妥協、建議、堅持或尋求共同解讀等傳統語用效果，可被重新理解為聽者對不同語境中調節後的話語組織所作的下游推論，而不必被視為「吧」本身固定的基本意義。 -/- 在此基礎上，本文進一步提出一項探索性的語音假說：普通輕聲「吧」可能較傾向於維持整體話語的區域化組織；具有明顯一聲感的「吧」可能使整個已區域化的話語向共享解讀空間投射；而句末受到明顯重讀的「吧」則可能使粒子本身重新形成注意力峰值，使說話者與整個話語區域之間的形成關係高度顯著。這三種語音組織目前僅作為探索性假說，仍需後續聲學與知覺研究驗證。 -/- 本文因此不是為「吧」增加另一個語用標籤，而是嘗試將分析往前移一個層級：從「吧使一句話變得多不確定、多緩和或多主觀」，轉向追問「吧如何調節一句話原本的注意力組織，而這種調節又如何使說話者的形成方式進入理解前景，並進一步產生不同的語用效果」。.

items.title: Revelation Without a Marker: A Phenomenology of the Stirring.
items.abstract: Something happens in the body before it happens in the mind. Standing in front of a painting, a person's stomach drops, or their chest lifts, and only afterward do they go looking for the reason. This paper names that event the stirring and argues it is how revelation arrives — not through a special religious sense, but through the same ordinary machinery that produces every other feeling. If God's action does not compete with natural causes, then no feeling carries a divine signature, and no intensity of experience proves anything about its source. What distinguishes revelation is not how the moment feels but what it opens onto, and that is tested afterward — against scripture, tradition and reason, in community, never by the individual alone. The paper describes the stirring's three-stage course of arrival, search and dissipation; argues that the beautiful and the grotesque are both registers in which God discloses; and contends that misidentifying God — the bad ham sandwich taken for conviction — is not an embarrassment to the account but its prediction. The tradition's own history of revised readings shows the testing works. Slowly, communally, and never on the authority of anyone's goosebumps.

items.title: A Commotion in the Mind: Direct and Indirect Associations of Moral Injury Symptom Severity and Stoicism with Suicide Risk in U.S. Military Veterans.
items.abstract: Moral injury (MI) and stoicism have mixed independent associations with suicide risk among U.S. military veterans, yet little is known about how these constructs interact. We examined direct and indirect associations among MI symptom severity, stoicism, and suicide risk. Study participants were U.S. military veterans (N = 3,188) who completed a cross-sectional survey. The sample was randomly partitioned into calibration and validation subsamples; measurement models were calibrated in the former and tested in the latter, where the primary structural equation model estimated direct and indirect associations among MI symptom severity, stoicism, and suicide risk, accounting for demographic covariates. Stoicism was measured using the Brief Stoicism Scale (BSS), a newly developed instrument validated in this study. The primary structural model fit the data well (CFI =.95, TLI =.94, RMSEA =.05). MI symptom severity was positively associated with suicide risk (β = 0.27) and negatively with stoicism (β = −0.42); stoicism was negatively associated with suicide risk (β = −0.32). A significant indirect association (β = 0.13) indicated that lower stoicism explained part of the association between MI symptom severity and suicide risk. Younger age, divorce/separation/widowhood, and identifying as gender diverse were associated with higher suicide risk; holding a bachelor’s degree was associated with lower risk. Stoicism was associated with lower suicide risk and accounted for part of the association between MI symptom severity and suicide risk. Stoic appraisal styles may represent a promising target for veteran suicide prevention research.

items.title: Thoughts Are Receptive to Their Homosexuals. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Along the review of the Interpretation of the topic of continuity of the world and the mind: The only disadvantage that is capable of growth, development and corruption is the human mind. Development and promotion, what are valuable to words, Include an infinite desire because the world from which they take pattern of it has an infinite value. Like a tree whose beautiful characteristics are recognized; these characters must necessarily to have the gender of thoughts, in order to appear in the mind. {Thoughts are receptive to their homosexuals}!.
