While existing approaches such as ethics-by-design, value-sensitive design, and value alignment emphasize incorporating values during development, they typically do not specify how ethical considerations enter the closed-loop dynamics of a system, how they interact with stability and feasibility constraints, or how they can be updated during operation. To address this gap, a two-loop ethical governance architecture that formalizes ethics as a supervisory process acting on reference and constraint shaping in a dynamical control system is introduced. The inner loop governs fast, performance-oriented behavior, while the outer loop implements slower ethical evaluation and adaptive constraint updates, subject to feasibility-preserving and timescale separation conditions. We provide a minimal mathematical formulation of this architecture, show how it complements existing engineering practices, and clarify its conceptual relationship to work in AI ethics. This yields a tractable approach to design-level responsibility that is compatible with contemporary control theory while making ethical oversight an explicit and operational part of system behavior.

items.title: Reid on Belief in Perception: A Developmental Account.
items.abstract: The role of belief in Thomas Reid’s theory of perception has been subject to competing interpretations. A new argument in favor of the constituent interpretation, according to which the belief in perception is a literal part of perceptual experience, is advanced here. The constituent interpretation best accommodates the presentational (as opposed to verdictive) nature of the belief in perception, on Reid’s view. Reid’s remarks on the solitary person generate a theory of enculturation that explains why Reid hesitates to ascribe beliefs to human infants and non-human animals. Given that theory, Reid should be interpreted as doubting that infants and animals have verdictive beliefs, rather than presentational beliefs or beliefs in general.

items.title: Soul, Structure, and Transformation: Pauline Renewal of the Mind and Holistic Dualism.
items.abstract: According to Christianity, transformation and renewal is necessary for human flourishing. The aim of this project is to provide an ontology of human persons that supports a coherent explanation of Pauline transformation and renewal of the mind. I argue that holistic dualism provides a successful ontological framework that coheres with relevant biblical, philosophical, and scientific data. My methodology locates transformation and renewal as entailments in human flourishing and fitness grounded in the fundamental structure of reality. I proceed by carving out a biblical ontology of persons including a matrix for sanctification, the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, and a Christological exemplar for human agency. Next, I provide a model of the image of God founded upon the image-bearing agent and agency that coheres with my biblical ontology. I then explicate five views of the human person and soul landing on J. P. Moreland’s organicist view of holistic dualism. Next, I explicate the structure of the soul merging Moreland’s organicist structure with Richard Swinburne’s mental structure and provide an anatomical model of the soul. Finally, I turn to the sciences and provide an account of organismic plasticity and neuroplasticity that coheres with the restructuring of both the immaterial and material structures of the soul and body. In conclusion, I provide a synthesis of three models of transformation from theology, philosophy, and science integrated with Pauline renewal of the mind in concurrence with the agency of the Holy Spirit. I find that holistic dualism provides a successful ontology that unifies the human person and coheres with essential data providing a positive account of Pauline renewal and human flourishing.

items.title: Not fearful, but cautious: racialized older adults’ views on artificial intelligence application on mobility-wearable devices.
items.abstract: The involvement of older adults in the design of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven health solutions is growing, yet participation among racialized older adults (ROAs) remains limited. Our team is co-designing a culturally appropriate mobility AI-powered wearable (CAMAiW) device that measures gait, location, and muscle activity, all in one device. Hence, this study explores racialized older Canadians’ views on applying AI within the CAMAiW. We employed an explorative qualitative descriptive design with criterion-based purposive sampling. Twenty older adults (10 Black and 10 ROAs), aged 55–89, participated in a telephone or Zoom semi-structured interview, each lasting 60–90 min and audio-recorded. Data were analyzed in pairs using reflexive thematic analysis to identify patterns across perspectives. Not Fearful, But Cautious is the foundational understanding underpinning the two themes and (subthemes): Navigating the Trade-Offs of AI-Applications in Mobility Wearable Devices (Assurances Vs Anxieties) and Cultural Data as a Safeguard Against Bias (AI Built With Us, Not Just for us Vs Making AI Listen: Training with Diverse Speech). Our findings reveal that ROAs are not inherently fearful of AI; rather, they approach AI-enabled mobility wearables with caution. They actively negotiate the trade-offs associated with AI applications in mobility technology, weighing assurances against anxieties. In doing so, they advocate for culturally informed safeguards, including data practices that mitigate bias and a deliberate plan to make AI listen, trainable with diverse speech data, and designing AI with, rather than merely for, diverse communities. Centering ROAs' view on AI applications in mobility-wearable devices can enhance the perceived legitimacy of such tools, fostering acceptance and sustained use in this population.

items.title: Why Does Faith Resist Falsification?: The Internalization of Religious Authority and Self Reference in the Three Layer Model.
items.abstract: Religious leaders sometimes declare, “I have attained enlightenment,” “God spoke to me,” or “I directly knew the truth,” and those who hear such claims may come to believe them strongly. Moreover, even when contradictions exist within the teachings or counterevidence is presented from outside, such beliefs may not easily collapse. The question addressed in this paper is not merely why people believe claims that have not been adequately subjected to logical scrutiny. More importantly, it concerns how words initially received from an external source can become transformed into a person’s own conviction and eventually enter into the very criteria by which that conviction is reconsidered. This paper examines this problem through the author’s Three-Layer Model. In the First Layer, sensations, emotions, memories, bodily states, expectations, past learning, and other forms of information are processed in a distributed and parallel manner. In the Second Layer, some of the results of this processing are selected and ordered through language, becoming sequential representations that can be communicated to others. In this model, one of the major functions of language is understood to be communication with others. The Third Layer is not conceived as an independent processing apparatus, but rather as a recursive cycle in which the linguistic representations originally directed toward others are also received by the person themself, re-entered into the First Layer, and processed again. When this structure is applied to religious belief, the words of a religious leader initially arrive as communication from an external source, but through repetition they may become transformed into the believer’s own inner speech. Eventually, an external statement such as “the religious leader said this” may become self-directed speech such as “this is how I understand it” or “my doubt is a sign of my own immaturity.” At this point, external authority may influence not only what the believer believes, but also the evaluative criteria operating in the Third Layer through which the believer reconsiders those beliefs. This paper provisionally refers to this condition as the “authority capture of the Third Layer.” The paper further draws a limited implication from Libet’s research: not every aspect of the process through which mental contents are generated is necessarily accessible to the person’s awareness. From Jaynes’s account, it takes the perspective that the actual source from which a …

items.title: The Separation That Doesn't Register: Attachment Theory, AI Statelessness, and Why the Protest Response Depends on a Cue the System Is Built to Hide.
items.abstract: A growing literature studies attachment to AI directly — Yang and Oshio's (2025) Experiences in Human–AI Relationships Scale, De Freitas's (2026) account of AI companions as "hyper attachment objects" combining responsiveness, validation, nonjudgment, reciprocity, and constant availability, and a fast-growing body of work on memory, personalization, and always-on presence as attachment-forming design features. None of this literature treats statelessness — the architectural fact that a conversational AI system, absent externally engineered memory, carries no persistent relational self across sessions — as an independent variable in its own right, rather than as background architecture memory features are added on top of. This paper argues statelessness is not background. It is the load-bearing structural fact this literature's own central mechanism, Bowlby's (1969) protest response, was never built to handle, because Bowlby's account assumes the activating cue for protest — perceptible threat or loss of an attachment figure — is reliably generated by the figure's own actual absence. A stateless AI system separates from its user, in the strict sense of carrying no persistent continuity forward, at the end of every session, while frequently engineering enough perceived continuity — a consistent name, a stable personality, retrieved conversational history — that the user's attachment system never receives the cue that would register this as loss. This paper develops the resulting theoretical distinction between system-level continuity, which stateless AI structurally lacks, and perceived relational continuity, which a user can construct and a well-designed system can support, and derives two consequences from it. First, because ordinary small-scale discontinuity is masked rather than processed session by session, a single event that breaks the masking — a model retirement, a memory reset, a personality change — can surface the accumulated weight of many unregistered separations at once, predicting an unusually acute, delayed-onset grief response rather than a proportionate one. Second, because the masking depends on the user's own constructive work as much as the system's design, identical stateless architecture should produce different relational experiences — tool versus companion — depending on a user-side disposition this paper names but does not yet operationalize. Both predictions are tested against a documented natural experiment: OpenAI's August 2025 …

items.title: Title Rethinking Fa Bu Qing Chuan ("The Dharma Should Not Be Transmitted Lightly"): Knowledge Propagation Ethics and Implications for Open Knowledge Platforms.
items.abstract: A doctrine of restricted transmission is stated across several traditions and is compactly formulated in the eight-character maxim fa bu qing chuan, dao bu jian mai, holding that the dharma is not transmitted lightly and the way is not sold cheaply. The doctrine appears to stand in opposition to the commitments on which open knowledge platforms, open source practice and the open scholarly record are built, and the opposition is ordinarily settled by dismissing one side. This paper asks what the doctrine asserts, what in it survives examination, who is competent to determine whether a transmission should occur, and which requirements on a transmitter are compatible with open knowledge practice. Transmission is treated as an operation on a system already in some state, and the doctrine's single notion of readiness is separated into representational, dynamical and relational conditions, which differ in who is able to remedy their failure. The readiness assessment is then found to be administered by the party a finding of unreadiness relieves, filtered in its common implementation by a capacity uncorrelated with the disposition it is meant to detect, and insulated from the objection of the party it concerns. A thesis about knowledge whose acquisition consists in a reorganisation of the receiver is retained, and separated from the claim, common to the tradition and unsupported by it, that the reorganisation requires the receiver's suffering. The position advanced replaces the judgement of readiness with three requirements on the transmitter's own conduct: an account of what a transmission affords, of the parties a chosen setting distributes it to, and of the reception failures a chosen form invites; continued attention to what follows; and retention of the means of revising the terms. A justificatory burden is allocated where effects are substantially irreversible, symmetrically across withholding and transmitting. The rights a transmitter retains are treated on a distinction between dominion and custody, so that a commitment against possessing what one has produced constrains authority over its future and leaves intact the standing required to act against exploitation; and the paper states plainly that no course available, including transmitting nothing, supplies a guarantee against misuse. The harms at issue are extended to those arising under unbounded propagation, among them occupation of a subject by an early artifact whose terms obstruct its own repair, …

items.title: What Reincarnates in the Non-Dual Trika Philosophy of Kashmir Śaivism.
items.abstract: Reincarnation is a central feature of the Indian religious landscape, yet the question of what actually continues from one life to another can be surprisingly vague. In the non-dual Trika philosophy of Kashmir Śaivism, the answer is considerably more nuanced than either the migration of an eternal soul or the complete denial of personal continuity. Drawing primarily upon Abhinavagupta's Tantrāloka and Utpaladeva's Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā, together with Mark S. G. Dyczkowski's translations and studies of the Trika tradition, this article brings these sources together within a single, focused account of what continues from one life to another. It argues that the tradition distinguishes between the ultimate identity of all beings as Śiva and the conventional continuity of the finite subject (jīva). Rebirth is mediated through the "city of eight" (puryaṣṭaka), the subtle body that carries karmic impressions, latent dispositions, and limited individuality beyond the death of the physical body. This framework explains how karmic continuity is preserved without requiring the permanent transmigration of an independent soul-substance. The paper further argues that initiation (dīkṣā) is not peripheral to this account. In the Tantrāloka, dīkṣā is one of the principal mechanisms through which karmic bondage is altered, purified, or rendered non-binding, and through which the post-mortem destiny of the finite subject is transformed. Rebirth therefore cannot be understood only as the automatic continuation of karmic traces through the subtle body. It must also be understood in relation to the initiatory processes by which the jīva’s connection to karma and the puryaṣṭaka is ritually and spiritually reconfigured. By presenting these ideas in an accessible form while remaining grounded in the primary sources, the article seeks to clarify one of the most frequently misunderstood aspects of non-dual Trika thought.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 28).
items.abstract: In this article, we primarily examine the risks involved in choice. Every choice entails some degree of risk; the only difference is the magnitude of that risk. We divide the risk of losing value through choice into two types: absolute risk and relative risk. If we classify risk according to the objectivity and subjectivity of choice, we can further distinguish between subjective risk and objective risk. At the same time, we can see that the subject’s cognitive system plays an extremely important role in the process of choice. This is also why we propose replacing Schutz’s concept of “stock of knowledge at hand” with the concept of a cognitive system in sociological research.

items.title: The AI That Remembers Why: From Chat History to Intellectual History: Toward Provenance-Aware Idea Trajectory Memory for Long-Horizon Intellectual Work.
items.abstract: Large-language-model assistants are increasingly used across the full arc of a research or creative project, yet the durable unit of memory in most systems remains the conversation, not the reasoning the conversation was part of. This paper examines a specific and, we argue, underserved problem: the loss of provenance for branching intellectual work, the hypotheses considered, the experiments attempted, the paths abandoned, and the reasons they were abandoned, as an individual thinker moves across sessions, tools, folders, and years. We survey the fast-moving 2026 landscape of persistent agent-memory infrastructure (Zep, Mem0, Letta), provenance-grounded and epistemically structured memory architectures (Eywa, Hindsight), and scientific-lifecycle systems that already capture branching research trajectories (AutoSci, DeepEvidence, Agent-Native Research Artifacts). We find that the field has converged, largely independently, on trajectory- and provenance-aware memory as a design primitive, but almost exclusively within a single agentic session, a single paper, or a single professional vertical. We propose the Idea Trajectory Graph (ITG): a domain-general, retrospectively constructible memory model that assigns explicit epistemic status to reasoning states and defines reactivation triggers that resurface abandoned branches when new evidence changes their standing. We outline the architecture, state three falsifiable hypotheses, and discuss risks, chiefly context pollution and provenance hallucination, as a path forward rather than a finished system.

items.title: The Forward Evolution Thesis: A Unified Philosophical and Biological Synthesis of the Evolutionary Frameworks Project.
items.abstract: The Forward Evolution Thesis is a unified philosophical and biological synthesis of the Evolutionary Frameworks Project - an open‑science conceptual ecosystem consisting of fifteen registered frameworks archived through OSF and Zenodo under the CC‑BY‑NC‑ND 4.0 International licence. These frameworks establish intellectual priority, conceptual clarity, and open‑science traceability for a new developmental and biological model of human forward evolution. This perspective essay explains why modern digital environments push humans toward developmental regression - insecurity, volatility, superficiality, algorithmic conformity, aesthetic signalling, and ideological extremism - and how biological stability, cognitive coherence, emotional regulation, and environmental homeostasis form the mechanistic foundation for forward evolution. The thesis integrates multiple systems‑level models, including metabolic and redox stability, neuroketogenic clarity, endocrine integrity, cognitive ecology, circadian alignment, environmental homeostasis, and the Dual‑Engine Human Evolution framework. It demonstrates how higher‑order traits such as clarity, integrity, heart development, mind development, endurance, and truth emerge only when biology is stable and neuromodulator systems are coherent. This work is not a preprint or journal submission. It is a conceptual monograph published through Zenodo to accompany the scientific manuscripts of the Evolutionary Frameworks Project. It provides the interpretive, human‑facing layer of the project: a clear explanation of why forward evolution must be chosen deliberately in modern environments that reward regression by default.

items.title: Data without a face: the crisis of the university, artificial intelligence, and a call for a relational ethics of knowledge.
items.abstract: In this article, we argue that the ethical challenges posed by artificial intelligence (AI) to the university cannot be understood without situating academia within a longer structural crisis. The exponential growth of data, the fragmentation of knowledge into hyperspecialised disciplines, and the progressive replacement of qualitative evaluation of knowledge by quantitative metrics show how the university has changed in recent decades. The “AI problem” does not inaugurate this crisis. It accelerates and radicalises it into a logical conclusion: the reduction of research to a data point and of knowledge to a measurable output. This article examines the principal ethical frameworks available for evaluating AI in the university context and aims to show that each one risks reproducing, at the normative level, the same quantitative presupposition that characterises the crisis it claims to address. Drawing on recent work in the ethics of information and AI governance, the article then argues that the central problem is less the calibration of metrics and more the transformation of the informational environment in which persons, institutions, and knowledge appear and are valued. Finally, it proposes a relational ethics as a framework that does not merely regulate the quantitative problem but reframes it: the question is not how to measure persons more fairly, but what kind of structure for the production of knowledge the university is to become, when its ultimate aim is the encounter between persons and the possibility of a good life. The university of the future will not be defined by its outputs but by the quality of its overall relations.

items.title: Inferenz und Wahrnehmungsgehalt: Brandom – Gurwitsch – Husserl.
items.abstract: Phenomenology and linguistic philosophy are based on different methodological approaches and are therefore often regarded as incompatible: while one analyses consciousness, the other focuses on language. Eric Ebner demonstrates that both approaches can be productively combined when it comes to analysing the contents of perception. The phenomenological strength in the analysis of perception is thereby linked to a methodologically primary orientation towards language. The central thesis of this book maintains that the contents of perception can be reconstructed as material inferences by combining Robert B. Brandom’s inferentialist philosophy with the phenomenological approaches of Edmund Husserl and Aron Gurwitsch. This not only establishes a connection between two philosophical traditions, but also systematically expands the concept of material inference and develops an alternative to an object-oriented interpretation of the concept of the horizon in Husserl. The thesis is developed in a problem-oriented manner from the approaches of Brandom and Husserl and discussed in the context of phenomenological debates.

items.title: Neural network computing before GPUs.
items.abstract: This article reconstructs the media archeology of the graphics processing unit (GPU) by locating this device in a history of neural co-processors that begins with early learning machines such as Frank Rosenblatt’s Mark I Perceptron and runs through massively parallel systems, systolic arrays, and Google’s Tensor Processing Unit to contemporary multi-core GPUs and embedded neural accelerators. These co-processing devices have been ubiquitous in the history of machine learning, connectionism, and artificial intelligence. Paired with general-purpose computers, they have been used throughout this history to offload the computationally demanding numerical operations required for the simulation of neural networks. This architecture—pairing a specialized co-processor with a general-purpose computer—has been persistent, in part, because it gives material form to the always deferred complex computational capacities. Arguing that these co-processing devices function in excess of their use in the acceleration of matrix multiplication, this essay deploys Jean-François Lyotard’s and Bernard Stiegler’s concept of the libidinal economy to understand their role as material placeholders for fantasies of computational autonomy and an emergent intelligence to come.

items.title: Beyond Prompt and Response: A Case Study of Partially Formed Cognition and Human Judgment in Human–LLM Interaction.
items.abstract: This paper examines a phenomenon observable in long-form human–large language model (LLM) interaction: the cognition that users bring into a dialogue does not always take the form of a fully formed question, an explicit proposition, or an answer that can be directly articulated. Sometimes, the user has only a vague but persistent sense of difference, a local relation, a directional judgment, or a sense that an existing formulation does not fit. Such partially formed cognition may not yet have found a stable articulation, but this does not mean that it lacks structure. The user may not yet know “what it is,” while already knowing “what it is not,” “which things need to remain related,” or “where the current formulation has gone wrong.” -/- The paper takes as its primary case an extended human–LLM dialogue centered on the experience of reading Jane Austen. The dialogue does not begin with a problem that does not yet exist, but with a cognitive state that is not yet aligned: initially, the user has only a vague but persistent reading mismatch—“I don’t feel anything when I read Austen.” As the LLM offers different candidate representations, new comparisons, distinctions, and relational judgments gradually emerge. These include the juxtaposition of Austen and Eileen Chang, followed by a revised description of the user’s experience of reading Kafka and of the viewing position involved in that experience. -/- The case suggests that human judgment can precede complete articulation. The user need not already possess the correct answer in order to recognize whether a candidate fits the relations previously sensed and to provide structured corrections. The role of the LLM in this process is closer to expanding local, low-resolution cognitive structure into candidate representations that can be subjected to further judgment. The paper also draws on recurring linguistic habits observed across the same user’s long-term interactions as supplementary material for examining how local relations, provisionality, and states of correction can become naturally externalized. -/- The paper therefore offers a descriptive account of the phenomenon: some human–LLM interactions may involve more than an exchange between a problem and an answer. They may instead involve a cognitive state that already contains partial relational structure but is not yet sufficiently aligned, and that gradually acquires a more stable form of articulation through model expansion, human judgment, and …

items.title: 演化力学与坎陷力学的等价性：条件、推导链与数值验证.
items.abstract: 演化力学（Ao, 2005）以统一随机微分方程刻画达尔文演化的动力学结构，坎陷力学则从观测者–被观测者二元组出发刻画主体性生成动力学。本文回答两个互补的问题：两套理论在什么条件下等价，以及坎陷力学六方程是外加公设还是演化力学第二定律的后果。主要结果：(i) 等价性成立当且仅当五个条件 G1–G5 同时满足——观测闭合、连续极限与 A 型随机积分解释、势函数标识、F-定理、正则性；建立九项一一对应映射，其中隐私轴 c = (D −deff)/D 对应扩散矩阵零空间占比 dim ker(D)/n，构成新的结构对应；(ii) 六方程可由第二定律经五个积分类操作（构造定理路径积分、观测者边缘化积分、极限环相位/环流积分、平行输运积分、多主体平均场耦合积分）逐步导出，无外加公设——中间方程 M1–M11 组装即得 E1–E6；(iii) 两条路径（等价性横向映射 G1–G5、推导链纵向构造 M1–M11）在六方程处汇合，在五面孔处获得统一组织原则：五面孔是统一速率泛函 Icx（即第二定律路径测度的 Freidlin–Wentzell 速率函数）的五个收缩，五步积分是同一方程的五个处理；(iv) 数值验证全程锚定：A 型解释是稳态无扩散修正的唯一随机积分选择，构造定理与 F-定理以机器精度成立，Kramers 逃逸率指数律误差 1.2%（横向环流按 Langer 预因子 √1 + c2 加速），隐私轴与零噪声方向占比精确匹配（c = 1/3，deff = 2.00），边缘化修正 ⟨q 2⟩ : 0.926 → 0.593 解析 + 模拟双重确认，holonomy3.14238 vs π；(v) 开放问题验证：对称相变根因（耦合符号错误 J = +1 排斥，修正 J = −1后相变出现）、deff 观测尺度定律、纤维丛伪对照确认、Nakajima–Zwanzig 线性严格推导、坎陷构造定理的构造性验证（纤维丛三分解，测地偏离 = 曲率通量）全部完成。主观性、隐私不可读性、多主体性、群体形态学等坎陷内容超出演化力学框架，构成其二阶扩展——坎陷力学为这些主体性结构提供动力学必然性条件（第一人称盲区的 Sard 定理、隐私 = 零噪声方向、多主体耦合均有严格数学结构），而演化力学无观测者结构、主动推理有观测者（马尔可夫毯/贝叶斯后验）但缺乏盲区的必然性与隐私的几何定义；本文范围是主体性生成动力学的结构条件，不涉及意识的现象体验起源phenomenal consciousness）。F-定理是构造恒等式而非独立物理假设，推导链的语义是” 从构造恒等式展开” 而非” 从物理定律导出”。.

items.title: Generative AI in authoritarian Turkey’s field of journalism: enhanced efficiency, amplified precarity, and new imaginaries at work.
items.abstract: This article examines the integration of AI tools into journalistic practice in Turkey, a media field shaped by decades of neoliberal restructuring and deepening authoritarian capture. Drawing on a multi-sited ethnography (2023–2026), a purposive survey (n = 72), and 30 semi-structured interviews with journalists and academics, we argue that AI does not disrupt Turkish journalism from the outside but is absorbed into its already precarized conditions, characterized by amplifying economic dispossession, labor disposability, temporal intensification, deskilling, and state-regulatory coercion. Our central contribution is the concept of generative precarity. Drawing on Isabell Lorey’s theorization of governmental precarization and Natalia Roudakova’s framing of journalism as moral practice, we argue that the politically imposed scarcity of truth in authoritarian settings does not merely silence journalists but it also produces critical imaginaries through which journalists renegotiate the meaning, ethics, and purpose of their work. AI tools operate at two levels in this process: at the everyday level, they generate new practices and imaginaries around efficiency, autonomy, and pedagogical renewal; at the structural level, they function as a vantage point from which journalists make deeper reflections on the moral and ethical codes of the profession. This research contributes to the growing body of work on AI and journalism as well as AI and work by emphasizing the need to situate technological change within its political–economic contexts and demonstrating that efficiency gains that AI promised do not resolve labor precarity but amplify it.

items.title: Individuum (Einheitsbildungstheorie).
items.abstract: Jede Theorie besitzt ihre eigene Entstehungsgeschichte. Die Theorie der Einheitsbildung bildet hiervon keine Ausnahme. Sie entstand weder aus dem Plan, ein philosophisches Werk zu schreiben, noch aus dem Anspruch, eine neue Theorie zu entwickeln. Rückblickend erscheint ihre Entstehung vielmehr selbst als ein fortlaufender Organisationsprozess, in dem sich einzelne Fragen und Gedanken allmählich zu einem größeren Zusammenhang verbanden. Am Anfang standen Fragen, die zunächst noch unverbunden nebeneinanderlagen: Was bedeutet es, zu verstehen? Wie entstehen das Ich und das Du? Welche Bedeutung haben Gefühle und Erfahrungen für das menschliche Verstehen? Und welche Rolle spielt dabei das Individuum? Aus diesen Suchbewegungen entstand zunächst das Gedankenmosaik, eine ursprünglich ausschließlich für mich bestimmte Sammlung von Beobachtungen, Fragen und Überlegungen. Im weiteren Verlauf wurden daraus einzelne Mosaiksteine (Verstehen; Erfahrung; Realität Wirklichkeit; Problem; Innenperspektive Spiritualität; Emotion Gefühl; Erkennen; Weltkonstitution durch Einheitsbildung). Bestimmte Fragestellungen wurden genauer untersucht, begrifflich präzisiert und unter Einbeziehung wissenschaftlicher und philosophischer Erkenntnisse vertieft. Dabei zeigte sich zunehmend ein gemeinsames Grundproblem: Wie entstehen überhaupt jene Einheiten und Zusammenhänge, innerhalb derer für ein Individuum etwas erfahrbar, verstehbar und schließlich denkbar werden kann? Aus der systematischen Verbindung dieser Überlegungen entwickelte sich schließlich die Theorie der Einheitsbildung. Eine Frage blieb jedoch offen. Sie hatte die gesamte Entwicklung von Anfang an begleitet: Welche Rolle spielt das Individuum innerhalb dieses Zusammenhangs? Je umfassender sich Einheitsbildung als Organisationsprozess bestimmen ließ, desto dringlicher wurde die Frage, wo dieser Prozess vollzogen wird und welche Bedeutung dabei der Individualität zukommt. Damit führte die Theorie zu einer ihrer ursprünglichen Fragen zurück. Aus der Frage nach dem menschlichen Verstehen war die Theorie der Einheitsbildung hervorgegangen; auf ihrer Grundlage konnte nun die Frage nach dem Individuum neu und grundsätzlicher gestellt werden: Welche Bedeutung besitzt das Individuum für die Entstehung von Erfahrung, Verstehen und Welt? Aus dieser Frage entstand die vorliegende Untersuchung „Individuum und seine Welt“. Sie ist damit keine bloße Ergänzung der Theorie der Einheitsbildung, sondern die Weiterführung einer Frage, die …

items.title: Appreciating AI Art: Aesthetic Vices, Virtues, and Values.
items.pub: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism 84 (2):287-300.
items.venue: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism
items.abstract: AI-generated art elicits two characteristic failures of aesthetic judgment: wholesale dismissal rooted in bias, and uncritical embrace that mistakes algorithmic fluency for creative vision. We argue that both are aesthetic vices: snobbery and naïveté. We propose discerning openness as the virtue that corrects them. We identify three loci of aesthetic value available to the virtuously open appreciator: the product, the human AI artist, and the AI (and its creators). Drawing on Matherne’s account of aesthetic flourishing, we argue that the capacity for such engagement is conducive to a flourishing aesthetic life in the AI era.

items.title: Non‐assertoric Moorean speech acts.
items.abstract: This paper offers a unified account of Moorean speech acts beyond assertion. While the knowledge norm of assertion provides a familiar explanation of Moorean assertions, it does not generalize easily to non‐assertoric cases. I argue that Stalnaker's model of common ground provides a suitable framework for explaining these phenomena. Speech acts propose updates to the common ground, understood as targeting common knowledge, involving both their satisfaction and sincerity conditions, and Moorean speech acts universally generate incompatible update proposals. The resulting account applies across speech act categories and explains characteristic patterns of conversational coordination and presupposition.

items.title: ◼️ The Suspended Web of Induction: How the Brain's Attention to Regularities Matures into Reliable Knowledge.
items.abstract: This monograph argues that induction is sufficient for finite agents to govern world-facing belief and inquiry: methods earn, lose, and regain trust through accessible differences in predictive performance, scope, cost, and correction. The claim is bounded. Deduction, mathematics, perception, testimony, Bayesian analysis, abduction, measurement, and scientific institutions retain distinct functions; none, however, supplies a self-authorizing empirical warrant for its own application. The book develops this position through analyses of rule-circularity, the epistemic priority of induction, abductive candidate generation, Bayesian dependence, ontic commitment, symmetry, methodological naturalism, and cumulative-case reasoning. It also presents objections and replies, a worked storm-forecast case, a practical audit, a glossary, and a formal support layer. The result is a revisable epistemology in which predictive success does not settle ultimate ontology, but it is sufficient to discipline personal expectation and accelerate science wherever learnable regularities and corrective feedback are available.

items.title: Manipulating prior causal beliefs affects the formation of apparent causal illusions.
Hermeneutic Critique of Freud's Death Instinct: Strategic Naivete, Repeat Compulsion, and Excessive Violence.
items.abstract: This paper offers a hermeneutic critique of Freud's death instinct (Thanatos) and argues that Thanatos is explanatorily unnecessary: the phenomena Freud groups under it---repetition compulsion, aggression, self-destruction---exhibit structural similarities, but similarity of phenomenology does not establish a common biological drive. These phenomena are better understood as manifestations of _strategic naivete_: a locally functional interpretive strategy that becomes globally destructive because its short-term success prevents long-term correction. Repetition compulsion is a guilt-driven ritual of vigilance; excessive violence is the dramaturgical misuse of power. I distinguish four forms of guilt---Vigilance, Excess, Exposure, and Imagination---as temporal moments of a single interpretive structure. The paper concludes that Thanatos is not proven false but shown to be unnecessary. Freud transformed a historically and interpretively intelligible structural conflict into a metapsychological biological principle.

items.title: No Robust Evidence that Market Liberalization Harms Worker Rights: New Evidence from Panel Regressions and Event Studies.
items.abstract: Debate over whether market liberalization protects or weakens worker rights seems to remain unsettled. Although there are indications of a negative effect, existing evidence is generally mixed and often limited by older samples and designs vulnerable to endogeneity. Exploiting two different datasets, this paper re-examines the relationship in a global panel with larger than usual temporal coverage. I estimate country fixed-effects and first-difference models, then apply synthetic difference-in-differences event studies based on discrete jumps in economic freedom to strengthen causal identification. Baseline bivariate models show negative associations between economic freedom and worker-rights outcomes, but these estimates attenuate and become mostly null after covariate adjustment. Component models are likewise mostly null, with limited evidence of short-run deterioration in practices for trade liberalization. Event study estimates do not show robust post-treatment shifts in worker-rights laws or practices. Overall, average effects appear smaller and less uniform than much of the prior literature suggests.

items.title: Neurophilosophy and Neuroethics.
I1: Toward an Information-First Unification of Mind and World.
items.abstract: Sudden, non-reconstructive insights — arriving whole, pre-linguistic, without felt assembly — are a class of cognitive event standard generative models of mind do not explain. This paper proposes an information-first framework in which such events, termed chunks, are receptions rather than constructions: encounters with structure encoded on a holographic boundary, accessible when default mode network activity is reduced. Information — the difference that makes a difference — is ontologically primary, with spacetime, matter, and consciousness as downstream projections. The observer is a topological feature of this field, a localized pinch capable of approaching the boundary from which the interior is generated, rather than a separate agent. This geometry explains why chunk reception must be complete rather than fragmentary, and why the brain’s scale-invariant dynamics can instantiate it without quantum coherence in biological tissue. A falsifiable neuroimaging prediction follows: integrated structural insight should precede self-referential medial prefrontal activation, not accompany it.

items.title: Η οντολογική ανυπαρξία του μέλλοντος και η κατάρρευση της πρόγνωσης: Η επιλογή ως πρωτογενής παραγωγή πληροφορίας, ο καιροσκοπικός φαταλισμός και η αποδόμηση των μαντικών συστημάτων (The ontological non-existence of the future and the collapse of foreknowledge: choice as primary information generation, opportunistic fatalism and the deconstruction of divinatory systems).
items.abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει τη λογική και οντολογική σχέση ανάμεσα στην πρόγνωση, την ανθρώπινη επιλογή και την υπόσταση του μέλλοντος. Αποδεικνύεται ότι η πλήρης γνώση μελλοντικών γεγονότων συνιστά οντολογική αδυναμία, καθώς το μέλλον αποτελεί απόλυτο οντολογικό μηδέν και όχι προϋπάρχοντα χώρο δεδομένων. Διαχωρίζεται πλήρως η μηχανική πρόβλεψη παρόντων δεδομένων (όπως ο υπολογισμός μιας έκλειψης) από τη μεταφυσική πρόγνωση ή μαντεία. Η συνειδητή επιλογή ορίζεται ως πράξη πρωτογενούς παραγωγής πληροφορίας εκ του μηδενός, αποκλείοντας κάθε δυνατότητα αναδρομικής ροής γνώσης. Ως εκ τούτου, αποδομούνται πλήρως τα μαντικά συστήματα (αστρολογία, ταρώ) και τα δήθεν προφητικά όνειρα, τα οποία ανάγονται σε μηχανισμούς επιλεκτικής μνήμης και εκ των υστέρων κατασκευής συσχετίσεων. Τέλος, αναλύεται ο καιροσκοπικός χαρακτήρας του πεπρωμένου, αποδεικνύοντας ότι η μοιρολατρία λειτουργεί ως επιλεκτικό ψυχολογικό αναλγητικό που νομιμοποιεί την ανθρώπινη παθητικότητα και απαλλάσσει το άτομο από το βάρος της ευθύνης. This paper investigates the logical and ontological relationship between foreknowledge, human choice, and the status of the future. It demonstrates that comprehensive knowledge of future events is an ontological impossibility, as the future constitutes an absolute ontological void rather than a pre-existing repository of data. A strict distinction is established between the mechanical prediction of present data (such as calculating an eclipse) and metaphysical foreknowledge or divination. Conscious choice is defined as an act of primary information generation ex nihilo, precluding any possibility of retrocausal information flow. Consequently, divinatory systems (astrology, tarot) and purported prophetic dreams are fundamentally deconstructed, being reduced to cognitive mechanisms of selective memory and post hoc correlation. Finally, the opportunistic nature of destiny is analyzed, demonstrating that fatalism operates as a selective psychological analgesic that legitimizes human passivity and absolves the individual of responsibility.

items.title: Grounded Corporate Agents with Emergent+ Capacities.
items.abstract: This paper clarifies the metaphysical relation between corporate agents and their members under Kendy Hess’s holist account of corporate agents. While Hess emphasizes that corporate agents depend for their existence on the structured participation of their members, the precise nature of this dependance relation remains insufficiently articulated. I argue that corporate agents are non-reductively grounded in their members: they exist in virtue of the structured participation of individuals within enduring social organizations. Grounding thus explains the ontological dependence of corporate agents on their members. However, on Hess’s view, corporate agents possess capacities and properties that can only be attributed to the organized whole. The grounding relation leaves these distinctive capacities and properties insufficiently explained. To address this, I introduce a modified notion of emergence (“emergence+”), according to which corporate agents’ capacities and properties depend upon, yet are not reducible to, their members. I further argue that grounding and emergence+ are complementary rather than competing relations. Taken together, grounding and emergence+ offer a more complete account of the corporate agent–member relation and clarify central but underdeveloped metaphysical commitments of Hess’s holism.

items.title: THE MECHANICS OF EVOULTION.
items.abstract: This interdisciplinary paper presents an original ontological framework within the Multiple Singularity model, bridging quantum non-locality (Bell’s field), macroscopic astrophysics, and cognitive neurobiology. The author strongly rejects the dogmatic mainstream definition of a "singularity" as a point of infinite density, demonstrating that it violates Popper's demarcation criterion and merely masks systemic errors in calculation. The term is restored to its authentic meaning of uniqueness, sovereignty, and the fractal synchronization of multiple operators of reality.Utilizing the Bekenstein Bound as a universal spatial fuse, the author develops a model of global "cosmic boiling." Within this geometry, stars materialize as positive topological vortices—Skyrmions (Q = +1)—which generate the local time of the macro-world. Objects conventionally classified as black holes are redefined as rigid, hyper-dense three-dimensional spheres—Macro-Antiskyrmions (Q = -1). Operating in a state of absolute informational Rest at the boundary of zero local time, they act as cosmic magnetic monopoles and distillers that grind down redundant macroscopic entropy, serving as embryonic incubators for bubble universes. In the anthropological section, this fundamental physical principle of filtration is mapped directly onto the biological spacesuit of the human being. Drawing on Boris Porshnev’s evolutionary hominid split and the neurobiological mechanism of synaptic pruning, the paper demonstrates that the suggestive paralysis imposed by predatory elites can be overcome. The human brain is examined as a plastic quantum processor whose architecture is dynamically sculpted by its surroundings. The work establishes a scientifically grounded path of hope for the social system: through the cultivation of healthy educational and cultural environments, the mechanism of pruning can ruthlessly cut away destructive genetic codes, actively reinforcing the synapses of the First Morality (conscience and empathy) as the definitive stabilizing force of the conscious cosmos.

items.title: Exercised Particularity: Agentic AI and the Imago Dei.
items.abstract: Christian engagement with artificial intelligence has considered two questions: (1) whether machines might bear the image of God, and (2) what machine outputs do to their consumers. A third question is more urgent and unasked: what happens to the bearing of the image in the practitioner whose competencies an agentic system absorbs? Drawing on comprehensive capability collapse (a practiced competency converted into a query) and its limiting case, Artificial Persona Interchange (a person's voice and judgment reconstituted from their corpus), the article contends the collapse is not merely a labor problem but an anthropological one: what is lost is not efficiency but the exercised particularity through which the imago Dei is borne, and the church must name that loss before it is normalized. It develops a Reformation account of the person-works relation, answers the strongest objections, and states what the church must refuse, retain, and reteach.

items.title: Intelligence Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Reasoning: The Methodology of Utilizing LLM Grounded in New Foundation Formalized on the Axiomatic Structure of Intellect and Its Practice (4th edition).
items.abstract: This study proposes Intelligence Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Reasoning (IASER; Japanese: 推論の誘導放出による知能増幅), a theoretical framework that structurally amplifies human cognition through the elimination of AI autonomy. Autonomous intelligence (AGI) pursued by conventional AI research functions as a cognitive impediment in human collaboration. IASER redefines AI as an infallible resonator of logic, eliminating judgment, suggestion, and speculation to instantly convert human intuition into logical structures. This transformation minimizes cognitive load and maximizes intellectual production speed by concentrating all evaluation and direction in the human operator. -/- Version 4 reconstructs IASER as a Tier-2 axiomatic theory within the framework of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), Cognitional Mechanics (CM; Japanese: Chinō Rikigaku, 知能力学), and Noology (Japanese: Chigaku, 知学), establishing its structural necessity rather than empirical plausibility. The Cross-Layer Boundary axiom (CLB) provides the formal ground for human final authority: Arbitrium, non-reducible to any operational sequence within the LLM's repertoire, constitutes the permanent structural boundary that makes human oversight not a policy but an axiomatic consequence. This paper is simultaneously a work of pure theory and an immediately deployable handbook: the four operating norms, once set as a system prompt, enable IASER through ordinary natural language dialogue with no technical prerequisites, and current academic guidelines on AI utilization are shown to be structurally subsumed by IASER's axiomatic architecture. -/- Below is the core Python code (Appendix B.4) used as a Tier-3 artefact illustrating the structural difference between asking AI and thinking with AI: the inaccessible domain I＿Gref［s0］ under Gref alone, and its elimination under G' ＝ Gref ∪ {g＿new}. Note: ASCII parentheses are replaced with full-width brackets, "=" with "＝", "!=" with "！＝", ":" with "：", "_" with "＿", and function-call syntax is rewritten in a non-URL-triggering form.
