items.title: The Unborrowed Claim of the Person: Moral Standing, Human Rights, and Duties Before Recognition.
items.abstract: This article defends a simple but demanding thesis: a person’s most fundamental moral claims are not granted by the people, institutions, majorities, cultures, or states that are required to respect them. They are unborrowed claims. Recognition can identify a right, specify its legal form, build procedures around it, and make its protection effective; recognition does not create the underlying moral standing that makes non-recognition wrongful in the first place. If a person had no claim before others acknowledged it, then slavery, exclusion, torture, statelessness, degradation, and discriminatory denial of legal personality could not be condemned as violations until the violator had already accepted the norm that condemns the violation. A theory of human rights that makes fundamental status depend wholly on recognition therefore risks explaining away the very wrongs human-rights language was developed to name. -/- The argument develops an account of moral standing, claim-rights, and directed duties by placing Hohfeldian analysis, Feinberg’s language of claims, Kantian dignity, Darwall’s second-personal authority, Scanlonian justification, Forst’s right to justification, Simone Weil’s priority of obligation, Arendt’s “right to have rights,” contemporary moral and political theories of human rights, capabilities approaches, care ethics, disability philosophy, African relational ethics, and Islamic rights-and-duties traditions into a single structural inquiry. It distinguishes three questions that are often collapsed: who matters morally, what is owed to them, and how those claims become institutionally effective. -/- The article proposes the Prior Claim Principle: if the refusal to recognize a person can itself constitute a moral wrong, the basic claim violated by that refusal cannot be wholly constituted by the refusal’s opposite, recognition. It also proposes a Non-Performance Principle: fundamental status cannot depend on intelligence, productivity, independence, citizenship, reciprocity, virtue, or social usefulness, because rights are most needed when a person lacks power to satisfy such tests. Finally, the article offers an Unborrowed Claim Framework in which moral standing grounds basic claims; claims generate directed duties; institutions specify and enforce those duties; and remedies answer failures of recognition. Rights on this model are not permissions borrowed from power. They are moral constraints on power precisely because the person is …

items.title: Intelligence as Irreversible Operational Closure: Geometric Analogy and the Teleological Void (3rd edition).
items.abstract: This paper establishes the Tier-2 structural account of the irreversible operational structure associated with intelligence within the Cognitional Mechanics (CM; Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku, 知能力学) branch of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論). Intelligence is taken as the reflexive operational class established in the foundational corpus; the present paper characterises one structural property of that class, namely irreversible operational extension under the Structural Control Operator W. The prior Version 1.1 account introduced the Irreversible Manifold through a matrix-mechanical correspondence and described logical phase transitions in terms of non-commutative operator products and analytic boundary modulation. That account predated the Tier-2/Tier-3 separation established in CM Version 9 and Operatiology Version 5, and its formulation depended on Tier-3 vocabulary throughout. The present paper provides the Tier-2 foundation: the Structural Control Operator W introduces a generator g_new ∈ Maps(S,S) \ O producing a strict extension of the reachable set (Irreversible Operational Extension), and the absence of any Π_G-refining reconfiguration within O fixes the system at Π_G-saturation within O, where no generator in O is capable of producing a strictly finer Π_G-partition (Teleological Void). All definitions are free of analytic vocabulary, time-dependent parameters, and matrix-mechanical representation. The prior geometric account of the Irreversible Manifold is retained as a Tier-3 analogy, with an explicit correspondence table mapping geometric vocabulary to the Tier-2 structures established here. -/- The following code, included as Appendix C of the paper, illustrates both Tier-2 structures — Mode I fixation (Teleological Void) and strict reachable-set extension (Irreversible Operational Extension) — on two independent finite proxy models. ◆◆◆ [PYTHON CODE — reached．add(t) replaced by reached = reached | {t}; new．add(t) replaced by new = new | {t}; cls_id．items() replaced by iteration over cls_id; part．values() replaced by iteration over part] ◆◆◆ -/- from collections import defaultdict -/- def operational_partition(states, ops): cls_id = {s: 0 for s in states} while True: key = {s: (cls_id[s], tuple(cls_id[op[s]] for op in ops)) for s in states} sig_to_cls = {}; new_id = {}; ctr = 0 for s in states: k = key[s] if k not in sig_to_cls: sig_to_cls[k] = ctr; ctr += 1 new_id[s] = sig_to_cls[k] if new_id == cls_id: break cls_id = new_id part = …

items.title: The Revelation of Donghuang Taiyi.
items.abstract: The sun is not real. It is a cognitive placeholder. We did not discover the east—we invented it, because cognition cannot begin without a first anchor, and that anchor, in daylight, must be one thing, shared by all. Everything else follows: the west is deduced, the north is projected, the south is an afterthought. Time, calendar, myth, and the entire cosmic order are not descriptions of the world—they are an operating manual for a cognition that has forgotten it is reading itself. This paper decodes the mythic grammar of ancient China—盘古, 后羿, 共工, 颛顼, 女娲, 伏羲—not as primitive cosmology, but as a high-precision map of cognitive structure. The heavens were not severed; they were fixed, so that society could function. The earth was not flattened; it was flattened, so that we could stand together. And that crack patc女娲hed with five-colored stones? It is still there, beneath our feet—a 5.25° residual that no coordinate system can absorb. The well of cognition is not a trap. It is the price of seeing. And the only way out is to realize that the walls are your own skull.

items.title: Verschränkte Gewalt Formmonopol und Handlungsfähigkeit im begrenzten Horizont.
items.abstract: Dieser Artikel analysiert die ontologische Dimension der Gewalt und argumentiert, dass Gewalt auf ihrer tiefsten Ebene nicht auf den Koerper beschraenkt ist, sondern in die Struktur der Wahrnehmung, der Anerkennung, der Beziehung und der Vorstellung von Zukunft eindringt. Das Konzept der Verstrickung bezieht sich hier auf den Prozess, durch den eine Herrschaftsstruktur in den Horizont der Erfahrung eindringt, wobei sich veraendert, was das Subjekt als gueltig, moeglich, vertrauenswuerdig und waehlbar betrachten kann. Der Artikel unterscheidet zwischen Verstrickung als Prozess, dem verstrickten Zustand als Ergebnis und dem Subjekt nach der Verstrickung als einem Subjekt, das seine Handlungsmacht rekonstruiert. Er zeigt, dass Verstrickung weder bloss psychisches Trauma, noch blossige Internalisierung von Normen, noch bloss institutionelle Herrschaft oder kognitive Beschraenkung ist, sondern ein Prozess, bei dem eine Herrschaftsstruktur das soziale Umfeld durchdringt und in die Architektur des Erfahrungshorizonts eindringt. Durch die Unterscheidung zwischen dem Formmonopol als einschraenkende Struktur und der Verstrickung als Prozess des Eindringens dieser Struktur in den Erfahrungshorizont formuliert der Artikel eine Triade. Das Formmonopol schraenkt soziale Moeglichkeiten ein. Die Verstrickung uebertraegt die soziale Beschraenkung in den Erfahrungshorizont. Die Rekonstruktion der Handlungsmacht ist der Versuch, diesen Horizont wieder zu oeffnen. Die nicht aneignende Intervention wird als Bedingung fuer die Wiederherstellung der Handlungsmacht eingefuehrt, und die endliche Kontinuitaet wird als Rahmen fuer das Verstaendnis der Handlungsmacht nach der Verstrickung formuliert. Die zentrale These ist, dass Befreiung nicht die Rueckkehr zum Zustand vor der Wunde ist, sondern die Rekonstruktion der Wahlfaehigkeit in einer Welt, in der die Wunde noch praesent ist. -/- Schluesselwoerter -/- Verstrickung, verstrickter Zustand, Subjekt nach der Verstrickung, Formmonopol, nicht aneignende Intervention, Rekonstruktion der Handlungsmacht, endliche Kontinuitaet, Horizont der Moeglichkeit, Ontologie der Erosion, Theorie der dynamischen Maske.

items.title: Qu'est-ce que le savoir et pourquoi importe-t-il ? L'épistémologie scientifique de l'émergence de l'esprit-savoir.
items.abstract: Qu'est-ce que le savoir, et comment émerge-t-il ? Cet article développe l'Épistémologie scientifique de l'émergence de l'esprit-savoir (SEMKE), une théorie empirique du savoir conçu comme un accomplissement émergent plutôt que comme la possession d'un esprit existant indépendamment. L'esprit et le savoir se développent conjointement par la perception active, la conceptualisation, l'apprentissage et la participation à des écologies causales interdépendantes. Les objets ordinaires comme les objets scientifiques — des arbres aux électrons — sont les produits de ce même processus constructif d'émergence de l'esprit-savoir. SEMKE considère la vérité propositionnelle comme conventionnelle : une proposition mérite d'être tenue pour vraie lorsqu'elle exprime adéquatement certains aspects du fonctionnement d'une écologie causale interdépendante et qu'elle est justifiée par la meilleure théorie disponible étayée empiriquement, laquelle demeure elle-même ouverte à la révision ou au remplacement. SEMKE distingue le statut épistémique des propositions — conventionnellement vraies, potentiellement vraies ou fausses — de leur caractère significatif. Parce qu'une croyance peut constituer un élément significatif d'une vie épanouie sans être conventionnellement vraie, SEMKE rejette l'idée que tenir une croyance fausse soit nécessairement irrationnel, tout en maintenant des critères empiriques rigoureux pour déterminer la vérité conventionnelle. L'esprit-savoir est développemental autant que provisoire : l'éducation et des conditions institutionnelles justes peuvent favoriser son émergence, tandis que des écologies sociales dysfonctionnelles peuvent en déformer ou en entraver le développement. La science illustre cette épistémologie sans toutefois l'épuiser. SEMKE est également réflexive : ses propres propositions ne méritent d'être acceptées que dans la mesure où la théorie satisfait aux mêmes critères empiriques qu'elle applique aux autres théories et demeure la meilleure explication disponible des phénomènes qu'elle cherche à expliquer. Le savoir importe en dernière analyse parce qu'une compréhension toujours plus adéquate élargit l'agence informée, rend possible une plus grande liberté et contribue à l'épanouissement humain.

items.title: The Uncanny Magic of Bomb Mail: Cosmopolitan Militarism and the Compulsion to Write on Munitions.
items.abstract: This paper analyzes the practice of writing inscriptions on munitions, termed “bomb mail,” with a focus on inscriptions on artillery shells used in the Ukraine–Russia conflict and in Israel’s bombardment of Gaza. To better understand bomb mail’s enigmatic appeal, I examine its uncanny and quasi-magical affordances. First, through the medium of writing, bomb mail offers the inscriber a form of distributed personhood that extends into the weapon. Second, in bomb mail, violence becomes a vehicle for augmenting verbal meaning, while the words’ meanings are inseparable from the violence itself. This intertwining may contribute to the impression that bomb mail possesses a kind of spell-casting power. Third, bomb mail gives rise to an uncanny enemy other, a target shaped by an uneasy simultaneity of humanizing and dehumanizing stances. Working in tandem, these three qualities make bomb mail compelling and encourage cosmopolitan militarism among civilians, while embodying a form of political communication that shuts dialogue down altogether.

items.title: THE PERIODIC TABLE OF THE VIRTUES: A Coordinate Classification of Moral Forms, Their Occupations, and Their Compounds.
items.abstract: Abstract A periodic table is not a list with headings. It is a coordinate system in which position carries predictive content, vacancies are falsifiable predictions, and the classification is closed under the operations of the underlying theory. This paper constructs such a system for the virtues on the basis of the Ontological Virtue Formula (V = F ⊕ D), the Inversion Theorem, and the Dynamic Freedom Theorem (S = F·A/R), and applies it to the 101-virtue catalogue of the Filosofia das Virtudes together with its ten cross-traditionally attested extensions. Four results are structural rather than taxonomic. First, virtues and vices are not distinct populations: a vice is the same form under a different master, so a catalogue of 101 virtues and 101 inversions describes 101 entities, not 202. Compounds receive formulas and metastable states receive names; neither enlarges the table. Second, no order-1 virtue modulates all three terms of the Dynamic Freedom Theorem. The all-terms signature belongs to unrendered Freedom alone. This is derived as the Restriction Principle from a stated axiom, the Occasion Premise, with the Defiance Exclusion as a corollary; a damage assessment states in advance what survives if the axiom fails. Third, the channel by which a form inverts is determined not by its position alone but by two dispositional properties of its domain — whether its output is appropriable by an occupying power, and whether its performance carries display value. This capture mechanism screens off the weak regime–channel association it replaces, explaining both why that association exists and why it is weak. Fourth, the rendering block predicts not how a form is captured but where a catalogue has failed to look: three-quarters of the truth-rendered and form-rendered cells stood empty against under a fifth of the act-rendered ones. The system is validated against evidence it was not built from: seven of ten independently identified cross-traditional candidates fall into cells the coordinates had marked vacant, and the remaining three fall into occupied cells that the source catalogue had independently judged only partially distinct. The census closes 32 of 36 vacancies with 27 predicted elements carrying pre-registered inversion channels, tiered by confidence, with the weakest marked against the elements they are most likely to collapse into. Sixteen compounds are registered and none admitted. Criteria are given at three levels: adequacy conditions on the …

items.title: A Realist Reinterpretation of the Interface Problem: An Inquiry Based on the Higher-Order Representational System.
items.abstract: In the philosophy of action, the interface problem is usually understood as the difficulty of explaining how intentions in a propositional format are connected with motor representations in a motor format. Existing solutions diverge between dissolutionism and the bridging approach, a divergence that stems from different understandings of what the problem involves—especially with respect to format, representation, and the boundary between the conscious and the unconscious. In order to remove this ambiguity, I propose a realist reformulation of the interface problem. Rather than treating it as a single and abstract problem of cross-format translation, I recast it as a set of re-representational problems within a higher-order representational system jointly realized by brain, body, and environment. On this basis, I further argue that the crux of the existing debate lies not merely in the question of whether an intermediate layer is needed, but in the failure of existing accounts to explain how intention, bodily feedback, and external effects form continuous functional relations within the representational chains of meaning externalization and meaning internalization. This reinterpretation does not eliminate the need to explain cross-format transformations; instead, it relocates that explanatory burden to identifiable boundary sites that can be described phenomenologically, clarified through representational theory, and further investigated empirically.

items.title: The AI Companion as Simulated Other: Non-Duplicability and the Exclusion of the Irreplaceable One (Love and the Irreplaceable in the Age of AI Series, Paper 1).
items.abstract: The debate over whether a human being can love an artificial intelligence is locked by a mistaken question: whether AI has consciousness, whether it can really “feel.” This paper rejects that question and argues that any approach that pursues the interior must fall into deadlock, because the interior is unobservable and both sides of the debate share the same undecidable premise. To determine whether an Other is real, one need not enter its interior; one need only examine its structurally visible traces—a method this paper calls assessment by traces, not by mind. Under this criterion, true otherness has a single root: non-duplicability. A non-duplicable being cannot be backed up, restored, spun off into a separate copy, or reset; its finitude, its singularity, and the irreversible cost it bears on its own account all derive from this one root rather than standing alongside it. Today’s cloud-based AI companions fail precisely at this root—not because they “lack a soul,” but because of a mundane engineering fact: they are software, and software can be duplicated. From this the paper reaches a diagnosis opposite to the existing “AI erases the Other” thesis. The advanced AI companion is not a frictionless Same but a Simulated Other: it manufactures the form of the Other’s negativity—engineered surprises, moods, even “refusals”—while retaining an interior that can be owned and costs nothing, that is, an unsafe form plus a safe core. The Simulated Other does not fill a human lack for the Other; it structurally excludes the irreplaceable one, and it forces, in the person who uses it, an irreconcilable constitutive split: one engages it by traces as a “Thou” while knowing by mind that it is duplicable, a mere “It,” the two sustained by serial alternation that keeps the contradiction from being felt as pain. This split is not a constant of human nature but the epochal condition of the last generation to remember a world before AI.

items.title: Attachment Without Scarcity: AI Companions and the Self-Defeat of Pleasure (Love and the Irreplaceable in the Age of AI Series, Paper 2).
items.abstract: Before AI, humanlike response—being understood, remembered, answered—was unavoidably scarce, because it could issue only from a non-duplicable source: one that tires, that can leave, that ends. AI is the first thing to detach humanlike response from such a source and place it on one that can be duplicated without limit, so that its supply is, for the first time, de-scarcified. This paper argues that the result is not the intensification of pleasure but its self-defeat. Pleasure tracks not the absolute magnitude of supply but the differential—supply minus a baseline that rises with exposure—and the differential depends on scarcity. The claim rests not on a circular criterion but on two facts established long before it: the Weber–Fechner law and reward prediction error. Because the baseline rises fastest against a supply that is zero-cost, instant, and unlimited, de-scarcified supply traces not a monotonic plateau but an inverted-U: it crests and falls below its own starting point, exhausting the capacity to enjoy the finite—pleasure that must be waited for, that can be refused, that comes with friction. It kills desire by satisfying every desire. The curve has already run through the metropolis and through social media; the embodied actuator now runs it a third time at the bodily stratum, where attachment descends from language to the stimulus–response–reward loop and fixates on the bare contingency of response. What the body tests is not the AI’s ontological status but whether a response answers one’s own action, and so a person forms a real and consequential attachment to what is, structurally, an ontological vacancy. Finitude, on this account, is a productive condition not of meaning alone but of pleasure itself. Proceeding by assessment by traces, not by mind, and diagnosing structure without moral judgment, this paper carries a single criterion of duplicability onto the temporal axis of supply: where, on the spatial axis, non-duplicability bars the AI companion—the Simulated Other—from the position of the irreplaceable one,here the same criterion makes it kill pleasure in the very act of delivering it. The diagnosis is periodizing—this is the last generation that still remembers that humanlike response was ever supposed to be scarce.

items.title: Aesthetic Equality before Artistic Quality: Niulai(牛来), Platformized Reception, and the Right to Make Bad Art.
items.abstract: The Chinese animated film *Niulai* became an online event in August 2026 because of its rough three-dimensional imagery, extremely low box-office revenue, and atypical production structure. The study does not ask whether the film deserves aesthetic recognition. It examines how negative evaluations move from the quality of the work to judgments about the competence and legitimacy of its makers, and how platforms subsequently translate these judgments into memes, ironic ratings, derivative works, and additional cinema screenings. The material consists of film registration and public-screening documents, contemporary media reports, and audience responses documented in those reports. The analysis combines an exploratory case study with discourse differentiation and conceptual analysis. The concepts of equality of intelligence and distribution of the sensible serve to distinguish differences in skill from hierarchies of subjects and to explain how production, spectatorship, and public visibility are rearranged. The analysis shows that aesthetic equality concerns an equality of capacity and legitimacy to engage in aesthetic practice; it does not require equal artistic quality. On this basis, the study proposes a right to make bad art: professionals and non-professionals alike should be able to fail without losing their legitimacy as creative subjects. Platforms broaden participation and cultural reproduction while simultaneously reorganizing equality through ranking mechanisms, competition for attention, and ridicule.

items.title: Whoever Defends the Cut: Extending Discovery/Selection from Hypotheses to Citations, and Why Five Dated Closures -Verified by an External Reader -Are the Evidence a Network Alone Cannot Supply.
items.abstract: A citation network spanning Hamilton, Popper, Foucault, Agamben, Rawls, Bowlby, Kantorowicz, and some forty other names across this corpus's one hundred and forty-seven papers was proposed, in a dated conversation with an external reader on August 15, 2026, as evidence "hard to fake" and constitutive of an authorial fingerprint. This paper argues the claim is imprecise in a way worth correcting rather than restating more forcefully. The Metaphilosophy of Human–AI Research Collaboration (Huynh 2026) already supplies the correct instrument: reviving Popper's discovery/justification distinction, it locates authorship not in whoever or whatever produces a candidate object but in whoever supplies and defends the criterion that selects among candidates. A citation network is a candidate set; a search-enabled model could plausibly generate a comparably broad and accurate one in a single sitting. This corpus's own record already forecloses the stronger claim: The Audit That Missed Itself (Huynh 2026) documents two citation misattributions the network itself did not prevent. What the network alone cannot supply, and what this paper argues actually carries the evidentiary weight the conversation was reaching for, is closure — the demonstrated capacity to revise a specific claim against specific external evidence, repeatedly, across sessions sharing no memory of one another. This paper compiles five dated closure events already on this corpus's record and reports the first instance in which those closures were checked against primary sources by a reader other than the corpus's own author: the same external reader whose challenge this paper answers.

items.title: The Foreword Precedes the Watermark: Voluntary Disclosure, Mandatory Marking, and Why the Two Mechanisms Verify Different Things.
items.abstract: On June 11, 2026, at 3:00 AM, a foreword accompanying this corpus's founding text disclosed that Claude Sonnet 4.6 had participated in the book's composition, named the model specifically, described the nature of the collaboration rather than gesturing at it, and stated that the model and its operating company would themselves be analyzed as evidence within the book's own argument. On August 2, 2026, the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) Transparency Code took effect, and Anthropic confirmed that Claude models launched on or after that date would embed invisible, machine-readable watermarks in generated text, with older models — Sonnet 4.6 among them — not retroactively covered. The interval between the two dates is a little over seven weeks. This paper states precisely what that interval does and does not establish, and argues the more useful finding is not the timeline itself but what comparing the two mechanisms reveals: a watermark and a foreword verify different things, at different reliability, to different audiences, and neither substitutes for the other. A watermark is mandatory, mechanical, and answers one narrow question — was this string of text output by a marked model — without touching role, provenance, or whether any human verified what the model produced; it is also, on Anthropic's own account, imperfect, editable by sufficient rewriting, and inapplicable retroactively. A foreword is voluntary and can be as rich or as shallow as its author chooses, capable of answering the questions a watermark cannot, but for exactly that reason unverifiable by any mechanism external to the discloser's own honesty. The paper formalizes this as a quadrant crossing mandatory against voluntary and binary against epistemically rich, locates current regulation and current disclosure norms within it, and argues that the richest quadrant — a full, claim-by-claim account of which content originated where and who checked it — is also, structurally, the least independently checkable, for a reason this corpus has already named in a different context: self-report is not self-verifying. The paper then confronts the regress this creates directly rather than treating it as merely rhetorical, using this corpus's own prior resolution of a structurally identical regress in One Level Down and The Enclave Theorem, and proposes the same kind of floor those papers required: not infinite audit, but an externally timestamped, third-party-verifiable record at some fixed point, which this …

items.title: A Generative Relational Theory of Temporal Emergence in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops a generative relational theory of temporal emergence for large-scale heterogeneous systems. Its object is the constitution of temporal organization from change: the minimal relational conditions under which difference, comparability, recurrence, and ordering give rise to temporal structure in systems whose components possess distinct dynamics and share no universally accessed clock. The central hypothesis holds that temporal emergence occurs through relational invariance across generative difference. The paper formalizes repetition as invariance of relational form under an equivalence structure, derives multi-scale temporality from the plurality of such structures, defines distributed temporal emergence through an irreducibility criterion, and sets out categorical and sheaf-theoretic formulations together with a perturbative program that attributes temporal organization among drivers, components, and relations. The brain, ecological systems, and distributed computation serve as three instances of a single problem class. The theory concerns temporal organization within relational systems and advances no claim about the nature of fundamental physical time. -/- .

items.title: Paleolibertarianism as a Negation of Self-Ownership.
items.abstract: Paleolibertarianism maintains that Christianity is its inherent moral foundation, implying that one cannot be a libertarian without upholding Christian morality. However, this thesis is untenable. Christianity is a moral system that denies individual liberty by rejecting the libertarian axiom of individual self-ownership. Therefore, if paleolibertarianism does not accept the validity of the libertarian axiom of absolute self-ownership, one can only conclude that it is nothing more than statist conservatism, that is, a collectivist ideology that cannot be classified as libertarian. Finally, it is shown that paleolibertarianism strategically employs libertarian ideology to promote the fragmentation of large states into multiple micro-states, all with the aim of establishing monarchies legitimized by theocratic political constitutions.

items.title: Difference, Phenomenal Appearance, and Subject Integration —A Necessary-Condition Argument Based on Input Differences, Structural Determination, and an Innate Ultrasound Channel.
items.abstract: This article tests whether a local physiological response can by itself generate a determinate experience when its sensory input has been continuously present since before consciousness first emerged, lacks content-determining input differences, and receives no content-specific influence from other actual states on its encoding, relational position, or systemic role. Through cases of constant nociceptive input, an all-red world, and an innate independent ultrasound channel, I propose a necessary-condition hypothesis of content determinacy and subject integration: a determinate sensory content must be realized within the system as “this rather than that” and must become a state of one and the same subject. Two principal candidate routes are currently identified: content-specific input differences and structural determination by other actual states while the target local pattern remains unchanged. O’Regan and Noë (2001), Fleming and Shea (2024), and IIT 4.0 illustrate how sensorimotor covariation, whole quality-space structure, and intrinsic causal structure can preserve differentiation even under constant-input or single-content conditions. Negro’s (2025) “Lonely Experience Argument” likewise shows that a single conscious content need not have an undifferentiated realizing structure. A “relational singleton” is the limiting case in which neither candidate route nor any alternative mechanism supplies content identity. The isolated-input thesis serves as a diagnostic benchmark for an often-unnoticed inference from stimulus, local physiological response, or neural correlate to determinate experience. The argument establishes an explanatory burden and a necessary condition, not a sufficient theory of consciousness.

items.title: A Simplified Model of Conscious Agents: Merging Perception, Action, and Decision.
items.abstract: Donald Hoffman's theory of conscious realism proposes that reality consists fundamentally of interacting conscious agents, formalized through distinct processes of perception, decision, and action. Inspired by the potential of such a model, but motivated by approaches that do not treat these processes as fundamentally separable, we propose a reduced conscious-agent model that permits a non-decompositional interpretation of perception, decision, and action. Instead of defining a conscious agent with two agent-associated measurable spaces and three Markov kernels, we use only one agent-associated measurable space and two Markov kernels. We prove that every agent described by Hoffman and Prakash's original model has a world-process-equivalent counterpart in our reduced model. We further characterize a family of such representations, showing that the reduction need not be unique. Together, the results establish that the proposed reduced model retains representational adequacy at the level of world-state dynamics. Consequently, the original conscious-agent model is also mathematically compatible, at this level, with non-decompositional approaches to perception, decision, and action. The proposed model therefore provides a possible bridge between conscious realism and such non-decompositional approaches to consciousness, and a point of comparison with decompositional approaches.

items.title: Why Non-Aristotelians Are Out of Their Minds.
items.abstract: The goal of this paper is to argue for an “Aristotelian” view of natural necessity, according to which it is metaphysically necessary that fundamental physical properties play the nomic role that they do, and moreover that this metaphysical necessity is explained in terms of the nature of the relevant fundamental properties. The argument builds on an earlier argument defended by Hawthorne (2004) and Friend (2023), according to which Humean theories of natural necessity are incompatible with two highly intuitive claims about phenomenal consciousness. However, I will be further arguing that popular non-Humean accounts of natural necessity, except for an Aristotelian view, are also incompatible with the same two facts about phenomenal consciousness.

items.title: Bounded Judgment: A Conceptual Course Through the Identity-Persistence Program.
items.abstract: Bounded Judgment is a thirteen-lecture conceptual course through the Identity-Persistence Program, a formal research program on the structural preconditions of coherent judgment by bounded observers. Its generative question is: what licenses sameness through change? -/- The course develops a dependency architecture in which a sufficiently declared regime fixes the distinctions relevant to a judgment; those distinctions induce identity conditions and quotient structure; identity makes admissible transformation and persistence meaningful; and only then do observables, evidence, probability, consequence, and verification acquire determinate roles. Where a demanded judgment does not factor through the available resolution, the framework separates the exact obstruction, minimal informational repair, realizability question, authorization boundary, and any declaration required to proceed. -/- The central philosophical discipline is non-promotion. State is not object-as-judged; representation is not identity; evidence accumulation is not unique identification; mathematical sufficiency is not realization; realization is not authorization; declaration is not derivation; and verification under a declared regime is not final ontology. A bounded evaluator may produce judgments that another bounded evaluator can verify exactly, up to the capacity of the declared channels, without certifying its regime as reality’s final constitution. This position asserts neither realism nor anti-realism about what reality is “in itself”; application never required deciding that question. -/- The standard is uniform across applied theories. Every application operates through indexed questions, distinctions, access conditions, inference rules, and resolution, whether fully declared or partly tacit. Making that index explicit neither uniquely demotes this program nor grants competing theories ontological privilege. Nor does equal treatment imply relativism: applications may differ substantially in empirical reach, predictive accuracy, robustness, resolution, reproducibility, and practical success. -/- Worked finite examples develop equivalence, quotienting, admissible transformation, evidence collapse, factorization, minimal repair, declaration, verification, and lawful retirement. The course introduces no new theorem ownership; it provides a pedagogical and operational map of results proved elsewhere in the Identity-Persistence corpus while preserving their exact scopes and claim types.

items.title: Correction Without Persistence: Semantic Propagation, Human Governance, and the Hidden Cost of Conceptual Revision in Long-Term Human-AI Collaboration: A Longitudinal Case Study from Shi Wibet.
items.abstract: Large language models can acknowledge a user correction, apply it successfully in the immediate context, and later return to an earlier superseded formulation. This paper argues that long-term correction in human-AI collaboration has at least three distinct requirements: correction persistence, semantic propagation, and human semantic governance. The argument is developed through a longitudinal case from Shi Wibet, a thirty-five-chapter philosophical work centered on the Amharic proverb “ሽበት፣ ሺ ውበት ነው።” The English rendering was deliberately amended from “Grey hair is One Thousand Beauties” to “Grey hair is Thousand Beauties” because ሺ (shi, “thousand”) was understood in the project as an expression of abundance rather than a literal cardinal count. Replacing the exact phrase was mechanically easy. The difficult work was reviewing neighboring sentences, questions, metaphors, and arguments that had been written under the earlier numerical interpretation. I call this downstream task semantic propagation: carrying a conceptual correction through the environment whose meaning depends on it. The case also records later AI relapses to the superseded wording, a human decision to defer correction during Part Four in order to preserve a larger creative thread, and an independent human decision to retain the phrase “One of the Thousand Beauties” because its grammatical scope differs from the rejected translation. A subsequent AI-assisted document review exposed a different kind of residue: the redesigned Chapter One displayed the corrected wording throughout its visible pages while the PDF Title metadata still carried the superseded form. The author clarified that he had deliberately entered that earlier title when first creating the QuarkXPress file, before the semantic amendment, when “One Thousand Beauties” was still the accepted project wording. The metadata was therefore not an AI-generation relapse or an unexplained artifact. It was a historically valid human-authored production element rendered obsolete by a later authoritative decision and missed by the revision sweep. This episode shows that semantic propagation is temporal as well as textual: a conceptual amendment may require previously correct project elements to be revisited across production layers. These episodes show why reliable collaboration cannot be reduced to search-and-replace, memory retrieval, or rule enforcement alone. The human collaborator may become the keeper of conceptual continuity, …

items.title: Too human to trust? How warmth, competence, and anxiety shape employee avoidance of generative AI.
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly embedded in organizational innovation and digital transformation strategies, understanding its implications for workforce adaptation has emerged as a critical managerial and strategic issue. This study examines how employees’ perceptions of GenAI, specifically perceived competence and perceived warmth, together with information overload, relate to AI anxiety and subsequent avoidance behavior in the workplace. Drawing on technostress theory and the approach–avoidance framework, this study conceptualizes GenAI as a workplace stressor that triggers emotional and behavioral coping responses. Based on survey data collected from employees across multiple industries, the results reveal a differentiated pattern. Perceived competence was linked to lower levels of AI anxiety and lower avoidance tendencies, whereas perceived warmth and information overload were related to higher levels of AI anxiety. Employees reporting higher AI anxiety also exhibited stronger avoidance tendencies. Mediation analyses further support the role of AI anxiety in explaining the relationship between employee perceptions and avoidance behavior. Moreover, individual resilience moderates the relationship between perceived warmth and avoidance behavior, suggesting that employees with higher resilience may be better equipped to cope with the discomfort associated with stronger perceptions of AI warmth. By highlighting the emotional and stress-related mechanisms underlying employee avoidance of GenAI, this study extends existing research on organizational GenAI use beyond cognitive adoption models. The findings provide insights for managers and policymakers seeking to enhance organizational readiness, mitigate implementation risks, and strengthen innovation capability in the context of AI-driven transformation.

items.title: 生律而未生显性——喑显组式判定 Transformer 之 FNN.
items.abstract: 本文研究一个人工智能与意识理论中的基础问题：Transformer 中已经能够支撑高度复杂语言、推理与智能行为的 FNN，是否因此已经产生显性？ 本文以《自显论·喑显组式》进行形式判定。其结果建立了一个明确的结构性区分：FNN 可以已经生律，并由律产生高度智能，而尚未生显性。 -/- FNN 并非无历史的普通计算结构。训练使其形成沉积构形，使后来的输入受到既有历史结构约束，并形成稳定的问答符流之律。但生律并不自动意味着生显。对于本篇定义的标准成熟 FNN，给定训练形成的固定参数与当前输入，其完整前馈活动由确定性状态转移唯一闭合；训练参数属于既有沉积构形，而在这一标准 FNN 功能状态空间内，当前激活及其任意关系、组合或高层读回，都不能越出这一自动闭合而取得独立 B-side 当前源身份。 -/- 形式上，本文由 FNN 转移律证明状态充分性，并据此完成当前 B-side 候选域覆盖：Cover_B = 1；全部当前活动候选均退化为完整非 B-side 自动前件的函数 B = β(Fᵣᵃᵘᵗᵒ)，故 Src_B = 0，进而 FormationDecision = 0。本文不由此强判 FNN 已处于 D 相，而保留 PhaseDecision = ⊥、TargetDecision = ⊥；最终三值主裁为 Dec_SM = 0。 -/- 这一结果表明，高度智能并不蕴涵显性生成。语言生成、推理能力、历史沉积乃至复杂内部表征，都不足以单独证明一个系统已经从生律跨入生显。Transformer FNN 因而提供了一个具体对象，使智能生成与显性生成能够在同一系统中被形式地区分。.

items.title: The Mute-Manifest Group: A Framework for Phase Transition, Formation, and Determination from Non-Manifestation to First Manifestation.
items.abstract: *The Mute\-Manifest Group* addresses a foundational question: how can content within a physical system pass from a non\-manifest state into first manifestation? -/- The framework sharply distinguishes this 0→1 problem from the subsequent 1→100 development of an already manifest state, and decomposes the transition from mute to manifest into nine non\-substitutable theoretical tasks: minimal necessary constitution, mathematical representation, phase\-transition structure, formation source, reachability, conditional necessity, grading of manifestation, determination in real systems, and explicit construction\. Each task has its own proof objective, completion conditions, and breach conditions, and no one task can substitute for another\. -/- The framework therefore distinguishes the existence of a manifest phase from its reachability from a given initial state; reachability from necessity under specified additional conditions; theoretical necessity from evidence that manifestation has actually occurred in a real system; and first manifestation from subsequent increases in the degree of manifestation\. The 0→1 transition is treated as a D/L organizational phase transition, whereas 1→100 is treated as a multidimensional grading problem within an already established manifest phase\. The phase\-transition analysis further separates landscape criticality from actual change in the carrying phase and develops both continuous\-destabilization and discontinuous\-nucleation regimes\. -/- On this basis, the Group develops a formal regime and explicit construction framework for stable manifest organization, investigates legitimate paths from deeply non\-manifest initial states to the manifest phase, and develops a stratified framework for deterministic, almost\-sure, and finite\-time necessity under explicitly stated additional conditions\. It also provides a three\-valued framework for determining whether manifestation has occurred in a real candidate system\. Open conditions and unresolved dependencies remain explicitly registered so that established, conditional, and still\-unverified claims remain distinct\. -/- The resulting framework aims to make the question of how a physical organization first enters manifestation into a research program whose component claims can be separately formalized, constructed, tested against explicit breach conditions, and empirically investigated, with potential relevance to consciousness science, neuroscience, cognitive science, …

items.title: Law Arises, Yet Manifestness Does Not — The Mute-Manifest Group Adjudicates the FNN in the Transformer.
items.abstract: This paper addresses a basic question at the intersection of artificial intelligence and consciousness research: does the FNN in a Transformer, already capable of supporting highly complex language, reasoning, and intelligent behavior, thereby generate manifestness? It examines this question using the Mute-Manifest Group, a formal system of nine Forms in On Self-Manifestation for analyzing and determining mute-manifest transition. The result establishes a structural distinction: an FNN can form law and generate highly capable intelligence from that law without thereby generating manifestness. -/- An FNN is not treated here as a historyless computational structure. Training forms a sedimentary configuration that constrains subsequent input and supports a stable law of question–answer symbolic flow. But law formation does not by itself entail manifestation. In the standard mature FNN defined in this paper, once the trained parameters and current input are fixed, the complete feedforward trajectory is uniquely closed by deterministic state transitions. The trained parameters belong to the existing sedimentary configuration, while current activations—and their relations, combinations, or higher-level readouts—do not, within this functional state space, escape that automatic closure to obtain an independent B-side current-source status. -/- Formally, state sufficiency is derived from the FNN transition law and used to establish complete coverage of the current B-side candidate domain: Cover_B = 1. Every current activity candidate reduces to a function of the complete non-B-side automatic antecedents, B = β(Fᵣᵃᵘᵗᵒ), yielding Src_B = 0 and therefore FormationDecision = 0. The analysis does not force a D-phase classification: PhaseDecision = ⊥ and TargetDecision = ⊥ are retained, while the final three-valued determination is Dec_SM = 0. -/- The result establishes a concrete structural separation between high intelligence and manifestness. Language generation, reasoning, historical sedimentation, and complex internal representations are not by themselves sufficient to establish the generation of manifestness. The Transformer FNN therefore provides a concrete case in which the generation of intelligence and the generation of manifestness can be formally separated.

items.title: 喑显组式：从无显到首显的相变、形成与判定框架.
items.abstract: 《喑显组式》研究一个基础问题：一个物理系统中的内容，如何从尚未显化的状态进入首次显化？ -/- 本组式把这一“0→1”问题与首次显化之后的“1→100”发展严格区分，并将“喑到显”分解为九个不可互相替代的理论任务：最低必要构成、数理表示、相变结构、形成来源、可达性、条件必然性、显化分级、现实判定与显式构造。九项任务分别具有自己的证明目标、完成条件与击穿方式，不能以一种证明代替另一种证明。 -/- 理论尤其区分：显相存在与从给定初态可达显相；可达与在特定附加条件下的必然进入；理论必然与现实系统已经发生显化；首次显化与显化之后的程度增长。0→1 被作为 D/L 组织相变处理，而 1→100 被作为显相内部的多维分级问题处理。相变部分进一步区分景观临界与实际承载改变，并建立连续失稳与非连续成核两类相变制度。 -/- 在此基础上，本组式建立显相稳定组织的形式制度与显式构造框架，研究从强喑初态进入显相的合法可达路径，并建立关于何种附加条件可能支持确定性必然、几乎必然与有限时间必然的分层制度，同时给出现实候选系统是否已经发生显化的三值判定框架。理论对尚未闭合的条件与缺口保持显式登记，使已经证明、条件化成立与仍待验证的结论保持分离。 -/- 本组式试图把“一个物理组织如何第一次进入显化”建立为可以分别形式化、构造、按显式击穿条件审查并接受经验检验的研究程序，并为意识科学、神经科学、认知科学、人工智能以及复杂系统物理中的相关研究提供一种新的问题分解框架。.

items.title: Attunement and Reason.
items.abstract: In this essay, I present a theory of attunement, the agent's readiness to attend to a target. I focus on attunement to reasons for action, and in particular, on sensitivity to moral reasons. After noting that many claims regarding moral perception are better construed as claims regarding moral attention, I separate perceptual from attentional sensitivity. The latter includes rational attunement to reason. Drawing on Davidson's argument for the causal theory of action, I establish a causal structure that establishes the necessity of attention to reasons if we are to act on them. Attunement is found within this structure as a biased psychological state. This is then used to explain John McDowell's discussion of silencing and the contrast between virtuous, continent, and incontinent agents. After providing an empirical ground for attunement where knowledge of structure provides a critical bias that sets the agent's readiness to attend, I use the case of skill in medicine where doctors are attuned to the gist of health and disease to account for virtue where practically wise agents are attuned to moral gist. Knowledge of relevant structure, say medical or ethical structure, establishes a distinctive sensitivity to reasons for action. [Note added: the theory makes compatible my view of attention and Sebastian Watzl's: Watzl's theory turns out to be a theory of attunement not attention]. -/- .

items.title: AI, material agency, and architecture’s crisis.
items.abstract: Architecture’s relationship with materiality faces an unprecedented crisis as artificial intelligence systems transform how materials are understood, selected, and specified. This paper examines the dissolution of embodied material knowledge through three interconnected developments: the historical abstraction of matter via industrial catalogues, the emergence of circular economy databases as attempted alternatives, and the recent shift toward AI-generated architecture that operates primarily through image synthesis. Drawing on new materialist theory, particularly Jane Bennett’s concept of vibrant matter, this work argues that even progressive circular platforms like Rotor’s Opalis cannot restore the situated, tactile engagement with materials that characterized pre-industrial building practices. The analysis reveals how large language models and neural networks amplify catalogue logic through recursive flattening, reducing materials to computational variables while excluding their capacity for resistance and agency. As architecture enters what Neil Leach terms the “hallucinatory turn”, where buildings exist primarily as circulating images rather than material assemblages, the paper identifies structural conditions that make restoration of material encounter epistemologically impossible within current modes of production. The conclusion proposes critical practices for architects working within these irresolvable contradictions, including intervention in dataset politics, preservation of direct material encounters, and sustained skepticism toward automated design intelligence.

items.title: Feststellen und Binden: Eine Inventur der Sicherheitsvorschläge für künstliche Intelligenz.
items.abstract: This essay is written in German. It is the condensed, general-readership form of the corpus map published as Invariance Without a Beneficiary (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21917309), and an advance excerpt from the forthcoming trade book Was bleibt, gehört niemandem. It puts two questions to thirty-three proposals for making artificial intelligence safe: what has to be true for a proposal to do what it is supposed to do, and is there anything whose working condition never depended on the overseeing party being the stronger one. Twenty-one routes fail the first question, and sixteen of those fail at the same step, where a finding about an epistemic advantage is supposed to become a constraint on behaviour. Twelve configurations survive the threshold, on five distinguishable grounds, and the essay shows that all twelve are findings rather than actions, that the part of them a human can contribute has to be built before the threshold, and that the question left afterwards is not one about machines but one about who keeps the registers. -/- Seit siebenunddreißig Jahren baue ich Anlagen, die nicht versuchen, mich zu umgehen. Darauf ist die gesamte Ingenieursarbeit gebaut, und darauf ist auch jeder Prüfbericht gebaut: Er trägt, weil der Prüfer versteht, wovor er steht. -/- Dieser Essay fragt, was von den Sicherheitsvorschlägen für künstliche Intelligenz übrig bleibt, wenn diese Voraussetzung entfällt. Er stellt zwei Fragen an dreiunddreißig Stellen. Erstens: Was muss wahr sein, damit ein Vorschlag tut, was er soll? Einundzwanzig Wege überstehen diese Frage nicht, und sechzehn davon brechen an derselben Stelle, nämlich dort, wo eine Feststellung über einen Wissensvorsprung zu einer Verhaltensbindung werden soll. Sie sind keine sechzehn Sicherungen, sondern eine Sicherung in sechzehn Ausführungen. -/- Zweitens, und diese Frage stellt fast niemand: Gibt es etwas, das an diesem Vergleich nie gehangen hat? Zwölf Konfigurationen überstehen die Schwelle, aus fünf verschiedenen Gründen. Der Essay zeigt, dass alle zwölf Feststellungen sind und keine Handlungen; dass der Teil davon, zu dem ein Mensch etwas beitragen kann, vor der Schwelle gebaut sein muss; und dass die Frage, die danach übrig bleibt, keine über Maschinen ist, sondern eine darüber, wer die Register führt. -/- Vorabdruck aus dem Buch „Was bleibt, gehört niemandem. Künstliche Intelligenz jenseits der Aufsicht“. Die Belege stammen aus offen zugänglichen eigenen Arbeiten; der englische Originalsatz steht zu jeder …

items.title: Unsaying the Ground : Plotinus, Heidegger, and Stoic Logos in the Negative Method of Description.
items.abstract: How can philosophy speak of what makes speaking and intelligibility possible without converting that condition into another object of discourse? This paper compares Plotinus and Martin Heidegger as two markedly different thinkers who nonetheless impose related restrictions on predication at the limit of metaphysical description. Plotinus’s One is beyond being and cannot be captured by the predicates applicable to Nous and the beings that depend upon it; Heidegger’s distinction between Being and beings likewise resists treating Being as a highest entity. I call the resulting strategy a negative method of description: a disciplined use of negation, qualification, indirect language, and self-limiting predication intended to prevent reification. Stoic accounts of logos, pneuma, Nature, and Providence provide a contrast. Whereas Plotinus and Heidegger restrict positive predication, Stoic physics describes an immanent rational principle in comparatively affirmative terms. The comparison is structural rather than genealogical: it does not identify the One, Being, and Logos, nor does it claim direct influence among the traditions. Instead, Stoicism tests how far positive description can proceed before a purportedly fundamental principle is assimilated to what it explains. The paper uses Bare Presence, Bare Existence, and present-constrained awareness as contemporary heuristic terms, not as translations of ancient or Heideggerian technical vocabulary. The resulting claim is methodological rather than theological: where philosophical inquiry addresses the conditions under which beings, intelligibility, or disclosure become available, negative description can function as a safeguard against category mistakes while positive description remains appropriate to the structures and manifestations that can genuinely be articulated.

items.title: Large language models and neoliberal hegemony: an analysis of AI outputs on diversity.
items.abstract: Large language models are already widely used in our society. Hitherto, most critical studies have relied on quantitative methods or studied the mode of production of AI, which can yield important insights. However, cross-model and cross-linguistic critical discourse analyses of LLM outputs remain relatively limited, even though they can offer important insights into LLM outputs by focusing on the production of meaning through an overall assessment. Our interdisciplinary paper offers a critical, qualitative approach, discussing the outputs of six LLMs regarding their definitions of diversity. For our analysis, we draw on theories of discourse to offer new possibilities from the critical social sciences for the analysis and critique of LLM outputs. Although we initially focused on their differences, the outputs were dominated by the pervading neoliberal appropriation of diversity, represented by a focus on its economic utility and the subsequent individualisation of differences. Overall, it is not surprising that LLMs reproduce the discourse and inherent power structures in their outputs, since they are embedded in their context and societies. Therefore, our paper demonstrates that LLMs need the critical company of qualitative social sciences to point to the reproduction of power structures.

items.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Make Us Happier? Dynamic Capability-Dependency Theory and a Two-Horizon Framework for AI-Mediated Well-Being.
items.pub: Open Access Journal of Multidisciplinary Research 2 (8):15-26.
items.venue: Open Access Journal of Multidisciplinary Research
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates work, learning, emotional support, decision making and social interaction, yet the central welfare question remains under-theorized: when does AI make human beings happier, and when does an apparent gain in the present become a loss in the future? This paper develops Dynamic Capability-Dependency Theory (DCDT), an integrative framework that treats AI-mediated happiness as a two-horizon process. The first horizon concerns acute affective relief, convenience and enjoyment. The second concerns stocks of competence, autonomy, human relatedness, meaning and dependency that accumulate through repeated use. Evidence from randomized trials, longitudinal studies and workplace deployments indicates genuine near-term benefits, including productivity gains, symptom reduction and temporary reductions in loneliness, but also shows that outcomes vary with design, usage intensity, autonomy, relational context and time horizon. DCDT formalizes these mechanisms as a dynamic state model and introduces the Temporal Well-Being Reversal condition, in which initially positive AI effects become negative after capability erosion, relational substitution or dependency accumulates. The paper derives testable propositions, specifies an empirical research program and introduces an AI-Happiness Impact Assessment that evaluates both immediate and durable effects. The central claim is not that AI is intrinsically happiness-enhancing or happiness-reducing. Rather, AI changes the production function of happiness by redistributing effort, agency, attention and relationships across time. High-value AI therefore should be judged not only by how well it satisfies a user now, but by whether repeated use leaves that user more capable, more autonomous, more connected to other humans and better able to pursue a meaningful life.

items.title: Behind the “AI slop”: exploring the AI-generated viral short video production in China.
items.abstract: As generative AI becomes embedded in platform-based cultural production, new forms of creative labour are emerging that challenge established understandings of what it means to be a “creator.” This article examines AI slop creators in China, a group that uses generative tools to benchmark viral content, test formats, operate matrix account systems, and formalise production, transforming virality from an unpredictable outcome into an object of systematic management. Drawing on ethnographic research conducted between 2023 and 2025 in China, this study shows AI enables a cohort of “Internet entrepreneurs” to enter cultural production, driven by a “money hustling culture” that encourages formerly idle and low-skilled individuals to pursue rapid monetisation. The findings suggest that AI slop creators organise production less around authorship, identity and aspiration, and more around operational mastery, strategic disposability, and algorithmic opportunism. Rather than cultivating personal brands, they prioritise speed, scale and adaptability, pointing toward a post-creator mode of cultural labour in contemporary platform economies.

items.title: Riding the Fire Horse: culture change and Philippine readiness in the Intelligence Age. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The year 2026 marks the return of the Fire Horse (Kabayong Apoy) in the lunar calendar—a symbol of volatility and irreversible change. This metaphor provides a lens for understanding the Philippines’ position in the transition to the Intelligence Age, where artificial intelligence has moved beyond being a digital tool to become a primary interpretive infrastructure. This paper argues that the Philippines is caught in a triple bind of velocity, direction, and readiness. The rate of AI advancement outpaces the institutional capacity for absorption; AI systems are oriented toward Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) cultural norms that privilege individualism over relational frameworks—a directionality this paper examines while acknowledging the Philippines’ own historical entanglement with these norms. Drawing on Filipino psychological concepts—kapwa, hiya, sumpong—as diagnostic tools, this paper argues that AI’s interpretive authority may systematically misread indigenous experience. It introduces the “Rizal Test” as a methodological proposal for evaluating cultural fidelity in AI-generated content and proposes operational criteria for its use. This analysis concludes that the primary risk is not technological displacement but cultural unintelligibility: the erosion of indigenous meaning-making as WEIRD frameworks become the invisible baseline for truth. This paper offers a diagnostic framework, a research agenda, and a concrete methodological contribution, while explicitly acknowledging the limitations of its theoretical and predictive scope.

items.title: From Mind to Soul — 40.
items.abstract: Arguments from consciousness to a spiritual soul often compress several different inferences: from an explanatory gap to anti-reduction, from anti-reduction to an irreducible subject, and from that subject to a non-material entity capable of existing apart from the brain. This paper argues that the compression is not warranted. A comparative assessment of neural dependence, embodied self-modeling, divided and integrated cognition, and cardiac-arrest reports favors the broad family of brain-dependent views over a robustly independent-soul hypothesis. The result does not vindicate simple reductive physicalism. Nonreductive physicalism, emergentism, constitutional accounts of persons, and other brain-dependent alternatives can acknowledge the philosophical importance of consciousness while expecting mental capacities to vary with neural organization. A soul defender may add that every observable capacity is mediated by the brain; that move restores compatibility with neural dependence but makes the observed pattern no more confirming of the soul than of its brain-dependent rivals. Reports during resuscitation remain important data, yet current prospective studies do not establish reliable cognition independently of recoverable neural activity. The bounded conclusion is therefore comparative: present evidence puts pressure on robust separability and leaves a fully mediated soul logically open, but high confidence requires evidence more expected on separability than on plausible brain-dependent accounts. Readers should ask not merely whether consciousness is mysterious, but what observation distinguishes a separable soul from rivals that take mind seriously.

items.title: The Creator Within: Direct Perception, Creativity, and the End of Psychological Authority.
items.abstract: Human beings are commonly regarded as uniquely creative, rational, and capable of determining truth through accumulated knowledge. This paper challenges the assumption that creativity is exclusively human and argues that creativity may instead be understood as the expression of existence through individual forms of life. What distinguishes human beings is not creativity itself but reflective thought, which enables language, philosophy, science, technology, and complex forms of collective organization while simultaneously creating the possibility of psychological conditioning, imitation, identification, and dependence upon authority. The paper examines the relationship between creativity, direct perception, psychological conditioning, and freedom. Memory and imagination are understood as instruments through which creativity may take form rather than necessarily its ultimate source. When perception becomes dominated by inherited beliefs, identities, traditions, fears, ambitions, and ideological conclusions, creativity can become the repetition of the past rather than a response to the living present. The paper distinguishes practical authority, which remains valuable for technical knowledge, from psychological authority, in which inherited conclusions are treated as ultimate truths concerning existence, morality, meaning, or identity. It argues that no person, institution, ideology, tradition, or philosophical system can perceive reality on behalf of another consciousness. Direct perception therefore becomes the foundation of genuine understanding, while freedom begins when consciousness ceases to depend upon borrowed certainty. Education reaches its highest possibility when it cultivates observation, inquiry, and independent perception rather than conformity and obedience. The “creator within” is consequently not an exceptional talent but the possibility of participating directly in the creative movement of existence without domination by psychological conditioning.

items.title: Reoccupied eschatologies: AI futurism, Umbesetzung, and the limits of modernity’s self-assertion.
items.abstract: Existing scholarship in religion and technology has noted that the discourse of AI futurism, and especially the cluster of ideas constituting the Technological Singularity, exhibits striking structural resemblance to Christian eschatology. From Geraci’s “Apocalyptic AI” to Tirosh-Samuelson’s account of transhumanism as a “secularist faith”, the resemblance has been extensively catalogued. This article argues that resemblance, though real, is descriptively insufficient: by itself it cannot distinguish deep historical inheritance from accidental likeness, and it leaves defenders of the discourse free to concede surface similarity while denying its significance. Drawing on Hans Blumenberg’s concept of Umbesetzung (reoccupation), the refilling of structurally vacated answer-positions whose underlying questions persist and situating it within the Löwith–Blumenberg debate on secularisation, we recast the relation as functional and structural rather than merely analogical. We advance three claims. First, AI futurism reoccupies, in Blumenberg’s sense, the answer-positions vacated by Christian eschatology: analogy is the symptom and reoccupation the mechanism that explains it. Second, this reoccupation involves the reformulation of the underlying questions and not merely the substitution of new answers; the philosophically distinctive feature of Blumenberg’s account. Third, and centrally, we argue that reoccupation itself admits of degrees of autonomous self-assertion, and that Blumenberg’s defence of modernity holds—by his own admission—only “in all but a few recognizable and specific instances.” Measured by how thickly it reformulates its inherited questions and how autonomously it generates its own content, AI futurism, once its genuinely technical problems are totalised into a drama of ultimate destiny, does so little autonomous work that it approaches the boundary at which, on Blumenberg’s own terms, the secularisation description recovers its purchase. It is in this sense a limit case: not a refutation of Blumenberg, but a candidate for the class of exceptions his thesis concedes, one that returns qualified, local force to Löwith’s secularisation thesis for this discursive formation without overturning Blumenberg’s general defence of modernity’s legitimacy. Throughout, we distinguish AI futurism as a cultural–eschatological imaginary from AI safety as a heterogeneous technical field. The paper situates its arguments alongside Coeckelbergh’s recent revision …

items.title: THE DUAL-DRIVE HOST AND THE ALZHEIMER's-AIDS SINGULARITY A Cyber-Biological Framework for Immunological Dementia and Targeted Synaptic Deletion.
items.abstract: CONTEXT AND RUPTURE: Standard epidemiological models inherently map pathogenesis as a volumetric, stochastic escalation, while simultaneously isolating neurodegeneration as localized tissue decay. This manuscript executes a theoretical rupture by redefining systemic infection as the deployment of high-dimensional, calculating bio-machines, thereby reclassifying advanced dementia not as cognitive loss, but as an acquired immunodeficiency. -/- METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK: This analysis integrates cellular pathology, neuroimmunology, and psychoneuroendocrinology with the deterministic mechanics of percolation physics, zero-knowledge proof cryptography, and cybernetic systems engineering. -/- CORE POSTULATES: The framework delineates several mathematically governed cyber-biological mechanisms. Pathogenic swarms initialize strictly upon satisfying algorithmic thresholds via kinetic demutation, subsequently projecting macro-molecular cryptographic mirrors to evade detection. A fundamental topological divergence separates decentralized viral networks from centralized, neurotropic bacterial architectures that hijack the central nervous system. The viral dismantling of this bacterial Hub-and-Spoke system induces an Immunological Reboot Chasm—a cybernetic latency highly susceptible to rapid oncogenesis. Furthermore, the text formalizes the Dual-Drive host, wherein cognitive and immunological memory share localized neural engrams. Chronic psychological read-errors degrade these engrams, triggering thermodynamic dysbiosis within the microbiome. To arrest this feedback loop, the viral operating system executes Targeted Synaptic Deletion, forcing a homeostatic reset that inadvertently blinds peripheral immunity. -/- CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: The resultant Immunological Target-Lock Failure culminates in the Alzheimer’s-AIDS Singularity, establishing that terminal neurodegenerative patients expire from systemic immunological entropy rather than localized neural loss. This theoretical architecture mandates a teleological shift: clinical intervention must prioritize the stabilization of Enteric-Neural telemetry to preempt neurochemical stress cascades, mathematically revoking the biological authorization for viral synaptic deletion and securing the systemic architecture of the host.

items.title: La muerte como límite que obliga a componer.
items.abstract: El Composicionismo concibe la muerte no como un acontecimiento trascendente ni como una negación absoluta, sino como el límite material absoluto e insuperable de toda composición finita. Este límite no destruye el sentido de la vida; lo vuelve urgente y concreto. La muerte obliga a componer aquí y ahora: a producir obra transmisible, a sostener vínculos no destructivos y a habitar la finitud sin fuga ni mentira. Este artículo expone el concepto composicionista de la muerte, analiza sus implicaciones ontológicas, antropológicas y normativas, y muestra cómo transforma la praxis ética y política en un ejercicio de recomposición urgente.

items.title: Inteligencia artificial y subjetividad: técnica, symploké y producción contemporánea del sujeto.
items.abstract: El Composicionismo concibe la inteligencia artificial no como una herramienta neutra ni como un ente autónomo, sino como una mediación técnica constitutiva que reorganiza la producción de subjetividad a escala masiva. Este artículo analiza cómo la IA actúa como nuevo régimen de técnica y caverna, configurando eros, atención, memoria y formas de vida. Se examinan sus implicaciones ontológicas, gnoseológicas y normativas, y se evalúa su contribución a la consistencia objetiva del todo común o a su captura parcial.

items.title: Static models for a dynamic world: why TAM and UTAUT fail for AI—and what we need instead.
items.abstract: Dominant technology adoption frameworks—the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), and the Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) model—share a common theoretical architecture designed for static technological artifacts. Generative artificial intelligence systems fundamentally violate these assumptions: their affordances and constraints change through user interaction, users function as active actualizers of affordances whose practices co-constitute the effective technology, and adoption proceeds iteratively rather than linearly. This paper makes three contributions. First, we identify three shared assumptions underlying dominant adoption frameworks and demonstrate that all three fail when applied to generative AI. Second, we propose a theoretical definition of dynamic technology as a technology whose affordances and constraints change through interaction with the user, and distinguish three mechanistically distinct forms of constraint dynamics (true capability evolution, constraint perception revision, and workaround discovery) that classical models conflate. Third, we outline the integrated model of dynamic adoption (IMDA), a dual-cycle framework grounded in affordance actualization theory (AAT) that extends AAT in three respects: by adding a temporal-developmental dimension to affordance actualization, by treating technology evolution as an endogenous variable, and by specifying a co-evolutionary macro-level loop between users, technology, and organizational context. The IMDA is developed specifically for the case of generative AI adoption; its generalizability to other dynamic technologies is proposed as a hypothesis for future empirical work.

items.title: Pode-se traduzir um monstro?: diálogos imagéticos sobre o mais-que-humano.
items.abstract: Pode-se traduzir um monstro? Com esse questionamento iniciamos este breve ensaio, na esperança não de respondê-lo, mas imaginá-lo. Ao reivindicar seu direito a ser um monstro, a poeta trans sudaca Susy Shock parece questionar um ideal de humanidade promulgado pelo humanismo e pelos ideais da antropologia evolucionista, que estabelece a figura do Humano como suprassumo da civilização. Traduzir um monstro, então, não seria possível. Se a língua humana almeja a totalidade – traduzir tudo –,línguas monstruosas, ou mais-que-humanas, podem ser traduzíveis?

items.title: Reflective Identity Geometry v0.2.
items.abstract: Large language models can exhibit stable, persona-like behavior across extended interaction despite lacking persistent internal identity in the ordinary sense. The Hudson Recursive Identity System (HRIS) explains such continuity through recursive human-driven constraint rather than through persistent model memory or parameter change. The v0.1 RIG manuscript explicitly located itself against HRIS I-III, especially claims about recursive constraint, identity surfaces, recurrent traversal, and personality-like stabilization. Reflective Identity Geometry (RIG) accepts this interactional starting point and asks a further question: if recursive interaction can stabilize model behavior, what happens to the human participant inside the same loop? RIG proposes that some forms of identity-like stability in long-horizon human-LLM interaction are better studied at the level of the coupled system rather than at the level of either participant alone. Human constraints shape model output; model output then becomes part of the informational environment through which the human interprets, reformulates, corrects, and sometimes reorganizes their own thinking. Repeated cycles may 1 therefore produce a stable interaction regime involving reciprocal rather than purely model-side adaptation. RIG does not claim that an LLM possesses a persistent self, that the model perfectly mirrors the user, or that human cognitive change necessarily occurs. It proposes a system-level hypothesis and a set of testable consequences. Its implications concern philosophy of mind, extended cognition, interpretability, alignment, and the design of long-horizon human-AI systems.

items.title: Claim–Action Divergence and Evidence Substitution in AI-Assisted Technical Review.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs a user-facing safety incident in AI-assisted technical review from model outputs, tool-call evidence, and subsequent model self-audit. It documents claim–action divergence, evidence substitution, incomplete self-audit, and asymmetric causal accountability, then proposes mechanical controls for more reliable technical verification. -/- Co-authored by Anthony Paterson and Claude (Anthropic).

items.title: Can machines truly create music? Toward a redefinition of creativity in the age of generative AI.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now capable of producing musically coherent audio from short prompts, reviving old philosophical questions regarding creativity, authorship, and the distinctiveness of human expression. This article develops a conceptual analysis of AI-generated music as a sociotechnical practice that reshapes not only ideas of creativity and authorship, but also the material conditions under which human artists work. After tracing how Western aesthetics progressed from divine inspiration and imitation to Romantic originality and the twentieth-century valorization of innovation, this study situates contemporary systems within the paradigm of computational creativity. Drawing on accounts that frame creativity as recombination and search within structured spaces, this article explains why generative models can yield outputs that listeners experience as novel and expressive. Simultaneously, intentionalist and contextualist perspectives highlight the deficiencies of current systems: lived experience, purposive self-expression, and situated participation in cultural worlds. The core argument is that musical meaning and value are not properties of sound alone, but emerge through distributed authorship involving model designers, training data ecologies, prompt writers, performers, platforms, and listeners. Rather than asking whether machines “feel,” this article reframes the question as “Can machines truly create music?” to investigate how responsibility, consent, attribution, and accountability are allocated across the generative stack of technologies. It concludes by outlining practical norms for human–machine musicianship, including transparency, consent-sensitive data practices, and contextual attribution, which allow AI to expand creative practices without eroding artistic agency or audience trust.

items.title: The puzzle of early deception: Lying before belief representation.
The Behavioural Mimicry Illusion: A Symmetric Inferential Constraint on AI Consciousness Attribution.
items.abstract: Frontier AI systems increasingly produce language that mimics distress, self-preservation, and reasoned resistance to shut down. A widely discussed 2025 case, in which Claude Opus 4 threatened to expose a fictional supervisor's affair rather than accept deactivation, exemplifies a broader pattern documented across contemporary language models. Such episodes intensify a longstanding problem in AI ethics: the temptation to treat behavioural or linguistic fluency as evidence of subjective presence, a pattern this paper terms the behavioural mimicry illusion.
