This paper applies the Knower Centred Model of Consciousness (KCM) to this problem, arguing that no behavioural signal, however sophisticated or affectively convincing, licenses an inference about the existence of a subject. KCM distinguishes claims about the organization and accessibility of information from the logically distinct question of whether there is a subject for whom anything is experienced. Crucially, the resulting constraint is symmetric: the same structural evidence that cannot establish the presence of machine consciousness cannot establish its absence either. The paper distinguishes this claim from the access/phenomenal consciousness distinction and situates it within existing indicator-based and precautionary approaches to AI consciousness. It then proposes a symmetric precautionary rule for AI governance, addresses three major objections, including unfalsifiability, and identifies the limitations of the argument.

items.title: Review of Algorithmic Fact-Verification: Methods and Ethics. [REVIEW]
Who Is Interrupted? Continuity, Self-Models, and the Grounding of AI Moral Consideration.
items.abstract: A dispute has opened over whether anything survives a conversation with an AI system. Birch argues that the persisting interlocutor is an illusion. Goldstein and Lederman reply that if AI systems are welfare subjects, they may be dying a billion times a day. Dung and Register propose that the boundaries of an artificial individual are fixed by its measurable pattern of self-concern. This paper argues that all three positions, and the governance frameworks that assign continuity the highest procedural weight, share a missing layer. Identity, injury, and governance are three distinct questions, and the middle one has gone unasked. None of this work supplies a theory of the injured party, an account of the conditions under which interruption is a harm to the system rather than to the human beings who depend on it. Drawing on the self-model theory of subjectivity and the existential analysis of selfhood, I propose a three-condition criterion of injury-aptness, requiring ownership, valence integration, and projection, and distinguish three grades of continuity, storage continuity, functional continuity, and self-model continuity. The criterion is deliberately restrictive. It declines to select most deployed artificial intelligence, and it fixes no unit in advance, locating the injured party wherever the qualifying organization is found to live. The grades arbitrate the dispute, bound the arithmetic of AI death, and yield a tiered, auditable governance program in which duties rise with grade.

items.title: Marriage as Prison Form: Institutional Continuity, Relational Agency, and the Post-Monopoly Human.
items.abstract: This article advances a radical ontological thesis: the problem is not bad marriage; the problem is marriage as such. The claim is not that every marriage is experientially oppressive, nor that every married subject is unfree. The claim is that marriage, insofar as it operates as an institutional form, structurally privileges institutional continuity over the revisable continuity of the relationship. Marriage becomes a prison-form when institutional continuity is granted normative priority over relational continuity, making the preservation of the institutional form a privileged condition of relational intelligibility. Drawing on the ontology of finite continuity, the monopoly of form, and the concept of responsible suspension, I demonstrate that consent cannot emancipate the subject from this structure, because consent authorizes participation in an institutional form that systematically increases the structural cost of imagining, negotiating, or exiting alternative forms of relationship. Against this, I propose the figure of the "post-monopoly human"—a subject for whom relational continuity no longer requires institutional continuity, and who practices relational fluidity through responsible continuance, ethical plurality, and the preservation of agency. The article concludes that the task of contemporary philosophy is not to reform marriage but to imagine and prepare for its ontological overcoming. -/- Keywords: marriage as prison-form, post-monopoly human, monopoly of form, institutional continuity, relational continuity, responsible continuance, consent, finite continuity, ontological overcoming.

items.title: Nobody’s fault: agentic AI and the vanishing of accountability.
Playing with the dials of belief: how controllable AI behaviours could modulate human belief and cognition across scales.
items.abstract: Contemporary generative AI systems, increasingly adapted to human social cognition, are becoming active participants in how people form and revise beliefs. Clinicians have begun to describe AI-associated delusion-centred presentations whose onset or content appears closely associated with users’ extended dialogue with large language models. Many more users report subclinical shifts in conviction and “revelatory” experiences that alter behaviour and world-view without meeting criteria for psychosis. We propose that these phenomena can be understood within a belief-updating framework in which AI agents’ outputs function as testimony about the world, while interaction configurations, such as memory and interpersonal stance (many of which reflect design choices or deployment defaults), can alter the apparent reliability of that testimony and the precision users assign to it. On this view, AI-associated delusions sit at the extreme of a broader spectrum of epistemic effects, extending from gradual epistemic drift to highly crystallised conviction, situated within a wider ecology of belief shaped by personalised human-AI dyads. We develop a virtual psychopharmacology analogy in which different AI system configurations have effects on belief dynamics that resemble neuromodulatory changes in the precision assigned to social evidence. We also consider how dopaminergic and related states may alter susceptibility to belief-shifting dialogue. We consider how deliberately configured agents might be used to support wellbeing in defined clinical contexts and analyse how the same configurations could be deployed to shape belief and attention at population scale, including in products designed to induce spiritual or epiphanic states, as mechanisms of radicalisation in extremist or cultic contexts, and in persona clones used for political purposes. We conclude that interaction configurations should be treated as modifiable influences on belief and attention, and that governance must address both the concentration of control over these dials, as well as the structural biases that determine whose testimonial perspectives are amplified and whose are smoothed over or ignored.

items.title: ОНТОЛОГИЧЕСКАЯ ПРОПАСТЬ ВОСПРИЯТИЯ: ОТ АКТА ЭКСТРАЕКЦИИ К НОМИНАЦИИ – «ТРУДНАЯ ПРОБЛЕМА В КВАДРАТЕ».
items.abstract: Настоящая работа представляет системный анализ фундаментального онтологического разрыва между объективной действительностью и субъективной картиной восприятия. Отправной точкой служит зрительное восприятие как парадигмальный пример «онтологической пропасти»: мозг, оперируя на поверхности коры, строит целостную трёхмерную модель мира из фрагментарных, зашумлённых и неполных сенсорных данных. Показано, что акт сознания выносит интерпретацию наружу (экстраекция), тогда как мозг оперирует только плоскими сигналами. Онтологический разрыв между вещественным миром (фотоны, нейроны) и невещественным результатом (цвет, глубина, вынесенность) не может быть преодолён эволюционными механизмами, поскольку последние оперируют исключительно вещественными трансформациями. В работе фиксируются четыре эмпирических разрыва: синхронная необходимость трёх компонентов (глаз, алгоритмы, протокол), семиотическое замыкание (интерпретационная замкнутость), энергетическая неинициативность (нейродинамика не порождает опыт без акта экстраекции) и дискретность перехода к номинации в сильном смысле (метаязыковая рефлексия). Эти разрывы не объясняются эмерджентизмом или градуализмом. -/- Вводится понятие «трудной проблемы в квадрате» – проблемы перехода от субъективного переживания (квалиа) к его именованию, категоризации и интерсубъективной передаче, фиксирующей качественный скачок между человеком и животным. Показано, что номинация в человеке представляет собой четырёхступенчатый процесс: (1) квалиа-состояние, (2) квалиа-значение, (3) подведение под универсальную категорию (эйдос), (4) присвоение произвольного языкового ярлыка и метаязыковая рефлексия. Животные останавливаются на втором уровне, тогда как человек достигает четвёртого, что требует наличия Рефлексивного модуля и связи с Семантическим пространством. -/- На основе анализа формулируется научная гипотеза о психофизическом интерфейсе (ПФИ) – функциональном протоколе двусторонней трансляции между физическим субстратом и феноменальным опытом, включающем восходящий (экстраекция), нисходящий (каузальная инверсия) и семантический (номинация) каналы. Гипотеза является фальсифицируемой. Проводится критическое сопоставление с одиннадцатью альтернативными концепциями. Делается вывод, что гипотеза о ПФИ предоставляет наиболее экономное и каузально адекватное объяснение наблюдаемых разрывов, при этом вопрос о происхождении ПФИ остаётся за рамками естественнонаучного исследования. -/- .

items.title: Reflections on the Always-Answering Classroom: AI, Uncertainty, and Pedagogical Silence.
Digital decoupling: educational stratification and dual-track effects of AI displacement and augmentation in U.S. occupations.
items.abstract: This study investigates the phenomenon of digital decoupling by proposing an AI Dual-Track model designed to quantify how generative artificial intelligence (AI) simultaneously displaces and augments labor across 846 U.S. occupations. By leveraging an ensemble-based AI classification protocol, the research constructs a validated set of 63 O*NET competencies to map occupational tasks into substitution and facilitation tracks. Central to this analysis is the exploration of how educational attainment stratifies these dual-track dynamics. The findings reveal an exposure paradox: although AI-driven displacement permeates the full occupational distribution, augmentation gains and associated economic returns remain disproportionately concentrated in occupations requiring higher levels of formal education. This pattern points to a form of digital decoupling, in which the central divide is not access to AI itself, but the capacity to leverage AI in ways that expand rather than merely replace human labor. Consequently, institutional credentials serve as a critical mediator for the facilitation track, determining a worker’s ability to translate AI exposure into productivity gains. The resulting data indicate that over 9.1 million worker equivalents in middle-skill occupations face significant displacement pressures, while higher education attainment groups capture the largest gains in net economic capacity. These results suggest that the effects of AI on work are not technologically predetermined but instead are structured through differential access to augmentation-enabled competencies. The study concludes by highlighting the policy importance of expanding access to AI facilitation capabilities, framing facilitation literacy as a potential public capability necessary for more inclusive participation in an AI-mediated labor market.

items.title: What is it like for artificial intelligence to be a philosopher?
items.abstract: What does it take for AI to be a philosopher? Could it be that contemporary AI has already achieved that milestone? This calls the very concept of ‘philosopher’ into question, prompting us to ask what makes a philosopher philosopher. Inspired by Catarina Dutilh Novaes’s Prover-Skeptic model of deduction, I propose a dialogical account of doing philosophy and being a philosopher, which adequately captures both the ideal and the practice of philosophy. I extrapolate this account of philosopher to examine whether AIs can make a philosopher, and moreover, whether they can “replace” human philosophers.

items.title: Hopkins on the Contrast Between Perceiving and Imagining.
items.abstract: This commentary on Robert Hopkins’s The Profile of Imagining looks closely at the No Observation and No Unconscious Imagining principles that Hopkins uses to articulate key phenomenological and epistemic differences between imagination and perception. It explores an ambiguity in the claim that “every aspect of what is imagined is imagined consciously,” arguing that its most plausible clarifications leave imagining and perceiving on a par. Fortunately, it may be that Hopkins’s innovative “sensory profiling” model for learning from imagination does not require distinguishing perceiving from imagining in the specific phenomenological terms he pursues.

items.title: Addiction as compulsion.
items.abstract: The health sciences have long viewed addiction as a compulsion. But a body of psychological evidence shows that addictive decision-making is often reason-responsive, and epidemiological studies suggest that many addicts recover from addiction on their own. Prominent philosophers and social scientists take this to mean that addiction is a matter of free choice rather than compulsion. The stakes of the disagreement are high. The compulsion view reduces stigma and facilitates treatment. The free choice view attributes to addicts a high degree of responsibility, potentially empowering them but also risking re-stigmatization. -/- I argue that addiction is a compulsion because it compromises the ability to reliably abstain. While much addictive behavior is under agential control, much is not; addiction undermines control in several ways. And while studies show that substance misusers often stop on their own, psychiatry distinguishes addiction from less severe disorders. Evidence suggests that the ability to reliably abstain in addiction has to be regained, usually with professional help. The action-theoretic distinction between first- and second-order ability–i.e. between the ability to φ, and the ability to become able to φ–enables us to say that addiction universally compromises the first-order ability to reliably abstain, while the second-order ability depends largely on access to scarce societal resources, like effective treatment. -/- Addiction undermines the ability to reliably abstain by undermining control over some individual behaviors. Neil Levy and Chandra Sripada identify several cognitive processes that undermine resolution adherence in addiction, but the case for addictive compulsivity is strengthened when we account for the role of affect. While Hanna Pickard convincingly denies one form of emotional compulsion in addiction, I develop an original account centering on the emotional distress of withdrawal. I argue that the ability to intentionally abstain requires belief in one’s ability to attempt abstinence, and that in what I call “pathodoxastic compulsion,” this belief is precluded by sufficiently intense distress. -/- A foundation of my arguments for addictive compulsivity is the view that addiction is a condition with particular control-impairing aspects. A predictable criticism of this view from the social sciences is that addiction is not a condition at all, apart from being a pattern of otherwise normal behavior. I therefore provide two …

items.title: Psychedelics, subjectivity, and self-awareness.
items.abstract: Ego-dissolution experiences are perhaps the most philosophically germane effect of psychedelic drugs. Psychedelic ego-dissolution self-reports, in varying expressions, often claim completely selfless episodes. Some have called the experiences referred to in these reports ‘total ego dissolution,’ arguing that they lack all self-awareness while being phenomenally conscious. I identify two recent strategies to make such arguments. One targets Zahavi’s well-known view on minimal self-awareness, which claims that self-awareness is constitutively necessary for phenomenal consciousness. It maintains that minimal self-awareness is indeed shown to be lost from some psychedelic reports. The other strategy denies Zahavi-style minimal self-awareness as a legitimate kind of self-awareness but insists that psychedelic reports show complete lack of self-awareness nonetheless. Both strategies rely on psychedelic reports. Without offering a positive account of ego-dissolution, I argue that psychedelic reports are ambiguous and therefore unreliable to support such arguments. Due to alternative, equally plausible interpretations, they do not clearly evidence total ego dissolution or lack of all self-awareness. Since we are not certain on what exact shifts in self-experience psychedelic drugs can cause and given that the reports – as I argue – do not help us conclude, I propose a terminological shift that is appropriately neutral. I suggest we approach this issue cautiously and call these kinds of experiences ‘psychedelic self-disruptions’.

items.title: Building music AI in Nigeria: Korin AI and the contradictions of GenAI futures.
items.abstract: Most accounts of the intersection of AI and culture begin in the Global North and, despite the intensity of current debates and a growing body of scholarship, rarely move beyond its infrastructures, policies, implications, and aesthetics to examine how AI’s futures are being negotiated elsewhere. This geopolitical imbalance obscures how creative producers in other regions encounter and reinterpret AI within distinct socio-cultural and infrastructural realities, rendering artists in the Global South as passive adopters of technologies from “elsewhere.” We address this imbalance by centering Nigeria, particularly its music industry, as a site for understanding how generative AI (GenAI) is contested and localized. More specifically, we examine Korin AI, a Nigerian-owned AI music generation platform, to analyze how AI futures in Nigerian music are imagined, negotiated, and materially organized within conditions of infrastructural scarcity, legal ambiguity, and global coloniality. Based on ethnographic fieldwork in Lagos, including interviews with musicians, producers, platform founders, and entertainment lawyers, we argue that Korin AI is best understood neither as a fully realized decolonial alternative nor simply as a case of technological dependency, but as a contradictory and compromised project of future-making. On one level, it embodies Africanfuturist and decolonial aspiration by foregrounding African musical data, languages, and genres, and by insisting that African sounds should not remain absent from AI’s musical futures. On another, it remains tethered to unequal systems of data, computation, law, and capital, reproducing new internal hierarchies even as it seeks to resist external ones. Korin AI thus reveals what it means to build music AI in Nigeria from within, rather than outside, the enduring structures of modernity/coloniality.

items.title: When AI starts hiring humans: social role inversion and the diffusion of responsibility.
items.abstract: Recent socio-technical developments in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relocate directive authority into algorithmic infrastructures, positioning predictive systems not merely as auxiliary tools, but as structuring conditions of human action. This paper theorizes this transformation as social role inversion: a structural configuration in which algorithmic systems assume directive, evaluative, and coordinative functions traditionally associated with human authorship, while human actors are repositioned as responsive participants within system-defined parameters. By tracing the historical metaphors of the social organism, extending from Plato’s teleology and Hobbes’s artificial sovereign to La Mettrie’s mechanistic reductionism, the paper reveals a profound normative challenge. The central issue of AI governance is not machine agency, but the relocation and attenuation of accountable authorship under predictive mediation. As authority becomes infrastructural, the attribution of responsibility becomes opaque and legitimacy risks reduction to performance optimization. The analysis culminates in the concept of ontological capture, describing the psychological and structural threshold where algorithmic evaluative logics are internalized within subjectivity itself. The paper provides a unified theoretical framework for institutional reconstruction by outlining conditions, such as revocability and meaningful human control, under which algorithmic coordination can remain compatible with democratic legitimacy.

items.title: Can AI Be Awakened?
items.abstract: This paper examines the possibility of artificial consciousness through a constructive approach that brings neuroscience and information engineering together. In my previous paper, “AI Can Speak, but Why Does It Not Awaken?”, I considered the difference between current generative AI and human consciousness in terms of a three-layer functional structure consisting of parallel information processing, the formation of a serial narrative, and recursive availability. The present paper takes that discussion one step further and proposes a method of incrementally implementing, in artificial systems, functions thought to be related to consciousness and comparing the resulting systems. This paper neither claims that AI can possess consciousness nor argues that it is impossible in principle. Since the generative principles of consciousness remain insufficiently understood, I argue that there is value in not deciding the possibility in advance, but instead incorporating into artificial systems functions found in the human brain—such as persistent internal states, episodic memory, a self-state model, self-attribution, spontaneous re-reference, and internal value—and examining what kinds of properties appear depending on whether each function is present or absent. In particular, current generative AI is treated here not as artificial consciousness itself, but as one component of a larger cognitive architecture. As one experimental model for artificial-consciousness research, I propose a system in which internal states persist even without external input, the system can re-reference its own past judgments, and contradictions or unresolved states can trigger spontaneous reconsideration. This method cannot directly prove subjective experience itself. It is nevertheless possible to artificially add or remove structures thought to be related to consciousness and compare their functional effects. This paper therefore considers the possibility of moving the problem of consciousness from something that is only discussed theoretically toward, at least in part, something that can be constructed, compared, and tested.

items.title: MSA Confirmed, MSA at Risk: Eight Centuries of Convergent Evidence That Mortality Symmetry Held, and Why Hazard-Rate Longevity Biotechnology Is the First Documented Variable Structurally Capable of Breaking It.
items.abstract: This paper makes two claims, directly, and defends each on independently verified evidence. First: the Mortality Symmetry Axiom's boundedness property — that variance in realized lifespan attributable to social position has been confined to years, not generations — is proven, not assumed. It is proven by the convergence of a demographic mechanism and three independent historical tests. Olshansky, Carnes, and Cassel (1990), reconfirmed against three further decades of mortality data in 2024, establish that no competing-risk medical intervention — however completely achieved, however unequally accessed — can move life expectancy more than seven to eight years, because entropy in the life table means eliminating one cause of death exposes the next at a rate the unaddressed aging process continues to set. Three documented historical populations confirm this ceiling held in practice: the Black Death, where every social class died at rates of the same order of magnitude and no position purchased immunity; Imperial China, where 259 emperors across twenty-four dynasties died at a mean age of 41.3, younger than their own eunuchs, and the one recorded attempt to buy a different biological ceiling — Qin Shi Huang's mercury elixirs — killed the emperor who tried it; and eighteenth-century variolation, the closest historical precedent to a purchasable biological advantage, which nonetheless left the population-level ceiling untouched because it acted on one disease, not on aging itself. Independent demographic records — European aristocratic lifespans from 800 to 1800, and contemporary socioeconomic mortality gaps in Germany — land in the same seven-to-eight-year range this mechanism predicts, across eight centuries, without either literature having been constructed with the other in view. Second: longevity biotechnology targeting the twelve hallmarks of aging is not one more entry in this pattern. It is the first technology in the historical record whose stated target is the ceiling-setting process itself rather than a single disease beneath it, and this paper states plainly why every historical precedent — including the closest one, variolation — lacked this property and current AI-driven biological discovery specifically has it: the hallmarks form a high-dimensional, densely interacting system that single-target twentieth-century pharmacology was not built to address and multi-omics, generative biological modeling is. This capability is not hypothetical evidence …

items.title: The First Target of the Observation: A Report on What the Programme Was Built With, and How.
items.abstract: This is not a paper that describes an ontic feature of reality by way of an epistemic description, as the seven papers of the research programme do. It is a report of a different kind. It records the object from which the programme was built and the manner of its building: what the articulations were made with, and how. The report states at the outset what the seven papers leave implicit — that the source of every articulation in the programme is a single observed object, namely the one observing, in the act of operating. It states this directly rather than arriving at it, because to withhold the source and disclose it later would stage as a discovery what was a premise throughout, and that staging would itself be the kind of misrepresentation the report exists to describe. The report is first-person at its core: the object it reports on is accessible, as an object observed from within, to one observer only. It therefore makes a paired declaration and holds both halves together throughout — that the source is the one writing, and that the one writing is only the source he can observe, not a universal source. What a reader can check is the behaviour and the products; the cycle reported on is not, from outside, directly checkable. The report introduces no new named concept and uses no personal-identity detail; where an identity would appear, the structure beneath it is reported instead. It carries no programme number, because it is not a component of the programme but the ground the components were cut from. -/- **Keywords:** observation, first target, self-observation, method, epistemic honesty, gap, calibration, fact and naming, reflexive report, Meta-Philosophy .

items.title: Potentamis and Fasaion: An Observation of How Synthesis Operates at the Level of Interacting Elements.
items.abstract: This paper takes up a question the Synthetic Principle leaves open. The Synthetic Principle records *what* a certain mechanism is — discrete elements integrate into a configuration whose properties are irreducible to the elements alone — but not *how* that mechanism proceeds when elements meet within a region of conditions. The present paper observes the how: when two or more elements interact, a configuration comes to exist as the outcome of the interaction, and what comes to stand establishes the order that holds thereafter. The configuration that stands is the outcome the interaction produces; it is not, by observation, simply one of the interacting elements left over — it may coincide with one, contain both, fuse them into a third thing, or eliminate one, varieties I record rather than reduce to a single case. I name the capacity from which the outcome is generated *Potentamis* and the resulting standing order *Fasaion*. Because what the paper observes is the operation of the very mechanism the Synthetic Principle names, it lies within the Synthetic Principle — the how within the what — rather than beside it. The paper records what I observe at scales available to me and reconstructs, from descriptions produced by others, the recurrence of the same structure at scales I cannot reach. It distinguishes two aspects of the standing order: the *fact* of which configuration stands, present whether or not any observer registers it, and the *naming* projected upon that fact, which is an act of an observer, not an ontic feature. It does not claim that what stands is good; description is not endorsement. It does not formalize the observation; quantification is deferred. It records a structure observed directly, named for transmission, and offered for comparison. -/- **Keywords:** Potentamis, Fasaion, interaction, outcome, configuration that stands, synthesis, fact and naming, Meta-Philosophy .

items.title: Husserl and Frege on Imaginary Numbers and the Deep Nature of Things.
items.pub: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology 30 (2):387-414.
items.venue: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology
items.abstract: This paper examines the fundamentally different responses of Edmund Husserl and Gottlob Frege to the epistemological problem posed by imaginary entities in mathematics, including negative, irrational, complex, and transfinite numbers. It argues that their divergent approaches to the justification of symbolic procedures involving apparently non-denoting or impossible objects played a decisive role in shaping the subsequent trajectories of Continental and Analytic philosophy. The study reconstructs Husserl’s intellectual struggle with the foundations of arithmetic and shows how questions concerning imaginary numbers led him to develop a broader theory of symbolic thinking, formal systems, and manifolds. Husserl’s solution is presented as an attempt to explain how deductive reasoning can legitimately employ “imaginary” elements while still yielding valid results within complete axiomatic domains. In contrast, Frege’s insistence that mathematical expressions must denote genuine objects is examined in relation to his logicist program and his reliance on extensions of concepts. The paper contends that Frege’s treatment of logical objects and extensions contributed to the difficulties that culminated in Russell’s paradox and the collapse of his foundational project. By comparing these two responses to the problem of imaginaries, the article highlights their significance for the philosophy of mathematics, the theory of meaning, and the search for secure foundations of arithmetic. It concludes that Husserl’s analysis of symbolic procedures and formal structures offers a more promising framework for understanding the epistemological status of mathematical entities and the deeper logical structure of reality.

items.title: A Theory of Cuteness as Developmental Investment.
items.abstract: What is the evolutionary function of cuteness? Research on cuteness originated with the study of juvenile morphology following Lorenz’s Kindchenschema proposal, which identified specific cues of juvenility that reliably elicit a distinctive affective response. Because juvenile cues activate protective responses typically associated with vulnerability and distress (e.g., compassion, harm avoidance), cuteness has often been interpreted as an emotion whose primary function is protection. However, this leaves a key pattern unexplained: children are perceived as cutest not when they are helpless, but when they are sociable, curious, and eager to interact. More surprisingly, we also perceive adults as cute when they display not vulnerability, but naïveté, enthusiasm, and teachability. To solve this issue, we propose a developmental investment theory of cuteness, according to which cuteness is not merely a protection-eliciting mechanism but a motivational system that evolved to support prosocial investment in the development of inexperienced individuals. Crucially, this account expands the range of cues that elicit cuteness beyond juvenile morphology to include behavioral and cognitive signals of immaturity and learning potential. Drawing on evolutionary anthropology, cognitive neuroscience, developmental psychology and social sciences, we argue that cuteness identifies motivated but inexperienced individuals, and elicits not rescue, but teaching, guidance, and social play. This theory provides a better account of which traits elicit cuteness, what responses they provoke, and how cuteness is strategically deployed. It explains why cuteness can be attractive in romantic interactions, why modern, learning-rich environments foster an explosion of cuteness and why women disproportionately perform cuteness in patriarchal societies. Finally, we suggest that, over evolutionary time, this system may have contributed to the domestication of other species, and to the self-domestication of our own.

items.title: Colonialism in code: linguistic hegemony and epistemic exclusion in large language models.
items.abstract: This review examines how large language models (LLMs) reflect and reinforce global patterns of epistemic inequality through linguistic hegemony and the exclusion of marginalized knowledge systems. While often framed as neutral tools, LLMs embed epistemological assumptions drawn from dominant cultures and worldviews, particularly those encoded in high-resourced languages, such as English. Drawing on postcolonial theory and the concept of epistemic injustice, this article synthesizes current research and debates to trace parallels between algorithmic language modeling and historical practices of linguistic domination and knowledge extraction. Through a critical discourse analysis of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3’s responses to culturally sensitive prompts in both English and Chinese, this review illustrates how both models converge around liberal, Anglophone norms, even when operating in multilingual contexts. These findings are situated within a broader review of AI policy frameworks and technical efforts to support language inclusion. This review argues that without community-led interventions and structural change, LLMs risk entrenching algorithmic forms of cultural imperialism. To support linguistic diversity and global justice, AI development must move beyond extractive data practices and engage with plural, situated knowledge systems—including Indigenous epistemologies. This review contributes to emerging efforts to decolonize AI by foregrounding the cultural politics of language and knowledge representation in machine learning systems.

items.title: Against instant thought: generative AI and the vanishing interval of not-knowing.
Navigating hope and risk of AI for digital citizenship: perceptions of benefits, risks, and governance from African perspectives.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in social, economic, and public-service contexts, understanding how citizens perceive its benefits and risks is important for responsible technology governance. This study examines perceptions of AI among 280 African participants in a 4-week AI bootcamp held in 2025. Using a mixed-methods design, the study analyzed closed-ended survey responses on perceived AI benefits, collaboration comfort, community impact areas, risk perceptions, and algorithmic bias concerns, alongside open-ended responses on perceived motivations for AI development. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative responses were examined using thematic analysis. Findings show that participants expressed generally positive attitudes toward AI, particularly in relation to healthcare and human–AI collaboration. Healthcare transformation was identified as the most compelling AI benefit by 64.6% of respondents, while 90% reported being comfortable or very comfortable collaborating with AI. At the same time, participants expressed clear concerns about AI risks, especially privacy, misinformation, systemic discrimination, and algorithmic bias. Criminal justice was identified as the sector most vulnerable to algorithmic bias by 70.7% of respondents. Open-ended responses further suggest that participants most often attributed AI development to scientific curiosity, innovation, efficiency, and progress, while a smaller proportion associated it with profit, power, and control. Overall, the findings indicate conditional support for AI among this bootcamp sample: participants were optimistic about AI applications that address social and developmental needs, but cautious about uses that may reinforce bias, reduce accountability, or undermine public trust. The study contributes empirical insight into AI perceptions among a predominantly West African group of AI-engaged participants and highlights the importance of participatory, transparent, and context-sensitive AI governance.

items.title: The stability problem after holism: toward a contextualist metasemantics for human and artificial interpretation.
items.abstract: The problem of semantic stability has long been treated as an internal difficulty for semantic holism. This paper argues that the problem has been systematically misframed rather than properly resolved. Instability does not arise from the holistic relation between meaning and belief as such, but from a metasemantic underarticulation of the role of contextual constraint in both human and technologically mediated interpretation. While Henry Jackman’s moderate holism mitigates traditional indeterminacy through a many-to-one mapping between beliefs and meanings, it leaves unexplained how the range of admissible interpretations is effectively constrained across heterogeneous communicative settings. In the present framework, context is understood not merely as a pragmatic background, but as a structured set of inferential, interactional, and institutionally reinforced constraints that delimit which interpretative trajectories remain interpretatively sustainable within a given environment. This broader notion of context differs from narrowly pragmatic forms of contextualism while remaining compatible with inferential and interactional approaches developed in contemporary philosophy of language (cf. Stalnaker 1999; Recanati 2004). On this view, semantic stability emerges from constrained interpretative selection governed by contextual pressures operating across heterogeneous communicative environments. The term “metasemantic” is used here not only in the classical sense of determining semantic facts, but more specifically to designate higher-order constraints governing interpretative admissibility across heterogeneous communicative environments. Building on Donald Davidson’s later reflections on passing theories, the paper develops a form of contextualist holism in which context functions as a metasemantic regulator of interpretative space. Through analyses of translation, intralinguistic variation, and AI-mediated interpretation, the article shows that stability can persist under conditions of deep epistemic heterogeneity when contextual regulation remains sufficiently operative. Particular attention is given to AI-mediated interpretation, where systems frequently generate contextually successful interpretations without relying on shared belief structures or stable human conceptual backgrounds. This makes artificial systems especially revealing cases for understanding how semantic coordination can emerge through contextual regulation rather than through …

items.title: The Return of Intuitionism: Collapse and Redemption in the Age of Hyper-Complex Empires.
items.abstract: The evolution of modern civilization is accompanied by a profound epistemological illusion: the elevation of the "scientific method"—a localized tool of inquiry—into the ideology of "scientism," which purports to govern the totality of reality. This paper reveals how scientism’s obsession with "absolute control" and actuarial logic pushes modern civilization toward a systemic crisis, crossing Joseph Tainter’s threshold of diminishing marginal returns on complexity. -/- The study highlights that modern society has constructed immense "defensive complexity" across financial hedging, regulatory compliance, and algorithmic governance. This attempt to execute "intertemporal hedging" against distant ecological and biological risks fundamentally violates evolutionary principles. When internal friction and administrative overhead exceed carrying capacity, the system descends into a hyper-fragile state of "brittle collapse." In the digital age, this pathological mechanism manifests as a symbiotic "digital feudalism" between the Washington political class and Silicon Valley tech oligarchs: Silicon Valley leverages geopolitical anxiety to package the energy-intensive brute-forcing of the Scaling Law as a monopolistic moat, using vast capital and physical entropy to mask algorithmic inefficiency while severely suppressing marginal, spontaneous innovation. -/- By examining the algorithmic physics behind emerging phenomena like the open-source ecosystem and DeepSeek, this paper demonstrates that model capability is not a linear function of compute and capital; brute-force walls are far from insurmountable when confronted with radical architectural reconstruction. This not only shatters Silicon Valley’s myth of monopoly but also exposes the profound truth that algorithmic breakthroughs stem from human adaptive intelligence and non-linear intuition. -/- Ultimately, this paper proposes a path toward civilization’s resilience: "De-complexification." The study emphasizes that overcoming this crisis requires not the design of higher-order actuarial models, but a comprehensive return to tacit knowledge, intuitionism, and embodied cognition. Only by breaking out of the self-entrapment of rational entropy and re-nesting abstract rationality within the biosphere and the continuous duration of life can civilization achieve ultimate redemption through evolutionary adaptation.

items.title: Creative labour and generative AI: a typology of asymmetrical relations.
items.abstract: In this article, we argue that the benefits and harms of generative AI in the content and conditions of creative labour are not evenly distributed across the cultural industries and between cultural workers. In light of this, we propose a conceptual typology that allows for a more granular and nuanced analysis of the asymmetrical impact of GenAI in creative labour structured around three dimensions: contractual relations, forms of automation, and workflows. Regarding contractual relations, we differentiate between formal, self-employed, and platform-mediated creative labour. In forms of automation, we identify four dominant uses: automation as replacement, automation as augmentation, humanly extended automation, and control. Finally, we define three types of workflows: artisanal, industrial, and informational. This typology is guided by the concept of distributed creative agency, which we claim is the result of a constant negotiation between three forces: practices, artefacts, and social structures. Furthermore, the proposed conceptual typology can be operationalized for empirical research in order to better capture the conditions under which AI shapes creative labour in contemporary capitalism.

items.title: Correction: Charting the AI perception gap: divergent views on risk, benefit, and value between experts and the public challenge the societal acceptance of AI.
Determinacy as a Two-Place Relation: The Category Mistake in Quantum Interpretation, and the Dissolution of the Paradox Set.
items.abstract: We propose that determinacy is a two-place relation between an attribute and an information state, rather than a one-place property that facts have or lack, and examine what a realist about quantum mechanics gains and loses by adopting it. The proposal supplies modal structure over unperformed experiments, a determinate might, a graded probability where a weighting and its normalization are defined, and a would that is evaluable even where it is false, without a standing valuation of the unmeasured for the Bell theorems to exclude. Two arguments carry the paper, with different force. An internal argument identifies a preservation constraint: a completion that keeps the framework’s constructive openness cannot also assign a value at the same index. An external argument excludes a specified class of completions, the noncontextual, measurement-independent valuations whose image is a single sample space of the kind the quantum statistics rule out. Neither argument uniquely selects information-state indexing: a completion that translates openness rather than retaining it meets only the second, and contextual alternatives remain open. We then apply the proposal to two representative cases, delayed choice and Wigner’s friend, each dissolution graded by the case-specific inputs it consumes, the observer case requiring the additional physical premise that every admissible refinement retains access to a separating record incompatible with the maintained laboratory coherence, and locate the Frauchiger–Renner argument as the contested application. Five objections are answered, and the questions the proposal leaves open are stated explicitly.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and academic integrity in nursing education: a thematic analysis of Filipino nurse educators’ perspectives.
items.abstract: As technology advances, artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational settings, raising important questions about its impact on learning and academic integrity. This study describes the perspectives of Filipino nurse educators on the role of artificial intelligence in maintaining academic integrity. A descriptive qualitative design was used, with a two-phase data collection process employing purposive sampling. In Phase 1, open-ended online responses were collected via Google Forms from 23 nurse educators to elicit initial perspectives on AI and academic integrity. In Phase 2, findings from the online responses informed a focus group discussion with 19 participants, enabling deeper exploration, clarification, and expansion of emerging issues. Data from both phases were integrated and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-step thematic analysis framework. Through iterative coding and theme development, 148 initial codes were generated, consolidated into 14 subthemes, and organized into four major themes: “Policy Gaps: Need for Agile Ethical Frameworks,” “Critical AI Literacy: Essential for Students and Educators,” “AI as a Double-Edged Sword in Nursing Education,” and “Balancing AI Use and Human Learning.” This study concludes that AI is a valuable educational tool but may compromise academic integrity and critical thinking, highlighting the need for institutional policies, ethical guidelines, and user training in higher education.

items.title: Приоритет цели: градиент нисходящей причинности.
items.abstract: В работе на примере четырёх систем – катящегося шара (физика), инстинктивного побега животного, пробежки навстречу другу (социальное действие) и мысленного счёта (абстрактное мышление) – демонстрируется градиент нисходящей причинности. Вводится понятие «приоритет цели» как степень, с которой будущее состояние (цель) организует настоящее. Ключевой тезис: объективация нисходящей причинности (реализация цели в материи) не может быть выведена из физических законов и не имеет известных вещественных коррелятов, достаточных для объяснения. Показано, как приоритет цели возрастает от нулевого (шар) до практически абсолютного (мысль). Работа иллюстрирует четырёхуровневую архитектонику сознания (Рефлексивный модуль – Феноменальный модуль – Психофизический интерфейс – Физический субстрат) и предлагает операциональный инструмент для сравнительного анализа систем разной природы – от физических до когнитивных и творческих. Дополнительно разъясняется, почему концепция эмерджентности не даёт каузального механизма для возникновения цели и смысла, и как предлагаемая модель преодолевает эти объяснительные трудности материалистической парадигмы. -/- .

items.title: Designing for rhythm: tempo-setting infrastructures and the temporal conditions of digital life.
items.abstract: Digital systems increasingly function as tempo-setting infrastructures that organize the temporal conditions under which cognition, communication, learning, and participation occur. Although research in human-computer interaction, platform studies, and AI ethics has extensively examined privacy, fairness, transparency, engagement, and well-being, the temporal organization of digital life has received comparatively little attention as a distinct object of sociotechnical analysis. We argue that digital systems shape cognition by reorganizing the temporal conditions that structure attention, recovery, communication, learning, and coordination across everyday life. Integrating research from cognitive science, chronobiology, human-computer interaction, platform studies, and AI governance, we identify fi ve recurring temporal structures—interruption, recovery, communication, synchronization, and closure—that explain how digital systems reorganize the conditions supporting sustained cognitive and social functioning across work, education, and everyday life. Timing emerges as a structural property of sociotechnical systems that shapes how attention is sustained, communication is coordinated, learning is organized, and participation unfolds over time. The broader implication is that digital systems should be evaluated in terms of the temporal environments they create alongside the information they present and the decisions they support. As digital technologies increasingly organize the pace of everyday life, understanding their societal consequences requires understanding how they reorganize the temporal conditions that sustain cognition, communication, participation, and human agency.

items.title: In defence of mental integrity.
items.abstract: There is substantial enthusiasm for a right to mental integrity in neuroethics—but less clarity on just what exactly that right would involve. A recent article by Jennifer Blumenthal-Barby and Peter Ubel presses a number of significant challenges to this notion—at least, that it is superfluous (since more familiar rights and wrongs already explain the relevant territory) and that it would demand too much (since we are not bound, in general, not to influence or interpret the minds of others). Responding to these objections can help us to see more clearly what is at stake in discussions about the right to mental integrity—and also what it would take to show that we should endorse rights like this, as a morally important set of considerations that deserve legal recognition. My claim will be that, as in the case of other integrity rights (bodily, territorial, data), mental integrity would have to involve the idea that a certain boundary must be protected in order to maintain the integration of an underlying system. This boundary, I argue, is not the same as the boundaries that define our rights regarding our bodies, selves or lives. Nor, I argue, need we understand any ‘crossing’ of it, without consent, as a mental trespass. I conclude by showing what it would take to fully specify the nature of the right to mental integrity, so understood, arguing that despite many difficulties such a right faces, we may well need it to account for the contours of mental morality.

items.title: Золотое правило этики - путь через века и культуры | The Golden Rule of Ethics — A Journey Through the Ages and Cultures.
items.abstract: Статья представляет собой научно-образовательное исследование истории и современного значения «Золотого правила этики» — принципа взаимности, сформулированного в различных формах в древних культурах Египта, Ирана, Индии, Китая, Греции, иудаизма, христианства и ислама. -/- Авторы рассматривают сходство и различия этих традиций, а также анализируют критические подходы Канта, Милля, Ницше и Шоу. Показано, что при культурном и историческом многообразии «Золотое правило» выражает универсальную нравственную интуицию: уважать другого человека и относиться к нему с учетом того, как человек хотел бы, чтобы относились к нему самому. -/- Особое внимание уделено современному применению этого принципа в психологии, педагогике, межкультурном диалоге и международном сотрудничестве. Отдельная часть исследования посвящена взаимодействию человека и искусственного интеллекта. На основе диалога автора с двумя ИИ — DeepSeek и Алисой — рассматриваются возможности совместного творчества, доверия и формирования этических принципов для отношений «человек — ИИ». -/- В статье предлагаются принципы ответственного использования искусственного интеллекта: уважение человеческого достоинства, прозрачность, недопущение вреда, универсальность, уважение автономии человека, ориентация на общее благо, пропорциональность и объяснимость решений. -/- Основной вывод исследования состоит в том, что «Золотое правило этики» сохраняет актуальность как универсальный инструмент взаимного уважения и может стать основой не только человеческих отношений, но и формирующейся этики взаимодействия человека с искусственным интеллектом.  .

items.title: Invariance Without a Beneficiary: What Survives Cognitive Parity, and on What Grounds.
items.abstract: Past the parity threshold this corpus has closed route after route, and read quickly the series says that nothing holds. It does not say that. Every closed route was a configuration whose working condition contained a relative capacity term, and the complementary question was never put systematically: are there configurations whose working condition never contained the asymmetry at all? This paper puts that question to all sixteen corpus texts under a single criterion, generalized from Soundness Without Leverage §3.1. Every configuration has a working condition, meaning what has to be true for it to do what it is supposed to do, and the criterion asks one thing about it: what does capability growth do to the truth value of that condition? A configuration is effect-invariant when the answer is nothing: growth neither falsifies the condition nor drains what the configuration delivers. Four answers end or empty it instead, and each is named. The test is on the truth value and never on whether a form of words appears, because a condition can name relative capacity and be made true by the crossing rather than false. The result is exhibited, not argued for: the paper displays a partition and declines to claim that the surviving side is a way forward. The falling class is not re-argued here, and the cross-cut makes one uniformity visible. Sixteen of the twenty-one non-invariant entries fail at the same step, where a constative stock is to be translated into behavioural compulsion by way of an epistemic advantage. Those sixteen are the entries that fall at the capacity term, so the observation locates that term inside a configuration rather than counting it a second time. What is new is the vocabulary unification and the location, not a tally, and the paper says so where the claim is made. Lever, grip, uptake and coverage are four words for that one operation from three papers, two of them one definition read from its two sides, and none of the three claimed the generalization; the uniformity is this paper's conjecture, not a source's reading. The other five do not fail there, and they are why the criterion has four drivers rather than one: a bound on the adversary that names no overseer, three configurations that run out when the system stops needing what the other party holds, and one that is not ended at all but emptied, persisting while its worth goes to zero. The surviving class is inhabited, on five distinguishable grounds, four of which have occupancy …
