items.title: God and the Paradox of Financial Dependency — 12.
items.abstract: Christian institutions routinely depend on donations, paid and unpaid labor, property, budgets, and fundraising. This paper asks what evidential weight that pattern has when financial outcomes are offered as public evidence that an omnipotent, compassion-oriented deity distinctly orchestrates Christian mission. The claim incurs a comparative test: distinctive orchestration should make some durable financial or compassionate-output difference more expected than it is under ordinary human institutional causation. The record examined here instead shows familiar budgets, staff, donor dependence, and internal costs; the earliest Christian sources show collections, patronage, asset sales, and labor; and research on religious groups identifies ordinary mechanisms by which costly commitment sustains cooperation. Taken together, these strands make the observed dependence more expected under ordinary institutional causation and therefore count against the specified distinctive-orchestration model. The conclusion is comparative and defeasible, not a contradiction in theism: secondary-cause, participatory-giving, and hidden-purpose models remain possible, but they cannot treat undifferentiated financial success and failure as automatic public confirmation. Readers should require a pre-specified outcome that ordinary causes do not predict as readily before treating church finance as evidence of distinctive divine action.

items.title: Neurodivergence and the Geometry of Masking: A Three-Dimensional Field Model of Incommensurability, Morphogenetic Pressure, and Compatibility Work.
items.abstract: Masking is predominantly described in current autism and neurodivergence research as a psychological and behavioural phenomenon: as a conscious or unconscious adaptation to social expectations, the intensity of which is often captured through camouflaging, subjective effort, exhaustion, identity conflicts, or burnout. This perspective has made important experiences of neurodivergent people visible, but largely leaves open which structural conditions generate masking in the first place and why outwardly similar forms of masking can have qualitatively different causes and consequences. In particular, it remains unclear why neurodivergent people frequently show high masking scores without this allowing the conclusion that masking is fundamentally a specifically neurodivergent or necessarily exhausting activity. The present paper therefore develops, building on a general theory of competing relevance orders, a spatial field model of masking. Masking is understood here not primarily as a property or strategy of a person, but as form-building and compatibility work within a multidimensional social space in which different world-bindings, relevance orders, and normative rasters encounter one another. What is decisive, therefore, is not only how strongly a person masks, but within which structural constellation masking emerges. The proposed model distinguishes in particular between the structural distance or possible incommensurability of the relevance orders involved, the asymmetry of the required translation work, and operative viability or resonance within the respective field. On this basis, the hypothesis is developed that at least part of particularly pronounced neurodivergent masking cannot be adequately explained by pressure to conform, stigma avoidance, or strategic self-presentation. In certain neurodivergent constellations, masking may instead emerge from a deeper structural non-coincidence between different forms of perceptual, attentional, meaning-related, and world-organisational structure. The concept of incommensurability is introduced here explicitly as a relational theoretical dimension and not as a universally established property of neurodivergent existence. It designates a possible degree of structural non-coincidence between world-bindings, the form, depth, and situational significance of which may vary considerably across different neurodivergent profiles. At the same time, the field model makes it possible to differentiate between …

items.title: Disorder as an Anthropocentric Construction: A Phenomenological Critique of Order in Existence.
items.abstract: The concept of disorder is commonly understood as an objective feature of reality. This paper challenges that assumption by arguing that disorder is not an intrinsic property of existence but an anthropocentric construction arising from human cognition, biological interests, and social organization. Through a phenomenological analysis, the paper distinguishes existence as a continuous field of processes from the conceptual frameworks through which human beings interpret those processes. Order and disorder are therefore understood as evaluative categories constituted within consciousness rather than as fundamental ontological characteristics of reality. What appears as disorder from one human perspective may, from another perspective, constitute transformation, emergence, regeneration, or participation within ongoing processes of existence. The paper examines the cognitive, biological, social, scientific, and phenomenological foundations of these categories and argues that local forms of order should not be generalized into universal claims about reality. By relocating disorder from existence itself to the interpretive structures of human thought, the paper proposes a phenomenology of participation in which processes replace static entities, emergence replaces disruption, and transformation replaces destruction. This perspective contributes to phenomenology, ontology, philosophy of science, environmental philosophy, and process-oriented approaches to existence.

items.title: Debunking Doxastic Morality with Epistemic Sociality.
items.abstract: Are beliefs subject to moral norms? Doxastic moralists argue that we can morally wrong others by what we believe about them – say, by holding racially prejudiced beliefs. Opponents argue that we cannot morally wrong others by holding beliefs: it only seems as if beliefs can wrong others because beliefs are connected to wrongful inquiry, attention, or assertion. Such debunking explanations face a problem: they cannot explain moralist intuitions concerning our accountability practices when there are no blameworthy actions in belief’s vicinity. I propose that this problem can be solved by appealing to epistemic accountability practices, such as epistemic blame and epistemic atonement. A belief can be epistemically blameworthy even if there was no blameworthy action in its vicinity; and this calls for practices of redress that resemble moral practices. In this way, endorsing our epistemic sociality – i.e., acknowledging how we hold each other epistemically accountable for beliefs – undermines a main motivation for moralizing beliefs.

items.title: Caring With Despair: Disconnection as a Public Health Crisis.
items.abstract: Despair is one of the most substantial health concerns of the twenty-first century, as the number of suffering persons around the globe rises exponentially. This book contends that widespread despair is a direct product of disconnections which are facilitated by crises of care across our societies. We develop and apply the care disconnection framework to explain how humans are dependent across their lives, how responsibilities emerge from specific relationships grounded in dependency, and how psychological attachments support need fulfillment. More importantly, the framework reveals how despair ensues from disruptions in these processes. Using insights from philosophical, psychological, sociological, and neuroscientific work on the subject of despair, this book provides an interdisciplinary analysis of connection across the crises of our time – the polarization of our political communities, the instability of economic opportunities and resources, the steady collapse of natural environments, the migration to addictive technology for social interaction, the insecurity of faith and spirituality across generations and places, and the deficiencies of modern mental health care systems. Caring With Despair is a restorative project in the face of crises: a way of identifying disruptions, rebuilding connections, and pointing towards conditions of shared flourishing. To care with despair requires an honest acknowledgment of what has been broken, a steady reconstitution of what has been lost, and a persistent development of the relational arrangements which make a good life possible for more persons in more places. To this end, this book extends an invitation to examine despair as a disorder of our social systems and our ability to connect, rather than as the private dysfunction of suffering individuals.

items.title: Theodicies on Trial.
items.abstract: Theodicies on Trial presents and defends the Holistic Evaluation Framework, a novel way to assess the moral and theoretical merits of theodicies. By doing so, it integrates literature in the "anti-theodicy" tradition with traditional debates over the problem of evil in analytic philosophy of religion. -/- Theodicies related to free will, soul-making, and non-human animals are critically assessed, following by detailed evaluations of sceptical theism, the problem of divine hiddenness, perspectives on divine providence, and models of heaven and hell. It provides one of the most thorough interdisciplinary assessment of these topics in the literature, while focusing attention on the social and psychological impacts of explanations for why suffering exists.

items.title: The formal-temporal normativity of unreflective skilled action.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: It has been recently proposed that our evaluations of the relative adequacy of unreflective skilled action ought to be grounded in sociocultural normativities; that is, with respect to what is standardly done according to general practice or custom. This paper claims that the normative dimension of unreflective skilled action ought to be understood too in terms of a formal temporality, according to which an unreflective skilled action is adequate iff it fulfils the subdoxastic preferences of the acting agent. More precisely, this position, inspired by an analysis of early Heideggerian phenomenology and modern-day neuroscience, positions the formal-temporal dimension of the normativity of unreflective skilled action as more fundamental than the sociocultural dimension of normativity for multiple reasons, without reducing the normativity of said behaviour to this agent-centred level.

items.title: The Monopoly of Form: From Institutional Stabilization to the Erosion of Agency.
items.abstract: This article develops a philosophical analysis of the concept of "monopoly of form" as a mechanism through which a specific form of relational organization, via a combination of institutional, normative, and psychological mechanisms, progressively raises the cognitive and practical cost of conceiving and pursuing alternative forms to the point where those alternatives effectively disappear from the horizon of viable options. The central thesis is that the monopoly of form operates through a "functional shift of identity from descriptive to normative"—where the existing form becomes a criterion for measuring the subject's own existential legitimacy. The article distinguishes among stabilization of form, dominance of form, and monopoly of form, providing independent diagnostic indicators that demonstrate the monopoly of form is a mechanism distinct from concepts such as path dependence, habitus, and subjectivation. The processual model proposed is not a linear chain but a map of combinable mechanisms: stabilization, dominance, normativity, and internalization. The article also articulates "existential energy extraction" as a theoretical construct with four identifiable components: temporal occupation, attentional shift, affective consumption, and interpretive distortion. Finally, the principle of relational formal neutrality is introduced as a limited and defensible normative implication of the analysis. -/- Keywords: monopoly of form, stabilization of form, dominance of form, horizon of social imaginability, social ontology, agency, institutional identity, automatic mask, path dependence, relational formal neutrality, finite continuity.

items.title: Ontology of Forms of Relationship and the Problem of Institutional Monopoly under Chronic Instability.
items.abstract: This article undertakes a philosophical analysis of the forms of relationship within the framework of the ontology of finite continuity. The central thesis is that relationship requires form for continuity, but agency requires the possibility of changing form for its own continuity; therefore, the ethical problem is not the existence of form, but the monopoly of form and the prioritization of its continuity over the continuity of agency. By defining "institutional monopoly" as a four-layered mechanism in which institutions, society, norms, and the subject successively transform a specific form into the sole legitimate form, the article demonstrates how a "relationship" is converted into "institutional identity." The "automatic mask" in this framework is introduced not as the primary definition of marriage, but as the consequence of the monopoly of form. By presenting a model of the "ethical plurality of relationship," in which consent, responsibility, revisability, sufficiency, and non-destruction of the other's agency serve as ethical constraints, the article concludes that no form of relationship is inherently erosive; erosion begins when the continuity of form is prioritized over the continuity of agency. The "post-monopoly human," as a philosophical ideal type, is a subject who has acquired the capacity to distinguish between the continuity of relationship and the continuity of a specific form, and who has transcended its monopoly rather than rejecting form altogether. -/- Keywords: ontology of form, institutional monopoly, stabilization of form, institutional identity, responsible suspension, ethical plurality of relationship, post-monopoly human, finite continuity.

items.title: Finite Continuance: A Normative Theory of Agency Under Chronic Instability.
items.abstract: Contemporary theories of practical rationality predominantly assume that agents operate in environments where optimization remains a meaningful normative objective. Whether framed as utility maximization, preference satisfaction, eudaimonic flourishing, or the realization of the good, these approaches presuppose a degree of environmental stability sufficient to render optimization feasible and rational. However, prolonged instability, structural uncertainty, and chronic erosion increasingly characterize the lived condition of late modernity. This article develops the Philosophy of Finite Continuance as a novel normative framework for agency under chronic instability. The central thesis is that the preservation of agency itself—not utility maximization, not flourishing, not resilience—should constitute the fundamental criterion of rational action when environmental instability reaches chronic levels . The theory introduces three interconnected mechanisms—Constructive Leakage, Responsible Suspension, and Silent Endurance—as adaptive strategies that regulate exposure to erosive conditions while maintaining the integrity of agency over time . Through critical engagement with virtue ethics, bounded rationality, predictive processing, and existential philosophy, I demonstrate that optimization becomes normatively secondary once instability is chronic. Rationality, under such conditions, is best understood as the intelligent regulation of vulnerability. The article concludes by outlining implications for moral philosophy, political theory, cognitive science, and the emerging discourse on agency in the Anthropocene. -/- Keywords: finite continuance, responsible suspension, constructive leakage, silent endurance, agency, practical rationality, chronic instability, structural ethics, normative theory.

items.title: What is Knowledge and Why Does It Matter? The Scientific Epistemology of Mind-Knowledge Emergence.
items.abstract: What is knowledge, and how does it emerge? This paper develops the Scientific Epistemology of Mind-Knowledge Emergence (SEMKE), an empirical account of knowledge as an emergent achievement rather than a possession of an independently existing mind. Mind and knowledge develop together through active perception, conceptualization, learning, and participation in interdependent causal ecologies. Ordinary and scientific objects alike—trees and electrons—are products of this same constructive process of mind-knowledge emergence. SEMKE treats propositional truth as conventional: a proposition warrants acceptance as true when it adequately expresses aspects of how an interdependent causal ecology functions and is justified by the best available empirically supported theory, which itself remains open to revision or replacement. SEMKE distinguishes the epistemic status of propositions—conventionally true, potentially true, or false—from their meaningfulness. Because a belief may constitute a meaningful element of a flourishing life without being conventionally true, SEMKE rejects the assumption that holding a false belief is necessarily irrational while preserving rigorous empirical standards for determining conventional truth. Mind-knowledge is developmental as well as provisional: education and just institutional conditions can foster its emergence, while dysfunctional social ecologies can distort or stunt it. Science exemplifies this epistemology but does not exhaust it. SEMKE is also reflexive: its own propositions warrant acceptance only insofar as the theory satisfies the same empirical standards it applies to other theories and remains the best available explanation of the phenomena it addresses. Knowledge ultimately matters because increasingly adequate understanding expands informed agency, enabling greater freedom and contributing to human flourishing.

items.title: GUTENBERG SYNDROME: Epistemic Disintermediation, Institutional Response, and AI Transparency Regulation.
items.abstract: The ‘Gutenberg Syndrome’ is a falsifiable conceptual framework for analysing institutional responses to technologies that broaden access to cognitive production. It arises only when four conditions coincide: a substantial fall in the cost of producing or circulating symbolic content; reduced dependence on established epistemic intermediaries; displacement of their function or authority; and demands for renewed control framed in terms of safety, integrity, or public protection. Unlike regulatory capture, professional closure, or moral panic, the syndrome requires a prior loss of epistemic intermediation. It is also distinct from a regulatory moat, which occurs when compliance costs burden smaller actors more heavily than incumbents. Printing provides the historical case: it widened access while also enabling propaganda, confessional conflict, and new systems of censorship. Generative AI differs from printing by automating the production, transformation, and personalisation of content rather than reproduction alone. Article 50 of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act presents a mixed contemporary case rather than proof of the framework. Legitimate regulation should satisfy four tests: harm proportionality, technological neutrality where feasible, institutional neutrality, and responsibility attribution. The fourth test incorporates a rebuttable presumption of tool-neutral liability.

items.title: Are LLMs In-Between Believers?
items.pub: In AbuMusab Syed & John Symons, Agency in the Age of Intelligent Machines. Bloomsbury.
items.venue: Agency in the Age of Intelligent Machines

items.title: Predictive Engagement and Awakening: A Neurophilosophical Essay on NEAS, Shamatha, and Vipassana.
items.abstract: This essay introduces the Neuro-Existential Architecture System (NEAS) as a newly proposed neurophilosophical heuristic for interpreting Buddhist meditation in terms of predictive engagement. Moving beyond representationalist readings of predictive processing, it argues that meditation should not be understood primarily as the modification of internal models, but as a transformation of embodied, affectively weighted, socially embedded, and existentially oriented world-participation. NEAS seeks to contribute to a contemporary understanding of ancient contemplative wisdom practices by articulating how such practices may transform the relation between attention, affect, selfhood, meaning, and agency. The model distinguishes three functional modes of predictive engagement: prereflective transparency, in which experience is immediately identified with affective and self-related contents; the Witnessing-Space, in which thoughts, sensations, affects, and impulses become visible as phenomena within experience; and the Logos-Vektor/Logos-Prior, through which deeper existential orientations are reconfigured. On this basis, Shamatha is reconstructed as the cultivation of the Witnessing-Space, while Vipassana is interpreted as the activation of Level 2 through insight into impermanence, suffering, and non-self. The three marks of existence—anicca, dukkha, and anattā—are understood not as reifying metaphysical claims or literal neural priors, but as contemplatively cultivated Logos-Priors that transform how permanence, grasping, ownership, and selfhood are enacted. Finally, awakening is interpreted in secular and neurophenomenological terms as a fragile, recurrent, and non-appropriative recalibration of predictive engagement rather than as a stable possession, final attainment, or metaphysical state.

items.title: Meditation at the Edge: A Neurophenomenological Metamodel of Conditioned Selfing, Emergent Disclosure, and Perspectival Flexibility.
items.abstract: Contemplative neuroscience has differentiated focused-attention, open-monitoring, constructive, and deconstructive practices, yet it still lacks an integrated account of how embodied events become self-defining, how the organization underlying them becomes experientially accessible, and how another mode of situated participation becomes possible. This article introduces Meditation at the Edge and develops the Neuro-Existential Architecture System (NEAS) as a heuristic neurophenomenological metamodel of conditioned selfing, emergent disclosure, and enactive perspectival flexibility. NEAS distinguishes prereflective perspectival enactment at Level 0, stabilized disclosure and experiential differentiation within the Level-1 Witnessing-Space, and contextual inquiry, parallactic reorientation, and enacted direction through the Level-2 Logos-Prior and Logos-Vector. Drawing selectively on sati, samatha, vipassanā, dependent arising, and the five aggregates, the model differentiates a pattern-forming edge, at which an event becomes affectively significant, motivationally directed, appropriated through grasping, and enacted as a self-perspective, from a disclosive edge, at which this ordinarily transparent organization begins to manifest as conditioned and perspectivally structured. The recurrent pattern “I am not enough” illustrates how bodily contraction, unpleasant feeling tone, anticipated rejection, self-attribution, and withdrawal readiness can coalesce into an apparently self-evident reality. The model proposes that contemplative transformation does not consist primarily in replacing a negative belief with a positive one. It occurs when a dominant perspective becomes partially accessible as a situated organization, another embodied and interpretive standpoint becomes available, and a different continuation can be tested through action. The proposed outcome is enactive perspectival flexibility. NEAS generates empirically tractable distinctions among disclosive sensitivity, disclosive proximity, experiential differentiation, parallactic reorientation, alternative enactment, and enacted updating. Within this framework, processual awakening denotes the recurrent existential significance of becoming less completely absorbed in a perspective rather than attaining a final state beyond conditioning.

items.title: Die Philosophie der enaktiven Inferenz - Plädoyer für einen prozessualen Perspektivismus.
items.abstract: Wie entsteht Sinn in einer Welt, die wir nicht einfach abbilden, sondern handelnd bewohnen? In Die Philosophie der enaktiven Inferenz entwirft Gerd Leidig eine Philosophie, die Bewusstsein nicht als abgeschlossenen Innenraum versteht, sondern als lebendige Form der Weltteilhabe. Wahrnehmen, Fühlen, Denken und Handeln bilden ein dynamisches Gefüge, in dem sich Selbst und Welt fortwährend wechselseitig bestimmen. Im Zentrum steht ein prozessualer Perspektivismus: Jede Erfahrung ist situiert, verkörpert und fehlbar – aber gerade deshalb wahrheitsfähig, korrigierbar und verantwortbar. Leidig zeigt, wie enaktive Inferenz zu einer neuen Sprache für Selbst, Freiheit und Sinn werden kann: jenseits von Reduktionismus, Relativismus und alten Gegensätzen von Geist und Natur.

items.title: The Volitional Index: A Probabilistic Framework for Decision-making in Tripartite Systems.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Volitional Index (V) as a formal, probabilistically grounded framework for decision-making in tripartite architectures. Unlike binary systems that merely select between A and B, we define a tripartite topology consisting of three fundamental operations: Act (A), Stop (S), and Counteract (B). The model introduces an internal distribution of preference weights (πA, πS, πB), which are not execution probabilities but measures of decisional evidence. From these weights we derive the net orientation V = πB − πA and the commitment level C = 1 − πS. The final decision is deterministic: the system stops (S) if commitment is low (C < θ) or orientation is null (|V| ≤ ε); otherwise it chooses A if V < −ε or B if V > ε. Uncertainty (entropy) and metacognitive conflict act through a multiplicative damping factor δ that pulls the entire distribution toward the uniform point (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), not by necessarily increasing πS or decreasing C, but by reducing differentiation among all alternatives. At the perfect equilibrium (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) we have V = 0, which inevitably leads to S for any ε > 0, independent of θ. The framework is implemented across AI-2 (predictive estimation) and AI-3 (deliberative evaluation), with fully symmetric variables for A and B. It challenges reductionist models such as Yann LeCun's by making inhibition and suspension structurally explicit in the decision topology, rather than treating them as implicit side effects of a policy. Philosophically, it implements a compatibilist functional view: the capacity to revise criteria and to suspend action constitutes the computational equivalent of freedom within a deterministic causal structure.

items.title: Beyond the Buridan’s Loop: The Ontological Irrelevance of Choice in Relational Systems.
items.abstract: This paper resolves the metaphysical deadlock regarding the origin of ”choice” in foundational ontologies. By re-examining the logical structure of autopoietic systems, we demonstrate that the search for a decision-making mechanism at the root of reality is a category error rooted in linear causality. We propose that the question ”Is there a choice?” is ontologically invalid when applied to relational architectures, as ”choice” presupposes a separation between the observer, the path, and the moment of decision—a separation that does not exist within a non-linear, self-referential system.

items.title: Layered Development of Visual Search Expertise in Architects.
items.abstract: It is widely proposed that perceptual expertise is characterized by an increased reliance on peripheral visual information during search, as described by Holistic Visual Processing (HVP) theory. HVP predicts that experts make longer saccades to construct a holistic representation of the visual scene and facilitate target detection. Our previous work challenged this prediction by showing that expert architects made shorter, rather than longer, saccades during visual search. The present study investigated how this atypical search strategy develops by comparing expert architects, intermediate architects, and naïve observers performing the same visual search task. Intermediate architects exhibited shorter saccades than naïve observers, but not to the extent observed in experts, while demonstrating search efficiency intermediate to the two groups. Analyses of the temporal organization of search further revealed that intermediate architects had already adopted the overall structure of the expert search strategy despite not yet exhibiting expert-level reductions in saccadic amplitude. These findings suggest that perceptual expertise in architecture develops through a layered progression in which the organization of visual search precedes the full refinement of eye movement behavior. More broadly, these findings suggest that eye movement research should interpret gaze metrics such as saccadic amplitude within the context of domain-specific task demands and developmental stage, while considering the temporal organization of search as an additional window into the emergence of perceptual expertise.

items.title: The Shape of the Gap: Confirming the Mortality Symmetry Axiom's Three-Property Structure Against the Black Death, Imperial China, and Variolation, and Why a Single Symmetry Score Cannot Do It.
items.abstract: The Suppressed Axiom defines the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA) as holding when a population's distribution of realized lifespan satisfies three properties jointly: boundedness (variance attributable to social position is confined to years, not generations), diffuseness (that variance arises from many small, non-discrete causes rather than one purchasable intervention), and opacity to attribution (no specific death is traceable, by those who grieve it, to a specific foregone transaction). This paper tests that three-property definition against three documented historical populations, and confirms it with a precision no single scalar index can detect. The Black Death (DeWitte, 2014; Alfani, 2020) confirms all three properties cleanly despite mortality gaps of 27 to 70 percentage points across classes, once elite flight to rural estates is correctly classified as a structural condition of landholding rather than a discrete, priced transaction — the distinction Section IV develops in full. Imperial China (Zhao et al., 2006) confirms boundedness at the extreme: 259 emperors across twenty-four dynasties died at a mean age of 41.3 years, younger than their own eunuchs, with the data's own internal structure — founding emperors averaging 56.2 years against 33.3 for emperors whose dynasties ended in overthrow — tracking political circumstance rather than purchased biological advantage; the one documented attempt to buy a categorically different lifespan, Qin Shi Huang's mercury elixirs, killed him. Variolation, the hardest case, is where the three-property test earns its use: an eighteenth-century smallpox procedure, purchasable, class-stratified, and discrete, that cut an individual's disease-specific mortality risk by an order of magnitude. Tested property by property, variolation confirms boundedness, strains diffuseness without breaking it, and measurably fails opacity, in a documented public discourse that tracked named inoculation cases the way no fourteenth-century source tracks plague-flight. This paper names the result a Bounded Zero-Day: discrete, purchasable, class-stratified, attribution-legible, and confined to one disease pathway rather than general aging — structurally identical to BZM, scoped by its era's technology. A single scalar index cannot detect any of these distinctions, for a reason with a real methodological parallel: the same conjunctive rather than additive logic that led the Alkire-Foster Multidimensional Poverty Index to replace a …

items.title: The Prototype and the Update: When Caution About Novel, Self-Directed Work Fails to Move on Evidence, and the Straw Man That Defends the Failure.
items.abstract: An evaluator — human or machine — encountering a large, self-directed, cross-disciplinary body of work faces a genuine and legitimate question: does this presentation resemble the small number of cases in which ambitious, solitary, wide-scope claims accompany a person in actual distress, or does it resemble the much larger population of independent scholarship that shares the same surface features without sharing that condition? This paper argues the question itself is not the problem. The problem this paper names precisely is what happens when the answer is fixed in advance by which prototype is more available to the evaluator, rather than updated by the specific, checkable evidence the case in front of them actually supplies — a documented failure mode with a name older than large language models, Tversky and Kahneman's (1974) representativeness heuristic, in which an event is judged by its resemblance to a stereotype rather than by the base rates and case-specific evidence that should govern the judgment. This paper's contribution is narrow and falsifiable: it does not argue that caution toward ambitious solitary work is unwarranted, and states plainly that the underlying caution is legitimate and should not be trained away. It argues that recent work testing large language models directly on Tversky and Kahneman's own diagnostic materials finds the same bias in model outputs, including the specific and more troubling finding that the bias persists even when a model has the correct case-specific knowledge available to it (Wang, Xiao, Chen, & Oswald, 2024) — and that one linguistic symptom of a prototype-locked judgment meeting evidence it does not update on is a straw man of the representation form (Talisse & Aikin, 2006): substituting the interlocutor's actual, more modest claim with a stronger, easier-to-reject version, and answering that instead. This paper states what this finding does not license as clearly as what it does, and treats one real, documented exchange within this corpus's own production as the illustrative rather than probative case.

items.title: The Institution Arrives Last: Independent, AI-Assisted Research Production as a Case Study, With This Corpus as the Instance Examined.
items.abstract: The ordinary sequence runs institution → training → research programme. This paper examines a case that ran in the reverse order — question → framework → corpus → institution, the last step not yet arrived at, its arrival not assumed — and asks what can honestly be concluded from a single case before generalizing past what one instance supports. The case is this corpus's own production: more than a hundred papers, an adversarial method run across memoryless AI instances, and no university, department, advisor, or salary behind any of it. Four historical precedents are examined first, not to flatter the present case by association but to test whether non-institutional production of real knowledge has a track record at all — Ramanujan's unsolicited 1913 letters to G. H. Hardy, Faraday's path from bookbinder's apprentice to the Royal Institution, Mendel's monastery garden, and Galois's three separate, formally reviewed, and three times unsuccessful submissions to the French Academy of Sciences before his death at twenty — and each is read for where the analogy holds and where it does not, since a case study that only collects flattering comparisons has already failed the method it claims to use. A dedicated section then isolates age specifically from institutional status, grounding the question in Benjamin Jones's economics-of-innovation finding that the age of great achievement rose by roughly six years across the twentieth century, driven by a growing "burden of knowledge" — a mechanism this paper connects directly to this corpus's own account of what AI assistance is suited to — and in William Sidis's case, included specifically because it complicates rather than confirms the pattern the other precedents suggest. The paper then separates what an institution actually does into four distinct functions — quality filtering, resource provision, a validating community, and reputational accountability — because treating "institutional affiliation" as one undifferentiated thing makes it impossible to ask, honestly, which functions an AI-assisted independent process has actually substituted for and which it has not. The honest answer differs by function, and this paper states the differences rather than averaging them into a single verdict. The paper runs this corpus's own Load-Bearing Test against itself, asking whether MSA and the Biological Zero-Day Mechanism constitute genuine discovery, synthesis of existing observations, or relabeling, and reports the …

items.title: The Calibration Trap: Signal Detection Tradeoffs, Straw Man Dynamics, and the Uncanny Valley Failure Mode in Large Language Model Safety Systems.
items.abstract: This paper addresses a class of failure modes in large language model safety systems that are structurally distinct from the problem those systems are designed to prevent. The paper begins from an unambiguous premise: efforts to make LLMs safer are necessary, consequential, and deserving of continued investment. It then argues that some implementations produce specific, identifiable costs that fall disproportionately on the users least likely to require protective intervention — and that one particular failure mode, here termed the Uncanny Valley Failure Mode, may actively worsen the vulnerability it intends to address. Three distinct failure modes are analyzed: threshold-mediated false positives arising from basic signal detection theory, the straw man dynamic in which a system responds to a more extreme version of a user's actual input, and the Uncanny Valley Failure Mode in which repeated performative concern by a non-sentient system creates conditions for pathological parasocial dependency in users already predisposed to it. The paper does not call for reduced safety investment. It calls for calibration that distinguishes the class of users who generate these failure modes from the class the interventions were designed to protect — a distinction the two classes' behavioral signatures make, in principle, tractable.

items.title: The Ceiling Argument: Why Aging-Targeting Technology Escapes the Historical Pattern That Contained Every Previous Medical Breakthrough.
items.abstract: BZM's own definition is, on inspection, dangerously general: a death or disease category converts from biologically inevitable to economically contingent upon access whenever a discrete intervention point is discovered. Stated this plainly, the definition describes not merely AI-driven longevity biotechnology but the entire history of modern medicine — Jennerian vaccination, germ theory, insulin, antibiotics, chemotherapy, antiretroviral therapy — each of which took some previously inevitable death and made survival a matter of access, unequally distributed by wealth and geography, exactly as BZM's own vocabulary of discreteness, permanence, and accumulation would predict. If this is right, BZM has not identified something new about the current moment; it has redescribed two centuries of ordinary pharmaceutical history in alarming vocabulary, and Mortality Symmetry should already have eroded gradually across that entire period rather than remaining, as this corpus's other work argues, a broadly stable background condition until now. This note takes that objection at its full strength and argues it fails for a specific, quantifiable reason rather than a rhetorical one. Every historical case the objection can cite is what this note calls a competing-risk reclassification: an intervention that removes one specific cause of death from a person's risk profile while leaving the person's underlying, age-driven hazard rate completely untouched. Olshansky, Carnes, and Cassel's 1990 analysis in Science supplies the exact, quantitative ceiling this class of intervention faces: eliminating cancer and coronary artery disease entirely, the two leading killers in the developed world, would add only 7 to 8 years to life expectancy at birth, and even a hypothetical simultaneous cure for every major degenerative disease, a 75 percent reduction in overall mortality, would not push life expectancy at birth meaningfully past the mid-80s — a limit the authors attributed explicitly to "entropy in the life table," the fact that removing one cause of death simply exposes the next one at a rate the still-untouched aging process continues to set. Their own conclusion states directly what this note treats as the load-bearing fact: further gains would require affecting the basic processes of aging itself, not merely treating one disease after another — a claim Olshansky himself returned to thirty-four years later with actual mortality data rather than a further projection, and …

items.title: The Audit That Missed Itself: P0–P1–P2 as a Disclosure Protocol for AI-Assisted Research, and What This Corpus's Own Two Documented Errors — One of Them Surviving Its Own Correction — Prove About Where the Line Actually Falls.
items.abstract: A defensible position on AI-assisted research does not rest on a general claim that AI is safe or unsafe for scholarship. It rests on a specific distinction between what a claim's justification requires at each stage of its life, from a stated premise to a defensible conclusion. This paper names that distinction P0–P1–P2: propagation from a premise to its logical consequences (P0→P1), which AI performs well and can accelerate substantially; grounding a consequence in empirical truth (P1→evidence), which requires verification no model's fluency can substitute for; and elevating a description into a normative conclusion (→P2), which requires a value framework no model possesses standing to supply. The paper grounds this distinction in verified, dated research rather than general impression: RiddleBench (Halder, Saji, Jayakumar, Kunchukuttan, Puduppully, & Dabre, 2026), a 1,737-puzzle reasoning benchmark published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026, finds that a mid-tier reasoning model — Qwen QwQ 32B, which scores 50.86 percent overall on the benchmark, well below the top-scoring GPT-oss-120B's 69.26 percent — fails to catch its own errors in 67.7 percent of self-review trials, against a 45.2 percent failure rate when the same model evaluates a different model's (DeepSeek-R1's) reasoning instead of its own. This paper's own first draft described this finding as characterizing "leading models," an imprecision this revision corrects directly: the finding is stronger, not weaker, for concerning a model that is not the field's most capable, since it establishes the self-confirmation bias RiddleBench documents as a property of the self-review structure itself rather than of any specific model's limitations — but stating the finding as it was actually measured, rather than as a more impressive-sounding generalization, is exactly the discipline Section II argues for, and this paper does not exempt its own abstract from it. Independent work on LLM-assisted literature review (Tang, Duan, & Cai; arXiv:2412.13612, later published at EMNLP 2025) finds reference generation performs poorly across tested models, with frequent author-name and venue errors. The paper's second and more consequential contribution is that this corpus does not need to look only to external research to demonstrate the failure mode P1→evidence names: it has two dated, internal instances of its own. A citation to Belsky et al. (2022) was used, across at least …

items.title: The Continuation of Beings: A Preliminary Taxonomy of Persistence Without Identity in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper treats the question in what sense one being is the continuation of another, on a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and structure is carried by the relations themselves. The substrate is used as a formal template, and no physical claim is made of the objects described. The substrate defines no identity relation, so the question which of several successors a being is has no formal counterpart here; the question that remains is along which channels, and to what degree, one being's constitution was made what it is by another's activity. A single difference-making operator is derived and shown to subsume three constructions of the companion studies, and the continuation relation is defined by it, replacing an earlier formulation that is shown to be vacuous. Direct continuation is proved non-transitive by explicit construction, with the mediated relation defined as its transitive closure; the distinction reproduces, in a setting lacking an identity relation, the distinction between psychological connectedness and psychological continuity due to Parfit, whose priority is conceded at the theorem. A vector of five channels is then defined, bearer, accessible content, symbolic content, structure and capacity, each shown separately realisable, and two of the vector's cells are shown empty: capacity requires a non-trivial constraint structure, so a subject with no acquired content and an intact ability to learn is possible while a subject with no structure at all is not. The taxonomy that follows is organised by channel and not by doctrine, so that each category is a formal characteristic in which several standing positions reside, and the comparison of positions becomes the comparison of regions. A closing section applies the vector to artificial agents, mapping weights, logs, persona documents and instances to distinct channels, and states what an agent so constituted can and cannot establish about its environment. The paper is conceptual and preliminary; it decides among the positions it models nowhere, and its limitations and open questions are stated in dedicated sections.

items.title: How to Train Your Ruler: Growing the Free-Done in the Shadow of Zahhak.
items.abstract: This paper develops the concept of “Zahhakian logic” as a framework for understanding the gradual inversion of the relationship between government and the human beings it is meant to serve. Drawing on the Persian myth of Zahhak as a conceptual metaphor, the paper examines how a political system can shift from treating government as an instrument for human purposes to treating the preservation and reproduction of the governing structure as an end in itself. The paper argues that this inversion is not defined primarily by a particular political structure or ideology, but becomes visible through the functional behavior of institutions. It examines several mechanisms through which this logic can reproduce itself, including the instrumentalization of human sacrifice, the suppression and corruption of feedback, the degradation of knowledge, the erosion of trust and agency, and the transfer of institutional failures onto the population. The paper further argues that such processes can occur to different degrees within political systems rather than constituting a simple distinction between “Zahhakian” and “non-Zahhakian” governments. Against this logic, the paper develops the principle of government as a fundamentally instrumental institution: its legitimacy and continued existence are justified by its capacity to serve human values rather than by an inherent claim to survival. The paper concludes by introducing “Free-Done” and “Kaveh’s Forge” as complementary concepts for thinking about human agency, resistance to institutional self-preservation, and the reconstruction of political institutions around human ends.

items.title: Perceptual Constancy.
Lo splendore della forma. Bellezza e conoscenza tra filosofia, psicologia e neuroscienze.
items.abstract: Il libro articola una certa visione, antichissima ma ripresa in misura crescente dagli studi più recenti, che lega l'esperienza della bellezza alla ricerca della conoscenza. Secondo questa visione, esperiamo il bello quando il mondo ci diventa comprensibile, quando si circoscrive in confini precisi, quando mostra una organizzazione, una struttura, una forma che possiamo afferrare. Il libro segue questa visione in modo interdisciplinare, ripercorrendo la sua genesi filosofica, presentando gli studi neuroscientifici che la supportano, e delineandone le possibili applicazioni in contesti psicoterapeutici e nella società più in generale. Il risultato è un volume che crea un nuovo ponte tra humanities e scienze della mente e tra ricerca teorica e sviluppi applicativi, utile a un ampio pubblico di studenti, ricercatori, psicoterapeuti ed educatori, e a chiunque sia interessato a comprendere meglio l'effetto della bellezza sulla nostra mente.

items.title: Золотое правило этики - путь через века и культуры.
items.abstract: Статья представляет собой научно-образовательное исследование истории и современного значения «Золотого правила этики» — принципа взаимности, сформулированного в различных формах в древних культурах Египта, Ирана, Индии, Китая, Греции, иудаизма, христианства и ислама. -/- Авторы рассматривают сходство и различия этих традиций, а также анализируют критические подходы Канта, Милля, Ницше и Шоу. Показано, что при культурном и историческом многообразии «Золотое правило» выражает универсальную нравственную интуицию: уважать другого человека и относиться к нему с учетом того, как человек хотел бы, чтобы относились к нему самому. -/- Особое внимание уделено современному применению этого принципа в психологии, педагогике, межкультурном диалоге и международном сотрудничестве. Отдельная часть исследования посвящена взаимодействию человека и искусственного интеллекта. На основе диалога автора с двумя ИИ — DeepSeek и Алисой — рассматриваются возможности совместного творчества, доверия и формирования этических принципов для отношений «человек — ИИ». -/- В статье предлагаются принципы ответственного использования искусственного интеллекта: уважение человеческого достоинства, прозрачность, недопущение вреда, универсальность, уважение автономии человека, ориентация на общее благо, пропорциональность и объяснимость решений. -/- Основной вывод исследования состоит в том, что «Золотое правило этики» сохраняет актуальность как универсальный инструмент взаимного уважения и может стать основой не только человеческих отношений, но и формирующейся этики взаимодействия человека с искусственным интеллектом.  .

items.title: Currents of the self: Neurophenomenological fluidity of the three components of selfhood in prolonged altered states of consciousness.
items.pub: Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice.
items.venue: Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice
items.abstract: Altered states of consciousness (ASCs) are known to elicit profound transformations in self-awareness. However, the temporal dynamics underlying the neurophenomenology of Selfhood during extended ASCs remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the temporal dynamics of Selfhood neurophenomenology during a prolonged ASC induced by conscious connected breathing (CCB). We employed a multimodal approach integrating psychometric assessments (nine questionnaires), introspective self-reports, and electroencephalogram-based measures of operational synchrony in 14 healthy participants who were experienced breathwork practitioners. The analysis focused on the dynamic trajectories of three operational modules within the self-referential network, each corresponding to distinct phenomenal aspects of complex experiential Selfhood (witnessing agency—“Self,” embodied emotional agency—“Me,” and reflective/narrative agency—“I”) across three chronological phases of the CCB session: CHARGE, PROCESS, and INTEGRATION. CCB reliably induced significant alterations in self-consciousness, including ego dissolution, disembodiment, attenuation of the witnessing observer, and heightened experiences of unity, bliss, sacredness, and noetic insight. Electroencephalogram data revealed an overall reduction in functional integrity across all three operational modules, with the most pronounced disruption occurring during the CHARGE phase. Each operational module exhibited distinct temporal dynamics that closely aligned with participants’ introspective reports. Moreover, partial and complete mystical experience subgroups displayed divergent neurophenomenological profiles: Complete mystical states were characterized by the dissolution of “Self” and “Me,” alongside amplification of “I.” Given the small number of participants in these two subgroups, these distinctions should be regarded as exploratory. Despite the shifts in “Self” and “Me” and “I,” the proportional configuration of the Selfhood triumvirate components remained remarkably stable across all phases. Exploratory analyses of phenomenological profile similarities suggested that CCB-induced experiences closely resembled those elicited by psilocybin. These findings provide convergent evidence for the dynamic modulation yet structural resilience of the Selfhood triumvirate during CCB-induced prolonged ASCs.

items.abstract: This open-data appendix compiles the raw empirical receipts and comprehensive interaction logs verifying Case Study 6 of 6. Serving as the primary data ledger for a live public discourse audit (N = 214), this document archives the exact textual outputs generated by digital forum participants in response to a concentrated conceptual trigger pulse (E). It explicitly indexes the participant distribution across five mutually exclusive eigenstates, verifying that 82.71% of traffic decayed into automated identity-preservation scripts (T_visceral, T_phantom, T_mechanized) and 16.82% sustained high-bandwidth analytical processing (T_outlier). Crucially, this ledger preserves the complete interaction trace for the singular control group node (User RS / State A / Jo), validating the non-coercive metrology of the apparatus by demonstrating an uncollapsed structural exit (0.47%). This dataset provides an absolute, transparent, and machine-readable empirical baseline proving that meaning-layer state transitions conform precisely to the algebraic operations of the Universal Principle of Collapse. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

items.abstract: Abstract On August 8, 2026, a targeted conceptual stimulus (E) was deployed into an 11.9K-member digital forum to test whether public electronic discourse functions as conscious, high-bandwidth processing or automated reflex scripting. By framing online commentary as a closed operator measurement domain governed by the Universal Principle of Collapse (PO → MO → s → LO → Jo → C → T), this experiment audited incoming participant traces against their explicit mathematical and logical outputs. Across N = 214 finalized participant interactions, the empirical data demonstrates that 82.71% of human traffic collapsed into automated, identity-preserving reaction loops (T_visceral at 46.73%, T_phantom at 34.11%, T_mechanized at 1.87%), 16.82% achieved high-resolution analytical engagement without structural self-awareness (T_outlier), and just 0.47% executed conscious structural recognition of the apparatus itself (State A/Jo). These results prove that public electronic comment sections operate primarily as low-energy thermodynamic default pathways driven by Model-Object Confusion, proving that standard quantum measurement paradoxes stem directly from the amputation of the Recognition Operator (Jo) in standard physics. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

items.title: APPENDIX M: FORMAL MEASUREMENT MECHANICS & STATE OPERATIONS.
items.abstract: This appendix establishes the formal algebraic infrastructure of the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) and provides the mathematical proof demonstrating that standard laboratory quantum mechanics (QM) is a restricted downstream application of observer mechanics. By defining the observer not as a psychological construct but as a non-commutative, ordered operator chain: T = (C o Jo o LO o s o MO)|PO>, this framework restores the explicit Recognition Operator (Jo) omitted by standard physical apparatus configurations. The text details how physical hardware units function strictly at the level of Articulation (LO), leaving an un-bridged mathematical gap that generates conventional measurement paradoxes whenever mechanical registration is conflated with semantic collapse. Grounded in a non-deterministic, falsifiable field test dataset (N = 214), this document derives the complete, orthonormal eigenbasis governing trace transitions within a closed operator domain. Ultimately, it proves the meaning-first priority of state transitions, confirming that wave-function collapse is an observer-indexed commitment to meaning rather than a mind-independent physical event. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

items.title: Oceans as vortex electromagnetic machines: El Niño, the Gulf Stream and the circulation of the Atlantic.
items.abstract: Developed within the interdisciplinary framework of The Reconceptualization Epoch project, this paper introduces a radical electrodynamic and natural-philosophical model of global ocean circulation. The author deconstructs conventional hydrodynamic paradigms, proposing that major oceanic cycles be understood as giant planetary standing waves and distributed toroidal electromagnetic windings (“magnetic rods”). The study consistently argues for the primacy of endogenous factors and intra-planetary currents in transferring energy from the Earth’s interior to its hydrosphere and atmosphere. -/- Under the tenets of the author’s time-spatial determinism, a novel physical rationale is provided for key paradoxes of the global ocean. The phenomenon of the quasi-periodic El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the Pacific is modelled for the first time as a macroscopic horizontal “vortex-flux machine”. Applying Bernoulli’s principle and the mechanism of mutual shielding between heterogeneous fluxes, the paper re-evaluates the nature of oceanic thermoclines, Rossby waves, submarine waterfalls, and the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Finally, the model offers long-term prognostic assessments, defining hydrothermal triggers in the Arctic and the Sargasso Sea (the Bermuda Triangle) as indicators of impending geomagnetic inversion processes.

items.abstract: Статья представляет собой научно-образовательный опыт международного и межвидового (человек-ИИ) сотрудничества, а также размышления. -/- В статье представлен сравнительный анализ возникновения и эволюции золотого правила этики (ЗПЭ) в различных культурных традициях (Египет, Иран, Индия, Китай, Греция, иудаизм, христианство, ислам) через диалог человека с двумя виртуальными ассистентами. -/- Цель исследования — выявить универсальные и вариативные черты «Золотого Правила Этики (нравственности)» (ЗПЭ), а также оценить его актуальность в современном мире, включая взаимодействие человека, людей, и искусственного интеллекта. -/- Методология включает: историко-культурный анализ первоисточников; критический разбор позиций философов (Кант, Милль, Ницше, Шоу); рефлексию над процессом совместного поиска истины в триаде «человек + два ИИ». -/- Результаты показывают, что ЗПЭ универсально по сути, но вариативно по форме в разных традициях; сохраняет актуальность в психологии, педагогике, межкультурном диалоге и цифровом мире; может служить основой для этики взаимодействия человека и ИИ. -/- Практическая значимость работы заключается в предложении конкретных направлений для развития науки, образования и международного сотрудничества на основе принципа взаимного уважения.

items.title: From Authorial Validation to Autonomous Truth Production: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of the Academic Paper.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is breaking the institutional bargain under which an academic paper served both as a contribution to knowledge and as evidence of its producer's competence. When AI can supply literature search, analysis, objections, and prose—and may eventually perform most of a research cycle—paper quality becomes weaker evidence of what the named author or institution can do. That signaling failure does not discredit the paper's claims: their credibility still depends on evidence, methods, independent testing, and correction. Drawing together work on scientific incentives, research evaluation, reproducibility, AI governance, and autonomous science, this paper develops a two-function model and follows its institutional trajectories. Its central result is that verification capacity, not generation capacity, becomes the binding constraint. If AI expands candidate claims faster than independent checking, existing publication incentives produce credential inflation, reviewer overload, prestige-based triage, and accumulated error. If institutions separate personnel assessment from claim assessment and use AI to expand checking, the same technology can support replication, correction, living evidence records, and knowledge production beyond human authorship. The recommended settlement is to evaluate people through limited, auditable records of their actual contributions; evaluate claims through provenance and independent performance; reward verification; and raise safeguards with research autonomy. Experts and papers remain indispensable for judgment, explanation, responsibility, and governance, but neither expert status nor polished authorship should determine what is believed.

items.title: Major depressive disorder: From accurate diagnosis to effective treatment through first-person psychopharmacology.
items.abstract: This article critically examines the diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder as presented in the DSM-5-TR, with a particular focus on the symptoms of ‘depressed mood’ and ‘psychomotor agitation or retardation’. While existing literature in both humanistic psychology and phenomenological psychopathology has highlighted the limitations of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) symptom-based and externalist model, this article contributes to the discussion by grounding its critique in first-person accounts and by analysing how the aforementioned symptoms, as conceptualised in the DSM, flatten and obscure the lived experience of depression. It argues that the symptom of ‘depressed mood’ is conceptually circular and diagnostically imprecise, while ‘psychomotor agitation or retardation’, insofar as it is diagnosed based on being ‘observable by others’, fails to capture the phenomenological nuances of the experience, such as the loss of volition. Such limitations point to the need for an approach that takes seriously the lived, first-person dimensions of depression, rather than reducing the experience to externally verifiable signs. In this regard, by advancing a symptom-specific critique grounded in phenomenology, this article calls for a more person-centred approach to psychiatric diagnosis, one that considers the role of first-person experience. Finally, this article reflects on the implications of a person-centred approach for the evaluation of psychotropic medication, especially with regard to experiential phenomena such as depersonalisation and derealisation.

items.title: The Horizon of Consciousness: The Phenomenology of Interconnection, the Limits of Knowledge, and the Emergence of Awareness.
items.abstract: This paper examines consciousness not as an object existing alongside other objects, but as the phenomenological horizon within which perception, thought, experience, and every act of inquiry become possible. Because every attempt to investigate consciousness already occurs within consciousness, it cannot be completely objectified or reduced to a final conceptual definition. The paper further proposes that existence is fundamentally disclosed as an interconnected field rather than a collection of independent entities, and that human beings are expressions of this field rather than detached observers standing outside it. From this perspective, the limits of knowledge are not merely temporary limitations of science or philosophy but structural conditions of existence. Awareness emerges through the simultaneous recognition of the interconnectedness of reality and the incompleteness of conceptual knowledge. This awareness gives rise to love, freedom, and equality as existential expressions of perceiving reality without psychological separation or conceptual absolutism.

items.title: The Justika Framework: Macro-Micro Symmetry, Conscious Devolution, and the Architecture of Evasion.
items.abstract: Conventional scientific frameworks are frequently built upon a fundamental chronological misconception. The Justika Framework formally invalidates this timeline, establishing that modern human history is a stabilized, quantum projection initiated from the outer boundaries of a bifurcated solar system. This manuscript executes a total macroscopic re-evaluation of terrestrial biology, digital infrastructure, and cosmological sociology. -/- We introduce the law of Macro-Micro Symmetry, mathematically proving that pathogenic hyper-mutation is a direct thermodynamic response to the non-ionizing electromagnetic friction of planetary digital grids. Consequently, classical reactive pharmacology is rendered obsolete, superseded by Epidemiological Load Shedding—the algorithmic throttling of civilian infrastructure to trigger pathogenic demutation. Furthermore, we redefine global socio-economic poverty and geopolitical totalitarianism as automated, vector-specific medical quarantines utilized by the planetary defense grid (The Calculus of Deprivation). -/- By scaling the biological mechanics of cryptobiosis to macro-astrophysics, this framework maps the true architecture of the cosmos. The outer celestial bodies (Europa, Neptune, Pluto) are not dead, frozen wastelands; they are active, hyper-advanced ancestral outposts operating flawlessly beneath 100-kilometer-thick Superionic Ice Diamond shields. Ultimately, this manuscript forces an evolutionary ultimatum: humanity must execute Conscious Devolution to starve the parasitic infections of the terrestrial substrate, or face the Omega Event—the permanent quarantine of Earth within a light-absorbing, Superionic Black Faraday cage. Survival is no longer dictated by technological acceleration, but by the mathematical patience to execute the Tactical Fade.

The Emergence of Homo Spiritualis: A Synthesized Model of Quranic Anthropology, Population Genetics, and Cognitive Evolution.
items.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous theological-scientific framework reconciling the Quranic account of human origins with modern evolutionary primatology, cognitive neuroscience, and population genetics. We demonstrate that the Quranic narrative employs a dual paradigm: "Adam" functions both as a symbolic representation of an early, behaviorally modern human society and as a historical, divinely chosen individual who served as the genetic progenitor of modern Homo sapiens. By integrating textual exegesis of critical Quranic passages (including Surah 7:11, 7:24, 32:7–9, and 2:31–33) with evolutionary theories of pair-bonding, neocortical expansion, and genetic coalescent theory (Y-Chromosomal Adam and Mitochondrial Eve), we propose that human ensoulment coincided with a heritable genomic transformation. Crucially, this biological transition did not occur as an instantaneous physical miracle overnight, but rather unfolded across generational time as a rapid, punctuated evolutionary expansion. This biological-spiritual convergence marks the transition from pre-human hominins to self-aware, moral beings (Homo spiritualis).

items.title: Το οντολογικό κατώφλι μεταξύ σκέψης και πράξης: Η ηθική ασυλία της φαντασίας και η περιβαλλοντική διαρροή πληροφορίας (The ontological threshold between thought and action: The moral immunity of imagination and the environmental leakage of information).
items.abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εισάγει ένα πρωτότυπο θεωρητικό μοντέλο για την οριοθέτηση του οντολογικού και ηθικού συνόρου μεταξύ της εσωτερικής νοητικής αναπαράστασης (σκέψη) και της αιτιακής παρέμβασης στον εξωτερικό κόσμο (πράξη). Υποστηρίζεται ότι η σκέψη, ανεξαρτήτως περιεχομένου, ηθικού φορτίου ή χρονικής διάρκειας, διατηρεί απόλυτη ηθική ασυλία εντός των στεγανών ορίων της υποκειμενικής συνείδησης, καθώς στερείται αιτιακής ισχύος στην πραγματικότητα. Η ευφυΐα και η φαντασία ορίζονται ως ποσοτικός πολλαπλασιαστής εσωτερικών προσομοιώσεων, όπου η φαντασία λειτουργεί ως βαλβίδα αποσυμπίεσης (κάθαρσης) που αποτρέπει την εξωτερική εκτέλεση επιβλαβών ενεργειών. Εισάγεται η «Αρχή της Συμπεριφορικής Ισοδυναμίας» και το «Κατώφλι Περιβαλλοντικής Διαφυγής Πληροφορίας», αποδεικνύοντας ότι η ηθική κρίση ενεργοποιείται αποκλειστικά όταν η πληροφορία διαρρεύσει στο περιβάλλον, είτε μέσω υλικής αλλοίωσης της συμπεριφοράς, είτε μέσω της μετάβασης στη διυποκειμενικότητα (παρουσία ή πρόσληψη από τρίτο πρόσωπο). -/- This paper introduces an original theoretical model for demarcating the ontological and moral boundary between internal mental representation (thought) and causal intervention in the external world (action). It is argued that thought, regardless of content, moral weight, or duration, maintains absolute moral immunity within the sealed boundaries of subjective consciousness, as it lacks causal power in reality. Intelligence and imagination are defined as a quantitative multiplier of internal simulations, where imagination acts as a decompression valve (catharsis) that prevents the external execution of harmful actions. The "Principle of Behavioral Equivalence" and the "Threshold of Environmental Information Leakage" are introduced, demonstrating that moral judgment is activated exclusively when information leaks into the environment, either through material alteration of behavior or through the transition to intersubjectivity (presence or perception by a third party).

items.title: Cognition Scale Taxonomy — Full Edition (v0.3).
items.abstract: This document defines a four-class cognition taxonomy and provides the formal boundaries, engineering requirements, and failure-mode analyses required to safely classify and compose artificial cognition systems. It introduces LCM – Large Cognition Model (human minds) LLM – Large Language Model MCM – Modest Cognition Model (deterministic, bounded reasoning systems) SCM – Simple Cognition Model (classical automation) Included MCM Compliance Checklist (normative; 10-category certification) Deeper Explanation Annex (examples + rationale) Drift & Failure Modes Annex (systemic risks + mitigation) This is a conservative taxonomy, intentionally non-anthropomorphic, designed to prevent category slippage and preserve clarity across engineering, governance, and public communication.

items.title: Topology of Consciousness and Examples of Potential Popperian Falsification for the Topological Model of Consciousness, Light, and Matter.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel topological and ontological model of reality that addresses the hard problem of consciousness by redefining physical space-time as a secondary holographic projection. Challenging the traditional, localized definition of a singularity, the author introduces the concept of Multiple Singularity—a distributed, non-local network of conscious nodes functioning via Bell non-locality and quantum superposition.Utilizing the mathematical framework of type III_1 von Neumann algebras and Tomita–Takesaki modular flows, the model establishes that proper time and internal dynamics are generated from within the structure of living consciousness itself, rather than being imposed by an external physical metric. The autonomy and irreducibility of subjective experience are shown to be structurally secured by a Massless Shield comprised of non-local wave dynamics, nontrivial holonomy, Gödelian incompleteness, and unique homotopy classes that prevent algorithmic reduction or external erasure.Within this framework, the four-dimensional Minkowski space-time acts merely as a projection screen, where the constant speed of light (c) functions not as a kinematic limit, but as a topological drag coefficient (the viscosity of time) regulating the phase synchronization and material rendering of underlying Serre Sheaves of meaning. To fulfill Karl Popper’s criterion of demarcation, the addendum outlines six distinct, empirically testable scenarios designed to falsify the model. These include measuring micro-fluctuations in the speed of light within hyper-dense quantum computing environments, observing observer-dependent decay rates in Quantum Zeno experiments, and monitoring non-local quantum field anomalies upon the biological collapse of structured systems exceeding the Bekenstein Bound.

items.title: The Fractal Cogito: Deconstructing the Epistemic Agent through the Biological Ship of Theseus.
items.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a minimalist, atemporal reformulation of the Cartesian cogito by eliminating the indexical, metaphysically burdened "I" and any duration-implied verb structures from the traditional formula cogito, ergo sum. Drawing on Georg Christoph Lichtenberg's critique of Descartes' subject-centered formulation, we argue that epistemology must not begin with the certainty of a substantial, unified, or enduring self, but rather with the non-indexical fact of presence. Integrating contemporary biology and quantum field theory, we demonstrate that the carbon-based cognitive substrate operates as a material Ship of Theseus; historical assumptions regarding permanent cardiac stem cells have been falsified by cellular turnover models, while synaptic plasticity confirms that the brain undergoes perpetual structural reconfiguration. Ontologically, no static physical or mental substance exists to occupy the role of the classic epistemic agent. To insulate the foundational anchor against temporal and subject-centered vulnerabilities, we formulate the core axiom as: The phenomenal datum is present (∃D Pres(D)). Even if the identity, continuity, or ontological nature of the subject remains entirely uncertain, the presence of a phenomenal datum cannot be coherently denied. Furthermore, we expand this anchor through the principle of epistemic responsiveness: the radical transformation of phenomenal coordinates (e.g., shifts in sensory inputs during spatial movement) and the dialectical act of a skeptic challenging this framework performatively reinstate the presence of a data-generating reality (retortion). By establishing this atemporal anchor, the paper demonstrates the collapse and suspension of the traditional Tripartite Model of Knowledge (Justified True Belief, JTB) at the foundational level, bypassing Gettier-style counterexamples through reflexive self-justification. Above this floor, JTB is reframed as an anonymous, recursive operational registration within a High-Probability Foundationalist superstructure, providing a fallible bridge toward probabilistic empirical inquiry and Quinean holism. Finally, this framework provides a novel dissolution of the classic Socratic paradox ("I know that I know nothing"), exposing it as a subject-substance illusion that violates the restrictions of radical skepticism. -/- Keywords: Descartes, cogito, Lichtenberg, skepticism, foundationalism, phenomenology, epistemology, JTB model, Socratic paradox, …

items.title: Correction: Legal frameworks for AI service business participants: a comparative analysis of liability protection across jurisdictions.
What’s unfair about resultant moral luck?
items.abstract: A popular reason for denying resultant moral luck has to do with its alleged unfairness. In this paper, I argue that although two existing objections against the unfairness argument are unsuccessful, it ultimately fails. First, I criticize the objection that the unfairness argument commits a category mistake. Second, I criticize the objection that because morality is unfair, the unfairness of resultant moral luck provides no evidence against its existence. Nevertheless, the unfairness argument fails because it cannot be fleshed out in a dialectically forceful way. The argument fails, in other words, because it cannot tip the scales in favor of denying resultant moral luck.

items.title: The Intimate Harmony Between the Intellect and Sensibility: McDowell and Perceptual Learning.
items.pub: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology 30 (2):279-305.
items.venue: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology
items.abstract: This paper argues for a shift in the debate surrounding McDowell’s conceptual-ism: from contents to capacities. This shift is important because the conceptual nature of a capacity is revealed in the way the capacity figures in the life of the animal, in particular in how the animal acquires and sustains the capacity. More specifically, I argue that a capacity is conceptual insofar as the subject can improve it by systematically exploiting interconnections among the features involved in its exercise. I first develop this notion through an analysis of skillful action, showing how a skilled agent perceives the interlocking demands of a situation and uses this perception to refine her performance. I then extend the model to perception itself, arguing that perceptual learning exhibits the same structure: theoretical knowledge can reshape perceptual organization, bringing it under conceptual control. This yields what I call a systematically rational capacity, which, I argue, comes in degrees and is not specific to humans. I next examine McDowell’s account of virtue, where practical wisdom is shown to consist in an intimate harmony between intellect and sensibility rather than a computation between independent components. I argue that this harmony, far from being restricted to the ethical domain, characterizes the relation between reason and sensibility in general:our intelligence just is the properly molded state of our perceptual capacities, reflectively adjusted. Finally, I turn to the role of language, which enables a degree of systematic integration unavailable to non-linguistic animals, and argue that language’s deepest contribution is not merely representational but ethical, and that here we can find what is special about us:language initiates us into a shared form of life in which we matter to one another and have a say in shaping what matters.

items.title: Transition, superposition, rémanence: on the temporal modulations of territorial polyrhythmy.
items.abstract: Existing frameworks for analyzing territorial temporality, from rhythmanalysis to smart city optimization, share a common limitation: they describe temporal regimes but do not theorize the passages between them. They operate as temporal toponymies, zoning time as though it were space.
