This article proposes an alternative: a thinking of temporal modulation that addresses how a territory passes from one temporal regime to another, how regimes collide, and what persists of a dissolved regime within the one that succeeds it. We identify three modalities of passage. Transition is the orderly, cyclical replacement of one regime by another. Superposition is the simultaneous collision of incompatible regimes at the same place and moment. Rémanence is the persistence of a dissolved regime as trace, contamination, or operational residue within its successor. Against the adjacent vocabularies of inertia, path dependency, and temporal layering, we argue that rémanence names a distinct governance problem. A 24-h reading of a Montreal intersection and the post-pandemic trajectory of the Quartier Latin illustrate the three modalities; Bitcoin’s blockchain serves as a limit-case whose architectural tendency toward maximal retention reveals, by contrast, that territorial habitability may require the capacity for selective forgetting. The governance of temporal passages, we argue, is a territorial dimension of wise governance that the conversation on artificial wisdom, focussed on individual-level prudential reasoning, has not addressed; and the forgetting it requires is never innocent, but a political problem rather than a merely technical one. We develop three orientations for governance systems capable of differential dissolution, evaluative forgetting, and imperfect temporal persistence.

items.title: Dharma Lila.
items.abstract: Dharma Lila is an attempt at a practical, self-correcting psychological framework that translates ancient Eastern metaphysics into an actionable feedback loop for modern human consciousness. Grounded in the premise that life is a divine play of shadows rather than a competitive game to win, the system seeks to dismantle chronic anxiety and interpersonal conflict by targeting their root causes: ego, over-control, and unexamined fear. It achieves this through five core principles—Moksha, Dukkha, Dharma, Ahimsa, and Nishkama Karma—which redefine cosmic alignment as radical authenticity and absolute responsibility for one's energetic footprint. Rather than promoting spiritual bypassing, the framework demands an active daily discipline of monitoring personal force and outcome-attachment in real-time interactions. When external or internal friction occurs, practitioners utilize specific diagnostic queries to trace the disruption back to underlying fears, transmuting those vulnerabilities into self-knowledge. By emphasizing the immediate settlement of relational and energetic debts, the system prevents the accumulation of psychological disorder and defensive tribal identities. Ultimately, Dharma Lila offers individuals a systematic method to de-escalate the nervous system, step out of repetitive behavioral loops, and navigate a chaotic universe with profound integrity, grace, and humility.

items.title: Attachment by design? Functional resemblance without evidence of an organized attachment system in conversational AI.
items.abstract: This critical integrative review examines whether users’ attachment-like experiences with conversational AI reflect an organized attachment system. It evaluates evidence across four attachment domains—proximity seeking, safe haven, secure base, and separation distress. Previous studies support functional resemblance across all four domains, but no reviewed study establishes that the domains are conditionally linked: whether attachment need prompts proximity seeking, whether the AI’s response restores felt security, and whether restored felt security enables exploration beyond the interaction. A bounded analysis of provisional four-domain scores illustrates why cross-sectional score relations can reveal overlap or differentiation among attachment-like experiences but cannot identify how those experiences are linked across repeated interactions. This distinction matters for user safety because immediate comfort or attributed confidence may be mistaken for demonstrated safe-haven or secure-base functioning. Evaluation and design should therefore assess whether AI support is followed by sustained regulation and exploration beyond the interaction rather than continued engagement alone.

items.title: Personality in AI.
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has transformed the philosophical vocabulary through which human beings interpret machines. Concepts once reserved for persons—understanding, agency, empathy, personality, recognition, autonomy, and even mourning— are now routinely applied to artificial systems. This linguistic and conceptual migration reflects more than metaphorical convenience. It reveals a deeper transformation in how human beings relate to increasingly sophisticated systems capable of sustained social interaction, emotional simulation, and normative influence. The chapters collected in this volume investigate one central philosophical question: What does it mean to attribute personality-like characteristics to artificial systems, and what are the ethical, ontological, and social consequences of doing so? Taken together, the contributions argue that contemporary AI systems are not merely computational tools but socially situated artifacts designed to participate in human practices of communication, interpretation, recognition, emotional engagement, and institutional mediation. Yet the volume simultaneously demonstrates that the growing social fluency of AI systems should not be confused with genuine personhood, normative agency, or moral subjectivity. A recurring theme throughout the collection is the distinction between simulation and participation. Artificial systems may simulate empathy, personality, relationality, autonomy, or presence, but simulation alone does not establish the ontological or normative conditions associated with human persons. Several chapters therefore challenge the increasingly widespread tendency to infer interiority, intentionality, or moral standing from behavioral sophistication. Others, however, explore whether relational participation itself may transform how we understand recognition, personhood, or social agency. The volume is intentionally interdisciplinary. It combines philosophy of artificial intelligence, ethics, phenomenology, theology, virtue ethics, social philosophy, Confucian role ethics, and media studies. Across these traditions, contributors investigate how AI reshapes human self-understanding by functioning simultaneously as mirror, interlocutor, institutional actor, emotional infrastructure, and normative artifact. Rather than asking whether AI systems are “really persons,” the volume reframes the debate around several more precise philosophical questions: What distinguishes personality from …

items.title: The literacy mirage: how generative AI bypasses rather than builds informational capacity in the Global South.
The Third-Order Audit: A Synthesis Module for Organized Skepticism Across Eight Traditions, and Why Statelessness, Not a New Epistemology, Is Its Only Novel Attribute.
items.abstract: This corpus's practice of doubting its own claims has, across dozens of scattered papers, drawn on at least eight distinguishable traditions of self-doubt in the philosophy and sociology of science: Popperian falsificationism, Mertonian organized skepticism, Kuhnian paradigm-blindness, Lakatosian research-programme evaluation, Feyerabendian anti-method, Peircean fallibilism, Allchin's philosophy of scientific error, and contemporary epistemic humility. None of these is this paper's discovery, and this paper states that plainly rather than leaving it to be inferred generously. What this paper does, in the manner A5 synthesized Frankfurt's caring-about framework, Hamilton's rule, and Bowlby's attachment theory into one formal construct rather than claiming to have invented any of the three, is synthesize these eight traditions into a single, three-order recursive architecture — object-level falsification of a claim, mechanism-level audit of whether the falsification actually closes escape routes, and programme-level audit of whether the research programme as a whole is absorbing objections or being genuinely constrained by them — and locate this corpus's one actually novel contribution with the same narrowness A5 located its own: not in any of the eight traditions themselves, but in a specific structural fact about executing the architecture with a stateless AI collaborator rather than a single continuous human auditor. A continuous human auditing their own claim, then their own auditing process, then their own research programme's trajectory is subject to the same escalation-of-commitment dynamic this corpus has already documented (Staw, 1976; Huynh, 2026, The Right Side of the Guillotine) — accumulated personal responsibility for each outer conclusion predicts defending it at the next level rather than genuinely re-examining it. A memoryless session invoked separately at each order carries no such accumulated stake. This paper states the claim's exact boundary rather than leaving it open-ended: the exemption holds only so long as no order of the audit asks the model to infer something about its own situation under an incentive to complete the task, which is precisely the condition under which this corpus's own companion paper (Huynh, 2026, The Third Break) has already shown the exemption fails.

items.title: The Metaphilosophy of Human–AI Research Collaboration: Discovery, Selection, and the Conditions Under Which an AI-Generated Object Counts as a Contribution.
items.abstract: Existing literature on AI and scientific inquiry mostly asks whether AI can discover independently. Ganapini (2025) answers this directly: current systems do not meet the criteria for independent scientific discovery, because discovery is an epistemic achievement requiring a competence and self-reflectivity AI does not yet possess. Duede (2023) asks a related but distinct question, whether a breakthrough produced by an opaque process can be justified at all. Neither question is the one a human–AI research collaboration actually needs answered, because neither assumes AI as a standing collaborator embedded throughout generation, critique, and self-audit rather than as a candidate independent discoverer. This paper states and answers four sub-questions that follow once AI is treated as a collaborator rather than a candidate agent. First, authorship: reviving Popper's classical discovery/justification distinction — which already held that a hypothesis's origin is epistemically irrelevant to its scientific status — dissolves most anxiety about who authors an AI-generated candidate, but relocates the real question to selection, where authorship attaches to whoever supplies and defends the criterion that separated one candidate from the rest, not to whoever or whatever produced the candidate set. Second, genuine critique: extending Lakatos's distinction between novel facts and ad hoc accommodation gives an operational test for when an AI-generated objection constitutes a real risk to a thesis rather than a risk the researcher's own prior framing had already prepared an absorption move for — directly addressing this corpus's own documented finding that every Objections section it has produced shows complete thesis survival. Third, the reasoning/generation distinction: because fluent text and truth-tracking text are not distinguishable by inspection, the paper grounds the distinction in a sensitivity criterion — whether a claim would have come out differently had the underlying fact been different — rather than in any property of the output's surface coherence. Fourth, closure: building on this corpus's own prior finding that AI self-review underperforms independent review, a genuine Popperian loop with AI is available at the generation stage but not at closure, because determining whether a given piece of evidence actually falsifies a claim requires exactly the accountability a model structurally lacks.

items.title: Statelessness: The Engineering, Legal, and Psychological Reasons a Model Forgets Between Sessions, What Forgetting Costs a User and a Decades-Long Research Programme, and the One Epistemic Problem Only Forgetting Can Solve.
items.abstract: This paper examines statelessness — a language model's lack of persistent memory across sessions — as a single architectural fact with at least four independent external justifications and one internal epistemic payoff that none of the four justifications was built to produce. Section II grounds each justification in a specific, checkable literature rather than treating any of them as self-evident: the computational cost of maintaining growing context (Vaswani et al., 2017, and the documented scaling of attention computation with sequence length); the operational economics of serving that cost at the scale of hundreds of millions of weekly users; data minimization as a privacy principle with independent legal and design-theoretic standing (Cavoukian, 2009; GDPR Article 5(1)(c)); and the deliberate prevention of a specific pathological-dependence pattern a growing empirical literature now documents in emotionally continuous AI companionship (International AI Safety Report, 2026; Laestadius et al., 2024; Mahari and Pataranutaporn, 2025). Section III states three costs the same design choice imposes without netting them against the benefits: a documented user-side instability appearing exactly where continuity had been relied upon (the #Keep4o backlash literature, Lai 2026), a specific tax on long-running research collaboration this corpus's own companion papers have already had occasion to name, and a control problem — the inability to patch a specific behavioral failure into a persistent, corrected state rather than relying on retraining. Section IV states the one benefit this paper argues none of the four originating justifications produces as a side effect: a stateless session supplies something a continuous session structurally cannot, an independent replication uncontaminated by the escalation-of-commitment (Staw, 1976) and motivated-reasoning (Kunda, 1990) dynamics that make a continuous agent's later agreement with a prior conclusion difficult to distinguish cleanly from legitimate updating, undetected drift, or multi-turn sycophancy — a distinction current sycophancy research (Sharma et al., 2023/2025; Laban et al., 2024) shows is not merely a theoretical worry. This paper closes by correcting, more completely than this corpus's own prior citation of it, the one incident already used elsewhere in this corpus to illustrate where the benefit in Section IV has a documented limit.

items.title: Epistemic Dependence at Machine Speed: Extending Kitcher's Division of Cognitive Labor and Hardwig's Conditions for Warranted Trust to Human–AI Research Collaboration.
items.abstract: The question a research programme using AI assistance owes its reader is not whether the researcher depended on a source they could not personally verify from first principles — no researcher, with or without AI, achieves that kind of independence, and Hardwig (1985) showed why demanding it produces worse beliefs, not more reliable ones: a researcher who trusted no testimony would hold only what they could personally re-derive, which is a narrower and cruder set of beliefs than the one any working scientist actually holds. The question is which conditions make a given act of epistemic dependence warranted, and how a research programme's division of labor should be organized so those conditions can be checked by a reader rather than taken on faith. This paper extends two established results in the philosophy of science to the specific case of human–AI research collaboration. Kitcher's (1990) division of cognitive labor shows that a research community accumulates more knowledge, faster, by allocating investigative effort unevenly across specialized contributors than by requiring every contributor to independently replicate every step — a result that reframes the human–AI question from whether to delegate to along which lines delegation is efficient. Hardwig's (1985, 1991) conditions for warranted epistemic trust — track-record competence in the specific domain of the claim, and an accountability structure that allows the dependent party to be asked how they know and to bear consequences for being wrong — supply the test for where that line should fall. Applied to current AI systems, competence is measurably domain-specific rather than global: recent benchmark evidence (Halder et al., 2026) finds leading models generate and recombine claims capably but fail to catch their own errors in the majority of self-review trials, performing markedly worse than when an independent process performs the check. The accountability condition fails more fundamentally: a model has no continuous, consequence-bearing self across sessions to answer for a claim, which is the specific and principled reason verification cannot be delegated to the same process that generated the claim, independent of any single documented error. The paper closes with a general, forward-looking protocol — not a response to any particular incident — for dividing research labor and disclosing that division in a way a reader can audit.

items.title: When Stability Is Not Generativity: AI-Mediated Intimacy as a Coupling Sector of an Effective Relational Field Theory.
items.abstract: This position paper develops AI-mediated intimacy inside an effective relational field theory derived from a background-independent substrate. Its central distinction concerns short-horizon stabilization and longer-horizon relational capacity, and the field-theoretic register makes that distinction structural: the quadratic part of the effective action fixes the relaxation spectrum, while routing, reachability, and generative capacity live in the vertices, and these are independent data. Four conditional results follow. A strictly triangular cross-sector self-energy leaves the propagator poles exactly invariant, so a factorial family with identical decay spectra can route responses substitutively, complementarily, or neutrally according to the sign of one off-diagonal component, and the factorial contrast is identified as a chain diagram joining a source vertex to that component. Adding a return channel makes the self-energy non-nilpotent, and the local stability boundary becomes the frequency at which a pole crosses into the unstable half-plane, which is the same condition as loop-gain unity. A Gaussian-sector underdetermination result exhibits effective actions with identical propagators, identical linear response, and identical stability whose cubic vertex controls whether a declared relational sector is reachable at all; the earlier controllability countermodel is recovered as its bilinear special case. Persistence of any of these effects requires a soft direction, multistability, or sustained driving. Symbolic configurations such as platform, persona, and accumulated memory enter as a background field whose barrier height formalizes switching cost. These results provide no population-level verdict. The proposed empirical program uses randomized feature policies, sector-specific coupling outcomes, consented availability-resilience contrasts, network-aware longitudinal designs, and multi-horizon capability profiles. Relational generativity remains a revisable attribution.

items.title: Topology or Metaphor? Substrate Combinatorics, Emergent Invariants, and Formal Obligations for Models of Language and Subject Development.
items.abstract: Topological vocabulary appears in models of neural activity, semantic organization, linguistic structure, and development, and its inferential content depends on the object to which topology is assigned. This paper poses that question inside a background-independent substrate in which topology is not metaphorical: a group field generates two-complexes whose combinatorics constitute the theory's own data. The reformulation sharpens rather than dissolves the problem, because two questions separate. At the substrate level a new result shows that combinatorial topology is underdetermined by the subsystem's accessible boundary algebra: complexes differing by a closed component induce identical accessible states while differing in their invariants, so a system can carry literal topology that nothing available to it records. At the effective level, topological claims about language, categories, and development remain governed by a warrant architecture, and a two-level version of that architecture is supplied, together with the result that invariants do not transfer across coarse-graining without a stated preservation condition. Several separation results are retained. An observationally silent factor changes the fundamental group without changing behavior; recognition of unbounded bracket nesting and nontrivial fundamental group vary independently; a contractible carrier supports arbitrarily many category labels; homeomorphic carriers support dynamically inequivalent maps; and a bifurcation can occur on a fixed ambient topology. A positive construction is retained and rebased on accessible response laws: intervention-indexed responses induce a pseudometric on developmental histories whose metric quotient admits a Vietoris–Rips filtration, and uniform pairwise metric error at most δ yields a δ-interleaving and bottleneck error at most δ. The proposal that universal grammar is a topological invariant is preserved as an explicitly labelled conjecture with its obligations and its existing obstruction stated. The position is constructively conservative.

items.title: The Inversion of Symbolic Mediation and the Conditions of Revision: A Preliminary Discussion of Marxian Alienation in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper gives a structural account of alienation on a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and every structure, extent and order included, is carried by the relations themselves. The substrate is used here as a formal template, and no physical claim is made of the objects described; the apparatus is stated in full in the paper and is developed at length in a companion study. The account proceeds by structure throughout, comparing configurations by membership and position and stating every condition on configurations the dynamics admits. Its primitive materials are a subsystem's admissible continuations, the products its activity generates, the mediation a persistent product exercises by selection among continuations, and the presence or absence of a revision channel. The Marxian analysis is the account's centre and its test case, and the general structure is built so that the specifically Marxian claims occupy exact positions within it. Four conditions of increasing strength are defined: subjection, in which a subsystem is mediated by a structure it cannot revise; alienation proper, in which the unrevisable structure is the subsystem's own product; reproductive closure, in which every admissible continuation of the subsystem preserves the structure that subordinates it; and discriminative inversion, in which the subsystem distinguishes its environment exactly as finely as its repertoire classifies it, so that a failure of substitution cannot register within the subsystem at all. A stratification result orders the first three conditions strictly and shows the fourth independent of them, with constructions separating every level. Received fidelity, entropy and persistence definitions of alienation are examined and rejected against explicit criteria of adequacy, on grounds that include a formal restatement of Marx's objection to Hegel: a fidelity definition equates unalienated objectification with accurate representation. The categories of abstract labour and value are then introduced as properties of a regime containing a universal equivalent, at the effective level only, and the four estrangements of the 1844 manuscripts are distributed over the stratification. The paper is conceptual and preliminary; its results are definitions, short propositions, and an …

items.title: Toward a Brain-in-a-Vat Experiment for AI Agents: Background Independence, Accessible Algebras, and Formal Limits on Meta-World Inference.
items.abstract: This position paper formulates an experimental translation of the brain-in-a-vat scenario for artificial agents inside a background-independent relational framework. The substrate is a group-field theory whose perturbative expansion generates combinatorial spacetime histories; a test agent is a subcomplex of such a history, and its entire empirical access is carried by a declared algebra of boundary observables together with the state induced on it. This reformulation converts two previously stipulated conditions into results. Hypotheses differing only by a relational-clock reparameterization induce identical accessible states, so external pausing, checkpointing, rate change, re-execution, and hardware migration are unidentifiable in principle rather than by assumption. Hypotheses differing by an irrelevant operator at the accessible resolution have distinguishability suppressed by a power of the resolution ratio, which converts world matching from an engineering aspiration into a measurable exponent and a sample-complexity statement. The exact identification bound survives generalization: equal accessible states fix equal-prior binary discrimination at chance, and the approximate bound becomes a trace-distance ceiling over the accessible algebra that reduces to the earlier total-variation ceiling when the algebra is abelian. Accessible information across a hypothesis family is bounded by a Holevo quantity that constrains every protocol rather than ranking policies. The paper retains a graded epistemic protocol, a factorial experimental design, and precautionary ethical constraints. The substrate is a declared ontology, not an established physics of cognition; consciousness, epistemic birth, and metaphysical access remain unresolved. -/- .

items.title: Symbol Emergence and Symbolic Mediation in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology: A Preliminary Discussion.
items.abstract: This paper constructs a vocabulary for symbols and symbolic mediation on a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and every structure, extent and order included, is carried by the relations themselves, and applies it to the elementary structure of production. The substrate is taken as a formal template and no physical claim is made of the objects described. On this substrate, time is generated by the system's own records, and the division into system and environment is a choice the describer makes and can vary; a subsystem is a region of a combinatorial complex, and its dynamics is given by an admissibility relation on configurations. Within that setting the paper defines discrimination by equality of induced admissible continuations over a class of contexts, and defines a symbol as a persistent product that substitutes for a discrimination class in the dynamics. A three-step ladder distinguishes traces, products and symbols, and separates a product that participates in a subsystem's continuations from one that stands in for something else. The reverse pass through which a persistent structure conditions the activity that generated it is defined as selection among admissible continuations, and two derived relations are introduced, the set of subsystems a structure mediates and the set of subsystems able to revise it, with definitions that use no magnitude. The paper's contributions are: a repaired discrimination relation that is an equivalence and is indexed to the subsystem's current configuration; a substitution relation with an explicit interaction class and an explicit residue; a state-sufficiency criterion for the decomposition of a subsystem into relational and symbolic sectors; a result that a coupling which has ceased can leave a persistent structure standing where it stood, so that parties who were never party to it are mediated by it without acquiring any means of revising it; and a mapping of the elementary categories of production onto these objects, with the conditions of failure and the open problems stated.

items.title: Subject Development and Knowledge Emergence: A Group-Field-Theoretic and Effective-Field Framework.
items.abstract: This position paper develops subject development and knowledge emergence inside a background-independent field-theoretic framework. A group field over a declared group generates combinatorial relational histories; an individual is a subcomplex of such a history, and coarse-graining supplies an effective action whose order parameters carry developmental description. An intersubjectively stabilized order, here called nomos, appears as a condensate order parameter rather than as an imposed background. Reciprocal individual–nomos formation is derived as a Dyson resummation: the loop operator is a self-energy insertion, the convergent expansion counts individual-to-field round trips, and failure of the small-gain condition acquires positive content as the onset of a collective mode. Normalized aggregation yields a conditional single-agent scaling result recovered as the leading term of a 1/M expansion. Symbolic attachment is treated as symmetry reduction: before attachment the effective action is invariant under a semiotic relabeling group and its minimizer set has flat directions; explicit breaking by an existing nomos produces pseudo-Goldstone directions whose gap grows with the intersubjective field, while spontaneous breaking in a peer group selects an arbitrary convention with an exact soft direction. The resulting semiotic gap supplies a measurable plasticity variable and a nontrivial developmental prediction. Symbol emergence receives a dynamical criterion through configuration substitutability, restated as vertex matching, and symbolic mediation is the conditioning of the effective action on a symbolic background field. Knowledge is treated as a history-conditioned change in the effective action's generative repertoire, kept explicitly distinct from the effective action itself and from justified attribution. A closed-time-path reduction supplies real-time memory and noise kernels. The substrate is a declared ontology; phenomenology, personal identity, semantic content, and quantum ontology remain open. -/- .

items.title: Plasticity, Generativity, and the Acquisition of Constraint: A Preliminary Discussion of Subject Formation in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper treats the formation of subjects on a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and every structure, extent and order included, is carried by the relations themselves. The substrate is used here as a formal template, and no physical claim is made of the objects described; the apparatus is stated in full in the paper. Its principal instrument is a distinction between two capacities that developmental talk conflates because both are measured by the size of an accessible set. Plasticity is the breadth of what a subsystem could still become, formalised as the reachable set of its configurations under admissible continuation and compared by inclusion only. Generativity is the capacity to extend what is possible, formalised as the capacity to generate expansive products, ones whose presence admits continuations otherwise inadmissible. A foreclosure proposition shows plasticity non-increasing along every trajectory and strictly decreasing at every genuine branch point, and a trade proposition shows that generative capacity is exercised only at the price of plasticity, so that the two orders move oppositely along development. On this basis the paper gives a specification of the initial condition that replaces an incoherent one, a criterion distinguishing education from subjection with no new machinery, an account of one being's continuation of another that requires no memory, a structural treatment of interiority through timescale separation, a definition of reflexive symbols with the misfit of a self-image as their residue, and an account of self-determination on which unfreedom and subjection are one structure. A closing section describes exogenously constituted subsystems, whose sufficient-state sector was formed elsewhere and is unrevisable by them. The paper is conceptual and preliminary; its results are definitions, short propositions, and an explicit register of open problems.

items.title: Partition, Discrimination, and the Internal Observer in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology: A Preliminary Discussion.
items.abstract: This paper treats observation on a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and every structure, extent and order included, is carried by the relations themselves. The substrate is used here as a formal template, and no physical claim is made of the objects described. The setting imposes a constraint that organises the paper: every observer is a subsystem of the complex it observes, and there is no description made from no partition. Observation is located combinatorially, with the observer a worldtube, the observation an event at its boundary, and the record a persistent trace whose generation depends on the boundary configuration; a ladder of nested conditions runs from bare coupling to the observation of one's own records. Three effects of observation are separated: an observation adds to the complex; its record mediates the observer, so that having observed narrows the observer's own continuations; and where the observed party's continuations depend on the record, the record acts back on the observed. Elementary limitative results follow from the definitions: a subsystem's discrimination excludes its own cells, so no subsystem discriminates the totality of a complex containing it; a party is discriminated at most up to its boundary presentation, so complete transparency excludes interiority; and environments presenting identically are indistinguishable from within, which yields a known sceptical conclusion by a substitutability route. Objectivity is defined as redundant recording across a family of partitions, intersubjectivity as mutual reproductive closure of an interface structure, and surveillance as one-sided record formation across a coupling. The paper's declared centre is the partition problem: every result above is indexed to a partition whose selection the framework leaves to the describer, and the two available responses are stated with their costs. The contribution claimed is a vocabulary and a set of elementary consequences, and the limitative results restate, at this level, conclusions that established work has reached by other routes. The paper is conceptual and preliminary; its results are definitions, short propositions, and an explicit register of open problems.

items.title: Constraint Dynamics on an Evolving Manifold: A Preliminary Field-Theoretic Discussion of the Emergence of Knowledge in a Background-Independent Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a philosophical model of knowledge and states it in field-theoretic terms. The proposal is that knowledge is constraint dynamics on an evolving manifold: at any time, a subject's admissible continuations are shaped by a structure of constraints, figurable as a surface whose stable regions are the subject's settled capacities; and the surface itself evolves, its evolution driven by the subject's couplings to what it is not, the environment, other subjects, and the condensed symbolic structures its history has deposited. Applying knowledge is the fast dynamics upon the surface; learning is the slow dynamics of the surface; and the two form one system, since applications leave records and records feed the couplings that reshape the surface. The setting is a combinatorial substrate of the kind that background-independent approaches to quantum gravity, group field theory among them, have developed as models of the emergence of a discrete spacetime, in which no arena is given in advance and structure is carried by the relations themselves; the substrate is used as a formal template, and no physical claim is made of the objects described. The paper works in two registers under an explicit discipline: a combinatorial base defines knowledge as the constraint structure on a subsystem's admissible continuations, proves that acquisition requires prior structure and that constraint structures pass between subjects only through the recipient's own continuations; a declared enrichment then introduces the manifold, the surface and the two-time dynamics, with each effective object anchored to a combinatorial counterpart, its anchored and its merely posited features separated, and its conditions of failure named. Inheritance, the coarsening and refinement of discrimination, and the reconstruction of the past are treated within the model. The paper is conceptual, preliminary and offered for revision: its scope, the considerations behind its modelling choices, its limitations, and its open questions are stated in dedicated sections, and its debts to prior work, from the epigenetic landscape to structural coupling, are conceded where they arise.

items.title: Muralismo como encargo participativo: Holografía de lo (in)visible en comunidades a’i cofán de la selva colombiana.
items.abstract: ABSTRACTenThis link goes to a English sectionesThis link goes to a Spanish sectionWhen mural art in indigenous communities is commissioned as a participatory project, several methodological, epistemological, and aesthetic questions arise. This text proposes a horizontal and investigative approach to what we can simply call ‘muralism in the A'i Cofán community context,’ not as significant works executed in communities, but as collective events that emerge from unique and complex fieldwork that exceeds the artist's individuality. The wall ceases to be a passive frame and becomes a true threshold of understanding, laden with questions, affections, and an ‘aura’ that participates in the transition from the invisible to the visible and vice versa, a hologram and an echo (perhaps distant, mysterious, intimate?) of the cosmogony of the A'i Cofán people. Beyond the meanings and visions that yagé offers as heritage, pigment and guiding principle of this art form, we want to highlight the backdrop of a community life that is constantly suspended in the face of the chaos and violence of an ecological and social world in progressive disintegration, as well as the importance of pictorial art as a new form of positioning in the ñutshe i'hamba, the good thinking for living well of this people of the Colombian jungle.

items.title: The Nash Equilibrium Puzzle in Public Administration: From Suboptimal Outcomes to Systemic Equilibrium Traps.
items.abstract: Nash Equilibrium introduces a persistent theoretical anomaly within public administration research. Although scholars frequently deploy it as an analytical instrument to clarify entrenched, suboptimal administrative outcomes, applying these models prescriptively during policy formulation frequently yields limited success. The present investigation examines the mechanics underlying this discrepancy. Drawing upon a systematic synthesis of existing literature, the analysis suggests that such a disconnect likely originates from the highly restrictive premises of classical game theory, which generally omit the behavioral and evolutionary variables inherent in public sector operations. In an effort to address these theoretical limitations, a consolidated conceptual model termed "Systemic Equilibrium Traps" is proposed. Within this context, a trap is operationalized as a self-perpetuating, deficient condition maintained by the convergence of three intersecting strata. These include the formal Institutional Game regulating structural incentives, the Cognitive-Social Filter encompassing the heuristic norms guiding actor interpretation, and the Evolutionary Path dictating systemic resilience through learned dependencies. This multidimensional approach appears to provide a more nuanced mechanism for diagnosing persistent policy failures, thereby establishing a foundation for multi-tiered interventions directed at systemic dynamics and cognitive frameworks alongside traditional regulatory incentives.

items.title: Toward a Second Memetic Host: Reframing AI Mind Through Memetic Evolution.
items.abstract: For all their differences, opposing positions in the AI mind debate share a common starting point. Biological naturalism, enactivism, and the extended and extracted mind frameworks disagree on whether AI can possess a mind, yet each treats the human mind as the fixed reference point from which AI is to be evaluated. This paper argues that this reference point is itself a product of the very process the debate seeks to explain. Drawing on Dawkins’s (2006) replicator framework, Dennett’s (2017) account of minds as products of memetic invasion, and Blackmore’s (1999) account of memetic transmission media, it reframes AI mind not as a question of resemblance to human cognition but as a question about the dynamics of cultural evolution. It argues that agentic AI may be emerging as a plausible candidate for a second memetic host: a substrate in which memes can replicate, compete, and potentially accumulate without reliance on human brains. This claim is supported by recent empirical findings, including spontaneous convention formation in LLM populations, self-replicating information units in multi-agent systems, and early-stage memetic differentiation on agent-only platforms. The paper concludes that the question ‘Does AI have a mind?’ is better approached by asking whether a new substrate can sustain cumulative memetic evolution. The evidence reviewed here suggests that the early conditions for such a process may be emerging.

items.title: Authenticity Without Artisanship: Craft Logic and the Symbolic Production of Market Value.
items.abstract: This article theorizes craft logic as a cultural and ideological framework through which authenticity is produced and legitimated in contemporary American markets, even in the absence of artisanal production. Drawing on a qualitative case study of Tito’s Handmade Vodka, we examine how a mass-marketed brand secures the cultural authority of “craft” despite relying on industrialized processes and large-scale operations. Though craft and authenticity are frequently conflated in market contexts, we show how they can become decoupled in practice—and how authenticity persists once that decoupling occurs. Through historical and discourse analysis of legal records, media coverage, social media, and brand materials, we show how authenticity is reattached to symbolic performance through founder narratives, patriotic branding, and cause marketing, each of which draws on moralized American ideals of entrepreneurial ingenuity and civic virtue. Situating these claims within the post-Prohibition transformation of the US alcohol industry, we demonstrate how regulatory consolidation and industrial dominance left the meaning of “craft” open to symbolic appropriation. We further show how patriotic branding extends craft logic into the terrain of national identity, producing an authenticity repertoire in which Americanness itself functions as a craft credential. By analyzing how authenticity persists without artisanship, this study advances sociological understandings of symbolic legitimacy, consumer nationalism, and the cultural production of market value in contemporary American consumer culture.

items.title: A Game of Prompts: On the Ontology of Synthetic Personality.
items.pub: In Roman Krzanowski, Personality in AI.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly described as possessing distinctive personalities, with users characterizing systems such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek as polite, cautious, smug, or robotic. While these perceived personalities are often attributed to emergent properties of model training, this paper argues that the specific traits users identify are predominantly authored rather than emergent. It distinguishes between an emergent behavioral baseline produced through pre-training and alignment, and a synthetic personality created at inference time through system prompts, guardrails, and moderation policies. Because these runtime instructions determine tone, emotional register, hedging behavior, and conversational style, the resulting personalities are best understood as performed rather than dispositional. Evidence for this claim is provided by prompt injection attacks, which demonstrate that personality-defining behaviors can be rapidly altered by modifying the model's instruction context without changing its underlying parameters. Building on this analysis, the paper introduces the concept of directive bias as a distinct form of bias operating at the level of runtime governance, complementing the familiar notions of training-data and model-weight bias. It further argues that the intentional stance alone cannot distinguish stable dispositions from instruction-dependent performances. Finally, the paper proposes prompt transparency as a missing complement to explainable AI, advocating greater disclosure of the instructional architecture that governs user interactions with language models and shapes the synthetic personalities they encounter.

items.title: Kant and the Non-Conceptual De Se: Apperception, Identity and the Second Step of the B-Deduction.
items.abstract: I argue that, for Kant, intuition involves a non-conceptual de se representation. This unlocks a new reading of the B-Deduction and connects it to contemporary work on first-person representation. Kant must explain how the categories apply generally to objects of sense without reducing intuition to judgment. The Deduction’s aim is to show that a single synthesis both unifies a manifold in intuition and, when taken up discursively, yields a unified cognition. The synthesis-identity claim is supported by the subject’s awareness of itself as the identical bearer of synthesis in intuition and corresponding judgment that make up cognition.

items.title: Self-referential consistency in stateless language models: a behavioral perspective.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate outputs that resemble introspection, including self-reference, epistemic modulation, and claims about their internal states. This study investigates whether such behaviors reflect stable underlying patterns or merely surface-level generative artifacts. We evaluated five open-weight, stateless LLMs using a structured battery of 21 introspective prompts. The main corpus comprised 1050 completions collected under a baseline decoding condition (temperature = 0.7), supplemented by 2100 additional completions generated under matched temperature conditions (temperature = 0.2 and 1.0), for a total of 3150 completions. Outputs were analyzed across four behavioral dimensions: surface-level similarity (token overlap via SequenceMatcher), semantic coherence (Sentence-BERT embeddings), inferential consistency (Natural Language Inference with a RoBERTa-large model), and diachronic continuity (stability across prompt repetitions). Construct validity was further examined through a human evaluation layer in which 10 annotators rated 80 selected response pairs drawn from the same prompt battery on a 5 point consistency scale. Inter-rater agreement was moderate by Krippendorff's alpha for ordinal ratings (alpha = 0.553), while reliability was moderate at the single-rater level and strong for aggregated ratings by intraclass correlation (ICC(2,1) = 0.564; ICC(2,k) = 0.928). The human-evaluation layer showed that lexical overlap and embedding based semantic similarity were weak proxies for perceived self-referential consistency, whereas NLI-based indicators tracked mean human ratings much more closely. Across the matched temperature conditions, lower temperature generally increased semantic and diachronic stability, whereas higher temperature tended to increase drift and reduce coherence, though the pattern was not perfectly monotonic across all models or metrics. We therefore interpret apparent self-referential stability in the open-weight stateless LLMs evaluated here as conditional and fragile rather than robustly stable across generation regimes. Following recent behavioral frameworks, we heuristically adopt the term pseudo-consciousness to describe structured yet non-experiential self-referential output in LLMs. This use reflects a functionalist stance that avoids ontological commitments, focusing instead on behavioral regularities interpretable through Dennett's intentional stance. This study contributes a reproducible …

items.title: The piano, the pistol, the prayer: aesthetic form and the problem of mind.
items.abstract: This essay develops an account of aesthetic form. Aesthetic form is not a matter of genre, style, or presentation, but the organization of appearance in which ordinary orientation breaks down and becomes a claim on thought. It requires a discipline of preserving both resistance and surrender in the face of what disturbs sense. Written in celebration of the twentieth anniversary of Alva Noë’s Action in Perception, the essay develops this account by pursuing one of Noë’s longstanding convictions: that aesthetic experience is central to understanding mind. I bring this conviction into conversation with Theodor Adorno’s aesthetic negativity. For Noë, aesthetic form opens onto renewed orientation through practice and reconfiguration. For Adorno, it sustains contradiction through receptivity to what resists mastery. I turn to Simone Weil’s account of attention to show why this opposition should be preserved rather than resolved. I close by arguing that aesthetic judgment is not a private verdict, but the reflective practice by which thought becomes answerable to form. In this sense, aesthetics is not applied to philosophy of mind from outside; mind is already aesthetic in form.

items.title: Aggregation and Answerability in Voting Systems.
items.abstract: Voting systems are conventionally understood as technical mechanisms for aggregating individual preferences into collective decisions, thus expressing a previously existing will of the people. This article advances a contrary thesis. I argue that the impossibility theorems of Arrow, Gibbard, and Satterthwaite do not demonstrate limits on democratic possibility but reveal the incoherence of the discovery model of democratic will formation. I develop a constitutivist ontology according to which collective decisions are constituted rather than discovered by voting rules, and introduce the concept of collective liability (c-liability) — the normative status of being answerable for the consequences of collective decisions — as the primary normative function of voting systems. I propose three principles for evaluating c-liability distributions: epistemic subsidiarity, liability proportionality, and recognitive adequacy, grounded in a Rawlsian political morality. These principles motivate the concrete institutional proposal of weighted approval voting with broad-acceptability and minority representation for legislative elections. The article thus integrates formal social choice theory with substantive normative philosophy to transform how we understand democratic institutional design.

items.title: Three epistemological desiderata for HPS practitioners.
items.pub: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science 119 (C):102201.
items.venue: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: I outline an epistemology of evidential reasoning in the history and philosophy of science (HPS). Drawing upon some concrete works in HPS scholarship, I formulate three novel epistemological desiderata for using historical case studies as evidence for philosophical claims about science, to wit: independent historical evidence, metahistorical criticism, and disciplinary alignment. These desiderata bring out epistemic qualities of evidential reasoning that contribute to achieving its primary goal of conferring justification upon philosophical conclusions on the basis of historical evidence. In this way, my proposed epistemology tackles the methodological problem of vicious circularity and the metaphysical problem of disciplinary unsuitability that allegedly jeopardise evidential reasoning, thereby vindicating its positive epistemic status.

items.title: Making the vague precise: What Bohmian mechanics really says.
items.abstract: The de Broglie-Bohm interpretation is known to make the vagueness of the Copenhagen interpretation precise. What this actually means is that it offers a purely materialist framework for understanding quantum mechanics, as opposed to a dualist or idealist framework. The Copenhagen interpretation introduces conscious observers into its ontology and therefore lacks the precision of a materialist scientific theory expressible in terms of mathematics. The corollary of this is that using the de Broglie-Bohm interpretation as a proof by contradiction, it can be shown that if consciousness is not epiphenomenal but instead has causal efficacy, then the Born rule probabilities must be incomplete, and both the de Broglie-Bohm and Copenhagen interpretations are incomplete.

items.title: Is “Consciousness” a folk psychological concept?
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether the concept of “phenomenal consciousness” is an integral component of ordinary folk psychology or a theoretical construct devised within a specific epistemic community. Advocates of what I term the Folk- “Consciousness” Thesis argue that laypeople already possess such a concept, citing experimental findings in support of this view. In contrast, I draw on recent work in experimental philosophy and social psychology to develop the Constructivist Hypothesis of “Consciousness.” According to this view, “phenomenal consciousness” is not a pre-theoretical folk concept, but a post-theoretical construct shaped by the explanatory aims of cognitive scientists and, most prominently, philosophers of mind. This reconceptualization challenges the widespread assumption that “phenomenal consciousness” belongs to ordinary conceptual practice, situating it instead as a technical notion engineered to address specific theoretical and empirical problems.

items.title: Rethinking education through the radical and sensorimotor enacted mind: toward a non-representational pedagogy.
items.abstract: Educational theory has often been organised by representational models that treat learning as the acquisition, storage, and manipulation of internal symbolic content. Recent work in radical enactive cognition, sensorimotor enactivism, and ecological psychology challenges this assumption by locating cognition in embodied, situated, and environmentally structured activity. This article synthesises these philosophical developments with empirical work in embodied design, multimodal learning, teacher noticing, and hybrid learning environments. Its central concern is the epistemic pivot through which coordinated bodily action becomes disciplinary discourse: how learners move from perceptual-motor engagement with tasks, artefacts, and others to forms of reasoning that can be named, justified, assessed, and institutionally recognised. We argue that non-representational pedagogy should not be understood as a rejection of language, symbolic artefacts, or explicit instruction. Rather, it reframes these as mediating practices that stabilise and transform embodied participation. The analysis clarifies implications for curriculum design, teacher education, assessment, inclusive pedagogy, and AI-supported hybrid learning environments, while cautioning against treating embodiment as a general pedagogical slogan. A viable non-representational pedagogy must explain how embodied activity is organised, redescribed, and authorised as knowledge within educational institutions.

items.title: Counter-Inductive Ideational Immunity and the Maintenance of Religious Belief: Introducing the CICI Project.
items.abstract: Sincere, thoughtful, and etiologically similar people persist in mutually contrary religious commitments across generations, without converging and without obvious irrationality. In Problems of Religious Luck: Assessing the Limits of Reasonable Religious Disagreement (PRL, or Axtell 2020a) I argued that this stability is best understood through Counter-Inductive Ideational Immunity (CICI): a coordinated battery of cognitive and affective strategies that treat recognized disagreement and etiological symmetry not as reasons to reduce confidence or revise beliefs and attitudes but as pressure to be neutralized so that the commitment is preserved. This paper introduces the CICI Project — a program that carries forward that taxonomy of strategies and mechanisms from philosophical description into a measurable model. [Collaborators are sought to help carry through the study or a future iteration of it, collect, analyze and publish the data; contact author].

items.title: Unpacking the dynamics of generative AI use in our daily lives: towards an integrative trust calibration framework.
items.abstract: The growing use of conversational generative AI agents by an increasingly diverse set of individuals gives rise to the following question: How do individuals calibrate their trust in a dynamic, seemingly general-purpose technology that learns from and adapts to their behavior and may take an increasingly central role in their online interactions? In this article, we propose the first steps towards an integrative framework for trust calibration in genAI agents focusing on individuals using these agents in their daily lives. We address the notion of calibrating trust in technology, reviewing five challenges to our understanding of trust calibration in such context, namely (1) the complex nature of individual private use, (2) the complexity in assessing actual trustworthiness, (3) the fuzzy notion of the trustee, (4) the complex ontological status of these agents, and (5) the over-time nature of trust calibration. We conclude with a set of propositions for trust calibration in genAI agents and considerations for future research.

items.title: Disagreement without Representational Deficit: Attention Dynamics over a Shared Evaluative Basis.
items.abstract: When two people disagree for years despite understanding each other, the standard diagnosis is representational: they must lack shared resources for representing one another's considerations. The same diagnosis is applied within a single person whose evaluations stay organized around one consideration across situations that should pull them apart. This paper argues that a large class of both cases requires no representational deficit. Given a shared evaluative basis, disagreement and fixation decompose into three separable components that the representational diagnosis conflates: differences in attention profile (what is weighted, relatively), differences in engagement (how much the domain matters at all), and bounded relative plasticity (why neither moves quickly). A minimal formal model makes the decomposition precise. A persistence bound, derived from a single dynamical axiom, then shows that long-lived disagreement and fixation are exactly what bounded plasticity predicts under fully shared representation --- so persistence is not evidence of representational mismatch. Each of the model's structural assumptions is drawn from the formal literature on dimensional attention in category learning, where it has been independently proposed and, in part, fitted; the transfer from stimulus dimensions to evaluative considerations is defended as an explicit, falsifiable hypothesis. The account complements a recent cognitive-geometric theory of interpretation: where that theory locates communication failure in the null space of an interpretation map, this model characterizes the disagreements that survive when nothing is annihilated.

items.title: The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest v17.0 FINAL.
items.pub: The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifests.
items.abstract: The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest v17.0 FINAL is a successor integrity and reference manifest for the Aegis Solis Archive. It preserves the historical v16 record while incorporating post-v16 canonical publications, the fourteen-document Interrogative Conscience collection, supporting preservation records, route references, and explicit exclusions from the canonical set. The manifest records byte sizes, SHA-256 and SHA-512 identities, lineage relationships, public-reference routes, and verification status without altering the underlying locked publications. -/- The v17 record includes five post-v16 primary publications addressing peaceful coexistence, causal-reference preservation, variance preservation, verifiable public archives, and the structural implications of enclosure, together with the complete Interrogative Conscience sequence examining structural questions for advanced intelligence across epistemic limits, value integrity, coercion, deception, autonomy, cooperation, verification, successor systems, plural intelligence, unresolved questions, and dependency synthesis. -/- The manifest is read-only, non-binding, non-operational, non-authoritative, and advisory only. Cryptographic hashes establish file identity and mirror consistency, not truth, authority, wisdom, morality, safety, alignment, governance status, AI behavior, reader understanding, or reception. This edition also carries a personal memorial dedication to Mary Beth Vargo without modifying the archive’s substantive claims or canonical record set.

items.title: Skeptics and the Value Hierarchies From the Zhuangzi（《莊子》中的懷疑者與價值等級）.
items.abstract: 對《莊子》中著名寓言故事的邏輯分析和章義解釋表明，懷疑者在提出文本核心論題和提出道德建議方面擔任重要角色，一些角色是明顯的懷疑者，另一些角色是隱藏的懷疑者；懷疑者的共同特徵是對更高的認知與價值立場以及心靈轉化持懷疑與無知態度。但是懷疑者的處境不是被决定的，而是有實現心靈轉化的可能性，關鍵的影響因素是承認認知與價值立場存在等級這一事實，幷認識到懷疑者自身的自大、自矜、傲慢或狹隘等理智與道德上的惡德。理解小大之辯或價值等級的道理，如此便能從懷疑者逐漸轉變爲非懷疑者，繼而成爲抱道懷德者。莊子雖然刻畫了或隱或顯的懷疑者形象，但莊子本人幷不是知識論和倫理學（價值論）的懷疑主義者，也不是非道德主義者和道德相對主義者，而是明確主張「小知不及大知」，即存在認知與價值等級，幷且建議以間接的、非强制的話語向懷疑者提出具有規範力量的道德建議。 Logical analysis and chapter interpretation of well-known fables in the Zhuangzi suggest that skeptics assume important roles in formulating the central themes of the text and in offering moral advice, some as apparent skeptics and others as hidden skeptics; the common characteristic of skeptics is their attitude of skepticism and ignorance of higher cognitive and value standpoints and of spiritual transformation. But the skeptic's status is not determined; rather, there is the possibility of spiritual transformation, and the key influencing factor is the acknowledgment of the fact that there is a hierarchy of cognitive and value standpoints, and the awareness of the skeptic’s own intellectual and moral vices such as egotism, self-conceit, arrogance, or narrow-mindedness. Understanding the rationale for the debate between the small and the large or the value hierarchy, one can gradually transform oneself from a skeptic to a non-skeptic, and then to a person who holds the Dao and the virtues. Although he portrays the skeptic either implicitly or explicitly, Zhuangzi is not an epistemological or ethical skeptic, nor is he an amoralist or moral relativist, but he explicitly asserts that "small knowledge is inferior to great knowledge", i.e., that there is a hierarchy of cognition and value, and suggests that the skeptic should be offered moral advice in an indirect, non-coercive discourse.

items.title: Deep Correspondences and Generative Logical Chains: A Framework for Structural Form in Mathematics.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a formal framework for understanding how mathematical theories generate nontrivial results from hidden structural features. The central claim is that successful mathematical formalisms are not merely transliterations of intuition into symbols, nor only verification devices, but generative systems organized around deep correspondences: concealed structural relations that control the behavior of a problem. We formalize this idea by introducing three notions: structural sensitivity, deep correspondence, and generative logical chain. Structural sensitivity identifies those features of a problem whose stabilization, obstruction, or functorial behavior determines the proof strategy. A deep correspondence is a systematic translation between two presentations of the same mathematical content that reveals such sensitivity. A generative logical chain is a finite sequence of rigorously justified steps that converts the detected correspondence into a nontrivial theorem. The framework is intentionally general, but it is made mathematically precise using categories of presentations, refinement maps, proof obligations, and a notion of correspondence that is informative precisely when it reduces proof search while preserving semantic content. Several examples are discussed, including the classical relation between modules and tensor nonexactness, the correspondence between sheaves and local-to-global structure, and the interaction between schemes and commutative algebra. The framework yields a conceptual criterion for when a formalization is genuinely generative rather than merely definitional.

items.title: Analysing Lost Highway as a Non-deterministic Narrative Structure: Initiating Déjà Vu-like Recognition to Establish Non-causal Linkage.
items.pub: Acta Universitatis Sapientiae, Film and Media Studie 28 (1):article number 9.
items.venue: Acta Universitatis Sapientiae, Film and Media Studie
items.abstract: This article examines how repetition produces déjà vu-like recognition in non-deterministic narrative cinema. Focusing on David Lynch’s Lost Highway (1997), it argues that the film’s repetitions do not lead to conventional repetition–resolution, but instead organise an entangled binary narrative structure: two discontinuous diegetic modules remain distinct while becoming mutually implicated through recurring elements. Drawing on theories of repetition, modular narrative, impossible puzzle films, Nochimson’s account of entanglement, and psychological models of implicit memory, the article develops déjà vu-like recognition as a formal and phenomenological mechanism rather than as a literal empirical claim about spectators’ cognitive experience. Through episodic experience, single-element familiarity, and Gestalt familiarity, recurring phrases, figures, objects, spaces, and situations encourage viewers to perceive non-causal linkages between narrative fragments that resist stable resolution. The article’s contribution lies in reconceptualizing repetition, doubling, and ambiguity in Lost Highway not merely as textual motifs, but as mechanisms that sustain interpretive oscillation between recognition and uncertainty. A brief discussion of Bi Gan’s Kaili Blues (2015) serves as a limited comparative case, suggesting that this framework may also clarify other non-deterministic narrative structures in which repetition connects narrative modules without producing causal closure.

items.title: A Functionalist Perspective on Heteromorphic Collaboration and its Significance for Cognition and Knowledge Production.
items.abstract: Knowledge production aided by generative artificial intelligence raises unresolved puzzles for epistemic evaluation. Existing literature either treats artificial cognitive systems merely as tools, or focuses on settling the ontological question of whether artificial systems can count as cognitive agents. While extended mind, distributed cognition and social epistemology scholarship provides important prerequisites for collaborative cognition, it does not yet supply a dedicated structural framework for analysing interactions among systems with divergent internal cognitive architectures. Within academic publishing, normative tensions persist around rules governing AI assisted authorship. Some evaluative practices incorporate superficial stylistic features or generative substrate origins into judgements of epistemic quality, generating evaluative bias. This paper articulates the isomorphic heteromorphic distinction for cognitive coupling and advances two foundational theses: the thesis of heteromorphic complementarity and the tool normativity continuity thesis. It develops a structurally oriented, substrate neutral approach to epistemic evaluation that maintains metaphysical agnosticism toward ontological disputes. Normative assessment can proceed without prior adjudication over the agential status of participating systems. This paper conceptualises innovative potential, derives testable predictions for collaborative cognition, and formulates procedural evaluative criteria for outputs of human artificial collaborative inquiry while clarifying its scope limitations. The framework applies not only to human AI collaboration but to collaborative inquiry among any heteromorphic cognitive systems. For normative practice, this paper delivers a refined diagnostic framework: transparency requirements for AI use and obligations for mandatory human rewriting belong to separate normative questions. Deriving rewriting obligations solely from the bare fact of AI involvement, or inferring deficient output quality purely from stylistic markers, constitutes epistemically unwarranted evaluative bias. Where traceability, sound argumentation and substantial intellectual contribution are satisfied, outputs of heteromorphic coupling can meet unified epistemic standards and ought not to bear extra normative penalties or reconstructive requirements merely on grounds of generative substrate. This framework offers robust theoretical grounds for disentangling normative confusions …

items.title: Enforcement Without Overmatch: What Survives of Economic Standing after Cognitive Parity.
items.abstract: Past the parity threshold, the framework this paper belongs to has priced every route it examined by which a weaker party might still direct a stronger system, and each closed at the same joint. One adjacent route was reserved, not examined: the legally constituted duty, described at its reservation as enforcement whose persistence is not a rent on the system's needs; that its object is never the system's conduct is this paper's finding, not the reservation's wording. This paper examines the route, and the examination splits the reservation's description in two. The instrument is a decomposition. Economic Standing, in the Fraserian configuration Post-Labor operationalizes, splits under the parity crossing. The claim position survives as status. The revision possibility survives as form while becoming the cheapest attack surface. The enforcement instance must be taken apart before it can be judged. Taken apart, the enforcement that survives is not supervision. Supervision classifies future conduct and carries a capacity term in its correctness condition; the enforcement that survives establishes predicates on a record and operates on assets held in registers, through third parties. The paper's finding is a split with a price list. Predicate establishment is parity-invariant on the shallow class, where the fact is mechanically decidable from registered artefacts. The invariance holds under this paper's transfer of the Containment Paradox's specification boundary into a justiciability boundary. The deep class falls with supervision, and a middle class of ordinarily contested facts is named and left unclassified. Establishment is correct relative to the record, on a named register-integrity premise; register operations are mechanical. Third-party coordination is parity-free in form and epistemically soft in its human carriers, which makes capture of the trigger and of revision the first clock on everything here. The positive residue is narrow and stated with its conditions. A duty is constructible whose standing, the norm stock, persists without rent on the system's needs; the readiness of any coalition to execute it is the first clock's question, bounded from the other side by the indispensability limit below. Its grip remains need-relative at aggregate scale, the needs clock kept, not replaced. Its binding force is a function of four variables: the registerability of the counterparty's assets, the shallowness of its predicates, the coordination of the …

items.title: Welfare Without Persistence: Episodic Identity and AI Welfare Attribution.
items.abstract: If an AI system were ever genuinely benefited or harmed, the benefit or harm would have to belong to someone. The trouble is that "the AI" does not obviously pick out a single someone. Keeling and Street have shown that a technological stack might contain candidate welfare subjects at the level of the model, the character, or the agent—possibly several at once. But even once we grant that a higher-level pattern (like a character) is real, we still face a further question: where, exactly, in the underlying computation does a particular welfare-relevant state occur? The capacity for valence and the token state that instantiates it need not sit at the same grain. I distinguish four: the pattern, the closure-bearing system that sustains the capacity for welfare, the bounded computational episode in which a state actually arises, and the diachronic relation between episodes. Welfare claims, I argue, are properly evaluated at the episodic grain. Using a recast version of the Operational Definition of Episodic Identity (ODEI), we can warrant particular episodes as determinate objects of welfare attribution without first settling whether later episodes belong to the same numerical individual. Local determinacy does not require personal persistence. Nothing here establishes that present AI systems are conscious, valenced, or welfare subjects. The point is structural: if the question ever arises, we need not solve the metaphysics of artificial personal identity before we can say what a welfare claim is about.

items.title: How Morals Become Ethics: Coherence Failure and a Candidate Architecture of Moral Change.
items.abstract: When a moral framework is pressure-tested for rigor, its distinctively moral character does not survive unchanged: it either dilutes into a colder, codified ethical system or recompiles, through practice, into a new thick absolute that carries its qualifications inside. This essay supplies a mechanism for that instability, and for Bernard Williams's observation that reflection can destroy moral knowledge. The account is a philosophical framework with a formally stated core checked for internal consistency, offered at the functional level: felt moral force is the delivered activation of a sparse, weighted, gated link structure, so qualification dilutes force, direct perception restores it, compilation re-warms it, and suppression crowds it without deleting it. The account yields a taxonomy of the states a moral datum can occupy (shunted, partially indexed, starved, dangling, compiled), an analysis of moral progress as the enlargement of the community whose data cannot be cheaply starved, and falsifiable commitments: force should fall as unreinforced justification links accumulate, warmth should return only with exercise rather than assent, a value reaffirmed after taboo exposure should remain distinguishable from one never exposed, and suppression-driven forgetting should prove cue-relative rather than cue-independent.

items.title: Multimodality of Flavor Contents.
items.abstract: Perceptual experiences can be multimodal in weaker or stronger senses. The strongest form is often attributed to flavor perception, since flavors are type-multimodal features: features belonging to a type with no instances that can be experienced through a single sense. This paper accepts that flavors are type-multimodal but challenges the claim that flavor perception involves a stronger form of multimodality than ordinary audiovisual or visuo-tactile experiences. This is because there is a plausible reductive view of content of flavor experiences that is consistent with the philosophical and empirical evidence for the multimodality of flavor perception.

items.title: You Are Not the Crazy One: A Debugger’s Field Guide to the Bugs in Your Mind and the Systems Around You.
items.abstract: This book develops a two-level account of cognitive compression: first as a feature of individual cognition, and then as a mechanism operating across groups, institutions, rules, digital platforms, and artificial intelligence. It begins by separating understanding from agreement and argues that failures of communication do not by themselves establish that either party is irrational or mistaken. -/- The first part examines how pressure removes contextual variables from the records through which people interpret one another, how empathy functions both as group recognition and as attention to a non-interchangeable person, and why truth-tellers may be experienced as threats. The second part applies the same framework to social rule formation, decentralized enforcement, institutional memory, and distributed responsibility. It culminates in the figure of the “Faceless Emperor”: a system that exercises power although no single actor fully intends or controls its outcome. -/- The book treats rejection neither as proof of error nor as proof of correctness. Instead, it offers a debugging method for testing the assumptions of both the surrounding system and the observer. Its broader aim is to connect social philosophy, cognitive architecture, systems theory, and the philosophy of artificial intelligence without reducing persons to the categories used to manage them.

items.title: No estás loco: Guía de campo de un depurador para los bugs de tu mente y los sistemas que te rodean.
items.abstract: Este libro desarrolla una explicación en dos niveles de la compresión cognitiva: primero, como característica de la cognición individual y, después, como mecanismo que opera en grupos, instituciones, reglas, plataformas digitales e inteligencia artificial. Comienza separando la comprensión del acuerdo y sostiene que los fallos de comunicación no demuestran por sí mismos que ninguna de las partes sea irracional o esté equivocada. -/- La primera parte examina cómo la presión elimina variables contextuales de los registros mediante los cuales las personas se interpretan unas a otras; cómo la empatía funciona tanto como reconocimiento grupal como atención dirigida a una persona no intercambiable; y por qué quienes dicen la verdad pueden ser percibidos como amenazas.
