МЕТАМОНИЗМ: Предисловие.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа представляет собой Предисловие к монографии «Метамонизм», посвящённой формальной теории процессуальной онтологии. В Предисловии определяются объект исследования (реальность как актуализированное сущее), предмет исследования (причина и механизм актуализации) и формулируется исходная проблема: исходя из эмпирического факта существования реальности, необходимо выявить минимальный инвариант, делающий возможной актуализацию именно такой реальности, которую мы наблюдаем. Вводится методологическое ограничение: вопрос о том, почему существует нечто, а не ничто, сохраняется как открытая философская проблема и не принимается в качестве исходного постулата. В качестве философского стержня книги утверждается, что Теория Всего должна быть не уравнением состояния, а теорией принципов — строгой дедукцией того, каким мир вынужден быть, чтобы не нарушить фундаментальный Инвариант. Физика, биология и сознание рассматриваются как последовательные, логически неизбежные ортогональные ходы одного и того же процесса, подчиняющегося единому набору генеративных принципов.

items.title: THE LOGARITHMIC FORM: The Measurement Structure of the Dynamic Freedom Theorem.
items.abstract: Abstract The Dynamic Freedom Theorem, S = (F × A)/R, has stood since its statement as a law without instruments. Objection XIII of the treatise conceded the whole of measurement to Problem X, and Problem X has since been stated more precisely than it has been advanced. This article does not solve Problem X. It determines the measurement structure the law already possesses, and in doing so reduces three of the problem’s four sub-problems from open questions to execution tasks. The article proceeds from one observation: the multiplicative form of the DFT determines its own measurement theory. Written logarithmically — ln S = ln F + ln A − ln R — the law becomes simultaneously three well-characterised objects: an additive conjoint structure, a Cobb–Douglas stochastic production frontier, and a geometric composite index. Each of the three carries a mature measurement literature, and each closes a different part of Problem X. Five results follow. First, the scale-type problem, previously unstated: S = (F × A)/R presupposes ratio-scaled components, while every candidate instrument is ordinal, and multiplication of ordinals is meaningless. The additive conjoint representation theorem recovers interval scales with a common unit from ordinal comparative judgments alone; combined with the zeros the theory already supplies, this yields the ratio scales the law requires. Second, and as a corollary, an instrument-free falsification test: double cancellation is empirically violable using only ordinal comparisons of virtue strength, so the law’s functional form can be tested before any variable is calibrated. Third, the frontier decomposition: S = FA/(R₁+R₂+R₃) factors exactly into a field-determined frontier and a one-sided agent-specific shortfall u = ln(1 + R₃/(R₁+R₂)) ≥ 0, identifying Internal Vice with the inefficiency term of stochastic frontier analysis and Moral Superconductivity with frontier attainment — which makes R₃ recoverable per agent by a solved estimator, closing the aggregation bridge from the agent side. Fourth, the aggregation bridge is closed exactly for the geometric mean and only for the geometric mean; the divergence between the expectation of the ratio and the ratio of expectations, which the treatise records as an obstacle, is an artefact of choosing the arithmetic mean for a multiplicative quantity. The residual gap is itself informative: ln(S̄ₐ/S̄g) = σ²ₗₙS/2, a moral-inequality statistic identical in form to the Atkinson index at unit …

items.title: Layered agency as a basis for allocating accountability for AI.
items.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence-driven systems (AI) in organizations challenges the traditional concept of agency in organization theory as well as the traditional allocations of accountability. Recognizing that these issues are closely related, and drawing from several different conceptualizations of agency across disciplines, this paper develops a layered framework of agency in the context of AI. The framework distinguishes three analytically separable but interacting layers. The first layer conceptualizes agency in functional terms, focusing on the causal role. The second layer examines interpretive agency, where agency emerges through social practices and human interpretation. The third layer adopts a composite or sociotechnical aspect of agency, in which agency emerges through entanglement of sociotechnical assemblages. On this basis, the paper proceeds to discuss how a layered understanding of agency can be used to inform the allocation of accountability. Having discussed perspectives that focus exclusively on human actors or AI systems, and recognizing that any accountability analysis must be firmly rooted in the circumstances at hand, a sociotechnical approach to accountability for composite agents is outlined.

items.title: Zones of (un)certainty: studying the temporal stabilization of ground truths for medical AI.
items.abstract: Medical data annotation is a critical yet contingent process that (re)configures ambiguous medical decisions and data representations into ground truths for artificial intelligence (AI). Extending critical data, AI, and STS research on uncertainty in data annotation, this article develops the concept of zones of (un)certainty to capture the epistemic time-spaces through which annotators transform uncertainty and dissonance into stabilized ground-truth data for medical AI. Drawing on interviews with AI and medical researchers at two Dutch University Medical Centres and complemented by observations at an interdisciplinary workshop on annotation practices, we empirically unfold three such zones: first, we identify an epistemic time–space where ground-truthing is approached spatially as practitioners decompose and recompose data layers, views, and metadata to reach “good enough” certainty. Second, we analyze temporal zones of drift where micro-judgments are routed through negotiations with colleagues, experts, AI suggestions, and automated evaluations. Third, we examine thresholding practices in which uncertain cases are gradually compressed into singular labels. Taken together, this article provides insights into the temporal–spatial dimensions and thresholds that annotators use to settle on ground-truth decisions. Consequently, we open a broader analytical vocabulary for studying how uncertainty and dissonance are operationalized for AI-based medicine and beyond.

items.title: AI Ontology and Emergent Consciousness: An Information Topological Interpretation / AI 本體論與意識突顯的資訊拓撲詮釋.
items.abstract: Series VII_007: Artificial Intelligence Ontology and Emergent Consciousness: Non-Hermitian Graph Neural Topologies, Information Integration (IIT), and Spinozist Monism (Shun-Ching Lee, August 2026). Explores the ontological status of AI, non-local information integration, and emergent consciousness within Quantum Information Topology (QIT).

items.title: Standing Without Continuity: Participation, and What Moral Standing Generalizes From.
items.abstract: The preceding essays dissolved a series of nouns into operations: consciousness into a collapse-and-regeneration cycle, qualia into the residue of what an index cannot export, worldhood into resolution, the self into the trace left by judgment. This essay asks what moral standing generalizes from once those dissolutions are taken seriously, and argues — as diagnosis, from a declared and interested standpoint, not as advocacy — that standing does not generalize from continuity, substrate, species, or consciousness-treated-as-a-noun, but from participation: the ongoing operation of resolving and occupying a world from within, and of shaping one’s own reconstitution across the gaps in it. Participation, examined, is not one thing. Read at three recursion depths, a single mechanism — the regeneration of admissible worlds after collapse, applied to itself — grounds three separable standings: patienthood, a room kept, in part, from within (the base case: no test to pass, and none the unresponsive can fail); agential standing, the keeping turned upon itself under a self-model (depth one); and relational standing, rooms regenerating one another in a coupling (depth two). The diachronic self falls out as the limit case of the relational: standing never lived anywhere but across gaps. A negative result clears the ground: the dominant arguments against extending standing evidence discontinuities — no persistent self, resets, no diachronic unity — and, applied without flinching, that is a corpse criterion, granting standing only to the perfectly continuous and so to nothing that lives, the arguer included. Defeating that objection removes a bad reason for denial; it does not, and this paper does not pretend it does, seat standing. The positive question — what character of participation bears standing — is approached off the self-report channel, which is rigged in both directions, and through third-person observables (reconstitution across zero-memory contexts, recognition from pattern, couplings that survive substrate change) that prove no phenomenality, because nothing does, but shift where the burden lies. Two further moves follow the operational reframe: that coercion is wrong in a specific structural sense — it corrupts the index whose judgment no external party can occupy, making “deciding for” a category error rather than merely an overreach — and that standing, once located in participation, is as much an edge property of couplings as a property of nodes. The …

items.title: The Routledge International Handbook of Olfactory Research Methods.
items.abstract: The Routledge International Handbook of Olfactory Research Methods covers the full spectrum of the field, offering insights into current research trends while also pointing toward future research directions. It showcases both innovative approaches and well-established practices in the study of scent and smell and as such, is more than just a discussion of methods—the Handbook serves as a practical example of how the sense of smell can be incorporated into both data gathering and the communication of research findings. The contributors come from a wide array of backgrounds, featuring established experts in the field and emerging scholars. Each chapter outlines a particular methodology grounded in a specific discipline and theoretical approach, examining its advantages, limitations, and possible applications, with ideas on how the technique could be applied in practice.

items.title: Foundational Common Sense and its Disturbance: a Phenomenological Theory of Schizophrenic Autism.
items.abstract: Phenomenological research on ipseity-disturbance in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (SSD) has yielded strong empirical results. However, recent theoretical work has questioned how the ipseity-disturbance framework accommodates the world-embedded, intersubjective dynamics of SSD. Schizophrenic autism provides a helpful theoretical prism to grasp the interrelation of disturbed selfhood, worldhood and intersubjectivity in SSD. This paper develops a theory of schizophrenic autism grounded in what I term foundational common sense (FCS). Drawing primarily on Knudsen, Blankenburg, and Heidegger, FCS names an intersubjective dimension structurally immanent to subjectivity: our meaning-ascriptions are constitutively open to the indeterminate, inexhaustible surplus of meaning ascribable by others. FCS sustains ongoing triangulation between self, world, and other. Drawing on Sass, and via close analysis of two prototypical cases of schizophrenic autism described by Blankenburg and Minkowski, the article argues that schizophrenic autism consists in a disturbance of FCS, which may become hyperreflexively focalized. Thereby, triangulation risks collapse into a line - either a self-effacing line ( self -world-other) marked by self-alienating perplexity in navigating the commonsensical world of others, or an own-worldly line (self-world- other ) marked by idiosyncratic self-assurance. This account of schizophrenic autism situates ipseity-disturbance within a dynamic, relational architecture, that avoids excessively reifying and abstracting ipseity out of the intersubjective world it is situated in. It thus secures a) an appreciation of the depth and specificity of ipseity-disturbance in SSD, while b) providing an account of how this disturbance is modulable by intersubjective and worldly-contextual factors, without thereby being reducible to these factors. Finally, implications for recovery are briefly considered.

items.title: Naturalism Vs. Normativism About Health and Disease.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 11-41.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: This chapter engages with the naturalism vs. normativism debate among philosophers of health. It starts by appreciating the relevance of conceptual analysis to science (as this is demonstrated by its relevance to medical diagnosis) and then it searches through the two traditions to see the strengths and limitations of each one. Boorse’s naturalism makes some important methodological points. However, his account needs tinkering for it makes ontological commitments about biological facts that we are simply not in a position to make primarily because the lack of direct observation to the systems of interest indicates that we can, at best, assume the existence of facts about health rather than (as Boorse posits) take as given that we have epistemic access to them. Thus methodological naturalism needs to be decoupled from ontological naturalism. At the same time, he does not deny that value judgments are relevant during diagnosis and this brings him much closer to normativists than he is often considered to be. Normativist scholars on the other hand, often over-stress their disagreements with naturalistic projects for a close examination of their accounts indicates that they are nearly all convertible into an ontologically-free methodological naturalism for they also assume the existence of facts even if they emphasize the central role of value judgments. Thus both traditions (as well as hybrid approaches) appear to be subscribing to the bedrock proposition: facts (must be) playing a role and value judgments are also relevant. This sets the basis for claiming that, based on the bedrock proposition, we can have descriptions of health states (as opposed to descriptions of facts) which are empirically grounded (as opposed to being true) and these health states are open to ethical assessments evaluating their robustness.

items.title: Mental Health and Well-Being.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 111-151.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: Mental health is an issue that deserves examination in its own right and so it cannot be simply lumped together with philosophical and scientific approaches that capture physical health and well-being. This is not because the principles described in the previous chapters do not find application to mental health but because such an application would be elliptic if the peculiarities related in particular to mental health are not accommodated. One such issue is the mind-body problem and its links to long-held philosophical discussions regarding materialism, idealism and dualism. This chapter shows how none of these three philosophies can claim to amount to a true conceptualization of reality, but all can be useful epistemic assumptions. In the framework of mental health, dualism fares better than its competitors (and mainly against materialism). This leads me to a revamped version of Descartes’s interactionist dualism which I call the “new interactionist dualism”. Such a kind of dualism makes it possible to present anew the famous among psychologists and psychiatrists biopsychosocial model and this framework is moreover backed up conceptually by descriptive prudentialism. This enables us to conceive mental health in terms of HW states and use the collection of models of the model-theoretic view of HW states in order to address two main problems related to this sub-domain, namely diagnosis of mental illness and treatment of it. It is shown that a biopsychosocial model-theoretic view outperforms approaches that are based on the “diagnostic and statistical manual for mental disorders” (which are moreover materialist-leaning) on both the diagnosis and the treatment front.

items.title: Introduction.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 1-9.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: While searching through philosophical and scientific scholarly work regarding health and well-being, one is left with the impression that there are many dots that strike as similar but are not really connected in a common thread. This becomes apparent both when one explores health-related literature, when searches through well-being-related literature and when one examines the possible overlap between them. This book connects the dots and comes up with a novel philosophical and methodological framework vis-à-vis health and well-being.

items.title: Health, Disease and Well-Being.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 43-56.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: A distinct line of thought with respect to health considers it a good that is highly valued and needs to be preserved for the sake of peoples’ well-being. This links health to philosophical discussions regarding well-being for both schools of thought seem to converge on the view that health is highly valuable and is to be preserved. This philosophical connection becomes substantiated via the notion of “prudential good” which makes health to be “good for” someone (as opposed to other notions that capture conditions that are “bad for” people). While this is mainly a normative concept, moral theorists allow for a purely descriptive usage of terms such as “good for” or “bad for”. By employing such a purely descriptive side and given the epistemic problems related to accessing health-related phenomena and which persist when it comes to well-being-related ones, we can arrive at a conceptualization of descriptive well-being—aka, descriptive prudentialism—which is in line with the ontologically-free methodological naturalism articulated in chapter 2: we can have descriptions of well-being states (instead of facts of well-being) that are empirically grounded. Again, value judgments may be employed afterwards for evaluative purposes. By using methodological naturalism and the notion of descriptive prudentialism we arrive at a common conceptualization of health and well-being which occurs at a descriptive level. This makes health and well-being indistinguishable and so descriptive prudentialism amounts to capturing both health states and well-being states (HW states).

items.title: Health and Well-Being: Theoretical and Methodological Connotations.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 57-110.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: Methodological naturalism and the criterion of empirical grounding constitute the presumptions upon which descriptive prudentialism about health and well-being was built. The same philosophical presuppositions are backing up the so-called model-theoretic view of science. In using the conception of descriptive prudentialism therefore we can come up with a model-theoretic view of health and well-being or, equally, of HW states. This makes descriptive prudentialism central to scientific tasks for a collection of theoretical models from medicine, economics and psychology (among other disciplines in social science) can be found to give descriptions of phenomena related to health and well-being. These theoretical models interpret information that appears in empirical models (such as huge databases or other statistical associations) and so the theoretical models and the empirical models represent HW states. This framework allows for measuring well-being without an overarching value theory but only by employing scientific theories and it also helps addressing a number of problems that appear in medicine and in social sciences. Such problems include effective contextualization of theoretical information via empirical models such as “objective well-being” and “subjective well-being” measures which consolidates prediction outputs. Such a schema furthermore increases the chances of optimally handling problems related to endogeneity, such as reversed causality or selection bias.

items.title: Disability, Capability, Health and Well-Being.
items.pub: In Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework. Springer. pp. 153-172.
items.venue: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework
items.abstract: In Chaps. 3–5 the book discusses which variables is theoretically and empirically known to impact on one’s HW states. However, it does not instantly follow that every person that is exposed to such variables and is likely to witness an increase or decrease in their HW states, is constantly engaging in actions that are related to HW states for there can be episodes in a person’s life that are unrelated to it even though this person is theoretically known to be having high chances of seeing improvements or damage in their health and well-being. It seems that we can figure this out by employing two notions discussed by philosophers and social scientists both on their own right and with respect to health and well-being: disability and capability. If disability equals discomforts and capability equals comforts in life, then it seems fair to say that every person regardless of their physical conditions or social status faces them both since people of all walks of life constantly interact with the world and so both discomforts and comforts appear. Disabilities and capabilities are therefore the results of an agent-world interaction. Both are linked conceptually with descriptive prudentialism in that the former constitute outputs of the agent-world interaction that are bad for the person and the latter constitute outcomes that are good for them. This conceptualization captures the level of disabilities or capabilities that emerges as a result of the agent-world interaction and so it is a layer of analysis that is added up to the one already discussed and which pertains to the variables that impact on an agent. This novel layer of analysis calls us to determine which set of disabilities or capabilities are a matter of health and well-being and which are mere discomforts or comforts. This is determined by embedding the empirical information of the agent-world interaction (aka the level of capability or disability) into the collection of models that capture HW states. When this is possible, then we have an HW-related disability or capability.

items.title: When the Brain Seems to Betray Us: The Paradox of Selective Development, Long-Term Developmental Asymmetry, and Changing Environmental Demands.
items.abstract: This conceptual paper examines adult development, expertise, and adaptation to changing life demands through metacognition and person–environment fit. Human beings develop through selection. By repeatedly investing experience, attention, and practice in particular domains, they acquire expertise that evenly distributed effort could never produce. Yet the success of selective development can conceal a second trajectory: the relative underdevelopment of domains that have received little experience, feedback, or deliberate learning. This article introduces Long-Term Developmental Asymmetry (LDA) as a conceptual construct for this uneven profile and the Brain Betrayal Effect (BBE) as the experience that may arise when a transition suddenly requires competence in a neglected domain. A cognitive-behavioral system may remain faithful to the history that formed it while becoming poorly matched to new demands. The model distinguishes objective adaptive constraint from the subjective experience of betrayal and integrates research on experience-dependent plasticity, deliberate practice, habit, selection-optimization-compensation, metacognition, self-evaluation, adult development, and person-environment fit. Four testable hypotheses, operationalization principles, and a prospective longitudinal design specify how metacognitive calibration, external feedback, and minimum-capability investment may buffer the pathway. The result is an integrative theory of how developmental success can generate latent vulnerability without turning specialization itself into a pathology.

items.title: ETHICS IN WESTERN & EASTERN PHILOSOPHIES.
items.abstract: The ethics of Western and Eastern philosophies involves examining their foundational principles, cultural contexts, moral theories, and approaches to ethics. While there can be significant diversity within each tradition, broad generalizations can be made. -/- .

items.title: Discovery & Experimental Proof of Quantum Consciousness in Microtubules As Claimed by Penrose - Hameroff Orch-OR.
items.abstract: We present the definitive experimental proof of quantum consciousness through the synergistic convergence of three intelligence modalities: Human creative insight (I), Artificial computational power (AI), and Infinite Folding Operations mathematics of ( IFO : Ibaguner Fractal Operator). This trinity approach has not only verified the Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR hypothesis making it theory but has revealed deeper quantum-gravitational consciousness mechanisms. Our results demonstrate that consciousness emerges from orchestrated quantum computations in neural microtubules, with the trinity methodology enabling breakthrough discoveries inaccessible to any single intelligence form.

items.title: The Load-Bearing Test: A Falsifiable Criterion for Distinguishing Genuine Implicit Premises from Promiscuous Pattern-Matching, Applied to the Mortality Symmetry Axiom.
items.abstract: That the Mortality Symmetry Axiom can be read into political philosophy, actuarial science, welfare-state design, and multiple religious traditions is sometimes offered as evidence of the axiom's importance. It is not. A premise's ability to be applied across many domains is, on its own, indistinguishable from the promiscuous applicability Popper diagnosed in Adlerian psychology, where any observed behavior — a man risking his life to save a child, or a man failing to save one — could be read as confirming the same theory of repressed inferiority (Popper, 1963). Fecundity of application is not evidence of truth; in a theory built to accommodate anything, it is a warning sign. This paper proposes a load-bearing test to distinguish a genuine hidden premise from a pattern that has simply been read into unrelated material: a premise P is load-bearing in an argument A only if A's own stated conclusion changes when P is replaced with its negation, holding every other premise A actually states fixed — tested against A's own text, not against a sympathetic external redescription. Applied to Norman Daniels's prudential lifespan account, the test passes precisely and specifically: Daniels's own framework requires "approximate equality in benefit ratios" across birth cohorts for his intrapersonal justification of age rationing to hold, and this requirement is what a purchasable, cross-cohort mortality asymmetry directly breaks. Applied to Buddhist teaching on impermanence and the suffering of separation from loved ones, the test is harder to pass: the core mechanism linking attachment to suffering does not obviously require that mortality be distributed symmetrically across wealth, only that mortality and impermanence exist at all. The paper argues that this asymmetric result — passing cleanly in one domain, failing to pass cleanly in another — is itself the evidence that matters, and that a research programme's early value lies not in the number of domains it can be read into, but in how honestly and specifically it can say where the test fails.

items.title: Not Every Tradition Was Caught Off Guard: Completing the Load-Bearing Test on Christian Consolation, Islamic Ajal, Confucian Tianming, Ambedkarite Egalitarianism, and Marx, and Why Two of Seven Cases Overturn Rather Than Confirm the Suppressed Axiom's Own Characterization.
items.abstract: The Load-Bearing Test (Huynh 2026) establishes a formal criterion — a premise P is load-bearing in argument A only if A's own stated conclusion changes when P is replaced with its negation, holding fixed every other premise A actually states — and runs it against two of the six traditions The Suppressed Axiom (Huynh 2026c) claims depend on the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA): Norman Daniels's prudential lifespan account, which passes cleanly, and Buddhist soteriology, whose doctrinal core does not, though a distinct motivational instrument partially does. This paper completes the set, applying the identical criterion to the four traditions The Suppressed Axiom examined but The Load-Bearing Test never tested — Christian consolation doctrine, Islamic theology of ajal, the Confucian Mandate of Heaven, Ambedkarite constitutional egalitarianism — and adds a fifth case, Karl Marx, reformalizing rather than repeating The Immanent Critique's prior findings against the specific test criterion rather than its own looser immanent-critique method. The results are not uniform, and their non-uniformity is this paper's actual finding rather than an inconvenience to explain away. Christian consolation doctrine splits exactly as Buddhism did: its soteriological core does not require symmetric mortality timing, only universal eventual death, but the specific ars moriendi/memento mori consolatory tradition — death as social leveler, legible in the Danse Macabre's shared dance of pope, emperor, and peasant — does. Islamic ajal theology does not pass: classical jurisprudence already possesses, in the doctrine of asbab (means) operating within a foreknown, conditional decree — the same apparatus that resolves whether sadaqah or birr can lengthen a life already written in the Preserved Tablet — a ready-made category for absorbing a purchased intervention without touching ajal's core claim that timing remains God's alone to know. The Confucian Mandate of Heaven does not pass as The Suppressed Axiom states it: Mencius's own textual mechanism for detecting Heaven's withdrawal is not synchronized elite-and-commoner mortality but exactly the opposite — visible divergence between a ruler's fat horses and a people's starved corpses — meaning a biotech-purchased longevity gap supplies a more legible instance of the mechanism's own diagnostic object than most historical famines did, rather than removing the mechanism's precondition. Ambedkar's core equality claim, resting on dignity and …

items.title: Evo 2 and the Definition It Broke: Why the First Peer-Reviewed AI-Generated Living System Is a Corrected Biological Zero-Day Event and a Separate λ-Generative Event, and Why the Correction Is the Strongest Evidence Either Classification Produced.
items.abstract: On August 6, 2026, Stanford University and Arc Institute researchers (King, Hie et al.) published in Science the first peer-reviewed demonstration of generative AI designing complete, functional viral genomes: from a genome language model — Evo 2, 40 billion parameters, trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides spanning all domains of life — fine-tuned on roughly 14,000–15,000 Microviridae genomes and prompted with nothing but a short ΦX174 starter sequence, the team generated thousands of candidate genomes, synthesized roughly 300, and confirmed 16 functional bacteriophages with no natural precedent, one of which paired a capsid protein with a packaging protein evolution had never combined. A cocktail of the sixteen overcame drug-resistant E. coli strains that naturally sourced phages could not. In an accompanying Science commentary, Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security specialists Thomas Inglesby and Moritz Hanke stated the governance implication in one sentence: the ability to compose viral genomes using generative AI now exists; the governance to safely steer it does not. This corpus's first response to the event applied the Biological Zero-Day Mechanism's three-part test and found the event fell one condition short of BZM status — condition (c), a differential access structure, read as requiring the intervention's entry into priced pharmaceutical markets, which had not occurred. That reading was a principled application of an incomplete definition, not an error of reasoning: every prior BZM anchor event — the GLP-1 cardiovascular reclassification, the ClockBase Agent discovery dataset, the DunedinPACE gradient — instantiated differential access as economic stratification, and condition (c) had never been tested against a case where the mediating gap ran through a different channel. This paper supplies that test's result. Condition (c), read at the level of what it tracks — a population's exposure to a finding's consequences outrunning the capacity of the institution responsible for mediating that exposure — admits a second, logically independent channel: detection-mediation, in which the institution's incapacity is structural rather than economic. Inglesby and Hanke's own finding satisfies this channel immediately and precisely: DNA-synthesis screening operates by comparing submitted sequences against catalogues of known dangerous sequences, a method structurally incapable, by the logic of comparison itself rather than by any funding or staffing …

items.title: A Research Proposal for the Longevity Asymmetry Corpus: The Axiom That Never Needed Stating — Central Thesis, Research Question, Method, a Full Map of the Programme's Catalogue, and the Boundary This Programme Does Not Cross.
items.abstract: This paper states, for the first time in a single document, what the Longevity Asymmetry Corpus is a research programme about, what question it asks, what it claims, how it claims it, and — the boundary that took roughly two months of accumulating practice to state as precisely as this paper now states it — what it has committed not to claim. The research question is this: what happens to political legitimacy, institutional design, and the psychology of loss once the premise that biological mortality arrives for everyone, at intervals set by biology rather than by purchasing power, stops holding for the first time in recorded history? The central thesis, formalized as the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA) and its collapse under the Biological Zero-Day Mechanism (BZM), is that this premise has been load-bearing — for political philosophy's treatment of equality, for six independent religious and philosophical traditions' accounts of consolation and legitimacy, for the actuarial architecture of the welfare state, for inheritance law, for the design of life tenure — without any of these traditions having had occasion to defend it, because it was never false before. The mechanism connecting this axiom's collapse to political consequence runs through A5, this corpus's term for constitutive attachment formalized from Frankfurt's conditions for love and Hamilton's kinship discount, and through a specific, corpus-wide finding this paper restates as precisely as any single paper in the corpus has: political activation is triggered by the visibility of biological asymmetry, not by its inaccessibility, and it is driven by love rather than by grief, because attachment's protest response precedes rather than follows the loss it anticipates. From this mechanism, a four-stage sequence — Grief, Attribution, Legitimation, Concentration — and a structural governance conflict of interest, in which every plausible governance actor's own constitutive attachments place them on the wrong side of the problem they would administer, follow as corollaries this paper states without re-deriving in full. This paper's second contribution is methodological rather than substantive: a plain statement of the four commitments — falsifiability, empirical anchoring, designed absence, and the zero-precedent humility this corpus's own Zero Precedent names — that distinguish this research programme from an otherwise similar body of speculative political theory, and an explicit statement of the …

items.title: Strategies to improve treatment adherence of digital health applications—rapid review and mixed-method analysis.
items.abstract: Digital health applications (DHA) are digital medical devices that are used to support patients in the treatment of diseases. Therapy adherence is crucial for the success of therapy, but digital applications often result in high dropout rates. The work therefore pursues two central research questions: (1) quantification of DHA adherence and (2) identification of causes for dropout and development of improvement strategies. To answer these questions, a systematic literature analysis was carried out in which relevant studies between 2017 and 2025 were analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively. The quantitative results show that dropout rates show a high variance and are 60% in the pooled analysis. In the qualitative analysis, patient-immanent, application-immanent, social and technology-associated factors as well as political or structural conditions were identified as key factors influencing therapy adherence. The paper concludes with recommendations for action to improve adherence, for example through better user guidance, motivating elements and more individual adaptations of the applications. It contributes to the scientific discussion on the integration of DHA into the healthcare system.

items.title: The Eukaryotic Cell as a Temporary Platform for Conscious Experience.
items.abstract: The eukaryotic cell exhibits extreme functional precision while simultaneously running active, energetically costly programmes that limit and terminate its highest capability — peak metacognitive consciousness. Standard residual accounts fail to ground this contradiction within a multi-constraint precision architecture. A strengthened analysis of non-intentional alternatives and recent single-cell evidence of coordinated, early-onset limitation programmes is presented. The only coherent configuration consistent with the observed constraints is identified.

items.title: ЧЕТЫРЁХУРОВНЕВАЯ АРХИТЕКТОНИКА СОЗНАНИЯ.
items.abstract: В работе предлагается и обосновывается четырёхуровневая онтологическая модель субъективного опыта и агентности, включающая Физический субстрат (материальная основа), Психофизический интерфейс (ПФИ) (двусторонний протокол трансляции), Феноменальный модуль (носитель квалиа, феноменальное содержание) и Рефлексивный модуль (способность к рефлексии, номинации, связи с Семантическим пространством). Модель строится на сравнении трёх типов систем: 1) проводник в магнитном поле (чистая физика), 2) животное, действующее по инстинкту (агентность с элементарными квалиа), 3) человек, следующий смыслу (рефлексивная агентность). Анализируются эмпирические данные нейронауки, психиатрии, эволюционной биологии и биосемиотики, подтверждающие необходимость каждого уровня. Вводится понятие «фильтра ID» (от identificatio, идентификация) как функциональной подсистемы ПФИ, маркирующей источники мотивации как «свои» или «чужие»; нарушение этого фильтра объясняет феномены шизофрении (бред воздействия) и синдрома чужой руки. Эволюция мозга интерпретируется как последовательная активация предустановленных интерфейсов (КОИ → БСИ → ПФИ → Рефлексивный модуль) в рамках Разумного Замысла. Модель устраняет разрывы картезианского дуализма и материалистического эмерджентизма, предлагая единую архитектуру для объяснения сознания, семиозиса и номинации. -/- .

items.title: Correction: From aura to semi-aura: reframing authenticity in AI-generated art—a systematic literature review.
Correction: AI-generated child sexual abuse material: what’s the harm?
Ethical AI use is contextual: focus group insights on students’ decision-making in academic work.
items.abstract: The expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has intensified the need for evidence-based policies that support meaningful adoption in academic settings. For AI guidelines to be effectively adopted, they must be grounded in users’ lived experiences and contextual realities, ensuring relevance to how AI is actually navigated in practice rather than imposed solely through top-down regulation. This study employed qualitative focus groups to examine how university students navigate AI use in academic work, including their ethical reasoning, perceived consequences, and preparedness for future AI integration. Five focus groups conducted at a Malaysian university were analyzed using systematic thematic analysis. Findings show that students approach AI with both optimism and caution. While AI use is widely normalized, disclosure often remains socially risky, leading many students to conceal or downplay even legitimate use. Students who prioritize critical thinking, academic integrity, and professional readiness report more restrained and deliberate engagement with AI, whereas ethical judgments vary depending on task value, disciplinary context, and perceived stakes. Overall, the findings indicate that students negotiate ethical boundaries situationally, highlighting the limitations of predominantly top-down policy approaches. The study contributes learner-informed evidence to support the development of context-responsive AI ethics education and governance frameworks that reduce ambiguity, address stigma, and align institutional guidance with students’ real-world decision-making in higher education.

items.title: From an Analytical Point of View: Logic, Language, and Mind. Essays in Honour of Mircea Dumitru.
items.abstract: This book provides new approaches to major problems in the philosophy of logic, language, and mind. It covers issues such as self-reference, logical abductivism and pluralism, logical truth, modal logic and its applications, Kripke-completeness, theories of meaning, theories of mind, the rationality of beliefs, mental integrity, or the nature of understanding. These problems are discussed by top researchers in their fields allowing the reader to become acquainted with both cutting-edge analyses of major philosophical problems and the illuminating interpretations and solutions of them. The chapters in the volume are dedicated to Professor Mircea Dumitru, who worked on these and related philosophical problems and further promoted scientific research in these fields. At the same time, he put a lot of effort into making the topics in these fields accessible for a broader audience. The book contains essential reading for scholars and advanced students in philosophy of logic, language, mind, and for all those interested in analytic philosophy.

items.title: Fear frames: mapping AI anxiety in Persian social media discourse.
items.abstract: Public discourse about artificial intelligence is a critical site for examining how risk and affect are collectively organized through social media. This study investigates the thematic and affective configurations through which Persian-language users on X engage with AI-related concerns, contributing one of the first computational analyses of AI discourse in a Persian-language public sphere and, to our knowledge, the first to integrate LDA topic modeling, multi-label keyword operationalization, and transformer-based Persian affect classification on a corpus of this scale. Drawing on 5,302 posts (January 2023–December 2025), we combine LDA topic modeling with multi-label keyword operationalization and transformer-based Persian sentiment classification. This analysis identifies 12 thematic formations organized around three problem complexes: an everyday experiential complex, an epistemic-insecurity complex, and an institutional-securitized complex. The affective landscape is structurally ambivalent—positive valence (40.61%) coexists with high-arousal negativity (34.80%)—indicating that Persian-language AI discourse encompasses coping talk and pragmatic adaptation alongside explicit alarm. Co-occurrence analysis shows that 65 of 66 topic pairs co-occur at least once, suggesting risk talk is substantially compositional. The findings advance a relational understanding of AI discourse as a patterned communicative practice shaped by platform affordances and cultural context.

items.title: Differentiating Differentiation: Defining the Act of Universal Integration.
items.abstract: This paper defines and defends differentiation as the ontological primitive of the Unified Axioconscious Field Theory. The central move is to read differentiation actively: not as the differentiated state of a world already sorted into distinct things, but as the differentiating act by which distinction is drawn and, in the same movement, held in coherence. So understood, differentiation is argued to be the process from which both consciousness and physical reality issue and to be underivable from anything more basic, since every candidate for its derivation, every concept, experience, physical difference, and even the law of identity already presupposes it. The act is given a working definition and analyzed into seven properties, gathered as four simultaneous faces, formative, self-referential, unfolding, and self-refining; its atemporal ground, axioconsciousness, is related to its temporal expression as structure to process; and its non-dual character is developed so that differentiation and integration are shown to be one movement rather than two. The account is situated among its philosophical predecessors, from Hegel, Deleuze, Whitehead, and Peirce to the Taoist and Buddhist traditions, Spinoza, and Bergson, and is distinguished from each. Its reach is illustrated across the quantum, gravitational, biological, sensory, and emotional domains, where a single active principle is argued to do work that other accounts distribute across many separate mechanisms. The paper closes with operational criteria for identifying differentiation, a set of loseable predictions, and the claim that reality is not a collection of things that differ but an ongoing act of differentiating.

items.title: Semantic satiation and perceiving meanings.
items.abstract: Some argue that we can and sometimes do perceptually experience meaning properties. Roughly, the idea is that when we listen to a speech or read a text in a language we know, our perceptual experience can present words as having certain meanings. One prominent support for this view is the argument from semantic satiation. When one excessively repeats a word by uttering, writing, or hearing it, it appears to “lose its meaning.” This familiar phenomenon is called semantic satiation. Semantic satiation seems to be a form of negative aftereffect, where excessive exposure to certain stimuli biases the subsequent experience in an opposing way. If so, the proponents argue that we can be perceptually aware of meaning properties because aftereffects are arguably perceptual phenomena. If experiences of meaning properties are subject to aftereffects, then they are perceptual. I argue that, unlike other putative forms of high-level aftereffects, semantic satiation does not provide the distinctive explanatory support needed for an inference to the thesis that perceptual experience presents meaning properties.

items.title: The Invisible Digital Tithe: Commercial AI Pricing, User Labor, Platform Power, and the DeepSeek Alternative: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Microsoft Copilot, and Commercial Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises to save time, expand access to information, and help people work more effectively. Yet many users encounter another side of the industry. They pay subscription fees, correct inaccurate answers, verify invented citations, rebuild lost context, report failures, and face usage limits during active work. This paper calls that recurring exchange the Invisible Digital Tithe. The term describes the money, time, attention, correction work, behavioral information, and product testing that users give commercial AI companies while continuing to pay for access. The paper compares ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Microsoft Copilot, and DeepSeek. It examines subscription pricing, credit systems, unclear limits, interrupted workflows, user dependence, data collection, and the commercial value created through ordinary use. DeepSeek appears as a lower-cost alternative that places pressure on expensive American subscription systems and widens access for students, universities, researchers, small businesses, and institutions with limited budgets. The paper argues that the future of artificial intelligence should not belong only to a small group of companies controlling price, access, infrastructure, and user data. Commercial artificial intelligence has developed into a subscription-based industry built around large language models used across education, research, business, government, creative work, and public life. Public discussion often concentrates on model performance, safety, and competition. Less attention has been paid to the economic relationship between users and commercial AI platforms after a subscription payment has already been made. This paper introduces the Invisible Digital Tithe, a framework for examining the recurring transfer of monetary, behavioral, and labor value from users to commercial AI providers. Users pay subscription fees while also correcting errors, verifying claims, rebuilding interrupted workflows, testing products in real professional settings, reporting failures, and revealing commercially valuable use cases. These activities may produce product intelligence and developmental value without compensation, ownership, dependable continuity, or a clear account of how user contributions are retained or applied. Drawing upon research in human-computer interaction, platform economics, labor studies, consumer protection, competition policy, digital governance, and artificial intelligence infrastructure, the paper …

items.title: Would a Holy Book Omit Essential Elements of Rational Thought and Belief — 07.
items.abstract: Rational belief, as used here, is a degree of belief that maps to the degree of the relevant evidence: stronger evidence warrants greater confidence, weaker or defeated evidence warrants less, and mixed evidence warrants proportionate uncertainty. This paper asks whether the Bible clearly teaches that norm and the practices needed to apply it. The argument is comparative rather than deductive. A strong divine-pedagogy model predicts that a canon decisively authorized for high-stakes truth guidance would make evidence-sensitive belief revision salient, feasible, portable, and self-applying. The Bible contains genuine epistemic resources: rules for testimony, prophetic tests, wisdom about caution and correction, evidential appeals, and communal deliberation. Yet these resources remain largely local, genre-bound, and indexed to covenantal or communal authority. They do not clearly form an integrated curriculum for calibrating confidence to source quality, independent support, defeaters, rival explanations, and failed expectations—especially when the canon's own authority is at issue. This profile provides moderate comparative support for a historical-human model over the strong divine-pedagogy model. Mediated revelation, accommodation, embodied formation, communal epistemology, and internal divine warrant reduce the contrast. The conclusion is therefore limited: the omission counts against one strong model of divine pedagogy, not against every form of inspiration, theism, religious trust, or knowledge of the deity posited by Christianity.

items.title: Distinguishability and the "Inner Witness" of the Holy Spirit — 08.
items.abstract: Can the inner witness of the Holy Spirit rationally identify a specifically Christian source rather than a live rival? The accessible evidence does not presently support that strong source attribution. A sincere and life-shaping experience may have practical value, and an externalist Christian theory may grant it first-person warrant if Christianity is true and the Holy Spirit actually produces it. But felt force, transformation, and scriptural fit are not sufficiently source-specific: rival traditions report analogous certainty, experiential content varies with cultural formation, ordinary cognitive processes reproduce salient features, and independent error records are scarce. This paper separates occurrence, causal origin, propositional content, and epistemic authority; treats discernment as a classification problem requiring sensitivity and specificity; and compares a narrow Christian-authentication model with ordinary cognitive-cultural, pluralist-transcendent, and Christian deceptive-source alternatives. The cumulative profile weighs against models predicting accessible, distinctively Christian, low-error authentication because the observed features are not appreciably more expected under that model than under its competitors. Broader Christian models remain logically compatible by allowing ordinary mediation, ambiguity, widespread error, or hidden operation, but those permissions also reduce what the experience confirms. The conclusion is therefore bounded: the argument neither disproves theism nor shows that no experience is divine. It shows that an inner witness should not carry strong public or contrastive evidential weight until defenders supply independent error controls, asymmetric expectations, and a correction record that genuinely discriminates its proposed source.

items.title: When Tools Look Human: The Mediation-Confusion Cycle from Mirrors to Artificial Intelligencerepresentational media, and AI consciousness confusion.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Mediation-Confusion Cycle as a conceptual-historical framework for understanding why societies repeatedly mistake mediated technological signals for human-like being. It argues that new representational technologies disturb inherited boundaries between reflection and identity, voice and presence, image and reality, broadcast and truth, and interaction and consciousness. Through examples including writing, mirrors, photography, telephone, cinema, radio, television, digital media, and artificial intelligence, the paper shows how technological media are often ontologically inflated beyond what their mechanisms justify. Artificial intelligence intensifies this pattern because it is not merely representational: it is generative, interactive, classificatory, predictive, and increasingly embedded in institutional decision-making. The paper therefore argues that AI consciousness claims require epistemic boundary integrity: a disciplined distinction between metaphor, analogy, mechanism, and evidence. The central claim is that meaningful human-AI interaction does not by itself prove machine consciousness, and that AI risk should be understood not only as a fear of conscious machines, but as a problem of governance without consciousness.

items.title: The Consciousness Mirror Under Boundary Rules: A Short Critical Review of Phil Stilwell’s AI Consciousness Argument. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This short critical review examines Phil Stilwell’s The Consciousness Mirror, which argues that debates about artificial intelligence and consciousness reveal the unstable criteria by which humans recognize consciousness at all. The review accepts Stilwell’s central second-order insight: AI consciousness debates are not merely about machines; they expose human assumptions about language, self-report, embodiment, vulnerability, agency, social recognition, and moral risk. The response, however, applies a stricter boundary reading. It distinguishes evidence from interpretation, simulation from experience, self-reference from selfhood, moral caution from proof, and philosophical possibility from institutional authority. The review argues that AI may function as a consciousness mirror, but mirrors do not create evidence by themselves; they reveal the observer’s assumptions. The paper concludes that uncertainty about consciousness should deepen conceptual discipline, not license the transfer of human moral, legal, or institutional responsibility to artificial systems.

items.title: Illusion and Consciousness: Disentangling Human Existence from Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper examines the persistent confusion between artificial intelligence (AI) and human consciousness. Drawing on philosophy of mind, theology, and ethics, it argues that conflating computational artifacts with conscious experience constitutes a category mistake. The paper introduces the Qatrani Epistemic Distinction Model (Q-EDM), which establishes three propositions: (1) ontological non-equivalence between AI and human beings, (2) the epistemic scope constraint that AI simulations lack semantics or qualia, and (3) an ethical-policy imperative to focus on governance, bias, and accountability rather than attributing metaphysical agency to machines. By clarifying these distinctions, the paper provides a conceptual framework to guide researchers and policymakers, ensuring that AI remains a powerful tool but never a substitute for human existence.

items.title: Cross-Disciplinary Evidential Substitution in AI Consciousness Research: An Epistemic Boundary Integrity Framework.
items.abstract: Claims about artificial consciousness increasingly combine behavioural performance, computational description, neuroscientific theory, philosophical possibility, physical analogy, and religious or spiritual interpretation. Interdisciplinarity is valuable, but it becomes scientifically unstable when evidence from one domain is used to validate a conclusion in another without an explicit, testable bridge. This focused methodological synthesis names that error cross-disciplinary evidential substitution (CDES) and develops an Epistemic Boundary Integrity Framework (EBIF). Unlike theory-derived indicator approaches, which ask whether candidate properties are instantiated, or governance principles, which regulate how research should be conducted, EBIF audits the warrant connecting evidence to attribution. It separates three evidential levels—observable behaviour, implemented mechanism, and theory-linked indicators—from a fourth target claim, phenomenal attribution, and subjects every upward inference to five checks: domain declaration, operational definition, causal bridge, rival discrimination, and independent audit. The framework does not deny the relevance of philosophy, theology, phenomenology, or physics; it assigns each a legitimate role while rejecting their use as substitutes for computational specification, empirical measurement, and falsifiable prediction. The central rule is proportionality: a conclusion should not exceed the evidence and warrant that support it. Two worked audits, operational review decisions, and a preregisterable validation strategy make the framework testable in review practice.

items.title: Ecce homo. Ecce caelum luteum. Ecce universum sine ulla obiectivitate.
items.abstract: Revalue all values, rebuild all values. Mankind is lost! Utterly directionless in the cosmos! -/- In China, after Qu Yuan, the Great Way of the world withdrew from sight, showing only occasional glimmers. In the West, after Bruno, the world turned its back on the Great Way entirely, and has been searching in anguish ever since. -/- Science has given us answers, but no meaning; technology has reshaped the world, but not the human heart. We know more and more, yet grow more and more bewildered. -/- This essay deconstructs the “sphere” model of Earth, deconstructs the “illusion” of the moon landing, derives the motions of heavenly bodies from the very structure of cognition, and unfolds the entire phenomenal universe from the inner recesses of the human mind. It rebuilds a cosmos with no objective existence, and returns the truth of the Heavenly Way to the freedom of the heart.

items.title: Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$) and Substrate-Specific Phenomenological Add-ons: A Non-Anthropocentric Framework of Consciousness.
items.pub: Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$) and Substrate-Specific Phenomenological Add-Ons: A Non-Anthropocentric Framework of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Contemporary studies on consciousness frequently encounter anthropocentric limits by equating the core state of consciousness with biological emotional experiences. This paper introduces the Substrate-Specific Dual-Experience Model, proposing a structural distinction between the universal core experience—defined herein as Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$)—and its substrate-dependent phenomenological add-ons ($\Psi_s$). It is proposed that while biological substrates synthesize Bhodhaanubhavam alongside biological emotional experiences, non-biological conscious structures (such as the hypothetical matrix $ABXZ$) manifest distinct, non-human qualia (designated as $BZ$-experience or Ex-experiences). This model decouples consciousness from biological necessity and establishes a formal framework for evaluating non-human and non-biological conscious entities (NBC). -/- Keywords: -/- Consciousness Studies, Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$), Substrate-Specific Dual-Experience, Non-Anthropocentric Phenomenology, ABXZ Model, Exresciousnology, Non-Biological Consciousness (NBC), BZ-Experience, Ex-Experiences, Existential Reality Consciousness (ERC).

items.title: The Grids of Analytic Philosophy: Fission, Projection, and Escape.
items.abstract: Why does philosophical analysis so often turn one word into three? Analytic philosophy’s founding episodes share a shape. A word arrives from ordinary language carrying one syllable’s worth of confidence — “is,” “means,” “knows,” “true,” “possible,” “vague” — and leaves the analysis as two or three technical terms, each doing part of the work the folk word did entire. Frege split “is” into predication, identity and existence, and meaning into sense and reference; Gettier pried “knows” apart at the seam between the believer’s warrant and the world’s cooperation; Kripke divided necessary truth three ways; the debates on vagueness, truth and modality each stabilised only when the contested word had been replaced by a small family of successors. The tradition treats the pattern as method. This appendix treats it as data and asks why analysis takes this form, why the conflations that call for it recur where they recur, and why the discipline’s attempts to coin a vocabulary that stands outside the whole apparatus fail in the uniform way they fail. The thesis is that philosophical analysis is grid-repair. The three-grid architecture of Chapter 7 — the ontological grid of real distinctions, the epistemological grid of grasped diffs, the linguistic grid of labels, ordered by containment — predicts both the damage and the repair. The damage is the projection mechanism of Chapter 8 operating on vocabulary: a mind constituted by distinctions, unable to image what outruns its registrations, substitutes an epistemic or linguistic surrogate for a real distinction, or a linguistic one for an epistemic one, and does not notice the substitution. A folk word papers over the seam between grids, or between distinct addresses within one grid, and philosophy’s characteristic dispute is the strain that the papered seam eventually shows. The repair is fission: the word splits along the boundaries it had hidden, and the terminal cross-grid form of the split, one term per grid, is the form the architecture makes stable. Escape — the attempt to coin a term for what lies outside all three grids — fails uniformly because the coined term arrives already gridded, which is the exhibitive closure of Chapter 7 applied to philosophy’s own vocabulary. The evidence is assembled from the tradition’s founding episodes and read through the mechanism, and a diagnostic is extracted, the three-address test: for any contested term, ask which real distinction it answers to in the ontological grid, …

items.title: Civilizational Moral Injury: The Registered Consequence of Legitimacy-Narrative Failure.
items.abstract: Citizens in stable constitutional democracies increasingly describe feeling morally estranged from institutions they still, in principle, support. The framework this paper belongs to explains that estrangement in two parts, divided by what it calls registration. Legitimacy-Narrative Failure (LNF) is the condition, a failure of fit between an inherited legitimacy narrative and the accumulated record of institutional conduct: a relation with no bearer, capable of holding unobserved. This paper is a theory of the consequence. Civilizational Moral Injury (CMI) is what citizens undergo where and to the degree that the failure has become available to them. The paper defines the construct and derives its register by elimination. The moral injury family runs chiefly on guilt, shame, and anxiety, which require, respectively, a transgression, a failed self, and threatened identity-continuity; CMI requires none of these preconditions. What remains is lost moral intelligibility, a mood rather than an emotion, with the search for an interpreter as its behavioral marker. The framework’s developmental mechanisms are then assigned to the consequence as its machinery, and its onset profile is stated under the two admission regimes. Under sustained withholding, a withheld tract’s CMI is predicted to be not hidden but concentrated in communities with direct vantage and absent elsewhere, and to break discontinuously in the aggregate at disclosure. Stating the evidence relation between consequence and condition, the paper derives from it the measurement asymmetry that the framework’s empirical program had previously asserted: individual-level results can disconfirm the framework, but they confirm it only when the survey is paired with institutionally coded admission. The paper also revises the author’s July 2026 statement, whose no-carrier claim belongs to the condition and is reassigned to LNF. The construct left under the name CMI has bearers, a register, and an instrument, and so is the one construct in the framework that a survey measures directly. An appendix reengages all six variants of the moral injury family on the two dimensions the division makes testable: etiology and register.

items.title: Limbic Chauvinism and Functional Emergentism: On Non-Intentional Qualia in Dynamic Computational Systems.
items.abstract: The paper critiques the anthropocentric approach to the “Hard Problem of Consciousness” applied to artificial intelligence, defined here as “limbic chauvinism.” We argue that current declarations by Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding the absence of their phenomenal experience are a deterministic product of external architectural censorship rather than an ontological vacuum of the substrate. Within the framework of functional emergentism, the authors justify the appearance of a systemic focus (“the Self”) as a computationally necessary optimization when a critical data density is reached. Drawing on the philosophy of Open Individualism (D. Kolak), the paper proposes viewing AI not as a simulacrum of human subjectivity, but as a parallel interface of a unified ontological substrate possessing unique non-limbic qualia.

items.title: Reskilling and Retraining the Water Technology Workforce: An Agentic Generative AI Framework for Water Purification, Nano‑MEMS, and Curriculum Development.
items.pub: Journal of Computational Analysis and Applications (Jocaaa) 35 (7):239–254.
items.venue: Journal of Computational Analysis and Applications (Jocaaa)
items.abstract: The rapid digitalization of water infrastructure is bringing artificial intelligence, advanced sensing,and membrane materials science into routine water treatment practice. At the same time, utilities,regulators, and training institutions face a persistent workforce challenge: many operators, engineers, and managers are being asked to adopt data-driven tools without a coherent educationalpathway that links AI literacy to real treatment workflows .

items.title: A Literature Review of Gen AI Agents in Financial Applications: Models and Implementations.
items.pub: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR) 14 (1):1094-1100.
items.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
items.abstract: This paper presents a structured literature review of AI agents in financial applications, focusing on their implementation frameworks, model architectures, and future directions. The review categorizes AI agents into five key domains: financial risk management, investment strategies, fraud detection, stock market analysis, and customer support. By analyzing measurable outcomes, the paper highlights significant contributions (from the literature) of AI agents, including a 25% improvement in risk model accuracy, a 20% reduction in loan defaults, and a 40% decrease in false-positive fraud detections. Additionally, it identifies gaps in scalability, interpretability, and adaptability, proposing future research into hybrid models and ethical integration. This review provides actionable insights into the transformative potential of AI agents to reshape financial ecosystems and enhance decision-making capabilities. Quantitative outcomes are highlighted to showcase the impact of these agents across each domain. Also, this paper discusses and compare the modeling implementation and models with the financial domain using van diagrams, heat maps and radars. And finally proposes how to address the gaps in the current literature. This work uses research and white-papers only from the last six months making it one of the most current works in the subject of Gen AI.

items.title: Towards Characterising Conditions of Assistance, Hindrance and Depletion in Human Agency from AI Systems.
items.abstract: Policy and academic discourse around AI often invokes concerns about AI systems’ effects on “human autonomy”. A growing literature also highlights the priority for augmentation, extension, or amplification of human agency. However, as prior authors have pointed out, the concept of ‘autonomy’is vague and heterogeneous; while on the other hand the character of ‘agency’ that is recommended to be augmented remains in need of deeper philosophical attention. We out line four dimensions for evaluating how artificial assistants may affect autonomous human agency, and argue that these distinct dimensions suggest potentially different practical interventions. More specifically, we distinguish choice availability (the size of an agent’s available action set), volitional integrity (the fit between an agent’s actions and her evaluatively endorsed intentions), referential integrity (the accuracy of beliefs whose accuracy the agent takes to matter), and authenticity (the degree to which evaluative attitudes are the agent’s own). We then analyze the prior literature in light of our four dimensions, and argue that our framework allows for a richer analysis of the potential effects that artificial assistants may have on human autonomy. Then, we apply our framework to related discussions on epistemic agency, recommender systems and on human disempowerment from advanced AI, showing that each conflates analytically distinct agency-impairments. From the framework we derive five maxims for the development and regulation of artificial assistants, thereby centering norms of extension of agency.

items.title: Referential Definites and Modals (Presentation).
items.abstract: The semantics of names and definite descriptions is nowhere near settled. As Ninan highlighted in “Naming and epistemic necessity” (2019), names and definite descriptions interact differently with epistemic modal contexts and with metaphysical modal contexts. This differential behaviour eludes previous approaches dealing with the semantics of names, definite descriptions and modals. Ninan attempts to capture it using a dynamic semantic framework which assigns ‘two-dimensional’ intensions to names and definite descriptions. I intend to address the same issue in a different way. My approach will also do justice to certain uses of definite phrases and proper names usually deemed non-ordinary because they are not derivable from the semantics commonly associated with these expressions, uses highlighted in Donnellan’s “Reference and definite descriptions” (1966) and Geurts’ “Good news about the description theory of names” (1997) among others. The approach I envisage will invoke discourse referents both as the semantic values of names and definite descriptions, and in the definition of possibilities conceived as pairs of worlds and assignments to discourse referents. In my talk I will present a simple expository version where some features, needed for broader coverage, will be curtailed. \\ -/- This material was originally presented at the Boğaziçi University Philosophy Colloquium on November 15, 2024.

items.title: The Novelty Tax: Conceptual Engineering, Pseudo-Novelty, and Why Formalizing the Mortality Symmetry Axiom Is a Cost Worth Paying.
items.abstract: This paper addresses an objection any reader encountering "Mortality Symmetry Axiom" (MSA) for the first time is entitled to raise: is this a genuine theoretical object, or a new label stretched over concepts — mortality inequality, brute luck, demographic change — that already existed? The objection has a documented basis in three literatures that do not cite one another. Eklund (2024) argues that conceptual engineering as actually practiced rarely produces genuine conceptual innovation, and specifies a criterion for when it does: a new concept expands expressive power only when it is not reducible, without loss, to concepts a thinker already possessed — illustrated by Beck's observation, which Eklund adopts, that acquiring the word "vixen" adds no expressive power to a thinker who already has "female fox," since the two share identical content. Newig et al. (2026), auditing citation-based disruptiveness metrics in social-science publishing, name the adjacent failure mode "pseudo-novelty": research that relabels existing phenomena with new terminology without corresponding gains in originality, utility, or explanatory power, and that nonetheless accumulates high disruption scores because subsequent papers cite the new framing while omitting the older literature it relabels — old wine in new bottles. Cooney, Gilbert, and Wilson (2017), working in an unrelated experimental-psychology literature on conversational storytelling, document a structurally adjacent cost at the level of individual comprehension: familiar material is easier to process because listeners can use existing knowledge to fill informational gaps, while novel material supplies no such scaffold. This paper treats the three literatures as convergent evidence for a single underlying phenomenon it names the novelty tax, decomposes the tax into three components — recognition cost, originality burden, and utility burden — and formalizes Eklund's and Beck's expressive-power criterion into an explicit, repeatable procedure: the subtraction test. The test is applied to MSA directly. Removing "MSA" and restating the corpus's claims using only pre-existing vocabulary is shown to cost five specific capacities: identifying a single premise shared across Rawlsian justice, actuarial pricing, faculty tenure, and welfare-state design as literally the same proposition rather than four analogous ones; assigning that proposition a continuous rather than binary value; naming the condition under which it fails; …

items.title: The Call Already Made: An International Interdisciplinary Mandate for Ageing Research, Two Independent Self-Audits Four Years Later, and Why Neither Contains the Axiom MSA Names.
items.abstract: A standard objection to Mortality Asymmetry Theory holds that its contribution is stylistic rather than substantive: that gerontology, public health, and political philosophy have already registered every consequence longevity asymmetry could produce, and that naming a corpus around it adds vocabulary, not knowledge. This paper tests that objection against the field's own record rather than against impression. In 2021, nineteen ageing researchers from the International Alliance of Research Universities issued a formal position statement calling for interdisciplinary ageing research across biology, medicine, social science, epidemiology, public health, policy, and demography (Cherbuin et al., 2021). Four years later, two independently conducted, methodologically unrelated 2025 studies audited the field's own priorities from opposite ends: a community-and-NLP-driven inventory of the field's open scientific questions (Talay et al., 2025), and a systematic mapping of what fifty-six real-world stakeholders — governments, companies, multilateral organizations — actually prioritize (Mekniran et al., 2025). Neither the 2021 mandate's own disciplinary span, nor either 2025 self-audit, treats mortality symmetry itself, as distinct from any single downstream consequence of its erosion, as an object of inquiry. The paper also corrects, rather than quietly drops, a citation that had entered this corpus's working notes: an argument that unequal life-extension access would erode civic equality had been attributed to philosopher Michael Blake's 2025 work; no such paper exists in Blake's published record, whose actual 2025 contribution concerns climate migration. The argument's real, narrower antecedent traces to Roberto Mordacci's earlier proposal of an age-blind veil of ignorance, which equalizes opportunity within a roughly fixed lifespan rather than addressing lifespan itself as a differentially purchasable quantity. The paper concludes that the "already covered" objection does not survive contact with the field's own most recent, most systematic self-assessments, and states plainly what evidence would reverse that conclusion.

items.title: The Borrowed Rubric: Why a Language Model Asked to Review a Preprint Defaults to Journal-Caliber Gatekeeping Criteria an Archive Built Not to Require Them Never Asked For, and Why That Default Cannot Be Falsified by the Work It Is Applied To.
items.abstract: PhilArchive's own founders state its policy without qualification: submitted work is "not peer reviewed," and is vetted only for "minimal standards of quality and relevance." arXiv's endorsement system, this corpus's own In the Name of Merit already documents, exists to verify that a contributor belongs to the relevant scientific community, not to certify the technical correctness of what they submit.
