items.title: PV-REC as a Time-Symmetric Boundary-Event Mechanics.
items.abstract: Phenomenological--Velocity Relational Event Completion (\(\PV\text{-}\REC\)) is formulated here as a time-symmetric source--absorber boundary-event proposal. The preparation-side source record \[ \lambda_0=(v,\epsilon,\mathcal J,\Xi) \] is assumed to be statistically independent of the later detector settings. It is not, however, identified with the complete Bell screening variable. The completed four-dimensional event includes the later local absorber boundary conditions, \[ \Lambda_{ab}^{\mathrm{comp}} = (\lambda_0,\mathcal B_A(a),\mathcal B_B(b)). \] Thus the proposal retains preparation independence but rejects emission-time scalar screening-off. -/- In the balanced singlet sector, the source--absorber compatibility of the candidate joint event \((x,y)\) is the usual singlet projector weight \[ m_{xy}(a,b)=\frac14\left(1-xy\cos(a-b)\right). \] PV-REC treats this as a linear boundary compatibility rather than directly as the final event probability. With \[ I_{xy}=-\log m_{xy}, \qquad \kappa(v)=\sqrt{1-\frac{v^2}{c^2}}, \] the PV rule rescales the event-action barrier by \[ I_{xy}\mapsto\kappa(v)I_{xy}, \] giving raw susceptibility \(m_{xy}^{\kappa(v)}\). To prevent setting-dependent total count-rate or latency signals, the physical hazards are normalized to constant total flux, \[ \widehat\Gamma_{xy}^{\PV} = \Gamma_{\mathrm{trial}} \frac{m_{xy}^{\kappa(v)}}{\sum_{x',y'}m_{x'y'}^{\kappa(v)}}. \] With independent exponential race seeds this gives \[ P_{\PV}(x,y\mid a,b,v) = \frac{m_{xy}(a,b)^{\kappa(v)}} {\sum_{x',y'}m_{x'y'}(a,b)^{\kappa(v)}}. \] Consequently, \[ E_{\PV}(a,b\mid v) = -\tanh\!\left[ \kappa(v)\artanh(\cos(a-b)) \right]. \] At \(v=0\), the ordinary singlet law \(E=-\cos(a-b)\) is recovered; fixed sectors with \(v\neq0\) predict a distinct non-Born angular deformation. -/- The construction is not Bell-local in the factorization/local-causality sense. Same-source replay generally fails: \[ (X,Y)=K_{ab}(\lambda_0) \] does not factor into separated scalar response functions \[ X=X_A(a,\lambda_0), \qquad Y=Y_B(b,\lambda_0). \] Thus the model is \emph{Bell-nonseparable}. In the standard Bell vocabulary this is Bell-nonlocality in the technical factorization sense. In the present ontology it is more accurately described as global boundary-contextuality: the completed event depends on the full source--absorber boundary context, not on a directed controllable signal from one wing to the other. Operational no-signalling is retained. -/- Beyond the …

items.title: Historical Coherence: A Structural Analysis of Collective Systems.
items.abstract: History is not a sequence of events but a temporal coherence field in which meaning, tension, and identity reorganize across centuries. This paper reframes history as the long‑timescale expression of the Second Triad (Objects 4–6), showing how alignment, drift, persistence, boundary formation, rupture, and large‑scale reorganization emerge from distributed interactions across symbolic, economic, ecological, and institutional systems. Historical regimes arise from repeated local coherence events—decisions, symbolic compressions, institutional negotiations—that accumulate into macro‑scale patterns. Persistence invariants, trauma sinks, and transmission across carriers shape long‑range historical structure, while drift produces linguistic, institutional, and cultural transformation over time. By presenting history at the signature level, this paper situates civilizational dynamics within the broader Wave C geometry of multi‑system coherence while preserving the upstream membrane around internal mechanisms.

items.title: Economic Coherence: Markets, Institutions, and Collective Stability.
items.abstract: Economic systems are not reducible to markets, incentives, or rational agents. They are multi‑agent coherence fields in which alignment, drift, and persistence stabilize collective behavior across time. This paper formalizes economics as a downstream expression of the Second Triad (Objects 4–6), showing how transactions, symbolic compressions, institutional membranes, and flow architectures generate recognizable regimes without invoking global operators. Economic stability, transformation, and crisis emerge from repeated local coherence events that accumulate into macro‑scale patterns. By presenting economics at the signature level, this paper situates economic behavior within the broader Wave C geometry of multi‑system coherence while preserving the upstream membrane around internal mechanisms.

items.title: Ecology as Multi‑System Coherence.
items.abstract: Ecosystems are not collections of species or environmental conditions. They are distributed coherence fields in which alignment, drift, and persistence stabilize life across interacting organisms and environments. This paper formalizes ecology as a multi‑system expression of the Second Triad (Objects 4–6), showing how trophic structures, seasonal rhythms, succession, co‑evolution, resilience, collapse, and hybridization emerge from repeated local interactions rather than global ecological laws. Ecological regimes arise from boundary‑layer events—energy transfer, signaling, niche formation, and environmental modulation—that accumulate into macro‑scale stability and transformation. By presenting ecology at the signature level, this paper situates ecological behavior within the broader Wave C geometry of multi‑agent coherence while preserving the upstream membrane around internal mechanisms.

items.title: Childhood Neurotechnology and Developmental Cognitive Sovereignty in the Global Cognitive Economy.
Associational Life and Freedom Insights from Philosophy and Law.
items.abstract: What is the reality of what it is to participate in associations, such as sports clubs, charities, trade unions, or political parties? This book explores the complexities surrounding the right of association from a legal and philosophical perspective. -/- Legal chapters explore how the right is protected in jurisdictions as diverse as Chile, Germany, Indonesia, Kenya, Slovenia, Türkiye and the United Kingdom, alongside thematic chapters on judicial review, associational schism and the lived experience of associational participation. Philosophical chapters employ social ontology to illuminate the nature of group interaction and the reality of associational life. -/- Offering the first interdisciplinary examination of freedom of association, this collection contributes significantly to our understanding of this fundamental right.

items.title: Building a Bridge: Sorgner and Euro-Transhumanism.
items.pub: In Andrei Nutas, Classical vs. Euro-Transhumanism Antagonism or Convergence? Basel: Schwabe Verlag. pp. 49-69.
items.venue: Classical vs. Euro-Transhumanism Antagonism or Convergence?
items.abstract: Euro-Transhumanism provides Stefan Lorenz Sorgner with a personal position statement, and it is seemingly aimed at reconciliation between a core of transhumanist ideas and important tendencies in continental, especially posthumanist, philosophy. The project is inherently worth development and discussion, and it has evidently attracted sympathetic interest. Sorgner's achievement in juxtaposing Euro-Transhumanism with what he calls classic transhumanism is to show that there are tenable positions that are at least weakly transhumanist but also at least weakly posthumanist. Euro-Transhumanism is such a position, but there could be others. For example, it would seem possible to construct coherent positions that include some elements of Euro-Transhumanism and some from classic transhumanism. Sorgner's work suggests possibilities for reconciling two traditions of thought. How far this can be taken in practice, however, remains an open question.

items.title: From Decentering to Dwelling: Ecopoiesis and the Ethics of Ecological Participation.
items.abstract: This paper critically re-examines the dominant environmental-philosophical imperative to overcome anthropocentrism in light of contemporary posthuman and relational turns. While ecological and posthuman discourses have productively challenged human domination and exceptionalism by emphasizing entanglement, relationality, and more-than-human agency, they often retain a residual abstraction. This abstraction lies in treating “the human” as a unified moral and conceptual problem. This paper argues that this framing risks obscuring the differentiated, situated, and reflexive capacities through which responsibility becomes possible and that the attempts to “decenter human” altogether prove both conceptually paradoxical and practically self undermining. To develop an ethic that genuinely cultivates ecological responsibility, recognition of human-situatedness and human capacities of moral discernment are inescapable, since we cannot think, evaluate, or care except from within human modes of experiencing and understanding. Rather than seeking to transcend anthropocentrism through decentering human, this paper proposes a shift from the logic of centrism to that of participation. -/- Drawing on processrelational philosophy and ecological thought, this paper proposes the concept of ecopoiesis—the relational making of a shared dwelling-place or home. Ecopoiesis reframes ethical life in terms of cultivating responsible participation in the ongoing co-creation of ecological relations. In this view, human-situatedness is not an obstacle to ecological ethics but its very condition of possibility. The task is neither to dissolve the human category into undifferentiated networks nor to reinstate human absolute dominance but to reconceptualize human reflexivity, moral discernment, and cultural capacity as modes of ecological participation. By repositioning responsibility within relational processes rather than abstract moral hierarchies, this shift—from centrism to participation, from collective guilt to differentiated responsiveness, from critique to renewal—offers a constructive contribution to posthuman environmental thought and offers a vision of “ecological civilization” grounded in ecopoietic practice.

items.title: If Phenomenological Absolutism Is False: A Reductio on Alternative Accounts of Experiential Reality under Austere Physical Realism.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the charge that Phenomenological Absolutism and Mutual Exclusivity (PA/ME) constitute a self-sealing metaphysical system engineered primarily to dissolve longstanding problems in philosophy and science by reframing every critique as another exclusive is-ness. We argue instead that the core commitments of PA/ME—the identity of localized actualized quantum-field configurations with absolute first-person phenomenology, the mutual exclusivity of successive is-nesses, and the collapse of the epistemic-ontic distinction—arise directly from the internal requirements of austere physical realism. These requirements include parsimony, ontological exhaustiveness for all phenomena (including experiential and high-level conceptual ones), internal coherence, avoidance of regress, and fidelity to localized actualization in relativistic quantum field theory. Through a systematic reductio, we examine major alternatives—illusionism, strong emergentism, epiphenomenalism, and standard reductive identity theories—under the assumption that PA/ME is false while austere physicalist constraints are retained. When these alternatives are required to account for the directly accessible character of experiential reality without extra-ontological ingredients, they reintroduce implicit dualisms, residual explanatory gaps, or question-begging redefinitions. The result is a comparative weakening of the coherence and explanatory power of physical realism itself. PA/ME is thereby positioned as a more consistent fulfillment of the very constraints that austere physical realism imposes rather than a mere evasion of difficulties. We conclude that denying PA/ME while remaining within those constraints yields less faithful and more strained accounts of experiential reality.

items.title: The Cognitive Theory of Generics.
items.abstract: Many linguists and philosophers of language view the cognitive theory of generics with suspicion. This paper discusses five of the most recent objections targeting the theory. Considered separately, the objections seem to have very little in common. Taken together, however, they represent the cognitive theory in a difficult bind: the first three suggest that it's too rigid to accommodate nuanced speech (specifically, the use of quantifiers in early childhood and the use of generics in metalinguistic negotiation), while the last two seem to indicate that it's too flexible — having been tailored to fit so many of our naive semantic judgments, it ceases to be explanatory. This paper argues the bind is illusory. All five objections rest on misunderstanding that independently motivated, adjacent psychological considerations help address. Demonstrating this point will reveal how resilient and resourceful the cognitive theory is as an account of language.

items.title: Friendship and Epistemic Injustice: A Reply to Warman.
items.abstract: What, if anything, can be morally objectionable about the practice of epistemic partiality commonly associated with personal friendship? Recently, Jack Warman has argued that it may lead us to insult non-friends and perpetuate testimonial injustice against them by refusing their relevant testimony about our friends. In this article, we challenge Warman’s view on three grounds. First, we show that it underspecifies the conditions under which refusal of non-friends’ testimony counts as insulting. Second, we argue that epistemic partiality, as discussed in the literature, does not in fact require or lead individuals to refuse non-friends’ testimony in an insulting way. Third, we show that Warman’s two arguments concerning the moral wrongness of epistemic partiality assign such wrongness in two competing ways and thus turn out to be incompatible with each other. Finally, we go beyond Warman’s proposal to consider whether epistemic partiality may generate epistemic injustice in another way, by bestowing friends with credibility excesses.

items.title: Russellian Monism and Neutral Monism: Scrutinizing Inscrutables.
items.abstract: This paper critically examines Haoying Liu’s recent challenge to Russellian monism (RM), often understood as the view that (1) physics describes natural phenomena entirely in structural terms; (2) such phenomena possess intrinsic characters, or quiddities, that constitute or ground what physics describes structurally; and (3) phenomenal consciousness is constituted, at least in part, by such quiddities. Liu argues that RM’s appeal is undermined by the epistemic inaccessibility of quiddities and their combinatory principles, rendering it liable to a historical decline akin to Thomistic hylomorphism. I contend that this critique overstates the degree of mystery inherent in RM. First, drawing on work by Torin Alter and Derk Pereboom (2023), I question whether RM is committed to the claim that physics captures only structural features of reality, thereby reopening the possibility that quiddities may be accessible to empirical or conceptual inquiry. Second, I situate RM within the neutral monist tradition that inspired it, showing how similar views in Ernst Mach and William James treat the fundamental constituents of reality as epistemically accessible. Finally, I revisit Bertrand Russell’s own formulation of neutral monism, arguing that it was intended primarily as a theoretical framework for situating mind and matter in nature rather than a discovery-oriented research program. These considerations suggest that Liu’s objection, while illuminating, does not decisively undermine RM’s philosophical viability.

items.title: Gendered asymmetries in AI stories in English and Spanish.
items.abstract: Creative texts produced wholly or partly by large-scale generative language models are increasingly circulating within literary markets and cultural institutions. Research on AI-generated texts has largely examined bias at the level of words and images; however, small-scale statistical co-occurrences in AI-output can generate macro-scale narrative phenomena, where narrative functions intersect with stylistic texture, for example through voice, focalisation, reliability, or omission. This article argues that literary criticism, and New Formalism in particular, offers a necessary methodological framework for identifying and historicising these stylistic asymmetries. A background premise, working against the current techno-utopian ethos that improving algorithms requires more algorithms, is that close, slow reading is necessary to addressing the ethical complexities in literary form, the unsettled nature of language, and the context-specific nature of bias, harm, and oppression (Jackson and Courneya 2023, p. 62). Through a new formalist reading of English- and Spanish-language short stories generated by ChatGPT-5, I demonstrate that distributional regularities in language modelling scale upward, producing gendered and culturally normative stylistic patterns. By shifting the analysis of AI creativity from representation to form, I hope to indicate how literary methods can illuminate narrative-specific dimensions of bias in generative AI output.

items.title: Introducción a la Filosofía Analítica. Volumen 1.
Envisioning AI futures: science fiction, the imagination gap, and its political consequences.
items.abstract: Dystopian AI tropes, grounded in science fiction, are pervasive in popular culture, but the effects of these narratives on lay orientations toward socio-technological futures remain under-researched. The article distinguishes between imagination (what people can envision) and expectations (what they think is likely), and explores the influence of science fiction on both. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with young adults, we identify an “AI futures imagination gap”: an asymmetry in people’s imaginative capacity, whereby dystopian sociotechnical futures associated with AI and robotics are vivid, coherent, easily elaborated, and often articulated through sci-fi-inflected narrative templates, while utopian sociotechnical alternatives remain abstract, fragmented, and difficult to articulate. Science fiction also shaped expectations in a more indirect way. Participants did not usually consider fictional scenarios as straightforwardly predicting the future, but instead posited that less extreme and modified forms of the problems depicted could be real issues. The findings suggest the problem is not a lack of will to imagine better futures, but a lack of narrative templates: dystopian futures were richly resourced by science fiction, but positive futures lacked comparable support from sci-fi or other cultural sources. This imagination gap may constrain the possibilities of public deliberation and limit democratic capacities for shaping socially desirable futures involving AI. Participatory futures methods such as backcasting may help to cultivate more socially grounded, politically plural and non-technocratic visions of alternative positive sociotechnical orders, but their impacts depend on whether such visions circulate beyond expert settings and enter wider public and policy debate.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on Biblical Scholarship: Opportunities and Challenges to Textual and Theological Inquiry.
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a game-changer in biblical scholarship for the past few years, as its technologies, particularly machine learning and natural language processing, has become more sophisticated and already reshaping the various methodologies used to analyze Scriptures. This paper examines the significant opportunities and the inherent challenges presented by AI in the area of biblical scholarship. Qualitative method of research is employed. The research found out that enhanced capabilities in textual criticism, accelerated linguistic analysis are opportunities AI presents to biblical scholarship. However, the adoption of AI also raises critical challenges, such as the potential for algorithmic bias, the risk of devaluing human interpretive skills in biblical scholarship, and the ethical implications of using AI to generate theological conclusions that has no consistent logic. The paper argues that though AI should be viewed as a powerful tool to augment, it should not replace traditional and human scholarly methods.

items.title: SHATTER: Formal Mechanics and Mathematical Dynamics of an Applied Identity Physics Game Architecture uuia.app/shatter.

Each card carries four stats — Pattern (P), Narrative (N), Behavior (B), Adaptation (A) — and clashes resolve through torsion mechanics derived directly from the corpus. -/- **The core shatter rule:** -/- > If opponent's final B ≥ 2 × your current P → your card SHATTERS -/- **The doubles immunity rule:** -/- > If a card rolls doubles even once during its roll, it cannot shatter that clash regardless of final B total.
