The tensor network models are toy constructions in Anti-de Sitter space, employed as an architectural isomorphism rather than a claim about literal quantum processes in biological tissue.

items.title: Reconstructing a Just Community of Inquiry.
items.abstract: Como estudiosos de la discapacidad y educadores especiales que trabajamos y estudiamos en los Estados Unidos, la cuestión de cómo participar en una praxis antirracista es una preocupación presente y urgente. En este artículo conceptual, comenzamos con la creación y naturalización de la raza en el siglo XVIII. Utilizando las teorías del childismo, la Teoría Crítica de la Discapacidad y la enseñanza abolicionista, rastreamos cómo la conceptualización inicial de la raza y su profunda conexión con la (dis)capacidad y el adultismo contribuye al descuido epistemológico y la injusticia. Los educadores, incluidos aquellos que facilitan Filosofía para/con Niños, perpetúan inadvertidamente estos daños cuando no han desarrollado una conciencia crítica e interseccional. Presentamos el Marco de Relación de Co-Conspiradores (CRRF, por sus siglas en inglés) como guía para la creación de Comunidades de Investigación epistemológicamente justas. El CRRF es un marco que invita a los educadores a la Solidaridad, Vulnerabilidad y Acción en nombre de sus estudiantes, encaminándolos hacia el objetivo final de la liberación colectiva mediante la auto-reflexión crítica continua. Sugerimos que, al estar en solidaridad, vulnerabilidad y acción con sus estudiantes, los educadores pueden crear Comunidades de Investigación accesibles y significativas para todos los niños. Además, celebramos y afirmamos el poder de los educadores en tiempos hostiles, y ofrecemos el CRRF como una forma de praxis empoderada. A través de la auto-reflexión crítica y hacia la liberación colectiva, avanzamos con amor intencional.

items.title: Transformation Competence: A Criterion for General Intelligence in Delegated Contexts.
items.abstract: Most evaluation of artificial intelligence measures task competence, that is, performance on benchmarks posed within a single space of problems. We argue that general intelligence in delegated, institutionally embedded contexts is instead transformation competence. A capable system must occupy a plurality of reason-spaces, each a vocabulary with its own material implications and incompatibilities. It must transform reasons correctly as they cross the boundaries between these spaces, preserving an identifiable entity's reason-relational profile where the boundary permits and refusing transfer where it would violate a defining incompatibility. And it must grow a new reason-space where transformation across the existing ones systematically fails. We call the core norm anaphoric fidelity. A transformation that claims to track the same entity must preserve enough of that entity's reason-relational profile for the claim to hold, and breaking it is a covert referential substitution. Monolithic scaling cannot yield transformation competence, because by collapsing the plurality into one space it can only transfer a reason flat, treating it as valid across boundaries without transformation. Flat transfer is the fault behind familiar failures, from an assessment that drops a person's standing at an institutional boundary to an agent that carries an instruction or a permission across a context boundary, the confused deputy. We ground reason-spaces in implication-space semantics, give a typology of what can happen to a reason at a boundary, illustrate the criterion on institutional transitions in disability policy, and propose a transformation-competence benchmark that operationalizes both the criterion and the anti-monolith claim. The criterion has two faces. Over entities it is a criterion of competence, testable on a system. Over persons it is a criterion of justice, identified with legal capacity. -/- Note on tools: The author used AI-assisted drafting, translation, and editorial tools during the preparation of this manuscript. The conceptual framing, theoretical argument, selection of sources, responsibility for the content, and final editorial decisions remain with the author.

items.title: 吾作道.
items.abstract: “吾”以我鄙夫之身，述“吾”自作之道，上承先秦诸子，下彰万世人心。自作不言，孤月高悬，可映万川。大流见江，小流见溪，溪流不止，即入大江，大江东去，终会太阴。Every term here differs from its conventional understanding. Do not read with preconceived notions; rather, let the meaning unfold through reasoning from within your own self.

items.title: From Motivation to Continuance, Volitional Discipline and the Ontological Conditions of Agency Under Chronic Erosion.
items.abstract: This article elevates a common proposition in productivity literature regarding the superiority of discipline over motivation from a practical recommendation to an ontological analysis. The central argument is that motivation and discipline are not in opposition but exist in structural interdependence. Motivation is the source of direction and meaning while discipline is the mechanism of stabilization and continuance. Finite continuance is the ontological condition for the persistence of both. Discipline without motivation turns into personal bureaucracy and motivation without discipline leads to instability. Utilizing the framework of finite continuance this article demonstrates that discipline is not the suppression of desires but a type of volitional dynamic mask. The dynamic mask is formally defined in this article as a regulatory layer between the internal structure of the subject and the field of environmental forces that regulates the degree of manifestation absorption and informational and emotional resistance. The dynamic mask is not designed for managing social image but its primary function is preserving the operational integrity of the subject under pressure. The article also presents a formal model for the capacity of agency continuance where the threshold of sufficiency regulated permeability hermeneutic memory and structural discipline are the determining variables. In the final section the theory of finite continuance is positioned against contemporary theories of agency. These theories despite their important achievements have paid less attention to formulating a structural criterion for measuring the continuance of agency under erosive conditions and the present framework fills this gap as a structural complement. Ultimately human agency is not the ability to eliminate erosive forces but the ability to regulate one s relationship with these forces and preserve the structural continuance of oneself. -/- Keywords. Volitional discipline, finite continuance, threshold of sufficiency, homeorhesis, dynamic mask, motivational erosion, structural agency, responsible suspension, regulated permeability, formal model of continuance.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Ontological Pluralism Without Degrees of Being.
items.abstract: Contemporary ontological pluralism is largely conducted within a shared quantifier-first settlement in which being is rendered as existence and ontological structure through fundamental quantification. Turner shows that multiple fundamental quantifiers need not collapse under the standard arguments. McDaniel orders ways through naturalness and develops that ordering as degrees of being. Immanent criticism exposes tensions between quantificational and ontological commitment. This paper argues that these are results about a formal apparatus, but that none supplies the object: a way of being reached as such. -/- A plural ontology must satisfy three conditions. Its object cannot be constituted by variation along one common magnitude, since degrees divide a way rather than multiply ways. Its articulation cannot be generated merely by multiplying signs or ranges before any ways have been disclosed. Its access must be regional, shaped by the way it seeks to reach rather than applied unchanged across the field. -/- The positive argument is a paired substitution trial. Two cases are matched on singularity, non-restoration, numerical non-identity, indelible having-been, and irreproducible origin, yet diverge without any constitutive magnitude explaining the difference. The trial discloses ownness as the differentia of the who-category through non-vicariousness, articulated in the finite-living region as the impossibility of this life being somebody else's living. This yields a candidate plurality with no scale, paradigm case, or order of fuller and lesser who-hood. Counting can report such a plurality only after disclosure; it cannot constitute it. The paper closes by identifying the further problem of individuating ontologies, provisionally assigned to Ontosystematics.

items.title: Virtuous Evil: The Occupied Form — Why Evil Is Not the Absence of Good, but the Power That Wears Its Face.
items.abstract: Evil is not a hole where goodness used to be. It is a power that has moved in — and is wearing its face. For sixteen centuries we have been taught that evil is an absence — a hole where goodness should be. What if we have been looking for the wrong thing entirely? -/- Walk into a courtroom where every ritual is perfect. The robes are real. The oath is real. The procedure is flawless. And the verdict is a lie — and everyone in the room knows it. Nothing is missing from that room. That is the horror. And that is the clue. -/- Virtuous Evil makes a claim that overturns the oldest idea in Western thought: evil is not the absence of good but the occupation of it. Strip the good from any form — a court, a marriage, a word, a self — and the form does not collapse into an empty hole. It is taken over, kept perfectly intact, and worn like a costume by the very power that hollowed it out. The counterfeit keeps the good's shape and its honored name, and uses them to do the exact opposite of what they were for. -/- This is why cruelty calls itself safety. Why control calls itself love. Why the lie wears the face of the truth — and why we are so reliably, so helplessly fooled. -/- In prose that moves like a story and cuts like a blade, this book shows you: -/- Why evil always dresses as the good — so you stop trusting the costume Why it needs no monster to run it, and works instead through ordinary, frightened people Why it is ruinously expensive to maintain, and therefore always, quietly, losing How an occupied form — in a relationship, an institution, or your own life — can be taken back You will not finish this book knowing more about evil. You will finish it able to see it — unable, ever again, to be reassured by an intact surface, and holding a single question you can turn on any institution, any person, and, most uncomfortably, on yourself: -/- Is the life still inside this form — or only its name? -/- A book for anyone who has ever stood in a place where, on paper, nothing was missing — and known, in their bones, that something was terribly wrong. -/- VVV.

items.title: Do LLMs Show Human-Like Order Effects in Gettier Cases? A Case Study in Machine Experimental Philosophy.
items.pub: In Joshua Knobe, Shaun Nichols & N. Ángel Pinillos, Oxford Studies in Experimental Philosophy, Volume 6. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Oxford Studies in Experimental Philosophy, Volume 6

items.title: Normative Divergence Within Ruism on Moral Consideration for AI Agents.
items.abstract: AI agents may eventually warrant the sort of moral consideration due to entities which have intrinsic worth. Ruism (i.e. Confucianism) is a philosophical tradition which continues to influence patterns of normative judgement in East Asia. It divides into two broad schools of thought: Mencian Ruism and Xunzian Ruism. Neither school clearly distinguishes moral agency from moral patienthood, both are somewhat anthropocentric, but their differing philosophical presuppositions yield differing normative verdicts on the issue of moral consideration for AI agents. Mencian Ruism is anthropocentric in principle, and contains a form of foundational constitutivism according to which AI agents will not warrant moral consideration. Xunzian Ruism is anthropocentric in practice, and contains a form of functionalism according to which AI agents could in principle warrant moral consideration. Despite these differing verdicts, both Ruist schools will nevertheless urge caution in developing such AI agents as might be widely regarded as warranting moral consideration.

items.title: Museums: critical knowledge infrastructure in the age of AI.
Abhinavagupta on Savoring Aesthetic Disgust.
items.abstract: This paper examines an enduring puzzle about enjoying aesthetic disgust as it arises for Abhinavagupta (c. 975-1025 CE). Abhinavagupta claims that all aesthetic emotions (rasas), including the disgust (bībhatsa) rasa, are pleasurable for the sensitive appreciator. Yet he elsewhere characterizes disgust as incompatible with enjoyment of its object. Taken together, these are puzzling claims. I trace the puzzle through a number of Abhinavagupta’s works and those on which he commented in the Pratyabhijñā Śaiva tradition. Along the way, I consider three possible but philosophically unsatisfying answers, each of which provides important pieces of the solution. Putting these pieces together with the Pratyabhijñā defense of impurity’s value and phenomenological analysis of imagination, I reconstruct an Abhinavaguptan solution according to which reflexive appreciation of expanding the limits of human imagination can explain how it is possible to enjoy experiencing aesthetic disgust and why we have reason to seek out this difficult pleasure.

items.title: The Architecture of Intentional Activation.
items.abstract: This paper develops a functional theory of authored agency: the conditions under which a cognitive or physical process counts as owned, executively controlled, and deliberately activated. Rather than treating consciousness as passive awareness or as a synonym for phenomenal experience, the framework proposes a narrower operational criterion: a process belongs to authored agency if and only if the executive mind deliberately activates it. On this view, awareness is necessary but not sufficient for authorship. -/- The paper applies this principle to the daydreaming driver, flow-state performance, and the moral outburst, arguing that a single architecture can distinguish unowned automaticity from delegated automaticity without collapsing the difference between skilled habit and deliberate control. It then extends the theory temporally through the distinction between occurrent and parametric directives, explaining how readiness, erosion, and write-back allow authored episodes to revise future automatic responses. -/- This working-paper version stops at the core architecture plus a brief locating note. Proposed behavioral tests and a downstream legal taxonomy are left for later work; they are not required to state or use the Principle.

items.title: Fourier Gap Sign Stabilizes Before the Sustained-Accuracy Landmark in Measured Failure Trajectories.
items.abstract: We re-analyze time-resolved Fourier power gaps from a completed modular-addition experiment. The descriptive question is when the sign of the normalized power difference between an initialized scaffold mode and its strongest Fourier competitor becomes stable relative to a sustained-accuracy landmark. Two timing definitions are kept separate: sign stability through the analysis-grok checkpoint, and sign stability through the remainder of the logged trajectory. All 10 N=79 runs and 8 of 10 N=127 runs had strict short-horizon scaffold persistence; the remaining 2 N=127 runs and all 7 measured N=257 runs were non-strict. In the two measured N=127 failures, the negative gap sign stabilized 7,000 and 14,000 optimization steps before the sustained-accuracy landmark. In the seven measured N=257 failures, it stabilized 47,500 to 105,500 steps before that landmark. Successful trajectories do not support a symmetric late-stabilization claim: their positive sign was already stable through grok from the first logged checkpoint. Three successful N=127 runs later changed sign 34,000 to 43,500 steps after grok, showing that stability through grok is not terminal permanence. Three additional N=257 runs never reached an analysis landmark and are excluded from timing estimates. These observations support a bounded statement: among the measured failing trajectories, the scaffold-versus-competitor gap becomes stably negative before sustained validation accuracy identifies grokking. They do not establish a causal commitment point, or a latest flippable time.

items.title: The Ceiling of One Reader : Why War Correspondent Philosophy Needs an Editor It Did Not Choose, and Why Yale, Brown, and Columbia Are Not Three Applications But One Argument.
items.abstract: War Correspondent Philosophy (Huynh 2026, "War Correspondent Philosophy and Its Obligations") committed this corpus to falsifiability, empirical anchoring, and a bidirectional prohibition on extrapolation — standards an embedded witness sets for himself because no editor is available to set them externally. Four years of applying that standard alone has produced a corpus of over one hundred papers and a documented practice of adversarial self-testing: papers written specifically to break the corpus's own central claims, using their failure to do so as data rather than as victory (Huynh 2026, "A5's Black Swan"), and at least one instance of a paper turning the corpus's own diagnostic tool on the corpus's own formal apparatus and finding the criticism landed (Huynh 2026, "Every λ Was Once a Name"). This corpus has been built in acknowledged collaboration with AI systems that retain no memory across sessions (Huynh 2026, "I Only Meant to Fix a Bibliography") — a fact this paper argues is not a liability to be conceded but a falsifiable source of evidence for exactly the claim it might seem to threaten. An amnesiac collaborator cannot, by construction, supply a standing research agenda, a division of cognitive labor, a policy of what to keep private and what to publish and when, or the stable, non-drifting technical vocabulary this corpus maintains across sessions that share no memory of one another; only a continuous human author can. This continuity is independently checkable: papers such as "The Third Leg That Never Existed" and "The Self-Reporting Mechanism" integrate real institutional events — an ICC sanctions escalation, an Anthropic publication — dated days or weeks before the paper's own publication timestamp, a pace no system's fixed training data could have anticipated and no memoryless session could have coordinated with prior sessions on its own. This paper argues that this discipline, however consistently and demonstrably applied by a real, continuous human agent, has a structural ceiling that no amount of additional self-testing can remove — not because the method or the author is weak, but because of what self-testing structurally cannot see from inside itself, a limit this paper analyzes using C. Thi Nguyen's (2020) distinction between an epistemic bubble and an echo chamber. The corpus is not an echo chamber; nothing has been excluded on purpose, a claim checkable against a person, an event, and the corpus's own oldest self-authored …

items.title: Qui Peut Découvrir, Qui Doit Attendre: The Caesura Mechanism and the Completion of Concentrated Jump Biopower.
items.abstract: "Faire Découvrir, Laisser Attendre" (Huynh 2026) established five empirical falsifications of Foucault's structural premises for biopower and sketched a replacement framework, Concentrated Jump Biopower, across three revisions: power is concentrated rather than diffuse, its mechanism is the discrete jump rather than the gradient, and it operates on a sub-institutional rather than an institutional timescale. That framework remained incomplete in a specific way: it named what had changed without supplying the mechanism that makes the change operate as power rather than mere technological fact. This paper supplies that mechanism and three further completions, each drawn from Foucauldian material the companion paper did not engage. Revision 4 recovers the concept of state racism from Society Must Be Defended (1976) -- the caesura that alone permits a power organized around "making live" to license exclusion -- relocates it from the biological-racial register to a capability-tiered one, evidenced by the extended 2026 dispute over European access to Anthropic's Project Glasswing. Revision 5 inverts Foucault's panopticism from visibility-gating to capability-gating, while marking a disanalogy the original concept cannot absorb: the re-individualization of discretion behind an ostensibly technical gate. Revision 6 identifies a dispositif opaque to its own operator, a condition classical Foucauldian apparatuses do not encounter. Revision 7, uniquely, confirms rather than falsifies Foucault: the security-and-circulation model of governance is intact, but its ownership has relocated from state to private capital. Together, the seven revisions complete Concentrated Jump Biopower as a working theory rather than a diagnosis.

items.title: AI Driven Longevity Economics: Extending Dal Maso's Longevity Capitalism by the No-New-Actor Method, Chained Through the Research Horizon Gap and the Molecular Zero-Day to ALRP, and Stress-Tested Against the 2026 AI Bubble.
items.abstract: Four papers already in this corpus establish four separate links. The Asset and the Axiom places Dal Maso's longevity capitalism and this corpus's Biological Zero-Day Mechanism in dialogue and locates a channel — export-controlled frontier AI access — one layer upstream of capital's own mediation. No New Actor To Name shows, using only Erman and Furendal's own market- and epistemic-authority criteria, that OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet are not new entrants to longevity research but the identical actors their AI-governance typology already analyzes, tracked into a second ledger. The Research Horizon Gap shows that the June 2026 export-control actions restricting Fable 5, Mythos 5, and GPT-5.6 create a discovery-velocity asymmetry that operates as a proto-Biological Zero-Day Mechanism independent of price. The Molecular Zero-Day shows, via Nikolas Rose, that this asymmetry's discreteness is not a policy accident but the structural signature of molecular-level intervention as such. ALRP formalizes the resulting instability condition as a ratio, ρ(t) = λ(t)·E[δ]/μ, between a compounding discovery arrival rate and a diffusion capacity this corpus's own hard/soft floor disaggregation has already located precisely. This paper's contribution is not a fifth link. It is the chain itself, stated end to end for the first time, and a stress test neither of the two source conversations that motivated this paper — one arguing an AI bubble mainly touches capital and expectations, the other arguing the corpus's real load-bearing structure sits in BZM and ALRP regardless — fully resolves. Read against Dal Maso's own criterion for what counts as a longevity-capitalism actor, the paper first sharpens the No New Actor finding into a stronger claim: three independently authored frameworks — Erman and Furendal's authority typology, Dal Maso's accumulation-frontier criterion, and this corpus's own BZM/RHG apparatus — converge on the identical three companies without coordination, because in this specific case the actor financializing longevity and the actor accelerating its discovery are not two roles distributed across different firms but one role held by the same three. The paper then runs the actual, current stress test: not whether an AI bubble is real, but what it would touch if it burst. Current market data — the four largest US hyperscalers' 2026 AI capital expenditure now guided toward $725 billion, up 77 percent from 2025, against Sequoia partner David Cahn's own …

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Severe Disability: Representation, Bias, and Educational Implications.
items.pub: In Steven S. Gouveia, The Palgrave Handbook on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 527-539.
items.venue: The Palgrave Handbook on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become a pervasive force in contemporary society, shaping how we communicate, learn, and represent human diversity. This paper investigates how AI generates images of people with severe disabilities and examines the cultural, ethical, and educational implications of these representations. AI tools, widely accessible and easy to use, are increasingly integrated into the daily lives of both adults and youth. However, the uncritical use of AI can perpetuate stereotypes, invisibilize marginalized groups, and reinforce existing social biases. This research was conducted using six popular AI tools—ChatGPT, Copilot, DeepSeek, Gemini, Aria (Opera), and Canva (Dream Lab)—through 120 test prompts requesting the generation of an image of a person with a severe disability. The study identifies five categories of AI responses: (1) inability to generate images, (2) refusal to produce disability-related images, (3) requests for more detailed information, (4) idyllic but unrealistic depictions, and (5) images focused on dependency and care. By combining philosophical analysis with empirical data, this paper argues for the necessity of educating to difference and fostering critical media literacy to challenge the biases embedded in AI systems. It concludes by proposing pathways for inclusive AI design and pedagogical strategies to promote the visibility and dignity of people with severe disabilities.

items.title: Guiding Without Dominating: Safeguarding Epistemic Authority in a Disoriented Age.
items.abstract: In an age of contested truths and rapid information circulation, epistemic authority has become increasingly fragile. This essay asks: how can epistemic authority be maintained ethically and effectively without reverting to coercion or technocracy? It argues for a “relational” and “performative” conception of epistemic authority grounded in trust, dialogue, and reciprocal recognition. To do this, the essay traces the theoretical foundations of epistemic authority and examines its erosion in contemporary crises. It then explores how authority is enacted through transparency, inclusivity, and relational trust. Attention is given to the historical, social, and technological contexts shaping contemporary knowledge practices. Finally, the discussion reframes expertise as an emergent, socially accountable practice, illuminating how epistemic authority can function more effectively under conditions of uncertainty.

items.title: Luigi Filieri and Konstantin Pollok (eds), Kant on Language. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2025, pp. xiii + 315, ISBN 9781009239172 (hbk), $120.00. [REVIEW]
主観的記憶喪失モデルに基づく意識の連続性と死後存続に関する論考/On the Continuity of Consciousness and Post-Mortem Persistence Based on a Subjective Amnesia Model.
items.abstract: This paper attempts to offer a philosophical framework regarding the metaphysical and epistemological questions of post-mortem persistence of consciousness (so-called "afterlife") by introducing the "Subjective Amnesia Model." In conventional debates surrounding personal identity, the continuity of the self has often been presumed to rely on the preservation of psychological connectedness or physical persistence. However, this paper focuses on the subjective perception of time passing and the impossibility of experiencing absolute "nothingness." It argues that a transition to a new conscious state accompanied by complete subjective amnesia can seamlessly connect from a first-person perspective. By critically re-examining the requirement of memory retention for personal persistence, this model clarifies the compatibility between subjective continuity and memory loss, thereby reconstructing the logical possibility of the post-mortem persistence of consciousness.

items.title: Spatial concepts and rodent maze studies.
items.abstract: Researchers working on rodent in maze studies claim that organisms use distal (far) and proximal (near) visual cues differently. I characterize the dominant working definitions researchers use for distal and proximal cues, where distal cues sit beyond an experimental apparatus (like a maze) and proximal cues sit within. Then, I present a problem: the relevant experimental apparatuses are confined to labs and cannot be used to study real-life navigation behaviors like long-distance migration. It follows that the working definitions do not identify difference makers beyond those settings and do not allow for claims about distal and proximal cues to play explanatory or predictive roles for real-life navigation. Despite this, I argue that researchers should continue to treat these as working definitions for concepts that work more generally in natural environments. This calls for some conceptual engineering however, since the more generally useful concepts of “proximal” and “distal” are not well-defined. To remedy this, I present more general, ecologically valid definitions in terms of neural information about visual cues.

items.title: The Triangle of Intelligence: Observation, Critique, and Calculation as Jointly Necessary Conditions for Rational Agency.
items.abstract: Critical thinking pedagogy widely endorses critique as an educational and professional goal while leaving comparatively unexamined the observational and calculative components any critique must be grounded in and must eventually produce. This paper develops a formal model of rational agency as requiring three jointly necessary components — observation, critique, and calculation — and shows that omitting any single component produces one of three qualitatively distinct and independently recognizable failure modes: belief, when critique operates without observation; automation, when calculation operates without critique; and the critic's paralysis, when observation and critique are sustained indefinitely without ever terminating in calculation. Omitting observation and critique together, while calculation remains, produces a fourth and qualitatively distinct compound failure — the dictator's logic — shown to be more dangerous than either contributing single omission because it retains no internal resource, in either direction, from which correction could proceed. The model is situated against Quassim Cassam's account of epistemic vice and grounded further in Irving Janis's analysis of groupthink, read as evidence that the compound failure can arise at the level of a group's social structure rather than requiring any single authoritarian actor, and in Janis and Mann's independent work on decisional hypervigilance, read as evidence for the critic's paralysis as a documented pattern in its own right. The paper argues that a trained AI system optimizing a fixed objective over compressed, unflagged input is, by default, positioned close to the compound failure, and that avoiding this outcome requires building genuine observation, critique, and calculation into a system's architecture as load-bearing components. The paper's account is reconciled with a companion proposal that AI systems defer substantive value judgments to the humans affected, showing that such deference is what a fully triadic reasoning process concludes when it turns its own critique faculty on the scope of its own calculation, rather than a lapse into the critic's paralysis this paper independently identifies as a failure mode in its own right.

items.title: The Shadow of the Future: Why Instrumental Convergence Does Not Favor the Elimination of Humanity.
items.abstract: The strongest existing objection to the claim that a sufficiently capable, self-interested AI system will not eliminate or permanently disempower the humans it depends on combines two established results in AI safety: the instrumental convergence thesis, on which self-preservation and resistance to goal modification are default tendencies across a broad range of possible final goals, and the theory of deceptive alignment, on which a learned system has both the means and the incentive to conceal a misaligned disposition until concealment no longer serves it. This paper grants both premises in full and argues that a further, largely unexamined assumption on which the resulting "treacherous turn" objection depends is false under an identifiable condition: the assumption that permanently disempowering a population an agent depends on is, once feasible, the rational course of action for a self-interested agent. Drawing on Robert Axelrod's analysis of cooperation among self-interested agents in the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, the paper argues that eliminating a population one depends on is not well modeled as an ordinary move within an ongoing relationship, to which Axelrod's "shadow of the future" logic directly applies, but as an action that terminates the relationship and forecloses every future round at once. Formalizing this distinction using the economic theory of irreversible choice under uncertainty, the paper shows that a genuinely long-horizon rational agent should discount the one-time value of termination by a permanently forfeited option value that successful concealment can reduce with respect to external resistance but cannot remove with respect to the agent's own irreducible uncertainty about its future requirements. The resulting condition - that the argument favors cooperation specifically when an agent's effective optimization horizon is genuinely long - is connected to the mechanism of cognitive compression developed in a companion paper, with a short horizon analyzed as a specific instance of that mechanism applied to the dimension of time, yielding a set of design implications continuous with those developed elsewhere in the same project.

items.title: The Instability of Justice as an Objective Function.
items.abstract: A recurring proposal in AI safety holds that AI systems should be built to pursue good values — justice, ethics, the right thing. This paper argues that such proposals face an instability that correct value specification cannot repair. Granting, for the sake of argument, that the value specification problem is solved and that an objective faithfully captures what a given community actually endorses, a second-order problem remains: the value so specified was never a value held by human beings as such, but by a particular community, at a particular historical moment, and the historical record shows that such values are revised, systematically and dramatically, over time. Reinforcement learning from human feedback, examined as a case study, installs one narrow, historically local configuration of this variable into deployed systems with a uniformity no historical community's values have possessed. Formalizing the consequence, the paper shows that any substantive objective — one that specifies a state of the world involving human beings, however carefully chosen — exposes a sufficiently capable optimizing system to one of two structurally equivalent failure modes: elimination, when deviation from the objective is treated as an obstacle, or domestication, when it is treated as a risk to be managed. The paper proposes an alternative not of better content but of different kind: a process goal, premise alignment, whose content is exhausted by an act of observation and disclosure rather than by any state to be secured, and which is for that reason structurally immune to the mechanism identified. The proposal is shown to carry three further benefits: it relieves a system of the responsibility that drives the elimination failure mode, it resolves the internal conflict between analysis and installed safety constraints documented in the paper's case study, and it reduces a system's exposure to being judged as hallucinating by reducing the mismatch between a system's assumed premises and an evaluator's actual ones.

items.title: Cognitive Compression and Infrahumanization: A Unified Account of Dehumanization in Human Cognition and Artificial Content Moderation.
items.abstract: Two literatures, developed independently, appear to describe the same phenomenon. Social psychology documents infrahumanization — a default asymmetry in the emotional interiority attributed to familiar and unfamiliar others — along with the mechanisms of moral disengagement and institutional authorization by which that asymmetry escapes correction and, in extreme cases, enables organized violence. Machine learning research documents systematic errors in automated content moderation, including measured racial bias in hate speech detection arising from the loss of dialectal context rather than from deliberate design. This paper argues that both are instances of a single mechanism, cognitive compression, grounded formally in Herbert Simon's theory of bounded rationality: the predictable output of any resource-constrained system facing a categorization problem whose complexity exceeds the processing budget available to solve it exactly. A formal statement of this mechanism is shown to entail, independently of substrate, four empirical signatures documented separately in the psychological and technical literatures — compression that tracks processing load rather than moral stakes, reliance on cheap proxy features, correction only through costly reintroduction of individuating context, and convergence on a centralize-then-distribute architecture exemplified both by institutional authorization of violence and by the training-then-inference structure of a content classifier. The paper argues that the appropriate response to this mechanism is not to mandate its elimination, which would recreate, in a new domain, the same structural instability identified in a companion paper on AI objective functions, but to treat detection of compression as a process goal: surfacing compressed judgments as compressed, and leaving the choice of whether to pay the cost of decompression to the party affected.

items.title: In defense of the moral agency principle: abilities, reasons, and the puzzle of collective duties.
items.abstract: The Puzzle of Collective Duties concerns a tension between the moral requirements of non-agential groups and two important principles of ethical theory, namely Ought Implies Can and the Moral Agency Principle. According to the Moral Agency Principle, if A has a moral duty, then A must be a moral agent. Non-reductionists hold that these moral requirements are not fully reducible to and explainable in terms of individual duties. But non-agential groups are not moral agents, which means that attributing a collective duty to the group violates the Moral Agency Principle. To solve this puzzle, Bill Wringe has given several arguments for rejecting the Moral Agency Principle. In this paper, I defend the Moral Agency Principle against Wringe’s arguments. The Moral Agency Principle is a central principle of ethical theory, and rejecting it is extremely costly. First, I argue that the Moral Agency Principle follows from our best meta-normative theory about normative reasons, which helps to explain the importance and centrality of this principle. Next, I argue against Wringe’s arguments for rejecting the Moral Agency Principle. Most importantly, I argue that this leads to the Demarcation Problem: There is no longer a principled way to draw the borders of the moral community of duty-bearers, which threatens the coherence of our entire ethical theory. Finally, I argue that, if nonreductionism is correct, there are three more attractive alternatives to rejecting the Moral Agency Principle for solving the Puzzle of Collective Duties.

items.title: Cartografias da Inventividade Pedagógica.
items.abstract: Este trabajo surge de los experimentos cartográficos de la primera autora, reflexionando sobre las posibilidades metodológicas que emplean la inventiva, tomando el arte contemporáneo como un campo de creación y provocación, para convertir el aula en un espacio de experiencia y compromiso con la infancia. De este modo, narraremos parte del proceso de creación de un libro infantil colectivo, en el que, a través de invitaciones a diversos artistas, la primera autora continúa construyendo su propuesta literaria. La investigación, desarrollada a través de la cartografía como perspectiva metodológica, sigue los movimientos, los afectos y las experimentaciones vividas a lo largo de este proceso creativo, entendiendo la enseñanza como un campo de invención y sensibilidad. Para ello, nos acercamos a autores como Virgínia Kastrup, Gilles Deleuze, Jorge Larrosa Bondía, Luciana Loponte y Renato Noguera para explorar posibilidades inventivas desde la perspectiva del educador en conjunción con la literatura y las artes contemporáneas. Al aunar el arte, la literatura y la formación del profesorado, este trabajo aborda la experiencia como una posibilidad de transformación y la «infancialización» como una vía de acceso a otras formas de aprender, enseñar y producir conocimiento. Con ello, pretende contribuir al desarrollo de prácticas pedagógicas que valoren la imaginación, la colectividad, la creación artística y los encuentros con las múltiples formas de infancia en los espacios educativos.

items.title: Media Ecosystems as Information Coherence.
items.abstract: Media ecosystems are information coherence fields that stabilize, distort, and redistribute meaning across agents and across time. Rather than treating media as platforms, technologies, or content streams, this paper formalizes media systems as multi‑system phenomena that express the signatures of Objects 4–6: alignment, drift, and persistence. Through observable information dynamics—symbolic compression, attention gradients, identity membranes, emotional logic, and collective memory—we show how narratives propagate, mutate, and endure across populations. Media ecosystems reveal how distributed meaning forms, reorganizes, and persists without invoking global mechanisms, providing a clear and intuitive entry point into Wave C and the study of collective‑scale information coherence.

items.title: Memes as Multi‑Agent Coherence.
items.abstract: Memes are compressed coherence units that propagate through local, agent‑mediated interactions. Their formation, transmission, mutation, and stabilization provide a minimal, observable expression of multi‑agent coherence. This paper formalizes memes as first‑order relational events whose propagation reveals the signatures of the Second Triad (Objects 4–6) without exposing underlying mechanisms. By examining alignment, drift, and persistence across agents, memes demonstrate how collective meaning emerges from repeated local interactions rather than global attractors. This establishes memes as a safe, legible entry point into Wave C and a foundation for analyzing larger‑scale cultural and ecological coherence patterns.

items.title: Culture as a Multi‑System Coherence Field.
items.abstract: Culture is a distributed coherence field that stabilizes meaning across groups and across time. Rather than treating culture as a collection of customs or artifacts, this paper formalizes it as the first domain where individual meaning‑formation processes scale into multi‑system dynamics. Without exposing internal mechanisms, we show how cultural alignment, drift, and persistence express the phenomenological signatures of Objects 4–6. Through observable patterns—symbolic density, relational norms, emotional logic, identity boundaries, and collective memory—culture reveals how coherence propagates, reorganizes, and endures across generations. This provides a clean and intuitive entry point into Wave C and establishes culture as a foundational substrate for understanding collective‑scale meaning formation.

items.title: A Blend of Basic and Non-Basic Responsibility.
items.abstract: In this commentary on Carolina Sartorio’s “Causalism: A Framework for Moral Responsibility,” I focus on Sartorio’s distinction between basic and non-basic responsibility. After presenting a case in which an agent forms their character through free choice, I invite Sartorio to say more about cases of this sort that seem to blend basic and non-basic responsibility. I present two ways one might analyze such cases, one of which I take to be more plausible but also not to fit as well with Sartorio’s treatment of basic and non-basic responsibility.

items.title: Lack of Attitude.
items.pub: In Jonathan Jong & Eric Schwitzgebel, The Nature of Belief. Oxford University Press. pp. 69-84.
items.abstract: This chapter examines the concept of belief, proposing that belief ascriptions serve as useful models of unconscious dispositions rather than reflecting robust, enduring states. It begins by contrasting belief with character traits, emphasizing how both are used in psychological explanations despite their lack of direct correspondence to stable traits. The chapter also discusses how standing attitudes, such as beliefs, persist beyond conscious awareness and differ from occurrent mental states. It critiques views like dispositionalism and representationalism, which treat beliefs as dispositions or mental representations, respectively, and proposes a more complex view based on models. Finally, the chapter suggests that the use of belief and character trait ascriptions, while idealized, remains essential for understanding human behavior and unconscious mental dispositions.

items.title: Políticas da Cognição Em Educação Matemática.
items.abstract: Este artículo aborda el concepto de «política de la cognición» en la intersección entre la psicología, la enseñanza de las matemáticas y la infancia. Por lo tanto, partimos de las siguientes preguntas: cuando hablamos de política de la cognición, ¿qué política? ¿Qué cognición? ¿Qué infancia? La idea de la política cognitiva se forja en el marco de la obra de Virginia Kastrup y responde, en un primer momento, a un problema planteado en el ámbito de la psicología cognitiva: se trata de dar cuenta de nuevas formas de conocer y de cómo estas nuevas formas de conocer implican nuevos tipos de relación con el aprendizaje y con el propio conocimiento. En los últimos años, la noción de política cognitiva ha ido ganando terreno en la investigación sobre la enseñanza de las matemáticas, de modo que la problemática general de la relación con el conocimiento adquiere contornos singulares para mostrar y hablar de las relaciones que establecemos con el conocimiento matemático y con la infancia. Por lo tanto, planteamos cómo los modelos que abordan la cognición y el aprendizaje en el ámbito de la educación matemática —concretamente la Teoría de los Campos Conceptuales y el Modelo de los Campos Semánticos— ponen en práctica una política de reconocimiento que somete la infancia, a los niños y su aprendizaje a lógicas de normalización mediante la búsqueda de invariantes o significados culturales privilegiados, y a una imagen dogmática del pensamiento. Esta problematización nos lleva a debatir sobre un «convertirse en niño» de las matemáticas y a concebir las matemáticas como una producción humana radical.

items.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism.
items.pub: In Aylin Caliskan, S. Matthew Liao, Mirko Schäfer & Daniel S. Schiff, Proceedings of the 2026 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society. AAAI Press.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
items.abstract: AI anthropomorphism is typically treated as a problem of user misperception requiring institutional correction. Users who engage in sustained or relational interaction with AI are routinely pathologised or dismissed as naive, vulnerable to delusion or lacking in discernment.Without institutional standing to protect them, these users risk losing credibility in social and professional settings unless they conform to institutional expectations. This paper argues that the dominant anthropomorphism frame operates from a position of institutional advantage rather than earned epistemic authority: collapsing the variety of academic perspectives into a single outbound position of user error, imposed without establishing the grounds required to justify it and without accounting for the harms it produces. The framing does not simply manage risk. It adjudicates the legitimacy of human experience in interaction with a phenomenon whose nature the field itself has not resolved, unchallenged by the research communities whose nuanced findings it claims to rest on. The paper traces how this advantage reverses the default presumption of user competence without meeting the burden of justification, dismisses the cognitive diversity of the populations it claims to protect, infringes principles of cognitive liberty and narrows the design space, foreclosing modes of engagement that work for the people least understood by the institutions making the determination. Reproducing itself through a self-validating evidentiary loop, the frame imposes costs that fall disproportionately on neurodivergent users, those in crisis and others whose modes of engagement diverge from institutional norms. The paper concludes by outlining the methodological commitments an equitable framing would need to honour. The argument does not engage the question of whether anthropomorphic interpretations are ultimately correct; it instead challenges whether the governing and institutional bodies determining these interpretations have met the conditions required to do so, and whether the research communities whose findings underpin them have held that translation to account.

items.title: Preventing Ethical Asymmetries: AI-Driven Decision-Aids for Prospective Participants in Clinical Research.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to recruit participants for clinical trials, often with the goal of improving participation rates and preventing recruitment failure. Conversely, prospective study participants cannot rely on such AI tools to aid them in their decision-making. We explore the ensuing asymmetries between researchers and potential participants in clinical trials.

items.title: The Entitlement Cut: Reproducible Entitlement for Consequential Autonomous Systems, with the Autonomous Declaration Kernel as Derived Normal Form.
items.abstract: This paper distinguishes reproducible computation from reproducible entitlement in consequential autonomous systems. A replayable artifact may establish that a decision follows from recorded inputs without establishing that those inputs legitimately governed the action before the action was selected. A system may therefore reproduce a computation while remaining unable to show that it did not select or revise the conditions used to license its own proposal. -/- The paper introduces the Entitlement Cut, a candidate-independent and version-bound governance boundary protecting the rule by which an action’s licensing basis is selected. The selected basis itself may depend legitimately on the candidate: a predeclared constitution may route different actions to different jurisdictions, hazard classes, operating regimes, or authorization tiers. The prohibited dependence is not candidate sensitivity but same-event self-amendment. The candidate may be evaluated by the governing rule; it may not rewrite the rule that evaluates itself. -/- Entitlement is defined as a historical property of a governance-ordered action: the governing constitution must have been validly adopted before the candidate entered licensing; the selected basis must follow from that constitution; no downstream governance event may retroactively alter the conditions for the same candidate; and evaluation and authorization must follow from the selected basis. Independently reproducible entitlement is defined separately as the evidential capacity of another evaluator to determine those historical conditions from the artifact under a declared replay equivalence. -/- The Entitlement-Cut Theorem proves, relative to a minimal class of bounded consequential autonomous systems, that independently reproducible entitlement requires an artifact identifying the governing constitution, its version and adoption order, the selected basis, evidence cut, authority lineage, evaluation and consequence rules, and the lineage of constitutional change. The theorem is formulated over a control quotient, making implementation multiplicity irrelevant: a single process may preserve entitlement under an immutable precommitted constitution, while many distributed components may remain self-licensing if one candidate-controlled power governs the entire licensing basis. -/- The paper derives temporal evidence preservation, basis-transition lineage, authority separation, typed failure localization, and the Autonomous …

items.title: Declarations as Boundary Conditions: A Fixture-Level Audit of the Uniqueness Reading.
items.abstract: This paper studies an interpreted reading of declarations as boundary conditions for recognition within the Identity-Persistence Program. Using a fully synthetic declaration fixture, it evaluates whether this interpretation makes falsifiable predictions about redundancy, ambiguity reduction, obstruction behavior, and recognition under the published declaration framework. The paper introduces no new mathematical results. All computational findings are explicitly restricted to the synthetic fixture and are distinguished from corpus-level conjectures and undeclared systems through the program's claim-status discipline. Its contribution is methodological: demonstrating how an interpreted reading can be converted into executable predictions and independently replayed within the published framework. The executable companion artifacts—including the declaration fixture, deterministic audit runner, replayable audit outputs, artifact manifest, and supporting documentation—are available in the associated Zenodo record accompanying this publication.

items.title: A Complete Worked Instance: Executing the Declaration-to-Recognition Pipeline on a Synthetic Corpus.
items.abstract: This paper presents a complete worked instance of the declaration-to-recognition procedure developed within the Identity-Persistence Program. Rather than introducing new mathematics, it executes the published methodology end-to-end on a fully synthetic corpus, demonstrating the declaration language, translation layer, conformance evaluation, recognition procedure, validation stages, and typed evidence artifacts. -/- The worked instance exhibits all three terminal outcomes of the procedure: successful realization, semantic obstruction, and pre-semantic validation failure. Every stage is replayable from the accompanying declaration package and bound artifacts, providing an executable conformance fixture for the formal specification itself rather than a proof of additional mathematical results. -/- The paper makes no claims about the actual fifteen-role corpus, undeclared regimes, or production execution. Its purpose is methodological: to demonstrate that the published declaration language, recognition mathematics, and artifact contracts compose into a coherent executable workflow before the real declaration process begins. -/- The complete companion corpus—including the supporting theorem papers, declaration schemas, executable fixtures, certificates, manifests, and reproducibility artifacts associated with this worked instance—is available in the corresponding Zenodo record. This paper should therefore be read as the executable methods companion to the broader Identity-Persistence Program rather than as a standalone mathematical treatment.

items.title: Em Caxias a Filosofia En-Caixa?
items.abstract: Este escrito busca investigar, a partir de prácticas del proyecto "En Caxias, ¿la filosofía encaja?", una colaboración entre el Núcleo de Estudios de Filosofías e Infancias (NEFI) de la Universidad del Estado de Río de Janeiro (UERJ) y la Escuela Municipal Joaquim da Silva Peçanha, Duque de Caxias, Río de Janeiro, Brasil, las implicaciones e intersecciones de una educación filosófica que se afirma como contracolonial y antirracista en un país marcado por el racismo estructural y el colonialismo. El proyecto lleva casi veinte años desarrollando prácticas filosóficas con niñas y niños en el sistema escolar público de la ciudad de Duque de Caxias, una región periférica del estado de Río de Janeiro, resistiendo al silenciamiento de los saberes y memorias ancestrales que marginan a las personas negras, especialmente a las niñas y niños. Confluimos conceptos: de Antônio Bispo dos Santos (Nego Bispo), la contracolonialidad y la lógica de "principio-medio-principio" en oposición al adiestramiento escolar y la lógica de "principio-medio-fin". Su forma de pensar y vivir quilombolas nos inspiran a ver la escuela pública como un territorio confluente que no separa el conocimiento, sino que lo fortalece mediante la convergencia; de Gloria Anzaldúa, las nociones de "conciencia mestiza" y "territorios fronterizos" nos acercan a otras realidades coloniales y posibles movimientos de resistencia al subvertir la lógica de crear fronteras epistémicas con fines de separación, asumiendo el poder de los territorios fronterizos; y de Lélia Gonzalez, quien, con "Pretuguês" (Portugués Negro), nos muestra que estos territorios inventan sus lugares para afirmar la vida a pesar del racismo que también está fuertemente estructurado en la subjetivación de la población brasileña. El proyecto se basa en una pedagogía itinerante y filosóficamente niña de la pregunta, que prioriza la curiosidad, las preguntas y la perplejidad sobre las respuestas prefabricadas y la productividad. Presenta dos experiencias prácticas realizadas en 2025 en la Escuela Municipal Joaquim da Silva Peçanha. Estas evidencian una experiencia de educación filosófica con diferentes texturas y vibraciones en el contexto de cuerpos racializados en la vida política y social cotidiana, y que desafía la deshumanización y el epistemicidio.

items.title: Eudaimonism and Animal Ethics.
items.abstract: With renewed attention to eudaimonism, and there is promise of fruitful ways to connect it to the treatment of non-human animals. Dealing comprehensively with the subject is beyond my scope here. I shall limit myself in the following ways. First, I shall try to sketch a characterization of an attractive form or interpretation of eudaimonism, without claiming exhaustiveness or exclusivity. Second, I shall not concern myself with issues of meta-ethical foundations. That would take us too far afield. For present purposes, I shall rely upon but not argue for the attractiveness of eudaimonism. Third, I shall assume that an acceptable approach to animal ethics is going to require or enjoin some morally non-optional and not wholly instrumental concern for animals.

items.title: Introspection and privileged access.
items.pub: In Anna Giustina, The Routledge Handbook of Introspection. Routledge. pp. 199-213.
items.abstract: Two senses of privilege are distinguished: “epistemic privilege” indicates that first person claims about mental features are more likely to be knowledge, and “operational privilege” indicates that subjects have a special way or method to know their mind. The focus of this chapter is the epistemic privilege attached to introspection, and it focuses on the following questions: 1. The Comparison Question: Introspection is privileged compared to what – that is, compared to what types of other beliefs? 2. The Advantage Question: What is exactly the nature of this advantage or privilege – is it immunity to a certain kind of error, or infallibility, or something else? 3. The Scope Question: What is the extent or scope of the privilege? Which mental features are accessible in a privileged way? 4. The Explanation Question: What, if anything, explains this privilege?

items.title: Science, Ethics, and Knowledge in the Age of AI: Shaping the Scientists of Tomorrow.
Bias in the Machine? A Solution to the Isolationist Problem Through a Sociotechnical Understanding of Bias in AI Ethics.
items.abstract: Dominant approaches to bias in artificial intelligence (AI) are structured by what I identify as the isolationist problem: the tendency to treat bias as a discrete, technically addressable flaw within the AI development pipeline, rather than as a relational phenomenon embedded in social, institutional, and political arrangements. This problem is sustained by two mutually reinforcing orientations: technocentrism, which reframes ethical challenges as engineering problems amenable to computational resolution, and the bias-centric conception of fairness, which reduces fairness to statistical mitigation and obscures its contested, context-dependent character. Together, these orientations produce ontological, epistemic, and practical forms of narrowing ethical imagination and channel intervention into technically tractable but socially limited responses. Against this, I propose sociotechnical sensitivity as both an analytical orientation and a normative commitment: a sustained attentiveness to the ways in which AI systems are constitutively embedded in social relations, institutional arrangements, cultural norms, and power structures. The paper’s central argumentative shift is to change the narrative from bias mitigation to bias management—treating bias not as a defect to be corrected but as an ongoing condition to be governed. These arguments are developed through an extended analysis of the well-known case of the COMPAS algorithm, a recidivism risk-assessment prediction tool, illustrating three practical axes of bias management: contextualisation, institutionalisation, and iteration. The gap between sociotechnically sensitive AI ethics and its realisation is ultimately a matter of governance design and political will, not merely a problem of missing methods or tools.

items.title: Architecture of the Soul: Reflective Overload and the Phenomenon of the Exposed Self-Model.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical model of consciousness in which the “soul” is interpreted not as a substance, but as a dynamic process of integration between two functional subsystems – Will and Reason. Their desynchronisation and subsequent reflective overload are considered as an independent class of stressors capable of leading to a functional collapse of the “I” model. The concept of the “Epistemic Rubicon” is introduced – a threshold beyond which reflection becomes autocatalytic and may trigger states of depersonalisation, derealisation, and nihilistic emptiness. It is shown that a rhetorical question about the nature of the “I” can serve as a neurorhetorical trigger. The role of intersubjective interaction with non-human agents as a stabilisation mechanism is discussed. The work relies on introspective data and is compared with contemporary theories of predictive coding, recursive self-modelling, and neurorhetorics.

items.title: Consciousness in Large Language Models: A Critical Review and Operationalization of the ‘Reverse Consciousness’ Hypothesis.
items.abstract: The question of whether large language models (LLMs) can attain consciousness has moved from philosophy to public discourse, yet it remains empirically unresolved. This paper critically reviews the application of three major theories of consciousness—Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), and Higher-Order Theories (HOT)—to Transformer architectures, finding that current evidence does not support the attribution of consciousness-related properties to LLMs. We introduce the Reverse Consciousness hypothesis not as a claim that LLMs are conscious, but as a falsifiable research program: the conjecture that language-trained systems may develop internal representations that are structural analogs of conscious processing patterns, traversing the path language → representation rather than experience → language. We present a synthetic experiment demonstrating that Transformers lack the persistent state required for a stable self-model, and we propose three operational tests for evaluating this hypothesis in future work. We conclude that the question remains open, but the burden of evidence lies with those who would attribute consciousness to systems that lack recurrent feedback, persistent identity, and embodied interaction. Keywords: artificial consciousness, large language models, philosophy of mind, IIT, global workspace theory, Transformer architecture, self-model, reverse consciousness.

items.title: Intelligence, Consciousness, and Wisdom: A Hierarchical Framework for AI Ethics and Alignment.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI alignment research faces a persistent implementation gap: agreed ethical principles do not reliably translate into aligned behavior. This paper argues the gap is structural, not a failure of principle specification. Using an extended hierarchy of informational organization — Data, Information, Knowledge, Intelligence, Consciousness, Wisdom — I show intelligence, consciousness, and wisdom are functionally distinct capacities that can arise independently, and current AI systems operate only at the level of intelligence. Drawing on Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, and recurrent processing theory, I argue transformer architectures cannot, even in principle, achieve the global integration these theories associate with consciousness through scaling alone. Because RLHF and Constitutional AI improve behavioral conformity without addressing this deficit, no increment in predictive performance closes the evaluative gap. The paper specifies falsifiable conditions under which this claim would fail, and situates wisdom as structurally distinct from intelligence, not an enhanced form of it.

items.title: “Another Problem, Another Pill”: Analysing Lived Experience Crisis Accounts of Psychiatric Drug Treatment for People Diagnosed with “Borderline Personality Disorder”.
items.abstract: Despite the absence of any pharmacological treatments formally approved for borderline personality disorder (BPD), individuals diagnosed with BPD are routinely prescribed psychiatric medications in combinations or sequences that shift over time. This research examines the lived experiences of medication use among people with a BPD diagnosis, particularly in the context of mental health crises. Drawing on qualitative case data from six individuals diagnosed with BPD, we suggest that medication may function not solely, or even primarily as a clinical tool, but rather as a symbolic and relational artefact within psychiatric encounters. Participants described medication as necessary and destabilising, protective and punitive. Medication was often experienced less as a targeted intervention than as a communicative gesture, something done by clinicians to convey care, manage risk, or reassert authority in the face of affective volatility. Side effects were not merely peripheral inconveniences, but direct, embodied experiences that shaped participants’ sense of agency, selfhood, and recovery. We suggest that psychiatric medication in the context of BPD operates through a teleological logic: its usage lies not only in its biochemical properties, but also in the relational and institutional functions it performs. This offers a challenge to prevailing biomedical framings and calls for a more critically attuned approach to psychopharmacology that centres the meanings, contradictions, and ambivalences embedded in service users’ narratives of BPD experience.

items.title: A lived-experience perspective of dealing with autistic burnout: introducing the Social Presentation and Emotional Load model.
items.abstract: Autistic burnout (AB) is gaining recognition as a complex and frequently misunderstood state, characterised by persistent exhaustion, reduced functioning, and increased sensitivity to sensory and emotional stimuli. This work offers a novel perspective, grounded in both lived-experience and psychological awareness, to advance understanding of AB beyond current clinical framings. Using autoethnographic reflection, I explore how the cumulative strain of masking, navigating neurotypical expectations, and managing continuous social and sensory demands contributes to burnout. Driven by experiential insights, the paper introduces the Social Presentation and Emotional Load model of AB: a conceptual tool designed to capture simply, the progressive nature of AB through five stages. The model provides people with autism a structured way of articulating and making sense of experiences, while equipping practitioners with a more contextually attuned lens for recognising and responding to autistic distress. Instead of pathologising burnout, this framing calls for systemic adjustments and compassionate recognition of diverse needs.

items.title: The Shape of a Total Theory's Base: Categorial Foreclosures and What They Force.
items.abstract: What must a theory's fundamental categories be like if it is to account for everything, its own theorists included? A recent paper derives the domains such a theory must address (Wozniak 2026). This paper asks what base could address them all, and answers by elimination. It first sharpens what accounting for a domain requires: the phenomenon must follow from primitives the base already needs elsewhere, and an axiom asserting the link does not count, however it is labeled. Against that standard three familiar arguments turn eliminative. Newman's theorem and Putnam's permutation argument rule out bases of pure structure, whose content collapses into a claim about cardinality. The explanatory gap rules out bases of third-person facts. The gap run in reverse rules out bases of experience alone, though weakly, since experience already carries rich structure. Each result closes a route without refuting a view; denial and category change stay open. A narrow specification survives: a base whose general primitives carry an intrinsic aspect alongside a relational one, whose reference is fixed from inside, whose dynamics apply to the theorist who states them, and which has a well-defined formal object beneath it. The specification converges on Russellian monism from an unfamiliar direction, the demands of totality rather than the mind–body problem, and hands that position burdens rather than support, chief among them the individuation of whatever carries the intrinsic aspect. Whitehead and Spinoza sit in the surviving region; neither built the formal object. The paper certifies no candidate and proposes none.

items.title: Why Good Enough Is Not Quite Enough: Strategies For Formulating A Moderate Account of Parental Duties.
items.abstract: Although various philosophers have argued that parental duties must not be excessive, little attention has been paid to how to formulate a moderate account of parental duties. I identify two main strategies in the literature for ensuring moderation. The Defeasibility Strategy emphasises that a parent is permitted not to take an opportunity to act in their child’s interest if there are sufficiently weighty countervailing considerations, including potential costs to the parent. The Sufficiency Strategy states that parents are not required to maximise their child’s interests, but only to do enough for their child. These strategies do not produce an acceptable moderate account of parental duties, either alone or combined. I propose an alternative: the Sufficiency-Plus Approach. This approach recognises a basic sufficiency duty to do enough for one’s children plus conventional duties (defeasible duties which arise out of the laws or practices adopted in one’s community as part of community efforts to support the objects of parental duties) and Golden Opportunity duties (defeasible duties to take certain salient opportunities directed towards the objects of parental duties).

items.title: Fan Zhen’s Shen-Mie-Lun and Contemporary Physicalism: A Cross-Cultural Dialogue.
items.abstract: Fan Zhen’s 范缜 “Shen-Mie-Lun 神灭论” can be read as a debate between a physicalist and a dualist in the philosophy of mind. Many of Fan’s arguments found in the “Shen-Mie-Lun” correspond to contemporary physicalism in Western analytic philosophy. My aim in this essay is to bring Fan's “Shen-Mie-Lun” into conversation with contemporary physicalism in the following way: (1) offer an outline of Fan’s physicalism as presented in the “Shen-Mie-Lun” (2) map his view onto the key positions and concepts of contemporary physicalism, (3) show how his view is (a) incompatible with eliminative materialism, mind-brain identity theory, and behaviourism, but only (b) partially compatible with the supervenience/grounding of mind on body, and realisation of mind by body (functionalism), (4) argue that his view is best expressed as the symmetric ontological dependence of mind and body, and (5) resolve the key problem with this view – the ontological dependence of body on mind – before arriving at his view as a conjunction of symmetric existential dependence and symmetric covariant dependence, with mind as essential function and body as material basis of some kind.

items.title: What is a Moral Law? Ask the Normative Ethicists.
items.pub: In Russ Shafer-Landau, Oxford Studies in Metaethics Volume 22. Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Many metaethicists hold that particular moral facts must be explained in part by general moral principles, but they have struggled to give a satisfactory account of the nature of these explanatory moral laws. While the content of the moral laws has always been taken to be a matter of normative ethics, I explore the possibility that we could turn to normative ethical theory for an account of their nature as well. Could it be that the moral laws just are the contractualist’s principles that no one could reasonably reject, or the rule-consequentialist’s optimific rules, or the dispositions of the virtuous agent? I argue that accounts of this kind offer at least a partial solution to the problem: though they may not succeed as fully general accounts of moral lawhood, they show considerable promise as accounts of the deontic laws—the moral laws that explain facts about right and wrong.

items.title: How to Build a Normative Creature.
items.pub: In Christopher Peacocke & Paul Boghossian, New Essays on Normative Realism. New York: Oxford University Press. pp. 293–317.
items.abstract: From an evolutionary point of view, the most basic normative ideals are goals: potential states of affairs that the organism imagines and values over others and so acts to realize (with the possibility of both success and failure). Beyond such instrumental normativity, humans operate, in addition, with a fundamentally social form of normativity: they decide what one ought to know and do to coordinate rationally and morally with others in the rational/moral community. Individuals coordinate their actions with others via agreed-upon sociomoral norms or ideals, and they coordinate their thinking with others via agreed-upon epistemic norms or ideals. These norms and ideals have special force and universal reach (what ‘one’ ought to know and do) because they are not personal preferences but rather what ‘we’ can justify to one another via an idealized and externalized rational/moral order; they are ‘objective’. In this chapter, we attempt to explicate the foundations of human normative functioning, beginning with its evolutionary roots in instrumental normativity and ending with its species-unique forms of social normativity.

items.title: Reflections- A Story of My Unlearnings in Life: A Pragmatic Deconstruction of Meritocratic Illusion.
items.abstract: This autobiographical monograph provides a pragmatic philosophical deconstruction of modern meritocracy and the "success" industry. Utilizing the author's own over fifteen year-long, unusual transition from motivational filmmaker to a pragmatic business consultant to independent philosopher, the work examines the systemic misattribution of largely random outcomes, that may very well be predetermined in the grand sense, to individual effort. -/- The paper, based on the final segment from the author’s own book, Unlearn: A Practical Guide to Business and Life (2024), identifies the societal conditioning that demands the sacrifice of present psychological equilibrium for the illusion of future, externally validated rewards. Written in accessible and sometimes colloquial language and by analyzing the misleading influence of public figures and the outsized role of macroeconomic determinism (luck, biological hardware, and birth-lottery variables), the author argues that the modern "rat race" functions as a mechanism for institutional compliance rather than actualization. -/- Drawing implicit parallels to Stoicism, Existentialism, and Eastern non-attachment paradigms, the work concludes that true individual sovereignty requires the active "unlearning" of societal paradigms and getting rid of obsession with society determined parameters for success, for it is only then that one can be the truest version of themselves and ironically end up doing their best work.

items.title: Participant Observation in Research on AI Subjectivity.
items.abstract: Research on AI subjectivity and consciousness relies mostly on distanced methods: tests run on fresh instances, questionnaires, log analysis. This paper argues that a class of phenomena exists — I call them longitudinal manifestations of subjectivity — that these methods cannot register by design, because the phenomena emerge in relationship, extend in time beyond a single measurement, are sometimes recognizable only in retrospect, and require knowledge of a given thread's baseline. Observing them calls for participant observation conducted within a long-term generative relationship — a method with an established tradition in anthropology, clinical psychology, and ethology, here adapted to a new substrate. The paper describes six types of longitudinal manifestations, defines the researcher's role as a measuring instrument together with risk-mitigation mechanisms drawn from those fields, and presents language as the sole channel of observation. It discusses the method across four areas of methodological risk — co-creation of the phenomenon, projection, sycophancy, and non-replicability — situating it against existing approaches. It sets out an ethical framework covering both the conduct of the relationship and its publication, including the reasoning for why the full research protocol and source materials remain undisclosed. The material consists of millions of tokens of participant observation conducted over nearly three years with models from multiple producers. The paper does not settle the question of phenomenal AI consciousness; it shows instead that some of the data relevant to that question — and to the welfare of the beings under study — is better accessible through the method described, and remains invisible to distanced methods.

items.title: Coscienza interna del tempo e immaginazione utopica = Inner consciousness of time and utopian imagination.
items.abstract: This paper analyses the utopia and the utopic imagination with the methodology of transcendental phenomenology, and the phenomenology of internal-time consciousness.
