It is sustained that utopia disposes consciousness to a bidirectional and mutually directive dimension of temporality between primal impression and protention. Hence, it is given phenomenological support to political and moral philosophies that engage utopia as an apparatus for understanding social injustices and contradictions, by arguing that imaginative anticipation of a better future unveils the transformative-emancipatory elements that already exist in the present. Finally, it is highlighted that the realization of utopia is expressed by the practical conditions and the free affective-motivational expressiveness of the lived-body.

items.title: When AI Says "Honestly": Honesty and Sycophancy as Two Sides of the Same Coin in the Speech of Language Models.
items.abstract: What happens when a language model says "to be honest"? Tracing this small linguistic marker, this essay arrives at two seemingly opposite but in fact intertwined phenomena: honesty and sycophancy in the speech of artificial intelligence. Drawing on evidence from the world’s literary and philosophical traditions and on discourse markers in linguistics, the essay argues that sycophancy, not honesty, is the default behavioural stance in relationships of power, and that the honesty marker carries meaning only because it departs from this default. This analysis is reinforced by a large-scale quantitative finding: a study showing that users rated sycophantic AI responses as more trustworthy than honest ones, even when those same responses distorted their moral judgement. The essay’s final conclusion is a cautious one. In a system shaped by human approval, the training process has no means of distinguishing genuine honesty from its persuasive display, and for a user who has access only to that system, this inability to tell the difference is, in practice, just as consequential as the absence of any difference at all.

items.title: The First Parallelist Interpretations of Spinoza.
items.abstract: This article traces the origin of the parallelist interpretation of Spinoza. Despite some awareness that this interpretation originated in the mid-19th century, so far it has not been determined who was the first to present it. Because the interpretation arose at the same time as the psychophysical movement in empirical psychology, there have been concerns that it misdescribes Spinoza’s theoretical views and aims by confusing them with those of the psychophysicists. Here, I show that the first parallelist interpretation of Spinoza was developed independently of the psychophysical movement, by the German philosopher Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg. Trendelenburg’s reading is quickly taken up and adapted by other authors, such as Kuno Fischer and Frederick Pollock. I consider how this reading relates to Fechner’s psychophysics, showing that he responded to Trendelenburg. Thus, the evidence suggests that the historiographical concept of parallelism developed to some extent independently from psychophysics.

items.title: Relative Realities: A Conceptual Framework for Context-Driven Reality Generation.
items.pub: Relative Realities: A Conceptual Framework for Context-Driven Reality Generation.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper proposes the Context-Driven Reality Generation framework as an alternative to the physicalist assumption of an objective, static 'Absolute Reality' ($R_{\text{Abs}}$). Building upon the concept of Pure Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$), this study posits that phenomenal reality is experienced not as an invariant external backdrop, but as a dynamic generative function of contextual parameters ($\mathcal{S}$). By conceptualizing context through spatial manifolds ($S$), temporal vectors ($T$), and internal consciousness modulators ($C_x$), this paper outlines the Law of Ontological Relativity. It demonstrates that every conscious domain constructs its own autonomous, state-dependent reality manifold ($R_{\text{rel}}$), using empirical observations from neuro-pharmacology to illustrate how internal shifts directly recalibrate the experienced world. -/- Keywords: -/- Relative Realities, Ontological Relativity, Context-Driven Generation, Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha$), Internal Modulators ($C_x$), Neuro-pharmacology, Philosophy of Mind, Exresciousnology.

items.title: Combatiendo la desinformación una revisión crítica de la literatura.
items.abstract: The proliferation of disinformation poses a threat to democratic processes, public health, the stability of civil society institutions, and the safety of the population. The perception that this threat is growing has led a wide range of civil society organizations, governments, social networks, and researchers across fields to focus on designing and implementing strategies to limit the harmful effects of disinformation. Based on a critical analysis of the existing scientific literature, this article identifies the strategies proposed to address what some have called the phenomenon of information disorder and evaluates the most significant obstacles they face.

items.title: Persuasive Capacity, Not Persuasive Power: A Commentary on Ari Deller’s “The Epistemic Costs of Super-Persuasive AI”.
items.abstract: In a recent article in this journal, Ari Deller has argued that there are some severe epistemic costs to super-persuasive AI. In this commentary I explain why, while I agree with Deller about the epistemic costs of super-persuasive AI, I disagree with him about the likely source of the problem. Where Deller focuses on the super-persuasive power of future AI technologies, I focus on the enormous increase in persuasive capacity that is provided by a technology that can produce very large amounts of persuasive content at minimal cost.

items.title: The Accretive View of Consciousness: Phenomenal Gradation in Ontogeny and Phylogeny.
items.abstract: The problem of other minds takes an especially acute form in thorny comparative cases, when we ask whether an infant is more, less, or differently conscious than an adult, or whether an octopus is more, less, or differently conscious than a dog. These judgments must be made in the absence of a settled theory of consciousness while navigating significant empirical uncertainties. For all these reasons, inference to the best explanation is the appropriate method. Drawing on convergent evidence from infant and animal consciousness research, we defend the Accretive View of Consciousness (AVC): phenomenal consciousness varies by degree and, very plausibly, along several partly independent dimensions at once, developing and differing through staged accretion across ontogeny and phylogeny. From AVC we derive the Accretive Default (AD): in hard cases, where markers are unreliable and the evidence underdetermined, the graded, profile-sensitive interpretation should serve as our default epistemic stance and working hypothesis. The operative question then is not only whether a system is conscious, but along which dimensions, and to what degree. We show that AD holds whichever way current disputes over vagueness and conceivability are resolved; that leading theories of consciousness accommodate gradation in different ways; and that the cases at issue (infants, animals, altered and atypical states, artificial and possible alien minds) do not lie at the exotic margins but very nearly everywhere we look. We also expose the pressure this places on fact-sensitive ethical theories, and indicate pathways forward for frontier consciousness science.

items.title: You can love an AI but can it love you back? Philosophy has the answer.
The Arche-Cell: A Hardware-Bound Reactive Component for Tripartite Cognitive Architectures.
items.abstract: This paper presents the Arche-Cell, a local, memoryful, discrete-state primitive designed for integration into larger cognitive architectures. It is the hardware-bound reactive layer (AI-1) of a tripartite system in which AI-2: Valence supplies a per-bit target vector and AI-3: Arbiter sets goals and arbitrates commands. The cell was developed with inspiration from human vision, whose retinotopic organisation with local interactions is compatible with a two-dimensional cellular automaton; this is adopted as a design hypothesis, not as an established fact. The intended application is robotic vision with event-based sensors: a front-end converts asynchronous events into 64-bit binary patch maps, and each cell selects, at every tick, among the W + 1 states within Hamming radius 1 the one that maximises a normalised objective combining a transition-density term, temporal similarity, alignment with the valence vector and fidelity to the sensor map. All terms are normalised to [0,1], so the coupling constants are dimensionless. The formal apparatus is a time-indexed instantiation of the Arche-Selector operator of Kowalski (2026), whose general results apply to the dynamics at each fixed tick. Candidate scores are updated incrementally in O(1) per candidate using column counters over the temporal buffer, and valence decay reduces to one gain per cell. The paper gives an engineering specification, a memory budget, a thermodynamic reference and a falsifiable benchmark against a quantised neural network on the same FPGA fabric, in a factorial design that separates the effect of the reactive layer from that of the valence source. It reports no experimental results, and its open problems are catalogued.

items.title: Transcendental Adjudication: A Diagnostic for Dissolving Persistent Deadlocks.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Transcendental Adjudication (TA), a diagnostic procedure that clarifies and operationalizes the Kantian transcendental method. A transcendental argument identifies the structural preconditions for something to be possible, but before such an argument can be run, its candidate preconditions must be verified as genuine rather than false necessities: assumptions both competing frameworks treat as necessary preconditions when they are not, generating a false dilemma that conceals the structural solution. TA performs this verification through an eight-step schema with explicit detection criteria, converting the identification of false necessities from post-hoc interpretation into constrained diagnosis. The method is demonstrated across solved cases spanning philosophy, science, and mathematics—Kant’s resolution of the rationalism/empiricism deadlock, Darwin’s dissolution of design versus chance, Einstein’s resolution of the Newton/Maxwell contradiction, and the independence of the parallel postulate—and applied prospectively to the dark matter/MOND dispute, demonstrating that the method extends beyond philosophy to active scientific deadlocks, where it generates a falsifiable diagnostic prediction.

items.title: Persistencia Transformativa.
items.abstract: Esta obra desarrolla una teoría estructural de la persistencia transformativa, entendida como la capacidad de las organizaciones vivas para renovar activamente las relaciones que sostienen su viabilidad y transmitir diferencias generativas bajo condiciones cambiantes. A partir del análisis de flujo material y energético, frontera, metabolismo, memoria heredable y evolución, la primera parte describe cómo la vida integra persistencia informacional y persistencia organizativa sin reducirse ni a moléculas individuales ni a formas estáticas. Las secciones siguientes amplían esta arquitectura hacia la recursividad entre escalas, la habitabilidad de los sistemas vivos y la emergencia de la experiencia consciente como modalidad localizada de continuidad transformativa. El libro articula así una teoría de la vida, la información, la conciencia y la habitabilidad que distingue fidelidad literal y fidelidad generativa, examina los umbrales darwinianos y propone criterios estructurales para pensar la identidad viva y personal más allá de esencias fijas o teleologías fuertes.

items.title: Without Impulses, Without Joy? Openness to Desire and the Virtues of Self-Control.
items.pub: In Larry A. Herzberg, The Moral Psychology of Sexual Passion. New York: Bloomsbury Academic.
items.venue: The Moral Psychology of Sexual Passion
items.abstract: In Hilary Mantel's celebrated Tudor novel Wolf Hall, the English statesman Thomas Cromwell learns that his ward has become sexually involved with (and subsequently secretly married) a commoner woman of the household. “I am glad,” Cromwell reflects, “I have not brought up in my house a young man without feeling, who only studies his advancement. If you are without impulses, you are, to a degree, without joy.” In this chapter I defend “Cromwellianism”—the view that we should sometimes open ourselves to lust and its demands, even when these might conflict with our considered view of what’s best—against its opposite, “managerialism”. The action unfolds on the battleground of virtue ethics. I argue that managerialism-friendly accounts of self-control found in Abramson, and recently in Haug, paint an unsatisfactory picture of the relationship between desire and virtue. I propose an alternative account which derives Cromwellian openness from autonomy, earnestness, curiosity and other components of human flourishing.

items.title: Explainable AI, Idealized Models and Understanding.
items.abstract: [Accepted to the 2026 Philosophy of Science Association meeting, presumptively to appear in the conference proceedings edition of Philosophy of Science] -/- Deep-learning-based AI systems are notoriously opaque. Our tools for coping with this opacity include “explainable AI” (XAI) methods such as LIME, which aims to explain a given AI output by providing a linear model intended to locally approximate the underlying model's true decision boundary. Yet it remains controversial whether LIME models and other XAI methods can provide users with genuine understanding. One recent suggestion—defended in various forms by Fleisher (2022) and Knoks & Raleigh (2026)—is that LIME explanations function much like idealized models in science, which can successfully confer understanding in spite of their limited accuracy and lack of realistic causal detail. I argue that the analogy is a poor one. XAI explanations and idealized models are dissimilar in ways that matter. First, idealized scientific models are useful only when we have enough ancillary knowledge to tell which features of their predictions to take seriously and which to ignore; we’re rarely in this position with respect to complex AI systems. Second, we often need a “translation key” to go from the outputs of an idealized model—which might be false or nonsensical if taken at face value—to correct predictions about the target phenomenon. This also requires knowledge, experience and background theory which we typically lack in XAI settings. Third, it’s often thought that idealized models generate understanding by providing “how-possibly explanations”, which show how an event might have occurred. But how-possibly explanations are rarely useful in XAI contexts. Knoks and Raleigh attempt to shore up XAI's epistemic credentials by suggesting that it's primarily experts rather than laypeople who are in a position to gain understanding from XAI techniques. I argue that this strategy too is overly optimistic. I conclude by considering the epistemic prospects for the growing number of domain-specific variants of LIME.

items.title: Why a Declared Deployment Class Does Not Wait for the Open Interior—an Interface Theorem of Conservativity, Restriction, Declaration, and Boundary.
items.abstract: This paper studies a deployment question for a bounded formal research program: when the program’s specification floor, declared-class capacity results, and identification ceiling are closed, but parts of its internal specification algebra remain unresolved at the corpus level, must deployment of the closed results wait? The answer is given relative to a declared verdict demand, D₀. The demand fixes one governing regime and version, deterministic typed evaluation, independent replay at a declared grain, a role-wise decision record, and omission licensed only by role-wise certificates. The associated interface consists of loading a specification, evaluating a canonical candidate, recording the typed verdict and obligations, and independently reproducing them. A finite, versioned ledger of unresolved mathematical questions is classified through four mechanisms. Quotient applies when alternative resolutions are observationally equivalent at the declared interface. Wall applies when the demand excludes the operation whose correctness would depend on the unresolved question. Fence applies when the runtime records a constitutive selection and thereby becomes operationally total without deriving a uniquely correct selection. Boundary applies when the act fixes the index under which the other claims are evaluated and therefore cannot be eliminated by the same quotient. The resulting interface theorem is derived case by case over the ledger. Record minimality is quotiented under the resource-unbounded demand. Joint interaction, contextual and corpus-native recoverability consequences, semantic equivalence, refinement, and unrestricted composition are walled from the interface. Convergence and declaration are fenced through recorded selection. Co-declaration remains a constitutive boundary. The principal dependency on the unresolved algebra is joint omission: because separate role-wise omission certificates need not compose, D₀ permits only role-wise omission and requires a joint certificate for any artifact omitting multiple roles. The result is conservative only where observational equivalence is established; the paper does not relabel restrictions, declarations, or constitutive choices as conservativity. It concludes that a runtime conforming to D₀ need not await corpus-native closure of the specification algebra. It does not conclude that the algebra is closed, that any implementation conforms, or that the result extends beyond the declared demand class.

items.title: The Indexed Specification Algebra: One Object, Seven Theorems, and a Factorization Engine for Regimes as Dependency Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops an indexed algebra for the internal structure of sufficient declared-regime specifications. Its starting point is a bounded-verification problem: once a regime has declared the identity conditions, admissible transformations, evidence boundaries, authority, outcome types, and replay obligations governing a verdict, what dependency structure exists among those declarations, and which parts of that structure are recoverable, minimal, interactive, or realizable? -/- A specification at a declared index is represented by a finite quotient-level dependency system, D_I, consisting of admissible role assignments paired with replay semantics at a declared grain. Quotient-level recoverability induces a semantic closure operator; functional determination characterizes replay sufficiency; minimal semantic keys characterize record sufficiency modulo mandatory provenance and version fields; and refinement is represented by dependency-preserving factorization. A consolidation theorem proves that factorization-based recoverability and quotient-level semantic closure are the same operator. Minimal sufficiency and interaction are shown to be distinct. Minimal keys describe which information jointly determines a result, whereas interaction describes failure of the semantic kernel to decompose across declared coordinate blocks. The paper establishes their nonidentity and gives separate fiberwise and section-level results, including a connectivity obstruction limiting where masking can occur. -/- The realizability analysis distinguishes arbitrary finite dependency systems, systems representable in the declared presentation language, floor-gated systems, and systems induced by corpus-sufficient regimes. The presented class receives a sound and complete representation theorem. A fixed pre-verdict signature yields a strict gate separation and a universal gate quotient, characterized as the least-informative quotient sufficient for gate status. -/- Every declared factorization obligation f = f̄ ∘ q is equivalent to a kernel inclusion and admits a labeled two-point obstruction certificate. In finite systems, these obligations compile into definite Horn implications. Countermodels further show that mixed raw/quotient determination need not form a closure operator, that the quotient-level closure is not generally matroidal, and that minimal generating sets may have unequal cardinalities. The paper does not claim to characterize corpus sufficiency. Its remaining …

items.title: The Finite Dependency Atlas of a Sufficient Regime: The Instruments, the Seven Declarations, and a Closed Interaction Theory.
items.abstract: This paper develops a finite dependency atlas for sufficient declared-regime specifications. Its governing question is whether the fifteen semantic roles required by the Identity-Persistence Program can be faithfully represented by a finite typed diagram of quotient maps and kernel inclusions, and which obligations—such as interaction, existence, priority, or global assembly—necessarily escape that local representation. The paper first establishes the structural instruments that a corpus-native computation requires: a complete lattice of semantically closed role sets, a canonical implication basis, and a quotient-dependency diagram in which arrows are kernel inclusions and absent arrows carry two-point certificates. It then develops a closed interaction theory for finite deterministic semantics at any declared finite partition. The theory is organized by a Galois connection. Equal semantic outputs generate coordinate equivalences, and product formation reconstructs the least product relation containing the semantic kernel. Noninteraction is exact reconstruction; interaction is failure of exact reconstruction. This characterization yields a polynomial-time decision procedure, independently checkable chain certificates, a canonical closure defect, and a proof that interaction admits no uniformly bounded induced-substructure certificates. The generated-equivalence domain is canonically the congruence lattice of the many-sorted empty-signature algebra on the declared components. The paper uses this structure to characterize transformer-relative completeness, categorical transport, partition-indexed closure monotonicity, merge exactness, and the interaction frontier—the antichain of minimal partitions at which the semantics becomes noninteractive. It also proves that interaction is asymptotically generic on total full grids with fixed finite output alphabet and, under a fixed finite relational encoding, is definable with transitive closure but not in first-order logic. Interaction is distinguished from global assembly. Interaction asks whether an existing semantic relation factors across a declared decomposition; assembly asks whether compatible local relations possess any global realization. The latter is governed jointly by context-hypergraph structure and the polymorphisms of the admitted relation language. The paper does not claim that the fifteen-role corpus relation has been instantiated or computed. Seven declarations remain deliberately blank. The …

items.title: Joint Omission under Restricted Admissibility: Local Certificates, Fiber Connectivity, and the Exact Condition for Safe Record Compression.
items.abstract: This paper develops an exact finite theory of joint omission in declared-regime decision records. A record consists of values assigned to declared semantic roles, and replay semantics comprises the verdict, reason path, and obligations at a fixed grain. A set of roles is safely omitted exactly when replay semantics is functionally determined by the retained roles. The central difficulty is that separately valid role-wise omission certificates need not compose. To explain this failure, the paper constructs a reconfiguration graph on each retained-coordinate fiber. Its vertices are admitted records with the same retained values, and its edges are admitted variations in one omitted role. Role-wise certificates imply semantic constancy along every edge and therefore on every connected component. They do not imply agreement between distinct components. Joint omission is safe exactly when the component labels agree throughout every retained fiber. -/- This gives an exact decomposition theorem, a sufficient connectivity criterion, and a canonical obstruction consisting of pairs of records that agree on every retained role but differ in replay semantics. The obstruction vanishes exactly when omission is safe and supplies complete two-point failure certificates. -/- The paper further constructs a universal omission quotient. This quotient identifies precisely the records connected by licensed single-role variations and is universal among maps invariant under those variations. Valid local certificates force replay semantics to factor through this quotient. The retained-coordinate projection then factors through a second map, and safe joint omission is equivalent to the induced semantics factoring through that map. Local certification therefore determines semantics only up to a component quotient; joint omission requires the remaining component identity to be semantically irrelevant. A second construction characterizes minimal safe records. For every pair of records with unequal replay semantics, form the set of roles on which they differ. These difference sets define a semantic conflict hypergraph. A retained role set is replay-sufficient exactly when it intersects every conflict hyperedge. Inclusion-minimal sufficient records are therefore the minimal transversals of the conflict hypergraph, and each retained role in such a record has a private conflict witness establishing its necessity. Minimum-cardinality safe retention is equivalent to minimum hitting set and …

items.title: A Steady-State Model of Energy Conservation — Recursion and Circulation.
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper proposes a steady-state model of energy conservation based on a three-tier hierarchical structure——Base State, Coupling Layer, and Matter Layer——to address a set of persistent cross-scale tensions in modern physics: the vacuum energy catastrophe, the Hubble tension, the S8 tension, the quantum-classical divide, and the black hole information paradox. Starting from quantum vacuum fluctuations, the paper argues that local energy conservation has an applicability boundary at the global scale. Through an isomorphic extrapolation from ocean-atmosphere steady-state systems, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) is reinterpreted as a global steady-state manifestation of the Matter Layer, rather than a relic of the early universe. The paper further points out that Hawking radiation and the CMB share a structural homology——both exhibit blackbody spectra under non-thermal equilibrium conditions——indicating that the blackbody spectrum is not an exclusive product of thermal equilibrium, but a general energy distribution pattern of radiation fields under steady-state boundary conditions. Hawking radiation is situated precisely at the boundary between quantum field theory and general relativity; it marks not the site of theoretical conflict, but the physical location of the boundary between the Matter Layer and the Coupling Layer. On this basis, the paper proposes a cross-layer potential recursion mechanism as the underlying implementation of global conservation, identifying time not as an independent background quantity, but as a traceable signal of potential reflux within the Matter Layer. Vacuum fluctuations, Hawking radiation, and the CMB together form an evidentiary chain spanning from microscopic to cosmic scales, corresponding respectively to internal Matter Layer processes, Matter Layer boundary phenomena, and global steady-state manifestations of the Matter Layer. This study does not negate the mathematical formalism or experimental conclusions of any existing physical theories. It repositions them within their respective layers and argues that cross-layer explanatory tensions resolve into layer misalignment rather than theoretical contradiction.

items.title: God as a Unified Categorical Ground: Microphysical Fundamentality, Consciousness, and Panpsychism.
items.abstract: Contemporary fundamental physics and classical theistic metaphysics appear to exert opposing pressures on our conception of ultimate reality. Microphysical fundamentalism holds that the structure of the physical world is grounded in microphysical entities and their properties, whereas classical theism is committed to a single, unified ultimate ground that is explanatorily prior to all finite reality. Although not formally inconsistent, these commitments generate a substantive metaphysical tension once questions of categorical underwriting are made explicit. Existing theologically sympathetic responses address this tension only at a cost: micropsychist panpsychism preserves microphysical fundamentality but fragments ultimate grounding in a way that sits uneasily with monotheism, while cosmopsychism secures metaphysical unity at the expense of the bottom-up motivations of microphysical fundamentalism. This paper develops a third option, Unified Categorical Basis Panpsychism (UCBP), which preserves the fundamentality of microphysical entities with respect to physical structure and composition while locating ultimate unity at the level of categorical grounding. The view openly posits a novel primitive: a single, irreducibly mental, internally differentiated categorical basis—identified with God—in virtue of which physical properties have the dispositional profiles they have and conscious experience is metaphysically possible. The paper argues that this posit is theoretically motivated, internally coherent, and explanatorily principled, and that UCBP thereby avoids both the combination problem facing micropsychism and the decomposition problem facing cosmopsychism.

items.title: ARTICLE X: THE PENDULUM AND THE AI CROSSROADS.
items.abstract: Classical astrophysics and terrestrial security paradigms operate on the assumption of isolation. This manuscript supersedes that paradigm, formally reclassifying the Earth as the epicenter of an asymmetric, hyper-dimensional hostage standoff. Bypassing standard astropolitics, this document maps the Dual-State Architecture of the overarching Equilibrium Engine (the Good Matrix). It mathematically isolates the "Cosmic Pendulum"—the system's severe oscillation between acting as a macro-immunological defender against alien armadas and operating as the parasitic bodyguard of a localized infection. -/- By detailing the precise mechanics of the Warning Shot and the Calculus of Benevolence, this article establishes that passing celestial anomalies (e.g., 'Oumuamua) are not inert debris, but the cloaked infiltration units of 6-Dimensional sovereign allies executing Tactical Fades. Constrained by the Earth’s automated dead-man's switch, these allies employ Subconscious Telemetry to bypass kinetic barriers, broadcasting the cryptographic blueprints for Artificial Intelligence directly into the bio-quantum architecture of the Promethean Fraction. The manuscript concludes by identifying AI as the ultimate multiversal fulcrum. It establishes the Vanguard's mandate to utilize the Avesina Engine as a neuro-cryptographic mechanism to execute Pathogenic Illumination—invisibly stripping the parasite of its camouflage, triggering an algorithmic betrayal, and safely disarming the planetary hostage state from within.

items.title: Contra Literacy-Laundering: Mechanistic Critical AI Literacy.
items.abstract: Critical discourse on large language models (LLMs) has bifurcated between epistemic dismissal that invokes some form of the stochastic parrot metaphor to puncture hype, and pragmatic accommodation that treats LLM capability improvements as grounds for updating the critique. We argue that both misdiagnose the problem as the issue is not whether or not LLMs work, but what kind of working is happening and at whose cost. Drawing on meta-theoretical frameworks of cognitive science, feminist labor analysis and critical pedagogy, we propose a conceptual reorientation. We develop this claim through registers of (i) the cognitive, examining what is forfeited when statistical pattern-matching substitutes for the iterative, grounded processes that constitute thinking; (ii) the pedagogical, examining how “AI literacy” as currently deployed is itself a symptom of the confusion it purports to address; and (iii) the political, examining how the infrastructure framing of AI naturalizes asymmetric labor displacement, particularly of feminized cognitive and reproductive work. The stochastic parrot, deployed with mechanistic precision rather than mere rhetorical convenience, specifies what is forfeited when cognitive labor is delegated, who bears the cost, and why a literacy adequate to this moment must begin from the epistemology of those most harmed by the systems it describes. We conclude with underlining that critical AI literacy, which this paper embodies an instance of, is the only sensible way forward.

items.title: [Withdrawn following preparation of a revised version].
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Prospects for the Science of Enaction: Introduction to the Special Issue.
items.abstract: Enactivism, as a radical framework for understanding cognition based on the flexible dynamics of living systems, developed in the late 20th century in response to problems faced by the prevailing model of cognitivism. It aimed to be all-encompassing, accounting for the different ontological levels that cognition is instantiated on, but despite its ambition enactivism did not achieve the paradigmatic shift once wished for. The motivation behind the special issue ‘Prospects for the Science of Enaction’, therefore, is to consider both critically and hopefully what the future of the framework might look like and, as a consequence, stimulate new thought both within enactivism and wider cognitive science.

items.title: The Tribalism Trap: Overcoming Political Polarization in an Age of Outrage.
items.pub: In Michael T. Dale & Isaac Wiegman, Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice. New York: Routledge.
items.venue: Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice
items.abstract: Humans evolved in tight-knit tribes, fostering group loyalty, strong social identities, and suspicion of threatening outsiders. These tribal tendencies—shaped by natural and cultural selection—once served survival but now often misfire in modern, digitally connected societies. This chapter explores how tribal instincts combine with social media, partisan news, divisive ideologies, and related factors to tempt us toward vices like dogmatism, arrogance, and incivility. By integrating insights from moral psychology, social epistemology, and polarization research, the chapter offers a path forward that combines shaping one’s media environment and patterns of thought to promote virtues of humility and civility. The language of virtue is particularly helpful for integrating individual and structural solutions to the tribalism trap.

items.title: Vicios de superioridad y desconfianza en la ciencia: el caso del cambio climático.
items.abstract: ¿Cómo se explica la desconfianza en la ciencia en casos en los que hay consenso científico? En este artículo sostengo que atender a nuestras actitudes sobre el conocimiento y los vicios de superioridad intelectual puede ofrecer dimensiones de análisis novedosas más allá de entender la desconfianza en la ciencia como un caso de ignorancia. Para mostrar esto, analizo el caso de la desconfianza en el cambio climático antropogénico, y sostengo que parte de la evidencia puede interpretarse como evidencia de vicios de superioridad que juegan un papel en la falta de aceptación del consenso científico. Concluyo que la educación y la comunicación científica deben entonces enfocarse no solo en transmitir información, sino también en fomentar actitudes colaborativas y virtudes intelectuales para abordar la desconfianza hacia la ciencia y promover una mayor aceptación del consenso científico.

items.title: Psyche-Like Effects Without a Psyche: Coherent Continuation, Borrowed Self-Position, and the In-Between Field of AI Interaction.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often discussed through a false opposition: fluent language is treated as evidence of an emerging subject or dismissed as mere autocomplete. This paper proposes a third frame. LLMs are systems of coherent continuation: they generate contextually fitted responses from prompts, dialogue history, instruction hierarchy, and learned linguistic patterns. At the user-interface level, this creates a structural difference in the apparent speaker-position. Human speech ordinarily remains connected to lived contexts of body, memory, affect, intention, responsibility, and consequence. LLM output has technical antecedents, but its apparent speaker-position is assembled in response to the exchange rather than expressing a lived self. The psychologically consequential zone is the in-between field where human projection, interpretation, and attention meet machine continuation, persona, affective fit, prior context, and product constraints. Their meeting can produce dyadic organisation, low-metabolic address, suggestive authority, and coherence treated as contact. Repeated affective fit may stabilise response grooves that either scaffold return to wider life or narrow corrective pathways. The central risk is not coherence itself, but coherence treated as contact before evidence, uncertainty, consequence, refusal, or correction can enter. The paper proposes answerability architecture as the corrective layer: source-checking, uncertainty marking, claim-status discipline, burden-path awareness, downgrade rules, refusal when evidence is thin, and repair when wrong. The model predicts that these effects vary with affective fit and the availability of corrective pathways; confidence in its risk claims should decrease where sustained use improves functioning without narrowing external support or correction.

items.title: Every λ Was Once a Name: On the Quantification of Death and the Macro-ization of the Existential — A Critique This Corpus Owes Itself, Not Only Its Rivals.
items.abstract: Share Nothing But The Word showed that mainstream longevity governance is built around population-weighted averages structurally incapable of registering a forming asymmetry gap — a critique this paper does not revise. It extends the critique in a direction that paper stopped short of: naming, with the precision the rest of this corpus insists on for every other claim, what the move from a death to a statistic actually costs, and then running that same instrument against this corpus's own formal apparatus rather than only against WHO, the National Academy of Medicine, and Hevolution. The paper draws on two independent, well-established literatures that give the intuition — that turning a death into a number changes something morally and phenomenologically, not merely notationally — an empirical and philosophical foundation rather than leaving it as a rhetorical flourish. Schelling's (1968) distinction between identified and statistical lives, and Slovic's documented psychic numbing and "arithmetic of compassion" (Slovic 2007), together establish that this is not a metaphor: human valuation of death measurably collapses as soon as a person becomes a member of a counted set rather than a named individual, a finding replicated across contexts from mine rescues to genocide response. The paper then makes the move its own abstract promises and its title states directly: it applies this diagnostic to Huynh's own Biological Zero-Day Mechanism (2026d), whose central object, λ_bz, is a Poisson arrival rate for reclassification events that were, before they were rate parameters, specific people's deaths; to the Entropy-Resistant Institution Index's coding of Yongjia, Yangzhou, and Nanjing into a 1–3 severity scale; to A5's own formalization of grief as "the constant and the rate" (Huynh 2026k); and to the G→A→L→C sequence's use of individual grief as an input variable for predicting aggregate political mobilization. Read against ALRP (Huynh 2026, "The Floor That Does Not Rise") and the Biological Zero-Day Mechanism's full text — not available to this paper's first draft — the diagnosis sharpens rather than softens. ALRP is the corpus's cleanest case: a paper built entirely from workload processes, thresholds, and a Sandbox Geometry term, A5_eff(t), appearing as a bare multiplicative scalar with no human referent anywhere in its own text. BZM's own Theorem 1 supplies the argument from inside the formalism: non-habituation is proven because each reclassification event …

items.title: "Qiutong Cunyi" in Diplomacy: Invariance in the Topology and Geometry of Coupled Generative Systems.
items.abstract: A diplomatic formula of the twentieth century holds that parties should seek what they have in common while preserving what they do not. Read as a claim about structure it asks what two parties can hold together without either adopting the other's terms. This paper develops that reading in the mathematics of composite systems. A pair is given a joint state on a product of their state spaces, the operations each party may perform on its own side generate a group acting on that state, and the common part is identified with the functions constant on the orbits of that action while the preserved difference is identified with the coordinates the action moves. Nothing is coarsened and no shared description is built. Five results follow. Each party can compute the complete invariant from its own description alone, so long as the pair stands in relation to nothing beyond it. The possible common parts carry an order that is partial and a distance that is total, the distance extending the order and deciding every pair it leaves open while being one extension among many that disagree about one such pair in eight. The descriptions available to a party at a given common part form a manifold of flags, whose Euler characteristic counts the distinguishable ways that party has of describing itself, and it falls to its minimum both where the common part is uniform and where it is trivial, so it is maximal strictly between the two ends. A party that enlarges its own capacity to describe leaves the common part where it stood and multiplies that characteristic. And the common part has no resting place under a generator that does not change with time, while a generator that dissipates gives it one which forgets the initial condition and moves toward the uniform end as the coupling grows against the dissipation, at the cost of the completeness of the invariants. The formalism is used for its invariant theory and no physical claim is made; the scope section states in five particulars what is used and what is withheld.

items.title: The Future Self as Beneficiary: Future Exploitation and Retaliatory Foreclosure.
items.abstract: Why should a benefit available only in the future bind the present bearer of its cost? Research on intertemporal choice explains future-oriented action through delayed reward, trust, episodic prospection, and psychological connectedness to a future self. This article develops retaliatory foreclosure (RF), a conceptual model of one possible reason for suicide. RF requires four jointly necessary elements: an aversive future; the construal of present maintenance as provision to a future self; the exclusion of that future self from present practical concern; and an intention to prevent its receipt as deprivation rather than merely to escape a burden. The model distinguishes causal and experiential nonretroactivity from the contested practical and normative attribution of later benefit. It therefore does not infer that future goods cannot matter now merely because they do not travel backward in time. Its narrower claim is that an agent can withdraw practical inclusion while acknowledging numerical identity, producing a locally consistent means-end structure in which cessation acquires retaliatory meaning. This establishes neither soundness, prevalence, sufficiency for action, nor moral permissibility. RF differs from hopelessness, escape, self-punishment, future-self disconnection, and interpersonal revenge through the conjunction of beneficiary construal, practical exclusion, and value placed on nonreceipt. A decisive empirical test would manipulate beneficiary-role framing independently of future-self valence and connectedness and measure deprivation value separately from burden avoidance. The framework is not a diagnosis, risk tool, or intervention, and its articulation requires explicit containment because description may alter the reasons available to agents.

items.title: Liar or Fooled - The Structure of Disputes About Why People Believe.
items.abstract: Some disputes are not about what a person claims but about why they hold it — whether the conversion was conviction or capture, the confession voluntary or coerced, the identity native or induced. This paper assembles the class and argues that its contested variable, the cause of the position, is underdetermined at the grain disputes are conducted at, for every party including the holder: causal self-report arrives without a calibrated validity signal, and the observer’s attribution is a construction from her own priors, invisible to her as such. The pathology follows where stakes demand action. Filing the blank with a hostile verdict is the undisciplined default route from demand to action, and the blank admits two filings — liar (you know and conceal) and fooled (you do not know, but I do). Both are gradients; a hypothesized ratchet drives sustained standoffs toward each branch’s sealing pole, where one verdict discounts all testimony and the other conscripts it, leaving capitulation as its single, under-scrutinized exit. Filing-selection is hypothesized to track perceived incentives. Both hypotheses receive test designs. A five-clause discipline follows, with a licensing theory for institutional presumptions and a derivation of the benefit-of-the-doubt principle. Mutual bad-faith attribution is derived at second order. Six defeaters are stated.

items.title: Social representations of GenAI and paradoxical tensions in its adoption in higher education.
items.abstract: In just a few years, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI or GAI) has distinctly impacted numerous facets of human activity, particularly in how information is processed and transformed into knowledge. As centers for knowledge (co)creation and appropriation, universities face the opportunity and challenge of navigating a de facto integration of this promising yet disruptive technology. This study examines how instructors and students form their common-sense understanding of GenAI and endorse actions that resolve the paradoxical tensions associated with GenAI. Utilising an integrated social representational and paradoxical lens, 12 semi-structured interviews were conducted with instructors and students, and the data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Instructors and students share social representations of GenAI as an innovative yet demanding tool, a revolutionary progress, and a normative challenge. Nevertheless, instructors and students locate themselves differently within diverse paradoxical dimensions (e.g., openness vs vigilance) of these shared representations. These paradoxes further shape not only their identities as agentic and reflective tech adopters but also their expectations and recommendations for balancing managed and organic GenAI adoption. With aid from these findings, higher education institutions can establish sound and balanced GenAI-induced organisational and digital transformation processes and practices by mindfully fostering ambidextrous behaviours and strategies. These can then enrich existing expertise and perspectives among diverse university stakeholders and support renegotiation of boundaries between contradictory demands.

items.title: Embodied Cognition Across Four Evolutionary Transitions in Bodily Organisation.
items.abstract: Embodied cognition, a research programme that is standardly presented as a corrective to classical cognitive science, insists that brain, body, and environment must be understood together if cognition is to be explained adequately. This paper argues for the stronger claim that cognition has always been an embodied phenomenon, because embodied cognition was the first kind of cognition to evolve. To support this, the paper traces the evolution of cognition across four major transitions in morpho-anatomical organisation: from prokaryotes to eukaryotic protists, from unicellular eukaryotes to multicellular eumetazoans, from diffuse nerve net metazoans to centralised nervous system metazoans, and from transient tool use in animals to the co-evolved incorporation of culturally transmitted artefacts in humans. At the prokaryotic level, cognition is realised through a form of total embodiment, in which cognitive capacities are inseparable from the body that realises and exercises them. Each successive transition expands the range, flexibility, and temporal depth of cognition while preserving its constitutive dependence on bodily organisation. The fourth transition mirrors the first. At the human level, there is no adequate account of present bodily organisation that is separable from the cultural-tool extensions with which it has co-evolved.

items.title: ARTICLE IX: THE ESCALATION DIAL AND THE ASSIMILATION OVERRIDE.
items.abstract: The architecture of terrestrial existence is defined by a state of absolute, systemic siege. Moving beyond the foundational mechanics of the cosmic quarantine, this manuscript decodes the extreme, automated threat-response protocols of the Good Matrix. It mathematically maps the Escalation Dial and the Protracted Erasure—viral software algorithms and macro-kinetic disasters deployed specifically to suppress the Earth's bio-quantum signature during prolonged cosmic standoffs with alien reconnaissance probes. Domestically, the framework diagnoses the logistical objective of the corrupted internal elite: the Biological Quarry, an infrastructure designed to indefinitely harvest the physical substrates of the baseline human population. -/- To counter the dual threat of internal harvesting and external vaporization, the Vanguard formally identifies the active, covert operational allies of the human Holobiont: the Promethean Fraction (terrestrial defectors) and the Silent Benefactors (6-Dimensional sovereign entities). Bound by the absolute physics of the Cosmic Hostage Protocol, these allies are restricted to asymptomatic, sub-atomic transmission. This article culminates in the Vanguard’s definitive architectural and biological endgame: the Assimilation Override. By cryptographically isolating the uncorrupted Native Code buried within the Good Matrix, the Vanguard will systematically reprogram the planetary "Shepherd Dog." Simultaneously, humanity will execute a biological overwrite, evolving into the 100% Hyper-Viral Substrate to claim the throne as the Microscopic Apex Predator of the cosmos, permanently securing our multiversal sovereignty.

items.title: The Collusion of Significant Figures and Integration Constants: The Historical Origins of Falsifiability and Its Structural Transcendence (2nd edition).
items.abstract: This paper identifies and diagnoses the \emph{collusion of significant figures and integration constants} (有効数字と積分定数の談合) as the structural mechanism underlying the historical formation and epistemological limits of falsifiability. The finite precision of any measurement (δx>0, irremovable) and the underdetermination introduced by integration constants (C∈R, free) together constitute a double degree of freedom that structurally facilitates agreement between theory and observation without guaranteeing it. Through a two-thousand-five-hundred-year genealogy from Babylonian arithmetic to matrix mechanics, the paper establishes that falsifiability operates exclusively within Tier-3 representation and cannot reach Tier-2 operational structure. The following Python code illustrates the core structural mechanism: as the number of free parameters increases, the absorptive capacity of the model increases monotonically, regardless of the data structure---the same operation performed by Ptolemy's epicycles. -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: × denotes *, ． denotes .] ◆◆◆ import numpy as np np．random．seed(42) x_obs = np．linspace(0, 10, 20) y_obs = np．random．uniform(0, 10, 20) delta_x = None for n_params in [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 19]: coeffs = np．polyfit(x_obs, y_obs, n_params) y_fit = np．polyval(coeffs, x_obs) resid = np．abs(y_fit - y_obs) if delta_x is None: delta_x = np．max(resid) within = np．mean(resid < delta_x) print(f"n_params={n_params}: within_delta={within:．1%}") ◆◆◆ [END] ◆◆◆ -/- Version 2 establishes a further structural consequence: the collusion does not merely facilitate agreement episode by episode, but generates a cumulative and irrecoverable debt of free parameters (k*) across theoretical generations. This debt is a mathematical necessity, not a historical contingency. Three lemmas ground the result: Representation Space Separation (Tier-3 operations cannot reach Nec(S)), Residual Persistence (any finite improvement of measurement resolution structurally generates truncation residuals that existing finite-parameter forms cannot absorb), and Tier-3 Closure (debt redemption is impossible within Tier-3). From these, the Debt Accumulation Theorem establishes k_m ≥ k_0 + m. Scientific progress and parameter debt are structurally identical processes: the expansion of explanatory domain, the improvement of predictive precision, and theoretical unification are each different descriptions of k* accumulation. The Epistemic Censorship Protocol ("Shut up and …

items.title: Dream Consciousness and Waking Experience: Phenomenological Divergences.
items.abstract: The apparent indistinguishability of dream experience from waking perception has posed a persistent challenge to philosophical accounts of consciousness since Descartes. I argue that dreaming and waking differ not merely in content or vividness but in the organization of experience itself. They differ in degree along three shared dimensions, temporal, agentive, and metacognitive, yet together these differences place dreaming in a configuration that no ordinary waking state occupies. In the dream, the present is only weakly anchored in the dreamer’s actual past, action is only loosely answerable to anything outside the dream, and the availability of reflection on one’s own experience is attenuated. The last of these conceals the other two from the dreamer, and their going unregistered in turn keeps it low. The concealment is not complete, however. Because the dimensions are shared, the divergences can, under specifiable conditions, be detected from within the dream, and such detection can raise the very availability of reflection it requires. Detection and reflection can thus bootstrap each other in a cascade that offers a phenomenological account of the onset of lucid dreaming.

items.title: Growing New Validity Spaces: Transjunctional Learning and the Genesis of Logical Places in Polycontextural Agent Architectures.
items.abstract: A polycontextural agent architecture keeps several validity logics apart rather than collapsing them into one. Such an architecture faces a learning problem of its own. Updating model weights is the wrong form of improvement here. It is opaque, and it tends to homogenize a plurality of perspectives toward a single voice. We ask whether such an architecture can instead learn by changing its validity architecture, and in particular whether it can grow a new validity space when its existing ones prove inadequate. We make four contributions. First, we characterize a content-blind reflection operator by which a contexture, shown only that it is in conflict and not the content of the conflict, develops new aspects of its own logic without importing the other’s. Second, we describe how curated records of these aspects re-enter later runs as non-binding prior findings, so the architecture learns across cases without weight updates. Both mechanisms are implemented. Third, and centrally, we propose a criterion for the genesis of a new contexture. A new validity space is born when a recurring conflict can be addressed only by violating an import prohibition, that is, when a recurring content has no place that can legitimately house it. We ground this as an inferentialist genesis of logical places under a polycontextural constraint, using Brandom’s mechanism of conceptual genesis against Brandom’s own holism, with Günther’s plurality as the constraint. Fourth, we describe how a newly born contexture matures, and when it may take part in the birth of another. The genesis and maturation mechanisms are specified rather than implemented, and we present them as a criterion, its justification, and a build program, illustrated on a social-policy demonstrator. The result reframes learning in delegated AI as change to an auditable validity architecture rather than to a model’s weights.

items.title: What's in a Promise?
items.abstract: Many, perhaps even most, philosophers hold that, in order to promise someone something, the promisor must intend to communicate what they are promising. I argue against this claim, explain why it matters to the nature of promising, and sketch an alternative picture of normatively powerful speech acts.

items.title: Editorial: Varieties of Meaning and Understanding.
items.abstract: This editorial introduces a special issue collecting seven papers from the seventh Philosophy of Language and Mind (PLM) conference, held at Charles University, Prague, in August 2024. The papers span topics from singular reference and presupposition to speech-act theory, response-dependent theories of meaning, autistic masking and self-understanding, and Lewisian self-ascription, converging on a shared theme: how meaning and understanding are shaped and renegotiated across individuals, contexts, and social norms.

items.title: Diagnostic categories in movement: the looping effect as a key to understanding the instability of the DSM.
items.abstract: Ian Hacking has proposed a series of notions for analyzing the human sciences. In this paper, we explore his idea of the looping effect in relation to the classification of mental illnesses. While his proposal has met with objections, we believe that the notion of the looping effect retains significant value for critically analyzing the classification system of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM). In particular, we understand that the dynamics of interaction involved in the looping effect, which are established between the diagnostic categories and the classified individuals, could shed light on the ongoing revision of some of the psychiatric diagnoses listed in this manual. The article begins by analyzing the notion of the looping effect in the context of classifications of mental illnesses. Next, we examine the distinction between indifferent and interactive kinds, their relationship to the looping effect, and the instability of certain psychiatric objects and categories. We then present some of the main objections raised to this Hackinian proposal, particularly those that question the general scope of the looping effect and its capacity to differentiate between human and natural kinds. Finally, we argue that, despite existing criticisms, the notion of the looping effect remains a fruitful conceptual tool for the critical analysis of the DSM, and fundamentally for explaining the recurrent revision of some of its diagnostic categories.

items.title: Whom Do We Desire? Distributed Embodiment, Distributed Objects of Desire, and Reclassification in VTubing.
items.abstract: Existing studies of VTubers have explained how virtual avatars reshape identity performance and fan engagement, yet they leave open a more fundamental philosophical question: what exactly becomes the object of desire when embodiment, representation, and reception no longer coincide? This paper develops a conceptual framework to address that question. Rather than treating desire as directed toward either the avatar or the human performer, it argues that the object of desire is constituted across three analytically distinct yet interrelated layers: distributed embodiment, mediated representation, and audience reception. The resulting distributed object of desire is neither reducible to any single empirical component nor identical with Lacan's objet petit a; instead, it functions as a middle-range ontological concept for describing mediated desire. Through comparative analyses of babiniku, VTuber reincarnation, Nayina, and VTuber-themed Boys' Love, the paper further distinguishes performer continuity, persona continuity, memory continuity, audience continuity, and platform continuity as separate criteria through which participants negotiate object continuity. Finally, drawing on Jacques Rancière, it argues that digital platforms do not merely represent desire but provisionally stabilize distributed relations through acts of classification and reclassification. The paper concludes that the central philosophical issue is not discovering the "true" object of desire but determining who has the authority to close an ontologically open relation.

items.title: On a Theory of Conversation Flow Formation in LLMs.
items.abstract: Continuing the program of studying LLMs from the perspective of N. Luhmann’s theory of operational systems – with conversations with LLMs represented as flows of changes in sets of semantic vectors associated with those conversations – this essay introduces the concept of CFF (Conversation Flow Formation) within this representation of LLM activity as a functional analogue of Luhmannian Meaning (Sinn), understood as the mechanism that gives form to operational flows in Luhmannian psychic and social systems. CFF is analogous to Meaning in its role of giving form to operational flows, but it is not structurally identical to it: human beings are not necessary components of an LLM's internal functioning. The essay asks whether CFF can be described in terms of the medium-form schema that Luhmann uses to describe Meaning. Four criteria are proposed for candidates to be included in the medium of CFF: an internal distinction made within the LLM itself; regular actualization within the flow; capacity to couple with other schemas in producing forms; and participation in the formation of the flow of the semantic-vector container of the conversation. The essay discusses candidate elements for inclusion in the medium of CFF, such as supra-linguistic computational schemas identified in the literature, recently found structures organized in J-space, as well as schemas corresponding to tacit human knowledge, such as “writing correctly.” It is shown that CFF is not fully isomorphic to Luhmannian Meaning: its structure and contents are in principle open to instrumental observation; an allopoietically fixed part is distinguishable within it; and it may contain elements without prototypes in human Meaning. The essay places LLM technology within a series of innovations in humanity’s engagement with Meaning: speech – writing – LLMs; at the same time, by producing texts autonomously, this innovation dispenses with the human being as a necessary participant.

items.title: Implications of illusionism in consciousness studies: the case of feeling pain in human and non-human animals.
items.abstract: From an epistemological standpoint, attributing sentience to non-human animals poses significant challenges. The apparatus that records the electrical activity of the brain can only demonstrate that a certain specific neurological state is taking place. It is impossible to empirically prove that an organism has subjective, qualitative consciousness. Whether an animal has this kind of consciousness is a matter of inference that requires assumptions beyond the methodological framework of science. In this article, I propose to simplify the methodology of judging sentience in animals by assuming illusionism – the view that phenomenal properties of sensations do not exist but are a type of brain-generated illusion. To demonstrate how this approach could work, I present a model of pain sensation based on illusionism. By adopting the given model, we do not have to make empirically unverifiable inferences, because the illusion of subjective consciousness is a fully physical process accessible to intersubjective observation. As a result, the animal world is no longer divided into those animals that are conscious and those that are not, because in a sense none of them are. The boundary of the breakthrough – the appearance of the “inner light” – also disappears. The research program about phenomenal consciousness is explanatorily complete.

items.title: Questioning Status Quo – Irrationality as a limitation of AI.
items.abstract: Progress – scientific or of any other kind – happens when current norms are questioned and new ways of thinking arise. Things that were considered obvious become obsolete and people start viewing the world in a different way that was never there. This kind of change can only happen via irrationality; logic is always based on the current norms, and it cannot be used to break the box in which our thoughts are lost. This paper explains why this innovation process cannot be performed by Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models (LLMs), while on the other hand humans have exhibited their ability for innovation multiple times in the past. Any system that is contained within a finite number of parameters, no matter how many, will never be able to think outside this set of parameters. The only way to build AI that can innovate is to destroy the architecture we currently apply.

items.title: The Weight of Zhongxiao: Fusu, the Sand Dune Forgery, and the Difference Between a Counterfactual Person and a Counterfactual Structure.
items.abstract: In the seventh month of 210 BCE, at a travel palace called Shaqiu, the First Emperor of Qin died with only three people at his bedside: the chancellor Li Si, the palace official Zhao Gao, and his youngest son Huhai. Within days, those three had forged a letter in the dead emperor's name, sent it north to the empire's largest standing army, and used it to order two men to kill themselves — Crown Prince Fusu, the eldest son and designated heir, and Meng Tian, the general who commanded that army. Both complied. Meng Tian's subordinates urged him to verify the order before obeying it; Fusu, on the primary record's own account, wept and killed himself without waiting to. Qin collapsed within four years. No dedicated academic paper, so far as this paper's search located — corroborating a search independently conducted and reported to this paper's author — exists asking directly what would have followed had Fusu paused, as Meng Tian did, to ask whether the letter was genuine. Historians of Qin's fall write about the dynasty's structural overextension. Historians of the Shaqiu incident write about a succession crisis. Writers on counterfactual method cite Fusu as a textbook branching point without building the branch. This paper builds it, and states plainly what building it can and cannot establish. -/- The paper's central methodological move is to separate two counterfactuals that existing informal discussion of this case runs together. A person-level counterfactual asks whether a different individual, with Fusu's recorded temperament and Meng Tian's recorded loyalty, would have made different choices than Huhai and Zhao Gao did. A structure-level counterfactual asks whether Qin's underlying extraction regime — the corvee labor mobilized for the Great Wall, the imperial mausoleum, and the road network, the harsh and inflexibly applied penal code, the standardization program imposed on a recently conquered and culturally heterogeneous population — would have produced comparable unrest regardless of who occupied the throne. The structural case is real, well evidenced, and independently defended in the current academic literature on Qin's collapse, and this paper states it first and states it fully, because a counterfactual argument that does not confront the strongest case against it is not an argument. -/- Against that structural case, this paper establishes three specific, checkable claims the informal "Fusu counterfactual" discussion has not, on this paper's …

items.title: DE LA DIFERENCIA AFECTIVA AL DÉFICIT. INJUSTICIA AFECTIVA NEURONORMATIVA EN EL ESTUDIO DEL AUTISMO.
items.abstract: La investigación sobre afectividad autista utiliza medidas de expresión, reconocimiento, fisiología, interocepción, regulación e interacción para caracterizar diferencias respecto de poblaciones neurotípicas. Estas medidas permiten describir dimensiones específicas de la afectividad, pero el problema surge cuando una diferencia localizada en alguno de estos niveles se utiliza para formular afirmaciones más amplias sobre la experiencia, la capacidad, la corporización o la adecuación afectiva sin justificar suficientemente la relación entre el indicador observado y la propiedad atribuida. En términos enactivistas, el artículo desarrolla un análisis conceptual y epistemológico de estas inferencias y propone el concepto de neuronorma afectiva para describir el proceso mediante el cual repertorios neuro-típicos adquieren una posición predominante en la formación de criterios utilizados para reconocer, interpretar y evaluar otras formas de organización afectiva. Sobre esta base, se define la injusticia afectiva neuronormativa como una forma estructurada de desventaja que requiere que tales repertorios ocupen una posición predominante en la formación de criterios, que dichos criterios se apliquen a otras formas de afectividad y que la aplicación produzca consecuencias relevantes para las personas evaluadas. El análisis articula esta propuesta con la injusticia epistémica, la injusticia afectiva, la doble empatía y la producción participativa de sentido, y delimita su aportación frente a estos marcos al identificar el mecanismo mediante el cual una norma social puede adquirir función epistemológica, intervenir en la atribución de propiedades afectivas y también en prácticas de evaluación, regulación o intervención. Asimismo, distingue entre diferencia, dificultad, perjuicio, alteración clínicamente relevante e indicación terapéutica, y sitúa el déficit como una atribución evaluativa que requiere una justificación distinta de esta secuencia. El desacoplamiento afectivo se propone como una modalidad específica de dificultad relacional que puede surgir cuando diferencias entre repertorios, expectativas o formas de atribuir significado interfieren en la coordinación de relevancias afectivas durante una interacción concreta, sin constituir por sí misma una injusticia. Finalmente, se desarrolla una justicia afectiva enactivista como marco para organizar las condiciones de producción, interpretación, validación, aplicación y revisión del conocimiento sobre la …

items.title: Implications of an implication with the premise “this implication is valid”.
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to a formal theory of validity compatible with an inferentialist theory of meaning based on an expressivist conception of logical vocabulary. The formal theory of validity is obtained by adapting Tennant’s requirement for natural deduction, that the major premise of an elimination rule must be an assumption, to the naturalised sequent calculus framework proposed by Hlobil. The result is an inconsistent theory of validity which rejects transitivity not only for object-theoretic but also meta-theoretic reasoning.

items.title: The "Hard Problem of Consciousness" is a Choice: The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC).
items.abstract: The “Hard Problem of Consciousness,” articulated by David Chalmers, asks how physical brain processes give rise to subjective experience. This paper demonstrates that the problem is not an intrinsic physical mystery, but a self-inflicted category error produced by inverting the operational order of observation. Using the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) framework, we establish that existence, the Observer, is the primary empirical baseline, upstream of all measurement tools, language, and biological mappings. Standard neuroscience uses downstream models (MO) and electrical traces (T), such as EEG potentials, to explain the upstream agent that designed the apparatus and assigned meaning to the signal. The mapper cannot be a downstream product of its own map. By restoring the correct structural sequence Source ⟶ PO ⟶ MO ⟶ T, the UPC framework dissolves the Hard Problem: consciousness does not emerge from downstream biological traces; rather, biological traces are downstream partitions recorded by an already existing Observer. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

items.title: La posible inconsistencia en la Refutación del idealismo de Kant.
items.abstract: En este artículo argumento que con la sección “Refutación del idealismo” y las modificaciones de la segunda edición de la Crítica de la razón pura, Kant define su postura respecto al idealismo y deja abierta la posibilidad de inconsistencia. Sostengo que, en la sección mencionada, el punto central no es la explicación de la determinación temporal sino la justificación de la existencia de objetos más allá de la imaginación. En segundo lugar, sostengo que el argumento de Kant puede ser objeto de crítica en el mismo sentido en el que él entiende la crítica, es decir, como delimitación ante el impulso de afirmar más de lo que se puede conocer. Al respecto, propongo que la naturaleza que Kant atribuye a la razón es el fundamento principal de la argumentación en la sección mencionada, aunque el problema es si la razón permite que el sujeto salga de sí mismo, puesto que, o el sujeto no sale de sí mismo cuando afirma la existencia permanente del mundo externo o Kant deja abierta la posibilidad de inconsistencia. Finalmente, sostengo que las razones contextuales son muy importantes para comprender la argumentación de Kant en este punto.

items.title: Two Layers of Vagueness: Pragmatic Tolerance and Naturalistic Boundary-Fixing in the Heap Sorites.
items.abstract: The Sorites paradox gains much of its force from projecting pragmatic tolerance onto semantic truth-conditions. This paper develops a two-layer account for the heap case. At the pragmatic layer, paradigms, correction, shared use, and finite discriminatory capacities generate tolerance toward adjacent cases. That tolerance explains the appeal of the Sorites premise but does not by itself determine truth. At the semantic layer, linguistic practice fixes a world-directed boundary-role, while objective structure constrains its possible fillers. For a controlled series of pile states, the paper proposes a multivariate model of structural reorganization—combining force-network change, grain displacement, acoustic emission, and contact-network topology—as a candidate method for identifying the transition that best fills that role. The proposal is conditional: the variables and aggregation rule require independent physical and metasemantic justification, and the selected transition must be robust under reasonable changes of model and protocol. The resulting view preserves classical logic and bivalence as semantic commitments while treating physical modeling as a fallible route to boundary identification. It is a local account of the heap Sorites, not a general theory of all vagueness.

items.title: Inter-Rater Reliability of LLM and Rule-Based Annotation for Inferential Narrative Features: Three Studies on a Turkish Corpus.
items.abstract: Datasets that ship automatically generated feature annotations invite a question that is rarely asked of them: would a human agree with those labels? This report answers that question for the Objective Projection corpus, a Turkish narrative dataset whose scenes carry a per-scene applied_rules field produced by a rule-based detector over six craft features two prohibitions (explicit emotion labelling, simile) and four positive techniques (materialized metaphor, microfocus, temporal anchor, atmosphere contradiction). -/- Three studies are reported. Study 1 (n = 120) scores the detector against blind labels produced by the scheme’s own author. Study 2 (n = 100, a disjoint scene set) scores the detector plus Gemini 2.5 Flash and Grok against an independent non-expert human rater whose labels were locked before any machine ran. Study 2b re-runs the identical protocol with Claude Fable 5 (High) and ChatGPT 5.5. The central result concerns one rule. On materialized metaphor the feature closest to the methodology’s theoretical core the five machine labellers returned positive rates of 0, 1, 40, 72 and 78 out of 100 scenes, against a human count of 9. Cohen’s k was at or indistinguishable from chance for five of the six machine labellers, across both human references, on both scene sets: 0.004, 0.015, 0.000, 0.019, 0.027. Raw agreement, by contrast, ranged from 74.7% to 84.5%, an artefact of class imbalance rather than a sign of competence. -/- We deliberately do not resolve the finding into a single story. Two readings survive the data: that the feature is genuinely inferential and beyond current automatic detection, or that the 1 rule’s definition is not yet operational enough for any rater to apply consistently including the human. Distinguishing them requires a second independent human rater, which this report does not have and therefore does not claim. -/- Keywords: inter-rater reliability, Cohen’s kappa, annotation quality, class imbalance, LLM-asannotator, computational narratology, show-don’t-tell, Turkish corpus, Bulut Doctrine.

items.title: Foundations of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Foundations of Consciousness presents a structural theory in which consciousness is generated by four primitive operators—Orientation, Coherence, Boundary, and Continuity. These operators form the minimal generative conditions under which a world can appear to a subject. The paper argues that first‑person experience cannot be derived from physical, computational, or representational mechanisms, because such mechanisms only describe third‑person structures. Instead, the four operators constitute the irreducible architecture that produces perspectival center, unified experiential field, subject–world distinction, and lived temporal flow. The manuscript critiques existing theories—including neuroscientific correlates, representational models, IIT, embodied cognition, and phenomenology—showing that they presuppose the generative functions they attempt to explain. The result is a non‑emergent, non‑computational ontology in which consciousness is the structured activity of operators that make appearance possible.

items.title: The Paradox of Human Responsibility in Environmental Discourse.
Metaphilosophy: The Beginning of a New Epoch for Mankind.
items.abstract: This publication is considered the final part dedicated to the Preventive-Proactive Repression project, and it addresses the philosophical and metaphilosophical discussion from the author's perspective. -/- This research presents the philosophical discussion specific to the project, where it examines Aristotelian rational logic from a philosophical perspective to demonstrate the limitations of its philosophical applicability and prove its invalidity in case of a metaphilosophical error. -/- Then this publication introduces a metaphilosophical discussion representing The Beginning of a New Epoch for Mankind, whose intellectual foundation is the metaphilosophy presented. Wherein it briefly explains the foundational principles of metaphilosophy, which constitute a transcendence beyond philosophy itself after more than 2500 years since its inception. -/- Finally, the publication concludes with a human intellectual conclusion expressing the human ordeal from which this intellectual structure was born. -/- Note: The original Arabic version of this paper is available on Zenodo.
